proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open threat models, security best practices, design patterns, and cross-cutting privacy guardrails across agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical body chartered to define open threat models, hardening baselines, privacy-preserving execution workflows, and verification patterns across autonomous AI agent architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e]. Operating as an intersecting architectural layer across AAIF initiatives, the group evaluates security implications spanning delegated authorizations, multi-agent interactions, secure memory, tool invocation boundaries, and sensitive data leakage [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

The group coordinates closely with peer AAIF workstreams—including [Identity and Trust](identity-and-trust.md), [Accuracy and Reliability](accuracy-and-reliability.md), and [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)—as well as external standard bodies such as the OWASP Agentic AI Project [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Priority Themes

The working group focuses on core threat modeling and defensive infrastructure patterns across agent lifecycles [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e]:

- **Capability-Based Auth and Delegated Identity**: Securing tool invocation constraints, agent-to-agent authentications, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server trust verification in concert with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e].
- **Privacy and Sensitive Data Protection**: Defining redaction, PII obfuscation, and zero-knowledge (ZK) or hardware-isolated execution boundaries (e.g., trusted execution environments and encrypted vector databases) to ensure agents query protected data without external leakage [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Blast Radius and Rogue Agent Containment**: Establishing kernel-enforced sandboxing, execution checkpoints, out-of-band kill switches, and attack surface metrics limiting rogue agent derailment or tool misuse [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Commerce and Payment Guardrails**: Formulating technical controls preventing unauthorized fund draining, account credential leakage, and unbounded spending authority during [delegated payment](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md) workflows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Internal Shared Taxonomy**: Establishing strict definitions for ambiguous security terms (e.g., clarifying traditional API secrets versus confidential training data and proprietary context) before upstreaming definitions to the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

## Boundary Scope and Exclusions

To avoid domain overlap across AAIF groups, specific boundary demarcations have been established:

- **Ethics, Morality, and Societal Impact**: Questions concerning moral value judgments, algorithmic bias, and business ethics are formally deferred to the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Model Hallucinations vs. Misbehavior**: While general hallucination benchmarking resides with the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](accuracy-and-reliability.md), non-malicious agent misbehavior that causes systemic derailment or creates exploitation vectors remains under active review by Security and Privacy [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-02-17**: Working group orientation convened by Linux Foundation leadership; initiated ideation on pen testing, hook standards, audit forensics, and cross-organization alignment with OWASP [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e].
- **2026-03-03**: Alex Frazer confirmed as elected chair; consolidated initial charter themes, scoped commerce guardrails, deferred ethics questions to Governance and Policy, and initiated working group taxonomy definitions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group bridging global AI policy developments and technical agentic systems, tracking compliance requirements, risk assessment frameworks, and regulatory interfaces.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body established to evaluate how evolving global AI policy, regulatory standards, and risk management frameworks intersect with autonomous agent architectures [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f]. Operating under Linux Foundation pre-competitive collaboration and antitrust policies, the group facilitates neutral technical alignment without duplicating existing industry compliance efforts [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f] [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

The working group connects technical agent architectures to international regulatory requirements—including the EU AI Act, eIDAS 2, and data protection regimes such as GDPR—and explores collaborative frameworks with regulatory bodies, including Singapore regulators [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f] [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

# Operating Model and Methodology

The working group executes against a structured three-step working model [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]:

1. **Landscape Analysis**: Cataloging existing standards, governance frameworks, regulations, and real-world deployment use cases relevant to autonomous agents [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
2. **Gap Analysis**: Identifying specific areas where established AI and software risk frameworks fail to mitigate or address novel risks inherent to agentic autonomy, delegated execution, and dynamic tool interactions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
3. **Distilled Guidance and Principles**: Formulating actionable guidance, risk assessment protocols, and reference principles for organizations deploying autonomous agents [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

# Deliverables

Active and planned deliverables maintained by the group include [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f] [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]:

- **Working Group Charter**: Formal scope charter submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in accordance with the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].
- **Problem Set Statements**: Explicit problem statements capturing regulatory, governance, and accountability bottlenecks across horizontal agent workflows [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
- **Regulatory Landscape Matrix**: Cross-jurisdictional mapping of AI frameworks and identity regulations relevant to agent operations [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].
- **Human Oversight and Risk Protocols**: Candidate protocols for evaluating agent risk, oversight thresholds, and human-in-the-loop escalation mechanics [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].

# Operations and Meeting Protocols

The working group meets on a biweekly cadence, using a shared Google Doc as its primary running collaboration space and Discord as a secondary channel [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]. Meeting records are formally committed to the working group repository under `meeting-notes/` [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d7a6875f36a3-5c7bc654].

Recordkeeping is governed by a canonical structure (`TEMPLATE.md`) and automated through agent operating instructions (`AGENTS.md`) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-6fa126354b0b-2d7e8a4a] [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732]:

- Notes are persisted as `YYYY-MM-DD.md` linking directly to meeting recordings, transcripts, and AI-generated summaries [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-6fa126354b0b-2d7e8a4a] [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732].
- Content is structured into Topics Discussed, Decisions, Deliverables, and a tabular Action Items list with explicit owners and deadlines [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-6fa126354b0b-2d7e8a4a].
- Empty sections explicitly record "None." to ensure consistent downstream parsing across meetings [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732].
- Meeting entries are indexed in descending chronological order within the repository `README.md` [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732] [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d7a6875f36a3-5c7bc654].

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation managing working groups, evaluating project proposals, and administering the project lifecycle policy.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Technical Committee (TC) is the governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), established as a directed fund of The Linux Foundation to oversee technical vision, project proposals, and working group operations.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941] In the event of any conflict between the TC Charter and the AAIF Charter or Governing Board actions, the AAIF Charter controls.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]

# Architecture / Specification

## Composition and Leadership

Each Platinum Member of the AAIF may appoint one representative to the Technical Committee.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941] The TC elects annually a TC Chair and an optional Co-Chair to preside over meetings and coordinate committee business until resignation or replacement.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]

## Core Responsibilities

The TC facilitates collaboration across Technical Projects and the wider open-source community, with responsibilities including:[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]
- Establishing, managing, and archiving AAIF working groups such as the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).
- Coordinating technical priorities, shared architectural vision, and cross-project collaboration.
- Recommending candidate projects to the Governing Board (GB) for acceptance as Technical Projects.
- Applying and maintaining the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) and deciding project stage transitions, subject to GB approval.
- Recommending resource allocations to the GB to support Technical Projects.

## Decision-Making and Voting

The TC operates on a consensus-first basis, with formal voting conducted on a one-vote-per-voting-member standard when required:[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]
- **Quorum**: Requires at least fifty percent (50%) of voting members present. Meetings may continue without quorum, but no binding votes can occur.
- **Lazy Consensus**: Routine decisions use a 72-hour silence-as-agreement model where proposals pass automatically if no formal objection is recorded within 72 hours.
- **Electronic Balloting**: If an objection is lodged, non-meeting electronic decisions require a majority vote of all voting TC members.
- **Escalation**: Unresolved votes may be referred by any voting member to the Governing Board for resolution.
- **Charter Amendments**: Modifying the TC Charter requires a two-thirds majority vote of the TC alongside Governing Board approval.

# Lifecycle History

The formal Charter of the Technical Committee was adopted on March 3, 2026.[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, security and privacy design patterns, shared taxonomies, and cross-workgroup review checklists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35] The working group produces open threat models, shared taxonomies, and architectural design patterns that providers, consumers, and peer working groups adopt to share responsibility for trustworthy agentic systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Leadership

The working group is co-chaired by Alex Frazer and Junjie Bu (Google).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec] Formal decisions are documented on GitHub following asynchronous socialization and bi-weekly working group meetings.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec]

## Scope and Boundaries

The working group addresses security architecture, threat analysis, and privacy engineering through targeted coordination:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]
- **Security Architecture & Design Patterns**: Technical patterns for bounding agent execution, including agent skills, runtime containment, and defensive postures.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]
- **Privacy Engineering**: Focuses on technical controls such as data minimization, runtime isolation, and sensitive memory protection rather than statutory interpretation of specific legal regimes.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]
- **Cross-Workgroup Requirements**: Provides security and privacy requirements to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) for identity and authorization mechanisms, coordinates behavioral anomaly tracking with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), and aligns commerce guardrails with the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]

## Key Deliverables

Deliverables stewarded by the group include:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec]
- A living taxonomy of security and privacy terms and definitions.
- An agentic AI threat model framework and attack surface mapping.
- Security and privacy design patterns for production agents.
- The [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) guide.
- The [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md) enabling peer groups to assess technical proposals against security baselines.

# Lifecycle History

On March 17, 2026, Junjie Bu was appointed as co-chair.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec] On March 31, 2026, the working group unanimously adopted its formal mission statement (Option G) and expanded its design patterns scope to explicitly incorporate agent skills.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group serving as a vendor-neutral coordination forum to align agent observability, trace session-level behavior, and upstream standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) advances the Agentic AI Foundation mission by convening practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies to build shared understanding of agent observability.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88] Rather than operating as a competing standards body, the working group serves as an open coordination forum that aligns existing efforts, identifies architectural gaps, and upstreams guidance into existing initiatives such as OpenTelemetry, W3C Trace Context, and OWASP AOS.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]

# Architecture / Specification

## Leadership and Organization

The working group is led by Primary Contact and Chair Pavan Sudheendra.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88] It operates within the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) governance model, utilizing focus areas and community working methods to execute its technical mandate.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]

## Problem Statement and Mandate

The OT-WG was established to resolve key ecosystem challenges in agent monitoring:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]
- **Landscape Fragmentation**: Incompatible proprietary trace formats across commercial vendors risk vendor lock-in and prevent cross-framework observability.
- **Call-Level vs Session-Level Gap**: Existing semantic conventions effectively capture isolated LLM invocations but lack standard representations for multi-turn sessions, recursive subagent delegations, and tool interactions over time.
- **Accountability and Multi-Modal Lineage**: Enterprise production deployments require verifiable auditability, content lineage, and grounding tracking across modality transformations.

## Guiding Principles

The group operates under six foundational principles:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]
1. **Coordinate first, specify only when necessary**: Default to aligning with and contributing upstream to established standards bodies.
2. **Interoperability over innovation**: Extend and compose with existing specifications rather than inventing competing protocols.
3. **Observable by default**: Ensure agent architectures provide out-of-the-box telemetry hooks.
4. **Move at the speed of the ecosystem**: Deliver iteratively and incrementally.
5. **Adoption is key**: Prioritize practical, implementable conventions over abstract models.
6. **Vendor and framework neutrality**: Avoid giving structural advantage to any single commercial product or runtime.

## Focus Areas and Deliverables

The working group's founding focus area is the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md), dedicated to standardizing workflow-level causal execution traces across multi-agent environments.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]

# Lifecycle History

The Observability & Traceability Working Group draft charter was prepared and updated on April 13, 2026, defining its scope, operating principles, and liaison model with upstream standards bodies.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, security and privacy design patterns, defensive guidelines, and cross-working group review workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing open threat models, architectural security patterns, defensive implementation guidelines, and cross-working group security review processes for autonomous and agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]. Operating under the technical governance of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group focuses on safeguarding agent tool invocation, context boundaries, identity delegation, and runtime containment.

# Charter and Scope
The working group's charter and operational scope define its technical purview across agent lifecycle security without prematurely binding resources prior to formal deliverable commitments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]:
- **Threat Modeling and Risk Assessment**: Developing domain-specific threat modeling methodologies addressing complex agent execution contexts, multi-agent trust boundaries, shared memory stores, and dynamic model plasticity [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns**: Cataloging actionable patterns for human-in-the-loop oversight, hook extensibility, logical and semantic constraint enforcement, and privacy-preserving execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
- **Agent Control and Containment**: Defining architectural principles for agent isolation, post-incident forensics, runtime boundaries, and out-of-band intervention [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
- **Cross-Working Group Review and Assistance**: Establishing lightweight review workflows and checklists enabling other AAIF working groups to evaluate security and privacy implications early in their specification lifecycles [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# Deliverables
On 2026-04-14, the working group unanimously approved five initial deliverables for its 3–6 month operational horizon [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]:
1. **Taxonomy**: A living reference document defining foundational security and privacy terms to be integrated into the overarching [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) catalog [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
2. **[Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md)**: A research deliverable evaluating whether existing frameworks (such as OWASP and NIST) adequately cover agentic attack surfaces or if a novel framework is required to address compound multi-tenant, identity, and shared memory threats [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: A builder-facing collection of technical design patterns, including [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) mechanics, interceptor hooks, semantic guardrails, and privacy-preserving execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
4. **[Agentic Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)**: Educational guidance covering operational security fundamentals such as secrets management and secure tool execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
5. **[Cross-Working Group Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)**: A triage and assessment tool modeled on IETF review traditions to guide other working groups on identifying security-critical boundaries early [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# External Coordination
The working group actively monitors emerging protocol and runtime security initiatives across the broader open-source ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]:
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP) Interceptors**: Standardizing specification-level hooks across MCP implementations to allow non-security platforms to integrate external security inspection and policy enforcement [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
- **MCP Apps**: Investigating browser-like security and site identity verification primitives for in-conversation agent applications [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
- **Project Glasswing**: Tracking Linux Foundation security-tooling efforts relevant to AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-04-14**: Working group charter, scope, and initial five deliverables unanimously approved in formal votes; charter scheduled for presentation to the Technical Committee [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# References
- AAIF Security and Privacy WG Meeting Notes (2026-04-14) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive ecosystem market map and catalog generated via CNCF landscape2 tracking open-source agentic projects and standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive directory and market map documenting prominent open-source software, member initiatives, and open standards across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]. Maintained in the `aaif/aaif-landscape` repository and published at https://landscape.aaif.io, the catalog provides a categorized view of foundational runtimes, orchestration engines, protocols, and developer tooling aligned with the foundation's mission[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]. It is curated in collaboration with Foundation working groups such as the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).

# Architecture / Specification

The landscape is built on the open-source CNCF `landscape2` generator, which consumes declarative configuration files and compiles the static web surface on a daily update cadence[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

## Repository Data Structure
- `landscape.yml`: The primary registry listing member organizations, open-source projects, and open standards in alphabetical order[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- `hosted_logos/`: Vector asset storage housing required SVG logos referenced by catalog entries[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- `extra` metadata fields: Schema extensions enabling contributors to attach descriptive metadata, repository pointers, and operational context to catalog cards[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

## Entry Guidelines and Qualification Criteria
Inclusions must satisfy strict criteria to maintain neutrality and relevance across the agentic landscape[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]:
- **Open-source traction**: Projects must be open source and generally maintain at least 1,000 GitHub stars while fitting squarely into an existing landscape category[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Single category placement**: A project is assigned to a single best-fitting category box to represent its primary capability[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Exclusion of proprietary offerings**: Closed-source software, proprietary standards, commercial repackagings of open-source projects, and closed products implementing open-source interfaces are excluded[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Trademark and ownership**: Organization mapping corresponds to the legal entity or owner of the associated trademark[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Asset conventions**: Logos must be SVG files containing the English product or organization name, avoiding reversed color schemes (must have a white or transparent background), and defaulting to vertically stacked layouts when multiple options exist[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

## Licensing and Third-Party Data
While configuration files and assets in the repository follow open foundation licensing, enriched organizational data imported from Crunchbase is subject to Crunchbase Data Access Terms, restricting usage specifically to Linux Foundation landscape operations[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

proposed_concept.title: Code of Conduct
proposed_concept.description: Community standards, expected behaviors, operational scope, and violation reporting procedures governing participation across Agentic AI Foundation activities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) Code of Conduct establishes community standards, behavioral expectations, and violation handling procedures to foster an inclusive and harassment-free environment across all Foundation activities[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588]. It mandates respectful and collaborative engagement across technical projects, working groups, committees, events, and online communication platforms[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

# Operational Procedures
## Scope and Applicability
The policy formally governs all proceedings of the Governing Board, [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), Working Groups, Outreach Committee, and any other administrative body of the AAIF, as well as general foundation activities not covered by a separate project-specific policy[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588]. In-person and virtual events managed by professional events staff operate under the Linux Foundation Events Code of Conduct in conjunction with this foundation policy, while individual technical projects hosted under the AAIF umbrella maintain and enforce their own project-level codes of conduct[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

## Expected and Unacceptable Behaviors
Community members are required to employ welcoming, inclusive language, respect differing viewpoints, accept constructive feedback gracefully, and act in the collective interest of the community[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588]. Prohibited conduct includes verbal, visual, or physical harassment; discrimination based on protected characteristics; deliberate intimidation or stalking; sustained disruption of discussions or presentations; publication of private information without consent; and trolling or personal attacks[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

## Enforcement and Appeals
Suspected violations are reported through designated foundation reporting channels and reviewed by designated community leadership[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588]. Enforcement determinations adhere to tiered corrective consequences ranging from private reprimands to permanent expulsion from AAIF communication channels, committees, and events[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588]. Respondents retain access to an appeals process to contest disciplinary actions[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an AAIF technical body developing vendor-neutral threat models, runtime boundary controls, privacy-preserving integration patterns, and cross-cutting architectural guidance for autonomous agent systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. The group collaborates across foundational initiatives, evaluating security and privacy implications in emerging protocol expansions such as Model Context Protocol (MCP) Interceptors and MCP Apps[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Operational Procedures
## Governance and Chartering
The working group's charter was submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) for formal approval[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. Although procedural voting thresholds encountered delays during initial TC balloting due to quorum timing and external infrastructure outages, the group resolved to proceed with charter deliverables based on unanimous informal support and the absence of substantive scope objections[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. All-hands meetings operate alongside asynchronous workstreams where individual deliverable leads manage drafting tasks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

## Cross-Working-Group Collaboration
The SP WG coordinates closely with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and sister working groups on shared terminology[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. Because multiple AAIF working groups chartered taxonomy work, the chairs designated taxonomy as the primary vehicle for cross-WG alignment, using the SP WG's preliminary terminology draft as the baseline contribution[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Lifecycle History
In April 2026, the working group initiated self-organizing deliverable workstreams, scheduled evaluations for MCP protocol hooks and browser UI integration boundaries, and adapted meeting schedules to accommodate global leadership, including the appointment of AAIF CTO Manik[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

proposed_concept.title: Identity & Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards, delegation models, and cross-organizational trust architectures for autonomous AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity & Trust Working Group (I&T) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with identifying, recommending, and promoting vendor-neutral, interoperable specifications and reference viewpoints for agent identity, provenance, authentication, delegation, and authorization [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]. Its core mission centers on enabling AI agents to establish verifiable provenance, represent organizational and human delegation chains, enforce short-lived fine-grained consent, and execute auditable actions across institutional boundaries [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

The group is led by Primary Contact Grant Miller [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c] and coordinates closely with horizontal efforts such as the [Security and Privacy Working Group](security-and-privacy.md) and [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](taxonomy-and-landscape.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Technical Focus Areas

The charter defines six explicit focus areas within the working group's remit [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]:

1. **Agent Identity, Authentication, and Provenance**: Frameworks establishing how an agent is uniquely identified, authenticates against remote endpoints, and conveys operational provenance, including host execution environments and producing software contexts.
2. **Delegation and Authority Chains**: Mechanisms documenting how an agent represents its mandate to act on behalf of a human principal, organizational unit, service account, or workflow process, including depth limits and authority attenuation.
3. **Authorization and Consent Models**: Short-lived, fine-grained access control formats, dynamic consent workflows, and governance constraints specifying duration and permissible tool invocations.
4. **Trust Evaluation and Cross-Organizational Trust**: Verifiable mechanisms for remote systems to evaluate, score, and authenticate foreign agents across administrative borders.
5. **Agent Discovery and Trust-Relevant Metadata**: Standards for advertising agent capabilities, directory listings, and operational metadata supporting [observability](observability-and-traceability.md) and verification.
6. **Enterprise and Consumer Contexts**: Evaluation of both high-assurance corporate compliance environments and decentralized consumer agent scenarios.

## Out of Scope Boundaries

To prevent mandate overlap across the foundation, the charter sets explicit operational limits [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]:
- **Standards Ratification**: The working group does not ratify formal standards on behalf of external Standards Development Organizations (SDOs), though it actively informs and contributes to external standards initiatives.
- **General Security Architecture**: Comprehensive runtime sandboxing, kernel hardening, and low-level agent execution defenses are deferred to the [Security and Privacy Working Group](security-and-privacy.md).
- **Normative AI Ethics**: Formulating overarching ethical principles or global regulatory policy positions is deferred to the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md).
- **Infrastructure Operations**: The group does not build or host production commercial identity registries or identity provider certification programs as primary deliverables.

# Lifecycle History

The Identity & Trust Working Group was chartered under the AAIF governance process to provide vendor-neutral architectural consensus for agent attestation, delegation, and trust verification across heterogeneous platforms [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

proposed_concept.description: Operational guidelines governing working group proposal intake, membership tier eligibility restrictions, and Technical Committee review schedules.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Working Group Submission Guidelines define the formal intake protocol, prerequisite credentials, and administrative evaluation stages for proposing new technical working groups to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c]. All working group charters must be proposed via the foundation's standardized GitHub issue template repository, where submissions undergo initial triage before entering formal review [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

# Architecture / Specification

## Submitter Eligibility and Intake Requirements

Proposals require direct sponsorship from verified Foundation participants [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c]:
- **Organizational Affiliation**: The primary submitter must be an active representative of an AAIF Member Organization [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
- **Membership Tier Verification**: Submissions require explicit declaration of whether the sponsoring organization holds Platinum or Gold AAIF membership status [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
- **Intake Assignment**: Incoming proposal issues are labeled with `New` and routed directly to designated foundation administrators for initial validation [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

## Form Structure and Supporting Documentation

The proposal template mandates comprehensive documentation across charter scope, resources, and prior art [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c]:
- **Prior Art Analysis**: Submitters must document existing initiatives, competing approaches, and prior art related to the proposed focus area (`existing_work`) [^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-2].
- **Supporting Materials**: Collateral such as whitepapers, draft specifications, or organizational commitments must be supplied under dedicated attachments (`supporting_documents`) [^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-2].

## Review Schedule and Moratorium Constraints

While the Technical Committee actively accepts new working group proposal submissions, formal committee evaluations and charter review cycles are scheduled to begin on June 1, 2026 [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure and review gates governing project proposal intake, technical evaluation, and admission across AAIF lifecycle stages.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Project Proposal Process specifies the operational intake sequence, assessment criteria, and committee approval stages required for open-source tools, specifications, and libraries seeking hosting under the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]. Administered by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the process governs project admission into the [Project Lifecycle Policy](project-lifecycle-policy.md) across Sandbox, Growth, and Impact tiers [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

# Architecture / Specification

## Proposal Intake Workflow

Project intake proceeds through standardized issue templates requiring technical scope definitions, maintainer rosters, and intellectual property compliance declarations [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

To eliminate artificial barriers for early-stage and Sandbox candidates, submission requirements strictly conform to the governing [Project Lifecycle Policy](project-lifecycle-policy.md) [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]:
- **Mandatory Disclosures**: Essential architectural overviews, licensing conformance (OSI-approved), source code repositories, and initial contributor rosters are mandatory.
- **Optional Disclosures**: A published forward-looking roadmap and an OpenSSF Best Practices badge are formally classified as optional intake items rather than required blockers [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]. Projects without established security badges or finalized public roadmaps may submit for initial admission without administrative rejection [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

## Governance Progression

Following intake validation, proposals enter public review where working groups and Technical Committee members evaluate technical alignment, vendor neutrality, and architectural cohesion within the broader agentic software ecosystem [^evt-project-proposals-pr-23].

proposed_concept.title: Observability & Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group serving as a vendor-neutral coordination forum aligning agent observability standards, cross-framework trace formats, and execution telemetry.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by convening practitioners, vendors, and standards organizations to build a shared understanding of agent observability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]. Approved on May 13, 2026, and led by Chair Pavan Sudheendra, the group serves explicitly as a coordination forum rather than an isolated standards body, aligning adjacent initiatives and upstreaming specifications whenever possible [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# Scope and Mandate

The working group addresses fragmentation across agent observability tooling and resolves the architectural gap between single LLM call tracing and multi-turn, multi-agent session understanding [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

### Guiding Principles
- **Coordinate first, specify only when necessary**: Prioritize upstream contributions to existing bodies (such as OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context) before proposing new specifications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Interoperability over innovation**: Compose with existing telemetry standards to avert proprietary lock-in [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Observable by default**: Advocate for built-in, out-of-the-box telemetry across agent execution runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Practical adoption**: Favor implementable conventions over theoretical designs, maintaining vendor and framework neutrality [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# Deliverables and Workstreams

- **Founding Focus Area**: Developing the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) to define standard causal schemas across multi-turn tool invocations and cross-agent exchanges [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Protocol Boundary Observability**: Investigating telemetry propagation across agent runtimes, tool boundaries, and model gateways [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# Governance

The working group operates under AAIF community governance modeled on Linux Foundation guidelines [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]. Working group decisions follow consensus-driven processes, escalating unresolvable disputes to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

proposed_concept.title: Security & Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, architectural patterns, control boundaries, and cross-working group security review processes for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security & Privacy Working Group (SPAA) establishes security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]. Approved on May 13, 2026, and chaired by Alex Frazer alongside Co-Chair Junjie Bu, the group provides foundational threat models, design patterns, and containment controls for autonomous agent interactions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].

# Scope and Mandate

### In Scope
- **Threat Modeling and Attack Analysis**: Identifying threat vectors such as prompt injection, confused deputy behavior, unauthorized cross-system tool invocation, and persistent agent memory corruption [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- **Security Architecture & Design Patterns**: Standardizing technical countermeasures, containment boundaries, and runtime control mechanisms like interceptor hooks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **Agent Control and Containment**: Establishing least-privilege baselines and isolation constraints for autonomous agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- **Data Protection and Privacy**: Mitigating unauthorized data extraction and leakage during cross-service agent workflows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- **Cross-WG Collaboration**: Serving as an intersecting review body supporting all AAIF technical groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

### Out of Scope
- Ethics, bias, and subjective value judgments, which are deferred to governance workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- Legal and prescriptive regulatory interpretations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- Product certification and compliance audit regimes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

# Deliverables and Workstreams

- **[Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md)**: Comparative framework evaluating existing security standards against unique agentic failure modes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **[Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)**: Lightweight review criteria assessing peer working group specifications [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **Security & Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Technical repository detailing implementation mechanics such as hooks, guardrails, and sandboxing [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **[Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)**: High-level guidance detailing operational posture and controls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **Taxonomy Integration**: Foundational security vocabulary originated in the group has been transferred to the cross-foundation initiative led by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

# Governance

The working group conducts bi-weekly plenary meetings and coordinates dedicated workstream sub-groups asynchronously [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]. Leadership terms run for 12 months with a maximum of two consecutive terms [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Ecosystem Architecture Map is an interactive, CNCF Landscape 2-based market map that catalogs open-source agent runtimes, interoperability protocols, security guardrails, observability platforms, commerce rails, and regulatory frameworks across the agentic AI landscape.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007] Maintained in coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the map organizes community and member projects into structured tiers to assist adopters in navigating the emerging agent technology stack.

# Architecture / Specification

## Visual and Project Tier Configuration
The landscape is configured through `settings.yml` using the CNCF Landscape 2 specification.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007] Items are organized into a card-based grid layout displaying project logos and descriptions. Projects and ecosystem contributions are classified into distinct tiers:
- **Graduated**: Mature, production-hardened foundational projects.
- **Incubating**: Actively developed technologies meeting defined governance and adoption criteria.
- **Member**: Technologies maintained by AAIF member organizations.
- **External**: Relevant third-party open-source runtimes, libraries, and specifications across the broader ecosystem.

## Continuous Integration and Validation
Changes to landscape metadata (`landscape.yml`) and configuration (`settings.yml`) are enforced through automated GitHub Actions workflows:
- **Schema Validation**: Automated CI runs invoke `cncf/landscape2-validate-action@v2` across pull requests and merge groups to verify data integrity and syntax against Landscape 2 schemas.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340]
- **Interactive Previews**: The `preview.yml` workflow triggers on pull requests targeting `main` that modify landscape definitions, settings, or hosted logos.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00] It automatically comments on the pull request with a dynamic preview URL on `https://aaif.landscape2.io` configured with runtime overlays pointing to the author's fork branch.

# References
- [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)

[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]: AAIF Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream, `landscape/settings.yml`.
[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00]: AAIF Landscape Repository, `.github/workflows/preview.yml`.
[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340]: AAIF Landscape Repository, `.github/workflows/validate.yml`.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive ecosystem market map and catalog generated using CNCF Landscape2 that tracks open-source and commercial technologies across the agentic AI stack [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14]. Maintained by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the landscape organizes foundation frameworks, execution harnesses, protocol bridges, evaluation harnesses, and security layers.

# Architecture / Specification
The catalog configuration decouples member organizations and open-source projects into distinct groups while highlighting AAIF member-backed initiatives [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14]. Key architectural components include:
- **Project Watchlist**: Curates leading open-source agentic AI repositories and software projects tracked by the ecosystem [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].
- **Decoupled Grouping**: Structures members and open technical projects under separate categorical hierarchies to prevent organizational conflation [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].
- **Telemetry Synchronization**: Integrates metrics and momentum data with the [LFX Insights Agentic AI Momentum Dashboard](https://insights.linuxfoundation.org/report/agentic-ai-momentum) [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

# Lifecycle History
In PR#14, the repository added the agentic AI project watchlist section, introduced explicit group-level decoupling between member organizations and projects, and integrated tracking telemetry aligned with LFX Insights [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Idea Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Operational guidelines governing working group proposal intake, membership tier eligibility restrictions, scope requirements, and evaluation workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Idea Submission Guidelines define the formal intake criteria, eligibility requirements, and structural template for proposing new technical working groups within the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. Submissions are evaluated by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) to ensure alignment with foundational priorities and prevent duplicative efforts across working groups [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

# Architecture / Specification
Working group proposals must adhere to strict membership and documentation criteria prior to review:
- **Eligibility**: Submissions are strictly restricted to Foundation Member organizations in good standing across any membership level; submissions from non-member entities are not reviewed [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
- **Submitter Metadata**: Submitter's full name, organizational affiliation, role, contact email, availability, and organization membership tier [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
- **Identity and Problem Statement**: Clear working group name, one-sentence plain-language summary, specific challenge or gap addressed, relevance to agentic AI, and strategic alignment with AAIF priorities [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
- **Scope and Deliverables**: Targeted outputs including technical reports, whitepapers, specifications, standards, datasets, benchmarks, or policy recommendations [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
- **Timeline and Structure**: Proposed meeting cadence, duration, and operational roadmap, typically framed around a 12–24 month charter lifecycle [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].
- **Stakeholder Alignment**: Required cross-disciplinary expertise, confirmed participating organizations, impact metrics, urgency, and resource considerations [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

# Lifecycle History
The submission guidelines were ratified in March 2026 as the standard operational intake mechanism for prospective working groups [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. Subsequent maintenance corrected external reference links resolving to the primary [Foundation portal](https://www.aaif.io) [^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-4].

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy defining project proposal requirements, lifecycle stage criteria across Growth, Impact, and Emeritus, and annual review procedures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Lifecycle Policy governs how open technical projects formally enter the Agentic AI Foundation and advance through defined developmental stages [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. Administered by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the policy establishes standardized intake criteria, stage progression gates, and annual reviews to align hosted projects with foundation governance and community resources [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

# Architecture / Specification
Technical projects participate at levels suited to their operational maturity and community footprint [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]:

## Project Proposal Requirements
Candidate projects must submit a formal pull request to the project-proposals repository detailing [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]:
- Name, description, mission alignment, and relationship to existing AAIF projects.
- Example use cases, evidence of production adoption, and identified [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) sponsor.
- OSI-approved permissive license and public repository location.
- Automated validation, public release mechanics, issue tracking, and external dependency licensing.
- Leadership governance structure, core maintainer roster, and official communication channels.
- Infrastructure requests and existing financial sponsorship.

## Lifecycle Stages
- **Growth Stage**: Maturing projects establishing multi-organizational governance, repeatable release mechanisms, and active ecosystem integration [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- **Impact Stage**: Production-grade reference technologies demonstrating widespread industry adoption, sustained contributor diversity, and mission-critical deployment [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- **Emeritus Stage**: Retired projects that are no longer actively maintained but preserved for historical reference and artifact continuity [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171] [^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

## Annual Review Process
All hosted projects undergo an annual audit evaluating governance health, license compliance, release cadence, and progression or reclassification across stages [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

# Lifecycle History
The Project Lifecycle Policy took effect on March 18, 2026, defining standardized criteria for proposal intake, stage expectations, and annual reviews [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. Typographical corrections to the Emeritus Stage criteria and proposal issue templates were merged in PR#30 [^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol gap analyses, and interoperability guidance across the agentic commerce lifecycle.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group (AC WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body that catalogs, aligns, and harmonizes open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows executed by AI agents on behalf of users, businesses, and software systems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. Co-chaired by Ilya Grigorik and Rahul Bansal, the group serves as a protocol-neutral forum providing interoperability guidance across discovery, cart composition, checkout handoff, payment orchestration, and post-purchase lifecycles without authoring competing proprietary or foundational commerce protocols[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

The working group interfaces directly with sibling foundation groups, including [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) for agent authority scoping and consent conveyance, as well as [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical scope strictly around interfaces, signals, and interoperability patterns between agentic systems and commerce stacks, intentionally leaving the operational internals of payment networks, fraud engines, and identity providers to domain owners[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

### In-Scope Domain Areas
- **Discovery & Negotiation**: Standardizing agent–merchant interfaces for product offers, dynamic availability, transaction terms, and fulfillment options[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Cart & Checkout**: Cart assembly, schema validation, and handoff protocols between agent execution runtimes and merchant checkout endpoints (such as [agentic checkout](../taxonomy/agentic-checkout.md))[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Identity & Delegated Authority**: Buyer identity verification, agent delegation boundaries, and consent signals in alignment with [agent-in-the-loop transaction](../taxonomy/agent-in-the-loop-transaction.md) and [agent-initiated transaction](../taxonomy/agent-initiated-transaction.md) flows[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Agentic Payments**: Standard interfaces connecting agents, client wallets, and payment rails (cards, real-time banking rails, and on-chain networks), covering payment intent, authorization, and settlement signals while excluding operational mechanics of specific rails (related to [delegated payment](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md))[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Fraud Signaling**: Exchange of risk-posture signals and context markers among agents, merchants, and external verification platforms[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Human-in-the-Loop & Autonomy Boundaries**: Formalizing confirmation triggers, policy escalations, and autonomy levels across commercial actions[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Post-Purchase Interfaces**: Claim reporting, dispute initiation, order status conveyance, and chargeback signals[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

### Explicit Out-of-Scope Boundaries
The AC WG explicitly excludes the following from its remit[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]:
- Operational internals and processing mechanics of payment rails, fraud detection/mitigation systems, or identity providers.
- Foundation-wide responsible AI policy and macro-societal governance.
- End-user consumer UI design, merchant marketplace product UX, and point-of-sale (PoS) terminal hardware.
- Non-agentic legacy commerce systems.
- Authoring net-new competing commerce protocol standards.

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05-15**: Working Group charter formally ratified and approved under leadership of Ilya Grigorik and Rahul Bansal[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure, status label taxonomy, and review gates governing project proposal intake, technical evaluation, and admission.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Proposal Process governs the formal intake, technical evaluation, and admission of open-source software projects seeking foundation-hosted status within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. Administered through the `aaif/project-proposals` repository, the process establishes a public path for prospective projects to seek classification as either Growth or Impact projects in accordance with the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md)[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

Submissions are evaluated by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), which conducts structured technical reviews and votes on admission before submitting recommendations to the Governing Board[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

# Architecture / Specification
The intake and review pipeline operates across sequential stages documented in the repository submission guide[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6][^evt-project-proposals-pr-35].

### Application Workflow
1. **Application Submission**: Prospective maintainers complete a project proposal application via the GitHub issue form template in `aaif/project-proposals`[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
2. **Backlog & Triage**: Submitted issues automatically populate the public Project Proposals Board under the `New` state[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
3. **Review Presentation**: Project maintainers prepare a formal review presentation supported by AAIF staff[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
4. **Technical Committee Meeting**: The project is scheduled for presentation and examination during a regular Technical Committee meeting[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

### Evaluation Status Taxonomy
The evaluation board categorizes applications across five explicit lifecycle labels[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]:
- `New`: The application has been received and placed in the review backlog.
- `Approved`: The application has satisfied technical criteria and been accepted into foundation hosting.
- `Declined`: The application has been rejected, with rationale documented in issue comments.
- `Waiting on Comment`: Additional technical clarification or operational detail has been requested from maintainers.
- `Too Early`: The project lacks maturity or required prerequisites; guidance for reapplication is provided.

### Voting Thresholds & Governance Rules
- **Voting Margin**: Admission requires an absolute majority vote (>50%) of all members of the Technical Committee[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Governing Board Ratification**: Positive TC recommendations are referred to the AAIF Governing Board for final sign-off[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Reapplication Window**: Projects not accepted may reapply as soon as three months following a declined vote, provided tangible technical progress is demonstrated[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].
- **Membership Decoupling**: Project hosting does not require maintainers or sponsoring entities to be AAIF corporate members, nor does project acceptance confer commercial membership status or Governing Board seats[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, architectural patterns, control boundaries, and security best practices for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an AAIF technical body focused on defining verifiable threat models, architectural security patterns, boundary controls, and implementation guidelines for autonomous agent runtimes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. Led by Alex Frazer, the working group conducts cross-cutting security reviews, authors hardened design catalogs, and evaluates runtime isolation primitives across the agent ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

The working group coordinates with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to apply security classifications to ecosystem tooling and collaborates with sibling working groups on governance and attestation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group executes its mission through self-selected contributor workstreams coordinated via weekly and bi-weekly synchronization meetings[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

### Active Workstreams and Deliverables
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Comprehensive implementation guide covering threat boundaries, container and kernel sandboxing, and in-hook policy controls ([guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Analytical evaluation comparing existing frameworks (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF) across agentic failure modes ([resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Formal pattern collection documenting isolation boundaries, kill switches, and hardware-bound authorizations (such as [patterns/attested-isolated-runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) and [patterns/kill-switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Standardized assessment checklist applied to evaluate sibling working group specifications and architectures ([guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

### Operational Model
- **Workstream Leadership**: Contributors self-select leads and co-leads within dedicated workstream channels rather than receiving top-down committee appointments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].
- **Cross-WG Collaboration**: Working group members contribute security and privacy classifications directly into the landscape taxonomy curated under Junjie Bu's leadership[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05-26**: Working Group charter formally ratified and approved; deliverable milestone deadlines extended by approximately one month to accommodate approval sequencing[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive ecosystem catalog and market map tracking open-source and commercial technologies across agent runtimes, orchestration, and guardrails.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an open-source ecosystem catalog and market map managed by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) that surveys software frameworks, orchestration engines, registries, guardrails, and telemetry platforms across the agentic artificial intelligence ecosystem[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. Chaired by Junjie Bu, the landscape maintains structured YAML definitions categorizing foundation-hosted member projects alongside external community technologies[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

The landscape directly aligns each major architectural category with corresponding AAIF technical working groups to foster consistent cross-group terminology and interoperability models[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape structure is codified in `landscape/landscape.yml` and organized into seven principal architectural divisions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]:

### 1. Agent Runtimes, Frameworks & Workflow Orchestration
Aligned with the [Workflows and Process Integration WG](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) and [Accuracy and Reliability WG](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]:
- **Autonomous Agent Frameworks**: Conversational and autonomous programming runtimes including Microsoft AutoGen, CrewAI, OpenHands, and Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].
- **Orchestration Runtimes**: Cyclical graph and stateful distributed coordination engines, including LangChain, LlamaIndex, Diagrid Dapr Runtimes, and LangGraph[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

### 2. Protocols & Discovery Registries
Aligned with the [Identity and Trust WG](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and trust anchor initiatives: catalogs transport protocols, dynamic capability resolution directories, and agent identity anchors[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

### 3. Security Guardrails & Firewalls
Aligned with the [Security and Privacy WG](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md): tracks runtime defense proxies, kernel sandboxing primitives, and policy validation enforcement engines[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

### 4. Observability & Tracing Telemetry
Aligned with the [Observability and Traceability WG](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md): indexes distributed tracing frameworks, token usage analyzers, and execution causal graph profilers[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

### 5. Agentic Commerce & Wallets
Aligned with the [Agentic Commerce WG](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md): maps autonomous checkout handoffs, intent authorization, and wallet interfaces[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

### 6. Global Governance & Regulatory Regimes
Aligned with the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory WG](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md): categorizes regulatory compliance monitoring frameworks and global risk standards[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

### 7. Agent Evaluation & Benchmarking Harnesses
Aligned with the [Accuracy and Reliability WG](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md): tracks repeatable scoring environments, safety harnesses, and failure recovery benchmarks[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05-26**: Junjie Bu confirmed as chair of the Landscape workstream and co-chair of the Taxonomy workstream, instituting weekly synchronization reviews and open contribution processes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Submission Guidelines establish the formal intake process, evaluation pipeline, and approval requirements for community members and member organizations seeking to form a new technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]. Proposals are submitted through standardized issue templates and progress through public triage and review by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

# Architecture / Specification
## Application and Intake Workflow
Proponents initiate the formation process by opening a Working Group Proposal Application issue in the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]. Submitted proposals are automatically registered on the public Working Group Proposals project board and placed in the triage backlog for scheduling on a forthcoming Technical Committee (TC) meeting agenda[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

## Evaluation and Voting Gates
Working group proposals are reviewed during scheduled TC meetings. Formal acceptance requires:
- An affirmative vote by a simple majority of all members of the Technical Committee[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
- Final ratification by the AAIF Governing Board[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

## Proposal Status Taxonomy
Proposals are tracked using a discrete lifecycle label scheme on GitHub[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]:
- `New`: Newly submitted proposal awaiting initial triage in the backlog.
- `Waiting on Comment`: Reviewers have requested clarifying details or revisions via issue comments.
- `Approved`: The proposal has met voting requirements and been formally accepted.
- `Declined`: The proposal has been rejected by the TC with explicit rationale recorded in the issue comments.
- `Too Early`: The proposal is not yet ready for formation; guidance for future resubmission is provided.

# Lifecycle History
The proposal intake process and status taxonomy were formalized in the `aaif/working-group-proposals` intake repository to provide an open, transparent pipeline for working group formation under TC governance[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

# References
- [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)
- [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an AAIF technical body tasked with establishing vendor-neutral threat models, defensive architectural patterns, security verification checklists, and implementation baselines across agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. The working group executes through specialized workstreams that coordinate with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and delegate representatives to cross-cutting foundation initiatives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

# Architecture / Specification
## Workstream Structure and Leadership
The working group divides operational deliverables across designated workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]:
- **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy; produces review checklists for assessing security across other working group specifications[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Matthew Khouzam and Fernando Lucktemberg; develops actionable guidance covering runtime containment, sandboxing, and credential controls[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg; assesses comparative coverage across external frameworks (e.g., OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, NIST) and defines agent-specific threat models[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Sagar Dashora and Dan Kommatas; catalogues reusable architectural patterns including runtime gates and credential boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

## Cross-Foundation Coordination
The working group delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman to serve as official representatives to the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), ensuring security and privacy definitions are harmonized across the foundation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. Technical Committee reporting follows an asynchronous monthly GitHub review workflow to ensure visibility without creating bureaucratic approval bottlenecks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

# Lifecycle History
In June 2026, the working group ratified its core workstream leadership slate, appointed official liaisons to the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream, and transitioned meeting and agenda administration into self-service LFX tooling[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

# References
- [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)
- [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)
- [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)
- [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)
