proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF body responsible for standardizing terminology, harmonizing conflicting definitions, and curating an authoritative market map and technological landscape across the agentic AI domain[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. Led by Junjie Bu, the workstream operates open collaboration models where all AAIF working groups contribute appointed delegates to maintain decoupled, version-controlled terminology data through GitHub pull requests[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

# Architecture / Specification
## Cross-Group Liaison Model
To prevent semantic divergence between vertical domains, every active AAIF working group is required to designate liaison delegates to the Taxonomy and Landscape effort[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]. Delegates actively review proposed concepts, surface domain-specific edge cases, and negotiate authoritative reconciliations[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. Confirmed group delegates include:
- [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md): Jay White and Katherine Druckman[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

## Asynchronous Contribution Workflow
The workstream mandates that all terminology definitions and landscape categorizations be stored as decoupled, machine-readable datasets managed directly in GitHub repositories[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. Technical debates, review commentary, and semantic resolutions are executed asynchronously via pull requests and issue threads rather than synchronous committees[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

# Lifecycle History
In June 2026, the cross-working group initiative was formally launched with a mandate for inter-group delegate participation and an asynchronous pull request workflow to decouple data maintenance from synchronous meeting schedules[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an AAIF technical body establishing vendor-neutral standards, open telemetry schemas, distributed execution tracing specifications, and runtime monitoring boundaries for agentic systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]. It coordinates cross-boundary observability frameworks covering LLM reasoning primitives, Model Context Protocol (MCP) server interactions, tool execution traces, and multi-agent coordination[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

# Architecture / Specification
## Focus Group Structure
The working group organizes technical deliverables into specialized focus groups[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]:
- **Observability and Multi-Agentic Systems**: Led by Ty; focuses on distributed tracing, agent-to-agent interactions, and swarm execution context propagation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].
- **Observability and Protocols**: Led by Matthew; defines telemetry data structures, protocol boundary mediation, and integration across standard interfaces such as OpenTelemetry and MCP[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Facilitated by Pavan with coordination from Richard and Kevin; explores telemetry instrumentation for agent reasoning loops, planning phases, and state reflection[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

## Asynchronous Collaboration and Onboarding
The working group conducts its core specification drafting and review processes asynchronously via GitHub pull requests and issues, transitioning away from synchronous meeting dependence and Google Docs[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]. Workstream leads curate concrete charter-aligned issues and onboarding checklists to facilitate new contributor entry, while participating in the cross-working group [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) effort[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

# Lifecycle History
In June 2026, the working group initiated operational focus group tracks for multi-agent observability, protocol boundaries, and agentic reasoning, while executing a migration of draft specifications to GitHub pull requests and integrating with the foundation-wide taxonomy workstream[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group bridging global AI policy developments and technical agentic systems, tracking compliance baselines, and establishing risk controls.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group (WG Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment) bridges emerging artificial intelligence regulatory requirements, compliance mandates, and operational safety guardrails with concrete agentic software architectures [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]. It identifies gaps between theoretical policy frameworks and runtime agent execution, providing technical guidance to align agent implementations with global compliance baselines.

# Leadership and Governance
The working group is co-chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]. Technical proposals and deliverables undergo oversight and alignment via the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).

# Reporting Cadence
The working group submits standardized monthly status reports to the Technical Committee using an established pull request review cycle [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-pr-4]:
- Reports are authored in `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` following the [working group reporting template](../guidelines/working-group-reporting-template.md).

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Reporting Template
proposed_concept.description: Standardized cadence, structure, review timeline, and pull request workflow for AAIF working groups reporting monthly progress to the Technical Committee.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Reporting Template standardizes how Agentic AI Foundation working groups communicate operational progress, blockers, priorities, and formal decision requests to the Technical Committee on a monthly cadence.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-9677055e316b-188b9d10][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f] It provides an asynchronous, structured reporting mechanism designed to keep Foundation governance informed without imposing heavy administrative overhead on technical workstreams.

Reports are published directly to working group repositories and reviewed by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) via GitHub pull requests.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-9677055e316b-188b9d10]

# Architecture / Specification

## Filing Workflow and Deadlines
Working group chairs execute the following process each reporting period:[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-9677055e316b-188b9d10][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f]
1. Copy the canonical template to `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` (for example, `reporting/2026-06-report.md`).
2. Open a pull request against the working group repository titled `[Report] <WG name> – <Month YYYY>`.
3. Assign the Technical Committee or its designated GitHub team as reviewers.
4. Submission deadline: Reports must be submitted by the last business day of the reporting month.
5. Review window: The review window closes seven calendar days after submission.
6. Merge criteria: The pull request is merged once the Technical Committee signs off or when the seven-day review window closes, whichever occurs sooner.

## Required Report Sections
The template mandates seven core sections:[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-9677055e316b-188b9d10][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f]
- **Header Metadata**: Working Group name, reporting period, chairs with organizational affiliations, and date submitted.
- **Summary**: A concise narrative of two to three sentences capturing the monthly status at a glance.
- **Progress Against Objectives**: Concrete deliverables and milestones shipped or advanced during the period, explicitly tied back to chartered objectives.
- **Blockers and Risks**: Issues requiring Technical Committee awareness; recorded as "None this month" if empty.
- **Decisions Needed from the TC**: Explicit, actionable requests requiring formal determination; recorded as "None" if empty.
- **Next Month's Focus**: Top two or three actionable priorities targeted for the subsequent period.
- **Metrics / Links**: Relevant pull requests, repository issues, release tags, meeting notes, and dashboards.

# References
- [Accuracy and Reliability Reporting Template](https://github.com/aaif/wg-accuracy-and-reliability/blob/10bc173f00e45d93a8f7038cb0c36a89e3219565/reporting/TEMPLATE.md)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-9677055e316b-188b9d10]
- [Workflows and Process Integration Reporting Template](https://github.com/aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration/blob/3b4d645499620b10b313297e7f365148fa6d0ee1/reporting/TEMPLATE.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9677055e316b-9220099f]

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to analyzing vulnerabilities, threat landscapes, and defense architectures across autonomous agent deployments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423] The group publishes threat taxonomies, reference security patterns, sandboxing specifications, and assessment checklists to secure agent communications and execution environments.

Repository operations and documentation practices are strictly governed through repository-level and directory-level agent instructions ensuring consistency and auditability.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]

# Architecture / Specification

## Repository Structure and Operations
The working group repository organizes artifacts into three principal functional directories:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423]
- `charter/`: Contains working group charter and formal governance documents; drafts remain prefixed with `DRAFT` until formally approved by recorded working group vote.
- `deliverables/`: Contains published deliverables, architectural frameworks, threat taxonomies, and technical checklists.
- `meeting-notes/`: Contains chronological meeting agendas, AI summaries, recording transcripts, recorded decisions, and action item trackers.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-eb9c68e792e7-3538ca31]

## Deliverable Lifecycle
Deliverables adhere to a three-stage lifecycle governed by explicit working group consensus:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]
- **Draft (`DRAFT-`)**: Every newly authored deliverable begins in draft status, designated by a `DRAFT-` file prefix and tracked in the directory index table.
- **Final**: A deliverable may only advance to Final status if a recorded meeting note under `meeting-notes/` contains an explicit approval decision from the working group. Upon approval, the `DRAFT-` prefix is stripped, and the document header references the approving meeting date and notes.
- **Moved**: When a deliverable transitions to a cross-working-group workstream or external repository, the existing file path is retained as a redirect notice to preserve external hyperlink integrity.

## Review and Assessment Integration
The Security and Privacy Working Group provides cross-workstream oversight through the [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md) and maintains implementation standards including [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) establishes open security standards, threat models, reusable design patterns, and baseline operational guidelines across the Agentic AI Foundation. Operating as an intersecting review and guidance layer across all AAIF working groups, the group assesses foundational security controls, privacy-preserving techniques, delegated authority limits, and supply-chain integrity for autonomous systems.

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical program into four core workstreams alongside cross-working-group delegations:

1. **Threat Modeling and Gap Analysis**: Led by Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) and Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP), this workstream evaluates foundational frameworks (CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, NIST AI RMF) against agentic risks such as tool invocation, multi-agent persuasion, and delegated authorization boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]. See [../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md).
2. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Led by Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase), this workstream curates reusable architectural patterns and anti-patterns addressing hooks and checkpointing, human-in-the-loop gates, confidential runtime isolation (TEE, ZK proofs), blast-radius containment, memory lifecycles, and intervention kill switches [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4].
3. **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson), this workstream authors practical builder guidance covering secrets handling, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation benchmarks, and forensic analysis [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]. See [../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).
4. **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy (Global Payments), this workstream operationalizes review gates for deliverables produced by peer working groups, including [identity-and-trust.md](identity-and-trust.md), [observability-and-traceability.md](observability-and-traceability.md), and [agentic-commerce.md](agentic-commerce.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]. See [../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md).

# Lifecycle History

On 2026-06-22, the working group's standalone Taxonomy of Terms and Definitions deliverable was officially merged into the foundation-wide cross-WG [taxonomy-and-landscape.md](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) effort chaired by Junjie Bu [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93]. The Security and Privacy WG designated Jay White (Microsoft) and Katherine Druckman (JetBrains) as its active review delegates within the centralized taxonomy effort [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

# References

- Threat Modeling Workstream: `workstreams/threat-modeling/README.md` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]
- Taxonomy Workstream: `workstreams/taxonomy/README.md` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7]
- Design Patterns Workstream: `workstreams/design-patterns/README.md` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]
- Review Checklist Workstream: `workstreams/review-checklist/README.md` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling: Gap Analysis and Framework Design
proposed_concept.description: Comparative gap analysis and framework design evaluating CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF against agentic-specific threats like tool invocation and delegated authorization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design deliverable evaluates existing AI security frameworks—including CSA MAESTRO, OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, and NIST AI RMF—to determine whether existing paradigms adequately address threats unique to autonomous and multi-agent systems. Produced within the [../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) working group, this analysis determines whether agentic risk gaps necessitate a bespoke threat modeling framework [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

# Architecture / Specification

The gap analysis assesses vulnerability and threat classes across four agentic operational domains [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]:

- **Multi-Agent Persuasion and Collusion**: Subagent deception, social engineering between distinct harnesses, and compromised peer coordination.
- **Tool Invocation Risks**: Dynamic function parameter injection, unsafe execution privileges, and tool-mediated prompt injection.
- **Delegated Authorization Boundaries**: Privilege escalation across agent execution chains and insufficient lease times on delegated bearer credentials.
- **Supply-Chain Integrity**: Tampering with system prompt definitions, unverified model provenance, and compromised tool manifest registries.

The findings feed directly into downstream foundation assets, specifically the Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog and the [../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

# Lifecycle History

The workstream is led by Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) and Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP), with contributors spanning Capsule, Twilio, Semiotic AI, IBM, Global Payments, Huawei, Ericsson, and TELUS [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide provides practical, actionable implementation guidance for developers and architects building agentic AI systems. Authored within the [../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) working group, it acts as a companion to the architectural Design Patterns Catalog by directing practitioners on recommended operational controls and curated external frameworks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55].

# Architecture / Specification

The guide focuses on core operational and runtime security disciplines [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]:

- **Secrets Management**: Ephemeral credential provisioning, scope limitation for agent bearer tokens, and out-of-band secret masking.
- **Secure Tool Invocation**: Enforcing input validation schemas, executing tools within sandbox boundaries, and mitigating tool poisoning attacks.
- **Runtime Guardrails**: Deterministic filters intercepting prompts, thoughts, and outputs to enforce behavioral boundaries.
- **Evaluation Frameworks**: Adversarial evaluation suites and red-teaming harnesses validating system resilience prior to production graduation.
- **Post-Incident Forensics**: Cryptographic trace logging, state snapshots, and audit trail reconstruction for non-deterministic agent executions.
- **External Framework Indexing**: Direct pointers to accepted external open-source tooling and standards rather than independent re-derivation.

# Lifecycle History

The guide workstream is led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson), supported by contributors across Keycard, Ocean Security, Capsule, Twilio, Circle, IBM, Global Payments, Huawei, Bluerock, Equinix, JPMorgan Chase, TELUS, and Lenovo [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative chaired by Junjie Bu that standardizes common terminology, harmonizes definitions across diverse agent architectures, and maintains machine-readable reference datasets for the foundation. Rather than managing fragmented vocabularies across individual working groups, all conceptual definitions are maintained centrally through open pull requests [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream operates via delegate representation from all active AAIF working groups. Each participating group designates delegates who participate in terminology reviews, provide domain-specific definitions, and reconcile conflicting semantic usages [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

Core responsibilities include:

- Harmonizing universal and domain-specific agentic AI terms.
- Managing decoupled taxonomy datasets updated through standardized pull request intake pipelines.
- Coordinating with active working groups to absorb historical or draft glossary assets into the universal vocabulary.

# Lifecycle History

On 2026-06-22, the [security-and-privacy.md](security-and-privacy.md) working group officially merged its standalone Taxonomy of Terms and Definitions workstream into this cross-WG initiative [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93]. The Security and Privacy WG appointed Jay White (Microsoft) and Katherine Druckman (JetBrains) as active voting delegates to represent security and privacy terminology within the consolidated taxonomy [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open threat models, security design patterns, cross-working-group review checklists, and best practice guidelines.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with developing vendor-neutral security patterns, threat modeling frameworks, privacy baselines, and cross-working-group review workflows across agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. The group serves as a core technical review authority for other AAIF deliverables while developing prescriptive builder guidance [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5].

# Architecture / Specification

## Workstream Organization

The working group organizes its technical production across five formal workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]:

- **Threat Modeling**: Conducts gap analyses of established AI security frameworks (including CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, and the NIST AI RMF) against agentic-specific threat surfaces such as memory poisoning, multi-agent persuasion, agent sabotage, excessive agency, and tool execution risks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Authors structured, reusable security and privacy patterns following a problem, context, solution, and trade-offs structure [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Best Practices Guide**: Develops higher-level defensive guidance and operational security baselines for practitioners and builders [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Operates an evaluation gate and structured checklist for assessing deliverables from other AAIF working groups through a dedicated security and privacy lens [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Taxonomy Integration**: Feeds security- and privacy-specific terms into the centralized cross-WG taxonomy effort [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

## Cross-Working Group and External Liaisons

The Security and Privacy WG originally initiated the foundation's general terminology catalog before elevating it on 2026-05-12 into the cross-WG Taxonomy and Landscape initiative led by Junjie Bu [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. The WG maintains continuous alignment through appointed delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. The working group also coordinates external collaboration with bodies including the OWASP Agentic Security Initiative (ASI), IETF, AARM, and MCP ACS [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-12**: Initial WG taxonomy draft elevated to an AAIF-wide initiative [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-05-26**: Junjie Bu appointed to lead the cross-WG Taxonomy and Landscape effort [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-09**: Jay White and Katherine Druckman designated as working group delegates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-22**: Terminology ownership formally migrated to the `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` repository [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-23**: Repositories made public; GitHub formally established as system of record for technical deliverables over external tools like Google Docs due to corporate access constraints [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]; workstream directory structure and leads formalized [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# References

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape workstream is an AAIF-wide coordination body chartered to harmonize terminology, reconcile overlapping domain concepts, and eliminate conflicting definitions across all foundational working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. It operates asynchronously through the centralized `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` repository and holds weekly coordination syncs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Intake Workflow

The taxonomy workstream aggregates 10–20 core foundational terms from each AAIF working group to assemble a canonical foundation-wide dictionary [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]:

- **Delegate Representation**: Participating working groups designate official delegates to represent their domain terminology and review unified entries (for example, Jay White and Katherine Druckman representing the Security and Privacy WG) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Structured JSON Ingestion**: Domain working groups structure intake and review through standardized schema slices aligned with central schemas (such as Accuracy and Reliability WG's section-and-priority sliced JSON indices) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-4].
- **Boundary Harmonization**: Reconciles conceptual planes across WG initiatives—such as distinguishing core OpenTelemetry alignment terms from AAIF-specific extensions in the Observability and Traceability WG [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10], or classifying emerging concepts like MCP real-time embedded deadlines between accuracy, reliability, and security [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-12**: Elevating the initial Security and Privacy WG draft into an AAIF-wide cross-working-group workstream agreed upon [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-05-26**: Junjie Bu appointed as workstream lead [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-09**: Initial formal WG delegate designations established [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-22**: Dedicated repository `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` designated as the single upstream system of record [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].
- **2026-06-23**: Intake expanded to encompass proposed agent archetypes mapped by tool use and network capability [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation framework capturing causal agent execution, tool invocations, approval checkpoints, and reasoning state.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a candidate standardization framework and behavioral data model developed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12]. It structures the causal and behavioral lifecycle of AI agents across three primary behavioral dimensions: execution structure, reasoning and planning, and outcomes and effects [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].

# Architecture / Specification

## Behavioral Planes and Crosswalk

The trace model maps observable agent operations across four architectural planes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]:

1. **Orchestration Plane**: High-level workflow state, subagent delegation, parent-child task lifecycles, and fan-out/join coordination.
2. **Execution Plane**: Concrete tool calls, subprocess commands, environment interactions, and hardware execution traces.
3. **Protocol Plane**: Inter-agent and client-to-agent communication framing, MCP exchanges, and distributed transport envelopes.
4. **Reasoning and Context Plane**: Model prompts, contextual window assembly, reasoning step chains, evaluations, and decision transitions.

## Standards Alignment and Evaluation Criteria

Rather than pre-committing to authoring a greenfield specification, the working group evaluates existing industry models across an explicit three-way decision path: adopt an existing standard, extend an existing effort, or author an independent specification only where verified functional gaps exist [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].

A primary guardrail for the trace model is strict alignment with OpenTelemetry standards, distinguishing standard OTel semantic conventions from AAIF-specific behavioral extension terms [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].

# Lifecycle History

- Tracked under WG 12-month charter objectives to deliver an objective evaluation report and recommendation across candidate trace formats [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].
- Architectural plane crosswalk and OTel alignment guardrails formulated under Issue #10 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].

# References

- Working group: [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- Core telemetry specification: [OpenTelemetry Reference Architecture](../resources/opentelemetry.md)
- Cross-boundary telemetry model: [Cross-Boundary Observability Model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an AAIF technical body established to align agent observability protocols, telemetry schemas, multi-agent trace correlation, and execution transparency frameworks across the agentic ecosystem[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical investigations into four primary focus groups[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]:
- **LLM Primitives**: Conducts landscape surveys and gap analyses covering fundamental model invocation observability and protocol boundary telemetry.
- **Agent State and Context**: Investigates persistent state tracking, memory frameworks, and context lifecycle telemetry.
- **Orchestration and Coordination**: Analyzes multi-agent workflows, inter-agent delegation protocols, and cross-boundary trace correlation.
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Evaluates internal reasoning step visibility, planning inspection, and white-box model execution traces.

Operational workflows utilize public GitHub issue trackers and Kanban project boards to track focus group deliverables, alongside biweekly working group meetings featuring community presentation slots[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

Cross-workstream alignment includes harmonizing core observability terminology with the `../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md` workstream and coordinating with emerging standards such as `../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md`[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]. Core working group deliverables under review include catalogs of prior work (`../resources/agent-observability-prior-work.md`) and agent observability use cases (`../resources/agent-observability-use-cases.md`)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-25**: Biweekly working group meeting confirmed transition of deliverable tracking to public GitHub issue boards, advanced the LLM Primitives landscape survey toward July completion, and initiated cross-workstream coordination on resource discovery[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

# Overview
Agentgateway is an open-source traffic mediation and policy enforcement proxy managing Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communications, cataloged as an AAIF member project[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-17].

# Architecture / Specification
Agentgateway mediates communication across heterogeneous agentic interfaces, providing:
- **Protocol Mediation**: Brokering interactions between client agent harnesses and MCP servers.
- **Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Routing**: Facilitating secure message passing and task delegation across independent agent runtimes.
- **Policy Enforcement**: Applying access controls, authentication checks, and traffic governance at the network and protocol boundary.

# Lifecycle History
- **2026**: Admitted as an AAIF member project and integrated into the `../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md` catalog[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-17].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining failure mode taxonomies, evaluation frameworks, reliable architecture patterns, and safe recovery specifications for autonomous agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical working group tasked with establishing standards, benchmarks, failure taxonomies, and engineering practices required for AI agents to operate accurately and reliably under real-world enterprise conditions [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. Formally approved on May 15, 2026, the group addresses visibility and evaluation gaps across non-deterministic agentic workloads by classifying failure modes, defining resilience mechanisms, and establishing clear triggers for human intervention [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

The working group is led by Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Boundaries
The working group's charter defines explicit technical boundaries [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:
- **In Scope:**
  - *Accuracy & Reliability Frameworks:* Establishing dimensions, evaluation metrics, failure modes, and quality thresholds for autonomous agents.
  - *Reliable Architecture Patterns:* Specifying proactive structural patterns, including verification loops and grounding against authoritative data sources.
  - *Recovery and Corrective Actions:* Standardizing safe-state restoration, rollback mechanisms, automated compensations, and human escalation triggers.
- **Out of Scope:**
  - Foundation model training, fine-tuning, and prompt engineering.
  - Trace and log emission standards, which are delegated to the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).
  - Production tooling, commercial guardrail platforms, and runtime hosting.
  - Domain-specific legal or regulatory compliance rules.
  - Production agent runtimes or orchestrators.

## Working Assumptions
The group's work proceeds under four architectural assumptions [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:
1. **Operational Predictability:** Agent frameworks will adopt standardized hooks for state recovery and trajectory management.
2. **Immutable Agent Identity:** System instances possess unique identifiers across versions and runtime environments for evaluation auditability.
3. **Versioning for Reproducibility:** Agent configurations, prompts, models, and tool definitions are frozen when evaluating accuracy and reliability.
4. **Availability of Trust Anchors:** Verifiable systems of record exist against which agent reasoning and outputs can be systematically verified.

## Deliverables and Workstreams
The ARWG work program is organized around canonical deliverables D1 through D6 and internal item I1 [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6]:
- **D1 (Accuracy and Reliability Taxonomy):** Architectural framing covering evaluation subjects, output quality, grounding, symptoms, root causes, and correction mechanisms, harmonized with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].
- **D2 (Applied Gap Analysis & Benchmark Survey):** Enterprise persona-driven field study documenting operational needs, benchmark coverage, and tooling gaps, led by Sanjeev Suresh [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].
- **D6 (Evaluation Protocol Scope):** Normative evaluation protocol specification built upon the gap synthesis of D2 [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

## Operating Cadence
The working group conducts biweekly plenary sessions alternating with dedicated deliverable working sessions rather than maintaining fragmented sub-groups [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Meeting Notes Guideline
proposed_concept.description: Standardized file-naming, structural requirements, table index maintenance, and editorial style rules for authoring Taxonomy and Landscape meeting notes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Meeting Notes Guideline specifies the repository structure, ingestion procedure, editorial style, and index management rules for documenting meetings within the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea]. It provides automated agents and human contributors with repeatable instructions for creating uniform records from call recordings, transcripts, and AI-generated summaries.

# Architecture / Specification

## File Naming and Location
Each meeting's notes must be authored in the `meeting-notes/` directory as `YYYY-MM-DD.md` using the exact date of the meeting (such as `2026-03-17.md`), initialized directly from `TEMPLATE.md` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].

## Ingestion and Assembly Workflow
Contributors and automated document generation agents must follow an eight-step procedure [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea]:
1. Copy `TEMPLATE.md` into the new `YYYY-MM-DD.md` file.
2. Replace the `YYYY-MM-DD` placeholder in the title with the actual meeting date.
3. Populate the **Resources** section with links to the recording, transcript, and AI summary.
4. Detail the discussion points under **Topics Discussed**, keeping each item to 1–2 concise sentences.
5. Document any formal agreements under **Decisions**; if none occurred, write "None."
6. Document expected outputs under **Deliverables**; if none occurred, write "None."
7. Fill in the **Action Items** table with owner name, task description, and due date.
8. Add a new row to the table in `README.md` directly below the table header to maintain descending chronological order. The row must contain the meeting date, a markdown link labeled "Full notes" referencing the file, and a 1–2 sentence summary of key topics.

## Section Handling Rules
Sections that have no recorded activity must never be omitted or deleted. The section heading must remain intact with the content set to "None." to guarantee structural consistency across all repository notes [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].

## Editorial and Communication Style
All documentation, commit messages, pull request descriptions, and agent responses across the repository must comply with specific stylistic requirements [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea]:
- Format entries as concise bullet points rather than narrative paragraphs.
- Attribute action items to named individuals whenever possible.
- Do not use contrastive language.
- Do not insert horizontal rules for line breaks.
- Avoid sycophancy or deferential filler.
- Be direct while avoiding incomplete clauses or fragmented sentence structures.
- Maintain a neutral, professional tone that remains approachable and playful.

proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing agentic terminology, resolving cross-group definition conflicts, and maintaining the foundation's ecosystem landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting technical body within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with standardizing terminology, eliminating siloed or duplicate vocabularies across working groups, and curating an authoritative ecosystem directory [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. Operating under a charter approved across AAIF working groups, the workstream establishes shared definitions and maintains the interactive landscape map in coordination with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream operates an asynchronous, pull-request-driven governance model supported by a core team of delegates and domain editors representing individual working groups, including [Accuracy and Reliability](accuracy-and-reliability.md), [Security and Privacy](security-and-privacy.md), and [Workflows and Process Integration](workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

### Core Responsibilities
- **Terminology Harmonization**: Intake, deduplication, and cross-workgroup reconciliation of universal and domain-specific terms using SKOS Lite metadata schemas [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].
- **Ecosystem Landscape Directory**: Structuring open-source projects, member initiatives, and commercial technologies using standard Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) landscape tool schemas deployed to `landscape.aif.io` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].
- **Standards Alignment**: Actively cross-referencing agent definitions with international baseline standards, such as ISO and NIST specifications, and documenting rationale for any intentional deviations [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].
- **Boundary Delimitation**: Treating high-level conceptual boundaries, such as the operational definition of autonomous agents, as continuous deliverables developed iteratively across working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

### Reporting and Quality Assurance
- **Technical Committee Reporting**: Monthly progress reports formatted per `YYYY-MM-report.md` are submitted by the final business day of each month, initiating a 7-calendar-day review window prior to merging [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b].
- **Human Curation Policy**: An editorial style guide and AI usage policy mandate human judgment and domain editor sign-off for all proposed terms [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

# Lifecycle History

The workstream was initiated in May 2026 to resolve fragmented vocabulary across foundation groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. In June 2026, the workstream finalized its charter with sign-offs across six working groups, adopted CNCF landscape tooling, established delegate representation, and reset repository terms into formal pull requests to enforce editorial review gates [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

# References

- [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md)
- [Taxonomy Contributions Skill](../skills/taxonomy-contributions.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive ecosystem catalog and market map tracking open-source and commercial technologies across the agentic computing landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Landscape is an open ecosystem catalog, directory, and interactive radar maintained by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to categorize tools, platforms, protocols, and runtimes across the agentic technology stack [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. Built on industry-standard CNCF landscape tool formatting, the directory prevents redundant market research and offers a unified map of member-driven and external industry components [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].

# Architecture / Specification

The landscape architecture decouples static metadata definitions from the rendering web application, enabling an asynchronous, pull-request-driven curation model [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0].

### Formatting and Directory Model
- **CNCF Schema Compliance**: Adopts the standard CNCF landscape tool data structure for defining categories, subcategories, project maturity tiers, and repository metadata [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].
- **Entity Scoping**: Distinguishes AAIF member-driven projects and hosted assets from external open-source and commercial solutions within the catalog taxonomy [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].
- **Domain Integration**: Centralizes visualization and explorer tooling on `landscape.aif.io`, with decoupled data stores supporting future dedicated vocabulary endpoints [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].
- **Intake and Review**: Updates are submitted via Git pull requests, requiring review by designated domain editors to verify categorization and attribution accuracy [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].

# Lifecycle History

Initial landscape design and portal decoupling were established in May 2026 under the Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. In June 2026, the workstream formally standardized on the CNCF landscape tooling specification and integrated directory outputs with `landscape.aif.io` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].

- [Taxonomy Contributions Skill](../skills/taxonomy-contributions.md)

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy Contributions
proposed_concept.description: Operational skill and contributor workflow enforcing SKOS-Lite schemas, horizontal indexing rules, and standards alignment for AAIF vocabulary terms.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy Contributions skill operationalizes the contributor workflow for authoring, submitting, and validating terminology definitions within the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. It provides agents and human contributors with schema validation, intake staging rules, and conflict resolution checks across AAIF technical domains [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].

# Architecture / Specification

The contribution skill implements a phased intake and review sequence to prevent overlapping definitions from entering the foundation vocabulary [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].

### Contribution Lifecycle
1. **Raw Term Staging**: Unrefined candidate terms are collected in an asynchronous tracking sheet or whiteboard across working group delegates to detect terminology collisions prior to drafting formal definitions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].
2. **Drafting Format**: Term files adhere to the SKOS Lite metadata structure and must supply both a concise, beginner-friendly summary and an extensive description field specifying technical scope and boundaries [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].
3. **Citations and Provenance**: Schema entries include explicit citations or normative notes linking definitions to originating literature, specifications, or reference implementations [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].
4. **External Harmonization**: Contributors must evaluate proposed terms against existing ISO and NIST definitions, documenting explicit rationale for any divergent terminology [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].
5. **Human Curation Policy**: Contributions must satisfy the workstream's AI usage policy requiring human oversight and judgment prior to pull request submission [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].
6. **Domain Editor Sign-Off**: Merging requires sign-off from designated domain editors and working group delegates to confirm cross-boundary coherence [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].

# Lifecycle History

The taxonomy workflow was outlined in May 2026 alongside the SKOS Lite schema adoption [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. In June 2026, the process was hardened by resetting existing unvetted definitions into pull requests, introducing dual-field summary/description requirements, and adding explicit ISO/NIST alignment and citation provenance checks [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

# References

- [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)
- [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md)

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing agentic terminology, resolving cross-group definition conflicts, and cataloging the ecosystem landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF effort established to harmonize terminology across foundational domains and maintain an open-source catalog of agentic technologies[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]. Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1], the workstream formalizes delegates from every AAIF technical working group to reconcile conflicting language, establish standardized SKOS-Lite taxonomy schemas, and curate a CNCF-style ecosystem landscape[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream operates an asynchronous, multi-phase intake and curation pipeline:

1. **Intake and Delegate Submission:** Each working group delegates formal representatives to submit 10–20 core terms relevant to their domain[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]. Initial seed terms were cleared to enforce peer-review governance[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].
2. **Unified Review Spreadsheet:** Proposed terms across all working groups are aggregated into a single tracking document to identify overlapping scopes, evaluate universality, and resolve conflicts globally before pull requests are opened[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]. Reviewers use a consensus-based "cull" column and conditional formatting to flag terms for elimination or debate[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e]. Universal terms are prioritized at the top of the review sheet[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].
3. **Publishing Pipeline:** Curated concepts map into SKOS-Lite schemas and landscape data representations rendered via an automated CI/CD web portal[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].

# Lifecycle History

- **May 2026:** Kickoff meeting established weekly cadence and reviewed the preliminary charter[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].
- **June 2026:** Secured charter approvals across participating working groups, onboarded formal delegates from all active working groups except Agentic Commerce, and launched the web portal CI/CD pipeline[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]. Identified attendance and contribution risks regarding the Agentic Commerce WG[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].
- **July 2026:** Extended weekly synchronizations to one-hour sessions to deliberate high-contention terms (such as "identity" and human versus AI agent definitions) and initiated global spreadsheet reviews prior to individual schema pull requests[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group coordinates AAIF alignment with international policy directives, statutory governance mandates, and compliance frameworks for autonomous agent deployments[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]. Chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase), the group evaluates global policy trends, develops comparative frameworks, and translates regulatory principles into architectural criteria[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group focuses on synthesizing policy frameworks into structured technical assessments:

- **Landscape Mapping:** Evaluating existing agentic AI policy frameworks, regulatory guidance documents, and industry best practices[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].
- **Comparative & Gap Analysis:** Structuring analyses across emerging AI baseline standards to identify operational gaps in current software harnesses and governance runtimes[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].

# Lifecycle History

- **June 2026:** Completed its initial 3-month milestone assessing and mapping global agentic AI policy frameworks and guidance standards[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]. Highlighted participation risks and noted that its planned gap analysis operates primarily as a comparative analysis until clear evaluation baselines are defined[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].
- **July 2026:** Initiated a 3-month sprint dedicated to conducting comparative policy gap analysis[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group aligning agent observability protocols, telemetry schemas, multi-agent trace models, and execution verification.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group defines open standards and telemetry patterns for monitoring, debugging, and reconstructing autonomous AI agent workflows[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]. Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group standardizes execution traces, protocol boundaries, state management, and multi-agent coordination metrics[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group partitions its charter deliverables across five dedicated focus groups led by designated domain leads[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]:

- **LLM Primitives Observability:** Monitoring model requests, completions, context boundaries, token usage, and latency.
- **Protocol Observability:** Telemetry across execution boundaries including MCP and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communications.
- **Multi-Agentic Observability (Orchestration & Coordination):** Tracing distributed subagent delegation, fan-out joins, swarms, and coordination trees.
- **Agentic State and Context:** Capturing dynamic context window health, memory graph mutations, and durable state serialization.
- **Agentic Reasoning:** Tracing planning paths, thought loops, verification gates, and chain-of-thought progression.

# Lifecycle History

- **June 2026:** Formalized focus group leadership, kicked off the 6-month deliverable schedule, drafted initial use case and gap analysis documents on GitHub, and established taxonomy alignment with the Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]. Moved issue tracking and consensus workflows to GitHub Discussions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open threat models, security design patterns, cross-working-group checklists, and secure runtime baselines.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes threat models, mitigation architectures, risk checklists, and hardened runtime patterns across agentic deployments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]. Chaired by Alex Frazer, the group actively collaborates with external standards bodies (including OWASP, ETSI TC SAI, and FINOS) while coordinating internal security reviews across the AAIF[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical output into five primary workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]:

- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis & Framework Design:** Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, evaluating frameworks like MITRE ATLAS, OWASP AI Top 10, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, documenting operational guardrails and secrets management baselines[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog:** Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, authoring architectural pattern templates for isolation, attestation, and containment[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Cross-Working Group Security & Privacy Review Checklist:** Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing lightweight security intake evaluations for other AAIF groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Taxonomy & Landscape Alignment:** Delegated to Jay White and Katherine Druckman, reviewing unified cross-group definitions and proposing terms like `Agent Card`[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Lifecycle History

- **July 2026:** Submitted the threat modeling gap analysis (Deliverable 4) and initial draft of the Best Practices Guide to GitHub[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]. Explored collaboration avenues with ETSI TC SAI on European AI Act standardization, aligned with OWASP on agent hooks, reviewed MCP tool attestation defenses against rug-pull attacks, and initiated investigations into potential overlap with the FINOS AI governance framework[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing agentic terminology, resolving cross-group definition conflicts via SKOS-Lite, and publishing the interactive CNCF-style ecosystem landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation initiative established to curate a consolidated glossary of agentic AI terms and maintain an interactive ecosystem landscape map [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]. Operating as a shared technical gatekeeper and collaborative peer-review body across vertical working groups, the workstream eliminates siloed terminology and redundant landscape research while providing enterprise stakeholders with a unified architectural guide [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream operates under a federated governance model where domain editors representing each working group arbitrate terminology and ecosystem entries rather than defining vertical domain specifications in isolation [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

## Scope and Boundaries
- **In Scope**:
  - Consolidation and standardization of technical terminology using a flexible SKOS-Lite metadata schema (`prefLabel`, `altLabel`, `broaderTerm`, `scopeNote`, `relatedTerms`, `contrastsWith`) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
  - Living curation of a CNCF-style ecosystem map (`landscape.yml`) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
  - Automated CI/CD deployment of the AAIF Standards Portal, Shared Taxonomy Explorer, and Landscape via GitHub Pages [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea].
- **Out of Scope**:
  - Authoring vertical legal or compliance whitepapers (retained by vertical groups like [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
  - Low-level protocol specifications, such as Model Context Protocol or Agent-to-Agent execution schemas [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
  - Closed proprietary commercial portals [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

## Governance and Operations
- **Charter Approval**: Approved on June 21, 2026 [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Leadership**: Chair Junjie Bu (Google) and Co-Chair Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Cadence**: Weekly on Mondays at 8:30 AM PT / 11:30 AM ET [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **Delegates**: Relies on two nominated domain editors from each technical working group to coordinate glossary ingestion and pull request reviews [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-21**: Formal charter approved establishing horizontal taxonomy consolidation and landscape publishing responsibilities [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].
- **2026-06**: Integrated terminology work from vertical initiatives, including vocabulary handoffs from the [Security & Privacy Working Group](security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7].

# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing standards, benchmarks, and engineering practices required for AI agents to operate accurately and reliably under real-world enterprise conditions [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]. The group investigates agentic failure modes, nondeterministic behavior, evaluation harnesses, and recovery strategies across multi-step execution flows [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group coordinates technical deliverables spanning failure taxonomies, enterprise reliability benchmarks, and practitioner evaluation suites.

## Governance and Operations
- **Leadership**: Chair Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Co-Chair Casper Nielsen (Diagrid), appointed by Platinum and Gold members for the term March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019].
- **Meeting Cadence**: Biweekly on Tuesdays at 9:00 AM PT [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019].
- **Communications**: Public mailing list (`wg-accuracy-reliability@lists.aaif.io`) and community Discord channel [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019].
- **Operating Principles**: Strict adherence to individual-capacity contributor neutrality and Linux Foundation antitrust compliance policies [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-03-01**: Working group leadership term commenced under Jordan Augé and Casper Nielsen [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019].

# Overview
The Security & Privacy Working Group develops threat models, security architecture patterns, privacy baselines, and vulnerability taxonomies tailored to agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]. The group coordinates security practices across foundation working groups while formulating guidance on tool sandboxing, credential isolation, and autonomous execution boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7].

# Architecture / Specification
The group's operational roadmap is organized across dedicated workstreams and cross-cutting foundation touchpoints [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7].

## Workstream Structure
As of mid-2026, the working group has stood up five distinct workstreams with designated leads [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7]:
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: Authoring comparative analyses against existing frameworks like CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7].
- **Best Practices Guide**: Producing implementation guidelines for runtime security, tool invocation guardrails, and secret management [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7].
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Relinquished localized glossary development to transition core agent security terms into the cross-cutting [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7].
- **External Alliance Engagement**: Reviewing liaison relationships and joint posture with external organizations, including OWASP, AARM, and MCP ACS via Technical Committee review [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06**: Transitioned from formation to active execution across five workstreams, published the June 2026 Technical Committee monthly report, and initiated external alignment proposals with OWASP, AARM, and MCP ACS [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-7].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group defines telemetry schemas, trace context propagation standards, and diagnostic evaluation frameworks for AI agents [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]. The group focuses on capturing causal execution across foundation models, tool invocation boundaries, and multi-agent peer-to-peer delegation flows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its activities into targeted focus areas spanning protocol boundaries and instrumentation standards [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].

## Technical Focus Areas and Integrations
- **Protocols and Primitives Merger**: Consolidated the protocols focus group and primitives focus group to unify core agent telemetry language and streamline working sessions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].
- **OpenTelemetry Collaboration**: Targeting upstream contributions to OpenTelemetry specifications, semantic conventions, and reference SDKs grounded in working group gap analysis [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].
- **Taxonomy Harmonization**: Actively reviewing universal vocabulary lists and advancing observability and traceability definitions in coordination with the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].
- **Network and Peer-to-Peer Observability**: Exploring cross-layer telemetry, libp2p agent networks, identity-aware telemetry, and IETF specifications for distributed multi-agent interaction [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-07-22**: Formally merged the protocols and primitives focus groups, advanced universal taxonomy reconciliation, and initiated explorations of peer-to-peer agent network telemetry with libp2p and IETF working groups [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5].

# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group catalogs, aligns, and harmonizes open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows executed by AI agents on behalf of users, businesses, and software systems.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration (W&PI) Working Group establishes a shared workflow model and common terminology for agentic AI systems, authoring interoperability guidelines and design patterns that allow agent workflows to operate across frameworks, tools, and execution environments.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]

# Architecture / Specification Scope
The working group charter, approved on May 13, 2026 and updated on July 23, 2026, defines three primary scope pillars:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]
- **Agent Workflow Models and Semantics:** Standardizing common [workflow primitives](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md) (tasks, tool calls, branching, handoffs, and retries), cross-framework representations, and the translation of deterministic models to autonomous agent workflows.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]
- **Long-Running and Stateful Agent Execution:** Formulating patterns for multi-hour or multi-day workflows, partial completion resumption, workflow state persistence, idempotency, failure recovery, and workflow audit logs (distinguished from runtime signals handled by [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md)).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]
- **Tool Invocation and External System Coordination:** Defining standard coordination patterns between agents, APIs, CLIs, and external services.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]

# Governance and Leadership
- **Chair:** Yaron Schneider (Diagrid)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]
- **Co-Chair:** Adam Seligman (Workato)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]

# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group defines failure mode taxonomies, empirical evaluation frameworks, and operational reliability benchmarks across autonomous and semi-autonomous agent deployments.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]

# Governance and Leadership
The working group is chaired by Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid).[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]

# Active Deliverables
As of the July 2026 reporting cycle, the group tracks three primary deliverables:[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]
- **Deliverable D1 (Terminology & Methodology):** Methodological grounding deliverable structuring 41 terms in Milestone 1, emphasizing 23 priority terms spanning outcome correctness, cross-run consistency, perturbation robustness, and system reliability.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]
- **Deliverable D2 (Enterprise Gap Analysis):** Practitioner-priority analysis addressing gaps preventing direct reuse of existing benchmarks, supported by the [Accuracy and Reliability Survey](../resources/accuracy-and-reliability-survey.md).[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]
- **Deliverable I1 (Liaisons):** Cross-group coordination note, with initial outreach established with [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes open threat models, defense-in-depth architectural patterns, security review checklists, and hardening guidance across agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]

# Active Workstreams and Deliverables
During July 2026, the working group coordinated five active deliverables:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design:** Co-leads Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg; draft PR submitted evaluating CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Co-leads Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam; initial draft reviewing prior projects and hardening controls.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog:** Co-leads Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora; catalog structure aligned with architecture guidance.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Cross-Working Group Security Review Checklist:** Lead Govindaraj Palanisamy; review framework evaluating cross-WG deliverables for security baselines.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
- **Taxonomy / Landscape Workstream:** Delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman coordinating security terms (including sessions, replay attacks, constraints, and guardrails) into the shared taxonomy led by Junjie Bu.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]

# Cross-Foundation Relations
The group conducts informal technical exchanges with external organizations such as OWASP pending formal liaison approvals from the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]
