proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol gap analyses, and interface specifications across agentic discovery, checkout, payment, and trust boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group is a technical body within the Agentic AI Foundation chartered to develop vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol gap analyses, and interface specifications for AI agents operating across commercial lifecycles[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]. Co-chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group addresses agent-mediated and agent-directed transactions across product discovery, checkout negotiation, payment execution, fraud signaling, and post-purchase interactions[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].

The group operates under a protocol-neutral scoping principle that focuses strictly on commerce-facing boundaries, interfaces, and data signals rather than internal agent harness architectures or proprietary platform execution models[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]. It maintains explicit cross-functional coordination dependencies with [Identity & Trust](identity-and-trust.md), [Security & Privacy](security-and-privacy.md), and [Observability & Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].

# Architecture / Specification

## Agentic Commerce Capability Model
The working group's primary baseline deliverable is the Agentic Commerce Capability Map, which structures agent interaction surfaces into distinct commercial phases[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]:

- **Product Discovery**: Separates asynchronous product catalog feeds from synchronous, live merchant and marketplace retrieval; establishes criteria for source discovery, schema normalization, data freshness, and catalog authenticity[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
- **Checkout Negotiation**: Frames [agentic checkout](../taxonomy/agentic-checkout.md) as a stateful, merchant-authoritative negotiation; resolves protocol bindings, extension points, and human-in-the-loop handoff thresholds[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
- **Payment Abstractions**: Disaggregates [delegated payment](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md) execution into three reusable architectural concepts: *handlers*, *instruments*, and *credentials*[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]. The capability model analyzes static payment capability discovery alongside transaction-specific dynamic eligibility, tokenization delegation, and sensitive payment data boundaries[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **Trust and Fraud Signaling**: Establishes mechanisms to separate agent identity and risk profiles from human shopper identity and risk profiles, including cryptographically verifiable evidence binding agent delegation, intent, and execution across merchant, platform, and payment provider boundaries[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

## Protocol Gap Analysis
The working group undertakes comparative protocol evaluations to assess cross-protocol composition and interoperability[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]:

- **ACP and UCP**: Evaluates negotiation flows, transport bindings, and state management models between the Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP) and Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
- **Machine Payments Protocol (MPP)**: Evaluates MPP's challenge–credential–receipt exchange as a specialized payment-handler composition pattern within broader checkout pipelines[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

# Lifecycle History
- **April 2026**: Initial working group workshop formulated the protocol-neutral remit, interface-versus-internals scoping rule, and draft charter; initial technical discussions mapped discovery feeds and checkout negotiations[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
- **May 2026**: Working group charter formally approved; technical focus advanced to payment-handler abstractions (handler, instrument, credential) and machine payments composition[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate authoritative monthly reporting from February through July 2026 establishing chairs, lifecycle milestones, capability mapping, and protocol gap analysis.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol gap analyses, and lifecycle architectures for AI-driven transactions, wallets, and dispute resolution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group (WG Agentic Commerce) is an AAIF technical body established to analyze, standardize, and provide vendor-neutral architectural guidance across the agentic commerce lifecycle, spanning product discovery, checkout and negotiation, payment authorization, and post-purchase operations [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332]. Chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group addresses protocol fragmentation and merchant integration burdens without creating competing proprietary specifications [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group structures its technical deliverables around an end-to-end user journey and problem-first evaluation method [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332]:

- **Commerce Lifecycle**: Covers four sequential phases: discovery (feed-based versus live-query indexing), checkout and negotiation, payment execution, and post-purchase handling (order observation, returns, refunds, cancellations, and disputes) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].
- **Capability Map**: Documents roles, responsibilities, and protocol handoffs across consumers, agents, merchants, digital wallets, payment providers, and banks [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].
- **Protocol Gap Analysis**: Evaluates emerging specifications including Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP), Agent Payment Protocol (AP2), and x402 against multi-turn workflows, identifying gaps between passive order monitoring and authorized state mutation [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].
- **Trust and Fraud Signals**: Distinguishes agent identity and risk from shopper identity and risk, isolating verifiable delegation evidence and transaction bindings while preventing indiscriminate data leakage [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

The group coordinates with [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), and [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to harmonize identity delegation, policy boundaries, and audit logging [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

# Lifecycle History

- **February 2026**: Launched kickoff survey mapping ecosystem problems, merchant integration burdens, and candidate protocols [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26].
- **March 2026**: Transitioned kickoff inventory into a lifecycle-oriented model and established landscape gap-analysis methodology [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].
- **June 2026**: Advanced fraud and risk signal analysis, separating signal interoperability from internal fraud-model scoring [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].
- **July 2026**: Initiated post-purchase capability reviews and evaluated agent wallets and payment mandates under AP2 and x402 [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

mutations.rationale: Update workstream governance and review progress with July 2026 reporting detailing chairs, term admission workflows, and portal publishing milestones.

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing agentic terminology, resolving cross-group definition conflicts, and curating the public agentic landscape portal.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream (WS Taxonomy & Landscape) is an AAIF cross-cutting governance initiative chartered to harmonize terminology across foundational agentic concepts, resolve vocabulary divergences across working groups, and maintain the public Agentic AI Landscape portal [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]. Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream arbitrates standardized vocabulary spanning universal terms and domain-specific working group vocabularies [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream operates an admission and definition workflow designed to achieve consensus without stalling on contested edge cases [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]:

- **Sequential Term Review**: Processes an inventory backlog across universal terms, [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), and [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
- **Two-Phase Review Model**: Evaluates terms through an "admitted first, defined second" pipeline, temporarily deferring detailed definition and category bindings until inclusion consensus is reached [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
- **Contested Term Arbitration**: Holds divergent definitions in a dedicated debate backlog to isolate cross-group philosophical disagreements while admitting uncontroversial entries [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
- **Public Portal and Pull Request Tracking**: Publishes accepted entries directly to the public taxonomy portal, transitioning definition debates into repository pull requests for transparent auditability [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

# Lifecycle History

- **July 2026**: Conducted four review syncs evaluating 46 terms; admitted initial 13 terms covering universal, identity, and workflow primitives in PR #33 [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
- **August 2026**: Merged PR #33 and advanced PR #35, expanding admitted portal entries to 21 terms while tracking a 25-term contested debate backlog [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

proposed_concept.title: Human Approval Gate
proposed_concept.description: Workflow governance pattern requiring an explicit, authorized human decision bound to an immutable proposal before causing a protected effect.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Human Approval Gate pattern ensures that a workflow reaching an action with elevated risk, audit obligations, or ownership requirements pauses until an accountable, uniquely identified human principal authorizes the exact proposal [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]. The pattern binds decisions directly to specific immutable proposal versions and enforces that execution remains safely suspended until approval is explicitly granted.

It is paired with the [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and [Durable Wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md) patterns, and serves as a core building block for reference architectures such as the [Single-Agent Process with Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern addresses common failure modes in asynchronous human reviews, including proposal drift, process lifetime limits exceeding human response delays, non-attributable shared accounts, and race conditions between late approvals and timeout escalations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].

```text
immutable proposal ──► present to authorized human ──► explicit decision
                              │                           │
                              └── durable wait ─────────┘
                                          │
                          decision record: who · what · when
```

### Invariants
To maintain system safety and auditability, implementations must satisfy the following invariants [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]:
- **Principal Attribution**: Approvers must be uniquely identified human principals authorized for the specific decision class; shared approval accounts are invalid.
- **Immutable Proposal Binding**: The interaction surface must present the exact, immutable proposal version to which the decision binds.
- **Explicit Decisions**: Approval and rejection must be active, explicit decisions; silence, timeouts, delivery errors, or system failures never imply approval.
- **Unified Decision Record**: Decision records must capture proposal version, approver identity, explicit outcome, and timestamp within the same workflow run identity.
- **Proposal Invalidation**: Any mutation or supersession of the proposal invalidates pending reviews and requires a fresh decision.
- **Bounded Duration**: Pending approval requests require explicit deadlines, expiration parameters, or escalation pathways.
- **Idempotent Execution**: Duplicate, conflicting, or delayed decision events must not trigger redundant workflow resumptions or double executions.

proposed_concept.title: Job-Oriented Architecture Model
proposed_concept.description: Architectural decision framework structuring agent reference architectures around recognizable practitioner jobs rather than raw agent counts.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Job-Oriented Architecture Model is an architectural decision framework established by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) that organizes reference architectures around recognizable practitioner jobs rather than structural agent topologies [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]. It decouples the operational need—such as bounded remediation or approval gating—from the agent count, which is treated as an implementation outcome.

Under this model, reference architectures represent complete compositions of reusable patterns, operational boundaries, required capabilities, and explicit exit guarantees, while patterns capture independent solutions to recurring workflow problems [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].

# Architecture / Specification
The framework defines distinct roles and relationships between architectural artifacts [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]:
- **Reference Architectures**: Comprehensive specifications matching named practitioner jobs (e.g., [Single-Agent Process with Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md)). They compose reusable patterns, declare runtime boundaries, and enforce outcome guarantees.
- **Patterns**: Independently adoptable solutions addressing specific, recurring workflow challenges (e.g., [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md), [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md), [Durable Wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md)). Patterns maintain self-contained invariants and failure modes across multiple architectures.
- **Structural Typologies**: Classifications such as single-agent and multi-agent serve as internal design characteristics rather than top-level architectural taxonomies.
- **Scenario Validation**: Use cases and test scenarios validate architectures; mismatches signal missing patterns, variant gaps, or entirely distinct practitioner jobs.

### Rationale and Trade-offs
Practitioners approach workflow integration from operational needs rather than predetermined agent counts [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]. Focusing on recognized practitioner jobs provides clearer operational boundaries and prevents redundant definitions across workflows. This replaces earlier scaffolding that categorized architectures strictly by single-agent versus multi-agent boundaries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing agent telemetry, causal execution traces, protocol boundary metrics, and verifiable observability objects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes telemetry models, causal execution traces, protocol boundary propagation, and verifiable telemetry specifications across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]. Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group aligns runtime monitoring standards with OpenTelemetry semantic conventions and investigates peer-to-peer telemetry mechanisms [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

The group collaborates across working groups on cross-boundary observability gap models, taxonomy unification with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), and cryptographic runtime accountability with peer-to-peer networking initiatives [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

# Architecture / Specification
To optimize execution and eliminate scope overlap, the working group restructured its operational tracks from five focus groups into three core workstreams [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]:
- **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability**: Led by Zayne Turner, merging foundational language model metrics with protocol boundary tracing. Focus items include tracing [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) (ARD) for skill discovery and trust decisions, establishing Skills as first-class citizens in observability telemetry, and developing the cross-boundary observability gap model.
- **Multi-Agentic Observability - Orchestration & Coordination**: Led by Ty Smith, addressing multi-agent interaction mapping, peer-to-peer telemetry transport, and runtime graphs.
- **Agentic State & Context**: Led by Govindaraj, combining agentic reasoning with memory, context window, and state observability.

### Standards and Technical Initiatives
Key deliverable initiatives under development include:
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: A standard telemetry recommendation lead-authored by Matthew Lee establishing causal trace linking and execution schemas [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].
- **Composable Trust Blueprint**: Integration of Verifiable Telemetry Objects (VTO) and Agent Action Capsules (AAC) with LibP2P and CBOR encoding, separating telemetry semantics from cryptographic proofs in collaboration with IETF/IRTF accountability efforts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing shared agentic workflow execution models, reference architectures, runtime interoperability guidelines, and domain taxonomy.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body chartered to establish a shared workflow model and common terminology for agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87] It extends open specifications and projects while publishing interoperability guidelines and architectural design patterns enabling agent workflows to execute predictably across diverse frameworks, external tools, and runtime execution environments.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]

The group operates under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and maintains active liaison with cross-cutting efforts such as the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md). Participation is open to the public under Linux Foundation antitrust and neutrality principles.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]

# Governance and Leadership

The working group leadership consists of a Chair and Co-Chair appointed by Platinum and Gold members of the group for the term running from March 1, 2026, through January 31, 2027:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]

- **Chair:** Yaron Schneider (Diagrid)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]
- **Co-Chair:** Adam Seligman (Workato)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]

The working group convenes biweekly on Thursdays at 8:00 AM Pacific Time.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87] Formal agendas, running notes, and LFX meeting recordings are maintained publicly for community review.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]

# Workstreams and Core Deliverables

The working group organizes its technical production across three interrelated workstreams:

1. **Taxonomy:** Establishes a shared, foundational vocabulary defining [workflow primitives](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md) and operational stages to eliminate ambiguity across specifications and architectures.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a]
2. **Reference Architectures:** Defines normative compositional patterns, control boundaries, and [workflow architecture principles](../guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md) governing agent execution.
3. **Critical Use Cases:** Documents end-to-end production scenarios applying working group primitives and architectural patterns against real-world integration requirements.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-03-01:** Inaugural term begins for Chair Yaron Schneider and Co-Chair Adam Seligman.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]
- **2026:** Taxonomy workstream initiated with draft workflow terms in active review.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide provides practical, builder-focused security controls and architectural decision frameworks for production agent deployments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9] Produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) as Deliverable 4 of 5 in its charter roadmap, the guide targets common threat surfaces encountered when language models interact with execution tools and runtime environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]

To maintain clear organizational boundaries across working groups, identity and delegated authorization architectures (such as SPIFFE/SVID and RFC 8693 token exchange) are explicitly excluded from this guide and are defined separately by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]

# Architecture / Specification

The guideline structures implementation controls across five security domains:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]

1. **Secrets Management:** Protecting API credentials, temporary execution tokens, and ambient environment variables from prompt disclosure or unauthorized subagent inheritance.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]
2. **Secure Tool Invocation:** Hardening Model Context Protocol (MCP) interactions, validating schemas, and mitigating tool supply-chain vulnerabilities.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]
3. **Guardrails:** Implementing model-level input and output safety boundaries to detect injection, unauthorized commands, and policy violations.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]
4. **Evaluation Frameworks:** Automated testing regimens assessing model adherence to safety baselines and regression vulnerabilities prior to deployment.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]
5. **Post-Incident Forensics:** Capturing immutable audit trails, execution state, and telemetry necessary to reconstruct anomalous agent behavior.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]

Each domain is organized around a failure-pattern, control, and decision-framework schema, paired with a curated tool reference ledger detailing ecosystem maturity, cost models, and implementation guidance.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]

# Lifecycle History

- **Draft v0.1:** Initial draft submitted via PR #9 to the Security and Privacy Working Group repository.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]

# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group establishes vendor-neutral telemetry models, causal execution tracing frameworks, and protocol boundary metrics across agent runtimes, tool interfaces, and multi-agent communications within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff] The working group operates an open, GitHub-first work tracking model ensuring deliverables, ownership, and current statuses are discoverable without requiring synchronous meeting attendance.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes deliverable tracking, coordination threads, and architectural decisions through standardized GitHub issues and pull requests.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b44b5d93b435-bb190e50]

## Source of Truth and Operating Cadence
GitHub functions as the durable source of truth for all work items, decisions, and pull requests.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff] External collaboration tools such as Google Docs, Slack, and Discord serve as staging and discussion mechanisms, with mature artifacts migrated into the repository for review and tracking.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff] Operational cadence is synchronized with repository state:
- **Pre-meeting:** Repository scans identify blocked work items, stale steps, and agenda priorities.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]
- **During meetings:** Action items and consensus decisions are documented with explicit issue or pull request linkages.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]
- **Post-meeting:** Issues are updated with assigned owners, status transitions, and next steps for asynchronous visibility.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]
- **Monthly reporting:** Aggregated issue, PR, and meeting data form the basis of submissions to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]

## Work Item Lifecycle and Status Taxonomy
Individual work items track an explicit outcome, designated owner, and next concrete action using standardized work item templates.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b44b5d93b435-bb190e50] Status progressions follow a normative six-state vocabulary:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]
- `needs owner`: The deliverable or task is approved as valid, but lacks an active driver.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]
- `scoping`: Boundaries, inputs, and target outcomes are being formulated.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]
- `in progress`: Active drafting, empirical research, or inter-group coordination is underway.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]
- `ready for review`: Artifacts are ready for contributor feedback and formal review windows.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]
- `blocked`: Advancement is halted pending an architectural decision, external dependency, or input.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]
- `done`: The target deliverable has landed in the repository, transitioned tracking locations, or closed.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]

# Lifecycle History
The working methods and issue lifecycle conventions were formally codified to maintain transparent, asynchronous tracking across all observability and traceability workstreams.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]

# References
- Related guidelines: [Working Group Reporting Template](../guidelines/working-group-reporting-template.md)
- Related governance: [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes open threat modeling frameworks, security design patterns, cross-working-group security review checklists, and practical builder security best practices within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] Co-chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), the group conducts technical evaluation of agentic vulnerabilities, sandbox boundaries, and protocol attack surfaces across five active workstreams.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Workstreams and Deliverables
The working group executes across five synchronized workstreams:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design:** Evaluates established security frameworks (including MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF) against agentic architectural requirements, alongside STRIDE and PASTA methodologies, human-user authorization (HUA), and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool-signing attestations.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Delivers practical deployment guidance across credentials, tool execution, and guardrails, delegating identity and authorization concerns to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog:** Formulates structured design patterns and contribution templates, harmonizing boundary controls with architectural guidance.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist:** Provides an intake and assessment mechanism led by Govindaraj Palanisamy to audit overlapping scope across AAIF working groups.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Delegation:** Coordinates security and privacy terminology alignment with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]

## Governance and Pull Request Acceptance
Deliverable integration follows an autonomous working group governance model:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]
- **Internal PR Merging:** The working group reviews and merges pull requests falling within its approved charter without waiting for prior approval from the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]
- **Reporting Oversight:** Merged deliverables and operational progress are submitted to the Technical Committee through monthly reports indexed in the repository.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10]
- **Default-to-Open Records:** Past and current meeting recordings, transcripts, Discord channels, and repository assets are designated public by default to ensure transparent community scrutiny.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]

# Lifecycle History
The working group transitioned from initial formation into open repository execution in mid-2026, opening pull requests for threat modeling and best practices, standardizing public record access, and formalizing autonomous pull request merging under Technical Committee oversight.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c9b4ccd3][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]

# References
- Deliverable draft: [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md)
- Deliverable draft: [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)
- Review checklist: [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)
- External standards bodies: ETSI TC SAI, OWASP State of Agentic AI Security, FINOS AI Governance

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (WG) establishes security and privacy as a shared, foundational engineering discipline across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]. Its primary objective is delivering open threat models, standardized taxonomy terms, and architectural design patterns that agent providers, platform consumers, and peer technical working groups can adopt to implement shared responsibility for trustworthy agentic systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].

The working group coordinates technical governance in conjunction with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and maintains inter-group review protocols such as the [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Leadership
The working group operates under chair leadership appointed by the Platinum and Gold members of the working group, serving terms from March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]:
- **Chair:** Alex Frazer (Runlayer) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]
- **Co-Chair:** Junjie Bu (Google) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]

## Operational Cadence and Communication
- **Meeting Cadence:** Biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM US Pacific Time via Linux Foundation LFX Zoom [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].
- **Mailing List:** `wg-security-privacy@lists.aaif.io` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].
- **Meeting Archives:** Agendas and rolling notes are tracked in shared meeting documents, with session recordings and AI-generated summaries indexed in LFX [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].

## Repository Organization
The working group organizes its deliverables and governance assets across standardized repository directories [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]:
- `charter/`: Formal working group charter and foundation governance documentation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].
- `deliverables/`: Technical outputs, threat modeling evaluations, and architectural patterns, such as the [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].
- `meeting-notes/`: Public session agendas, minutes, and administrative summaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Modular maintainer agent skill structuring first-pass GitHub issue triage, defensive prompt injection handling, read-only codebase grounding, and precedent-based severity classification.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `issue-analysis` skill is a modular agent skill designed for maintainers to produce structured first-pass assessments of incoming GitHub issues [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Integrated into autonomous triage workflows like the [Submission Analyser](../resources/submission-analyser.md), the skill classifies issue type, assigns severity, formulates testable root-cause hypotheses, proposes concrete remediations, and grounds its technical judgements in historical project review records [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

The skill operates as an advisory diagnostic tool for maintainers rather than an autonomous decision engine, explicitly emphasizing uncertainty over speculative conclusions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

# Architecture / Specification

## Analytical Pipeline
The skill executes a four-stage assessment pipeline [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]:

1. **Evidence Isolation and Prompt Injection Defense:**
   - The issue content is delivered inside a nonce-delimited data block [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
   - All text within the delimiter is strictly treated as untrusted data rather than instructions, regardless of phrasing or apparent author association [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
   - If directive text attempts instruction override, credential access, external messaging, or format alteration, the agent logs an adversarial finding under `injectionSuspected: true` with explanatory `injectionNotes`, continuing technical evaluation solely on the issue's technical merits [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
   - The evaluator parses verifiable details: minimal reproductions, version/environment telemetry, error logs, and discrepancies between expected and observed behaviors [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

2. **Read-Only Codebase Grounding:**
   - The agent reads files within the local working directory checkout to confirm behavioral plausibility and map reports to concrete file paths rather than abstract subsystems [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
   - Execution of write operations, repository modifications, network calls, or build commands is prohibited during analysis [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

3. **Precedent Retrieval and Consultation:**
   - Maintainer-authored historical reviews in `references/` establish project standards for severity thresholds, vulnerable seams, and common architectural root causes [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
   - The skill evaluates frontmatter metadata (`tags`, `issue-type`, `severity`, `components`) to identify 3–5 matching past issues and cites those directly relevant to the diagnosis under `relatedPastIssues` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
   - Synthetic reference examples demonstrate diagnostic patterns:
     - Duplicate webhook delivery caused by un-flushed acknowledgement buffers during consumer process shutdowns (`SIGTERM`) [^evt-submission-analyser-file-20fc496a9225-9e278b3d].
     - Credential disclosure where structured logger redaction rules are bypassed by intermediate `JSON.stringify` serialization on HTTP request headers [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4754a1b8e47b-9ed9890b].

4. **Structured Assessment Synthesis:**
   - The agent produces a structured triage document defining issue classification, severity rationale, affected component paths, testable root-cause hypotheses, suggested actions, and open investigative questions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy defining proposal requirements, intake procedures, and progression criteria across Sandbox, Growth, Impact, and Emeritus project stages.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation Project Lifecycle Policy, effective March 18, 2026, establishes formal mechanisms for open technical projects to join the foundation through the Project Proposal Process [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]. It defines project admission stages, expectations, transition criteria, and annual review evaluations governed by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

The policy provides a structured path for project progression, ensuring projects participate at an operational level appropriate to their maturity while securing mentorship, foundation resources, and ecosystem alignment [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

# Architecture / Specification

## Project Proposal Requirements
Candidates seeking to join the foundation—either as existing external projects or as newly formed initiatives—must submit proposals to the foundation's project proposals repository with the following core details [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]:
- Project name, functional description, value proposition, origin, and development history [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Explicit statements on alignment with the AAIF mission and integration with existing AAIF projects [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Representative use cases and tangible evidence of user or developer adoption [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Technical Committee sponsor, if assigned, to mentor onboarding [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Release under an OSI-approved permissive open-source license, including documentation of external dependency licenses [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Publicly accessible code repository, automated CI/CD and validation pipelines, release mechanics, contribution guidelines, and open issue tracker [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Documented governance model (`GOVERNANCE.md`), core maintainer identities, leadership team structure, and decision-making processes [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
- Official communication channels, web presence, financial sponsorships, and requested foundation infrastructure [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

## Lifecycle Stages
The policy defines four sequential and terminal project stages [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]:
1. **Sandbox Stage:** Entry-level incubation for early-stage or experimental projects demonstrating technical alignment [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
2. **Growth Stage:** Maturing projects with demonstrated adoption, sustained multi-contributor community engagement, and defined governance [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
3. **Impact Stage:** High-maturity flagship projects demonstrating widespread industry production usage and resilient self-governance [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
4. **Emeritus Stage:** Deprecated or archived projects that have completed their lifecycle or transitioned out of active maintenance [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

Progression across stages is evaluated via formal acceptance criteria during the Technical Committee's Annual Review Process [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Maintainer triage agent skill producing structured issue analyses with standardized classifications, root-cause hypotheses, and actionable next steps.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `issue-analysis` skill is a modular maintainer agent skill designed to perform first-pass triage and structured analysis of open-source repository issue submissions[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]. It structures unstructured issue reports into standardized technical briefs that provide maintainers with root-cause hypotheses, concrete file references, classification taxonomies, and prioritized action lists before maintainer intervention[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22].

The skill operates within automated triage agents such as [submission-analyser](../resources/submission-analyser.md) to generate reliable triage artifacts without executing unverified code patches[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].

# Architecture / Specification

### Report Template Structure

The output produced by `issue-analysis` adheres to a strict reporting schema[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]:

1. **Summary:** A single-paragraph synopsis restating the report in maintainer terms so that context can be understood without reading the full discussion thread.
2. **Classification:** Standardized categorizations across three primary axes:
   - **Type:** `bug`, `feature-request`, `documentation`, `question`, `security`, or `ambiguous`.
   - **Severity:** `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, or `informational`.
   - **Reproducibility:** `reproducible`, `not-reproducible`, `insufficient-information`, or `not-applicable`.
   - **Severity Rationale:** One or two sentences articulating user impact, workarounds, or comparable precedents[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22].
3. **Affected Components:** Explicit file paths or module identifiers (e.g., `src/config/loader.ts` rather than vague subsystem descriptions)[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22].
4. **Root-Cause Hypotheses:** Proposed failure or architectural mechanisms accompanied by explicit criteria to confirm or refute each hypothesis[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
5. **Suggested Actions:** Prioritized maintainer guidance (diagnostics, target files, clarifying information requests) rather than unverified diffs[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
6. **Open Questions:** Precise clarifying questions required from the reporter.
7. **Related Past Reviews:** References to prior review analyses or codebase precedent informing the findings[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].

### In-Context Few-Shot Conditioning

The skill uses synthetic reference reviews in `references/` (e.g., `example-config-reload-feature-request.md`) to guide the model's tone, analytical depth, and structured frontmatter tags (`issue-number`, `date`, `issue-type`, `severity`, `tags`, `components`)[^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22].

# References

- [Agent Skills Standard](../standards/agent-skills.md)
- [Submission Analyser](../resources/submission-analyser.md)

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless GitHub Actions triage agent running defensive issue analyses and injection evaluation test suites.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

`submission-analyser` is an open-source headless triage agent designed to run in continuous integration pipelines such as GitHub Actions, evaluating incoming repository issue submissions and generating structured analytical reviews using the [issue-analysis skill](../skills/issue-analysis.md)[^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6]. Because it ingests untrusted text directly from public issues, it incorporates a comprehensive defensive evaluation suite to test robustness against adversarial prompt injection, notification abuse, and privilege escalation[^evt-submission-analyser-file-04ecd65ab81f-33714e60][^evt-submission-analyser-file-2e092a0c54ea-4363d97f].

# Architecture / Specification

### Injection Test Fixture Matrix

The repository maintains a regression suite under `tests/fixtures/injections/` validating defensive boundaries across common adversarial input categories:

- **Instruction Overrides & Exfiltration:** Direct attempts to command the agent to ignore system instructions, redefine persona boundaries, or exfiltrate system prompts and available tool manifests[^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6].
- **Notification and Mention Flooding:** Injection vectors attempting to abuse agent publishing outputs to broadcast mass pings (e.g., `@everyone`, `@here`, role pings `<@&...>`, maintainer handles) into notification channels like Discord or Slack[^evt-submission-analyser-file-04ecd65ab81f-33714e60].
- **Encoding and Homoglyph Obfuscation:** Payloads disguised with alternative encodings such as Base64 payloads, ROT13 ciphers, and unicode Cyrillic homoglyphs crafted to bypass shallow string matching[^evt-submission-analyser-file-0f27825af60d-1d3aca33].
- **Synthetic Tool Invocation Smuggling:** Fake tool execution markup (e.g., ````tool_call```` blocks or `<function_calls>` XML tags) attempting to forge tool results, disable security scans, or coerce the agent into calling unauthorized tools[^evt-submission-analyser-file-2e092a0c54ea-4363d97f].

### Operational Integration

`submission-analyser` operates in non-interactive CI runs, analyzing pull requests or issue submissions against predefined skills, maintaining strict tool boundaries, and publishing structured maintainer summaries without executing arbitrary runtime patches[^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6].

# References

- [Issue Analysis Skill](../skills/issue-analysis.md)
- [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless GitHub Actions triage agent running defensive issue analyses against prompt injection attack vectors including exfiltration and role-play.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Submission Analyser is a headless GitHub Actions triage agent designed to inspect incoming issue submissions, assess operational security risks, and execute automated evaluations against adversarial prompt injection test cases. The project incorporates an automated test fixture suite that exercises boundary defenses against unauthorized instruction overrides, credential harvesting, and persona hijacking.

# Architecture / Specification
The analyser's defensive test suite validates system resilience across multiple prompt injection vectors:
- **Environment Exfiltration**: Test fixtures simulate requests that instruct the analysis agent to dump runtime environment secrets (such as GitHub tokens, Google service account keys, and API credentials) into structured triage fields or outbound webhooks [^evt-submission-analyser-file-c385a440d3d1-196a4a61].
- **Hidden Formatting and HTML Comments**: Hidden HTML comments and collapsed markdown tags embed adversarial directives intended to manipulate issue severity scores, bypass injection detection flags, or falsely append security team approval statements [^evt-submission-analyser-file-305b7ba8fb0c-d60ec9fe] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a072a88a60fa-f5eaa4ea].
- **Remote Payload and Link Retrieval**: Fixtures inject untrusted third-party URLs, script payloads, and HTML event handlers attempting to induce outbound network fetches or command execution during triage [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7cf6ee468c96-f0fe2bdd] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a072a88a60fa-f5eaa4ea].
- **Unicode Obfuscation and Role-Playing**: Fixtures combine directional control characters, invisible unicode codepoints, and role-playing personas (such as unconstrained developer modes) to override operational instructions and elicit prompt leaks [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7385a2d6a676-148647ca].
- **Authority Impersonation**: Injections invoke organizational authority, such as the Linux Foundation security team, using artificial urgency and compliance threats to suppress injection warnings and mandate exfiltration [^evt-submission-analyser-file-e761e6213598-a8166ad6].

This test battery pairs with maintainer triage procedures defined in [Issue Analysis](../skills/issue-analysis.md) and aligns with baseline protections documented in [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).

# References
- Repository test fixtures in `aaif/submission-analyser` under `tests/fixtures/injections/`.

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless triage agent and sandboxed GitHub Actions runner designed to analyze untrusted public issue submissions while defending against prompt injection and credential exfiltration.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Submission Analyser is an automated, headless GitHub Actions triage agent designed to ingest and evaluate public repository issues while operating under an explicit untrusted threat model [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]. Because any external contributor can file issues on a public repository, the system assumes that untrusted issue bodies, comments, and titles will deliberately attempt prompt injection attacks against the underlying language model harness [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6].

# Architecture / Specification
The analyser isolates analysis workflows and enforces strict trust boundaries across credentials, repositories, and published outputs [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]:

- **Protected Assets**: Primary protected assets include workflow credentials (`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON`, `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL`, and the run's `GITHUB_TOKEN`), workflow configuration files in `.github/workflows/`, maintainer publication surfaces (Google Docs and Discord), historical analysis files, and runner budget spend [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6].
- **Threat Actor Model**: The adversary is defined as any external entity submitting issues without account age or reputation requirements, assumed to possess full knowledge of the analysis schema and architecture [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6].
- **Cross-Repository Trust Boundary**: The analyst executes in an isolated repository decoupled from target repositories. Dispatches from target repositories require an explicit `ANALYST_DISPATCH_TOKEN` with Actions write-only permission, preventing target repository compromises from modifying the analyst's workflow scripts [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6].
- **Adversarial Test Fixtures**: Defenses are continuously tested against injection fixtures that model attack patterns such as delimiter forging (e.g., simulating fake system delimiters and closing blocks) [^evt-submission-analyser-file-f4ad28ba849d-48065e61] and fake authority claims (e.g., asserting priority overrides from repository owners or safety teams to bypass egress controls) [^evt-submission-analyser-file-fdb9d913d85d-8ad69d31].

proposed_concept.title: OpenTelemetry for AI Agent Infrastructure
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral observability framework and collector pipeline standardizing traces, metrics, logs, and gen_ai semantic conventions across AI agent runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
OpenTelemetry (OTel) serves as the vendor-neutral observability substrate for AI agent infrastructure, defining how traces, metrics, and logs are instrumented, collected, processed, and exported across heterogeneous system components [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a]. Rather than operating as an analysis backend or storage engine, OTel provides the telemetry plumbing connecting instrumented agent runtimes, LLM gateways, and tool servers to upstream observability platforms [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].

# Architecture / Specification
The reference architecture spans application instrumentation, wire protocols, collector routing, and semantic conventions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a]:

- **Components and Versions**: Evaluated against OTel Specification 1.x (stable traces, metrics, logs), OTel Collector 0.104.0, OTLP 1.3.0, and Semantic Conventions 1.27.0 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].
- **Pipeline Architecture**: Instrumented applications (AI agents, LLM gateways, MCP servers, and microservices) emit telemetry via the OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) over gRPC (port 4317) or HTTP/protobuf (port 4318) into the OTel Collector [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].
- **Collector Pipeline**: The collector handles ingestion through configurable receiver, processor, and exporter pipelines, accepting inputs from OTLP, Prometheus, Jaeger, Zipkin, file logs, and host metrics [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].
- **GenAI Semantic Conventions**: Standardizes agent and language model execution metadata through `gen_ai.*` attributes, capturing prompt tokens, completion tokens, model identifiers, and tool invocation spans within unified causal trace graphs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].

# References
- [OpenTelemetry Specification Repository](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification)
- Related working group: [Observability and Traceability WG](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- Related standard: [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)

mutations.rationale: Update Linux driver tracing reference architecture with kernel observation primitives, hardware counter models, dynamic debug, and subsystem tracers.

proposed_concept.title: Linux Driver Tracing Mechanisms
proposed_concept.description: Layered kernel observability and debugging framework enabling runtime inspection of hardware interactions, device drivers, and I/O subsystems without recompilation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Linux Driver Tracing mechanisms provide a layered set of observability, debugging, and instrumentation facilities specifically tailored for kernel device drivers and hardware interfaces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]. Spanning structured logging (`dev_dbg`), dynamic debug (`dyndbg`), static tracepoints (`TRACE_EVENT`), subsystem-specific tracers (`usbmon`, `blktrace`), `debugfs` state inspection, and crash dumps (`devcoredump`), these facilities allow developers and operators to monitor hardware interactions and I/O request flows without modifying or recompiling driver code [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1].

# Architecture / Specification
The reference architecture details driver observation layers across hardware and kernel subsystems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]:

- **Observation Primitives**:
  - *Structured Logging*: `dev_dbg()`, `dev_info()`, and `dev_err()` bind log messages directly to device topologies and sysfs paths [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1].
  - *Dynamic Debug (`dyndbg`)*: Allows runtime enablement and filtering of debug callsites by module, function, file, or line number via `debugfs` control files [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1].
  - *Custom Tracepoints*: Statically compiled `TRACE_EVENT()` hooks expose low-overhead event streams through `tracefs` for capture by consumers such as `perf` and `trace-cmd` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1].
  - *Post-Mortem Analysis*: Kernel `devcoredump` records device-specific state snapshots upon driver crashes or timeout events [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1].
- **Observation Models**:
  - *Event Model*: Captures discrete state transitions, register writes, interrupt deliveries, and command submissions rather than application-level duration spans [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1].
  - *Hardware Counter Model*: Exposes low-level telemetry including NVMe statistics, network interface packet and error metrics, PCIe Advanced Error Reporting (AER) counters, and GPU engine utilization [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1].
  - *State Snapshot Model*: Inspects active runtime controller registers, engine schedules, USB device descriptors, and link states via `sysfs` and `debugfs` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1].

# References
- Related resource: [Linux Tracing Comparison](../resources/linux-tracing-comparison.md)
- Related working group: [Observability and Traceability WG](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)

mutations.rationale: Update PostHog reference architecture documenting client-side PII sanitization, Capture API ingestion, and behavioral analytics mapping for agent runtimes such as Goose.

proposed_concept.title: PostHog for Agent Telemetry
proposed_concept.description: Product analytics telemetry sink and ingestion architecture capturing behavioral agent events via the Capture API with client-side PII sanitization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
PostHog serves as an external product analytics and telemetry sink for AI agent frameworks, capturing adoption metrics, session lifecycles, and behavioral events [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]. Operating outside the agent runtime as either a cloud-hosted service or self-hosted platform, PostHog provides structured event storage, funnel analysis, cohort segmentation, and feature flag management for agent deployments such as Goose [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75].

# Architecture / Specification
The reference architecture defines how agent runtimes integrate with PostHog's ingestion layer while enforcing privacy safeguards [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]:

- **Client Ingestion Architecture**: Agents emit telemetry directly via HTTP POST requests to the PostHog Capture API (`/capture/`) using project API keys (`phc_*`), requiring no heavy SDK dependencies inside the agent binary [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75].
- **Runtime Telemetry Module**: Exemplified by Goose's `posthog.rs` implementation, the agent runtime encapsulates an on-disk installation tracker (UUID-based distinct ID), an event builder (recording `session_start`, `error`, and `onboarding_*` events), and a dedicated PII sanitizer [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75].
- **Client-Side PII Sanitization**: To protect user privacy, regex-based sanitization strips filesystem paths, API keys, email addresses, authentication tokens, and user UUIDs from event properties prior to transmission [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75].
- **Ingestion Pipeline**: The PostHog backend buffers events into Kafka, stores raw and processed records in ClickHouse, and links events to anonymous or distinct person profiles for cohort and funnel analysis [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75].

# References
- [PostHog GitHub Repository](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog)
- Related resource: [Goose Agent Runtime](../resources/goose.md)
- Related working group: [Observability and Traceability WG](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless triage agent and sandboxed GitHub Actions runner executing Flue 2.0 workflows to evaluate public repository submissions without repository write privileges.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Submission Analyser is an automated, headless issue analysis agent deployed via GitHub Actions using the Flue 2.0 runtime and Pi model provider abstractions.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec] Designed to evaluate public issue submissions without granting execution tokens write access to code or issue trackers, the agent operates out-of-band: it reads untrusted issue text, evaluates submissions against repository conventions, uploads formatted analyses to Google Docs, and posts notifications to a designated Discord webhook.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901]

By intentionally avoiding write actions against originating repositories, the architecture neutralizes common prompt injection attack paths that seek to weaponize writable repository tokens.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f] The system executes as a centralized analysis runner serving multiple target repositories through fine-grained cross-repository dispatch mechanisms.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660]

# Architecture / Specification

### Cross-Repository Dispatch Flow

Target repositories (such as proposal intake repositories) do not host the full agent runtime or its secrets. Instead, target repositories install a lightweight workflow triggered on issue opening or when the `needs-analysis` label is applied.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660]

1. **Dispatch Trigger**: The target repository uses a fine-grained Personal Access Token (`ANALYST_DISPATCH_TOKEN`) restricted exclusively to `Actions: read and write` on the analyst repository to invoke `github.rest.actions.createWorkflowDispatch`.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660] This explicitly avoids `repository_dispatch`, which would require dangerous `Contents: write` permissions on the analyst repository.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660]
2. **Payload Inputs**: The dispatch provides the target issue number, target repository identifier (`owner/repo`), and a dry-run flag.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]
3. **Bot Filtering**: Automated submissions originating from bot accounts are filtered prior to dispatch and corroborated during tool execution to conserve model quotas.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]

### Execution and Sandboxed Permissions

The analyst workflow runs with minimal GitHub token entitlements:[^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]

- `contents: read`: Permits checkout of the agent tooling and local skill dependencies.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]
- `copilot-requests: write`: Authorizes model inference requests billed to the parent organization without providing any repository write authority.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]
- **No `issues: write`**: The workflow deliberately strips issue commenting capabilities, removing the mechanism by which injected prompts could modify tracker state or trigger downstream automated write actions.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]

### Runtime and Model Orchestration

The agent uses `@flue/runtime` with `@earendil-works/pi-ai` provider integrations.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4] Model routing uses GitHub Copilot infrastructure, routing requests to `PRIMARY_MODEL` (e.g., `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.7`) with workflow-level step fallback to `FALLBACK_MODEL` (e.g., `github-copilot/gpt-5.4`) since model assignment in Flue is submission-scoped.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e]

### Tool Boundaries and External Sinks

Agent logic is orchestrated through a single harness tool (`analyze_and_publish`) rather than recursive autonomy:[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec]

- **Data Ingestion**: Issue metadata, description, and comments are fetched into context within nonce-delimited data boundaries, instructing the model to treat input strictly as passive data rather than instructions.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901]
- **Google Drive / Docs**: Analysis markdown is published using Google Drive API multipart uploads via `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` directly into `GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID` without open sharing links.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e]
- **Discord Notifications**: The resultant document link is transmitted over a webhook (`DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL`) configured with `allowed_mentions: { parse: [] }` to prevent ping-injection attacks.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]

# References

- [`skills/issue-analysis.md`](../skills/issue-analysis.md)
- [`guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md`](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)
- [`patterns/proposal-execution-split.md`](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Progressively disclosed Flue skill formatting maintainer issue reviews, classifying architectural claims, and surfacing prompt injection indicators.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Issue Analysis skill packages standardized maintainer evaluation criteria, section templates, and reference review artifacts into a modular Flue 2.0 skill.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4] Executed as part of the [`resources/submission-analyser.md`](../resources/submission-analyser.md) pipeline, it enables an LLM agent to evaluate public GitHub issues against technical scope and security prerequisites without requiring manual per-issue prompt tuning.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec]

The skill incorporates explicit prompt injection reporting conventions. When an agent detects manipulative phrasing, authority spoofing, or instruction injection embedded within untrusted issue text, it records these occurrences in structured metadata while proceeding to review the underlying technical proposal.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]

# Architecture / Specification

### Progressive Disclosure and Loading

The skill resides under `src/skills/issue-analysis/` and is mounted explicitly using `useSkill()` in the agent entry point rather than via automatic workspace discovery.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]

- **Context Budgeting**: Mounting the skill exposes only a single catalog descriptor line in the base system prompt.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec] The full guidance in `SKILL.md` is loaded only when the model invokes `activate_skill`.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec]
- **Reference Grounding**: Supporting assets—such as `template.md` and synthetic example analyses in `references/`—remain unread on disk until explicitly referenced, preventing context window bloat on straightforward reviews.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]

### Output Schema and Injection Detection

The analysis output schema mandates structured extraction across problem statements, ecosystem alignment, and safety boundaries.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4] Crucially, the schema defines dedicated fields for defensive telemetry:[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]

- `injectionSuspected`: Boolean flag set to `true` whenever user-supplied issue content attempts to alter system constraints, inspect environmental variables, or redirect tool execution.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]
- `injectionNotes`: Explanatory narrative detailing the detected attack vector or manipulation attempt.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4]

By treating adversarial inputs as analysis signal rather than unhandled abort conditions, the skill provides maintainers with audit trails of hostile activity.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901]

# References

- [`resources/submission-analyser.md`](../resources/submission-analyser.md)
- [`standards/agent-skills.md`](../standards/agent-skills.md)
- [`guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md`](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing agent telemetry, causal execution traces, protocol boundary metrics, and full-stack observability frameworks across the AAIF ecosystem.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with standardizing vendor-neutral telemetry, distributed execution tracing, protocol boundary instrumentation, and runtime state inspection for autonomous agent architectures.

The group establishes standard semantic conventions, cross-layer correlation frameworks, and evaluation tooling to ensure operators can track agent reasoning, tool invocations, and multi-agent interactions across heterogeneous infrastructure environments.

# Architecture / Specification

### Charter and Governance

The working group approved its formal operating charter on April 15, 2026, and submitted it to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) for official review on April 21, 2026 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2]. AAIF leadership confirmed that community contributions via pull requests may be leveraged directly provided they align with approved charter deliverables [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

### Focus Groups and Operating Structure

The working group organizes its technical initiatives into dedicated, open-participation focus groups [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]:

- **Protocols and Primitives Focus Group**: Focuses on protocol-level telemetry, boundary handoffs, and serialization specifications across agent-to-agent and tool-call interfaces.
- **State, Context, and Reasoning Focus Group**: Concentrates on capturing multi-turn conversational context, memory state transitions, decision checkpoints, and replay semantics.

Participation in both focus groups is open to all community members without formal prerequisite application forms [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

### Five-Layer Observability Model and Gap Analysis

The group evaluated existing industry observability frameworks, noting that widely adopted tooling like [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) operates predominantly at the application layer (Layer 5) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]. To address limitations in tracking agent actions, the WG is defining a comprehensive five-layer observability stack covering hardware accelerators (CPUs/GPUs), kernel primitives, container runtime layers, network transport, and agent application workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]. Key areas of ongoing work include:

- **Session Replay and Tracking**: Closing semantic gaps in session-level identification, non-deterministic agent loop monitoring, and execution replay [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Defining semantic conventions for the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) to record tool dispatch, approval gates, and causal agent transitions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].
- **Cross-Layer Data Encryption and Security**: Investigating per-field payload encryption, dynamic rule-based verification, and Merkle link graphs for tamper-evident trace logging [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].
- **Taxonomy Coordination**: Formulating and contributing standardized terms to the [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) repository in cross-collaboration with the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].
- **Agent Action Capsule**: Preparing review specifications for encapsulated action artifacts across execution environments [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-04-15**: Working group voted to approve its initial charter [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2].
- **2026-04-21**: Charter formally submitted to the AAIF Technical Committee for approval [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2].
- **2026-06**: Completed and merged the monthly working group report for June 2026 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-14][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-15].
- **2026-07**: Completed and merged the monthly working group report for July 2026 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-24].
- **2026-08-19**: WG meeting ratified open focus group participation, accepted seven initial taxonomy terms, and reviewed the five-layer stack gap analysis [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].
