proposed_concept.title: AAIF Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure governing project proposal intake, technical review, voting gates, and onboarding into the Agentic AI Foundation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Project Proposal Process defines the operating workflow for proposing, reviewing, approving, and onboarding projects into the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. Implementing the governing [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md), this procedure establishes a six-step pipeline plus parallel contributor clearance, emphasizing offline and asynchronous evaluation to scale across geographically distributed committees [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

A core principle is the guaranteed engagement bar: rather than requiring an upfront individual champion, each proposal must receive meaningful asynchronous engagement from multiple [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) members before advancing to a formal vote [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Workflow Stages
The process progresses across sequential evaluation phases and parallel administrative milestones [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]:
1. **Initial Intake (Step 1)**: Owned by the CTO and assisted by an automated intake agent. The submission undergoes initial smoke testing, public technical compliance checks on the tracking GitHub issue, and a private advisory review for the Technical Committee.
2. **TC Q&A Window (Step 2)**: Offline review window conducted asynchronously across GitHub issue discussions. Advancement requires reaching an engagement bar of multiple active TC members. If the engagement bar is unmet, TC chairs may designate an on-demand TC supporter to champion the submission, or the proposal is closed. An optional live presentation may be scheduled upon TC request.
3. **Contributor Paperwork (Parallel Step)**: The submitter, coordinated by LF PMO, completes organizational contribution agreements and contributor paperwork concurrently with review.
4. **TC Vote (Step 3)**: Formal admission and initial lifecycle stage vote conducted via LFX Vote by the Technical Committee.
5. **Governing Board Approval (Step 4)**: Confirmation of organizational readiness, budget, and resource implications via LFX Vote.
6. **LF Legal Formation (Step 5)**: Preparation and execution of contribution agreements, technical charter, and trademark/asset transfers via DocuSign.
7. **Technical Onboarding (Step 6)**: LF IT and project maintainers assume repository custody and configure foundation infrastructure.

## Defined Roles
- **Project Submitter**: Authors the proposal, engages during the Q&A window, executes legal paperwork, and oversees repository transfer.
- **CTO**: Oversees Step 1 intake, conducts smoke tests with the intake agent, prepares the TC brief, approves Q&A extensions, and triggers supporter escalations.
- **Intake Agent**: Automated system running public technical compliance checks and generating advisory reviews for the TC.
- **Technical Committee (TC)**: Evaluates technical alignment, participates in Q&A, requests presentations if needed, and votes on project admission.
- **TC Supporter (On-Demand)**: Designated TC member assigned to champion proposals struggling to meet asynchronous engagement thresholds.
- **Governing Board (GB)**: Approves resource allocation and operational fit.
- **LF PMO, LF Legal, LF IT**: Operational support managing intake records, charter legalities, and repository migrations.

# References
- AAIF Project Proposal Process v0.3 [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Use Cases
proposed_concept.description: Catalog defining multi-category agent observability use cases, cross-cutting telemetry requirements, and tamper-evident evidence criteria.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Observability Use Cases catalog documents technical and operational requirements for monitoring, debugging, and evaluating agentic AI workloads across execution boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30]. Maintained by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the catalog organizes capabilities across performance, debugging, safety, and compliance domains, feeding directly into the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

# Architecture / Specification

## Safety and Compliance Category
In addition to baseline behavioral telemetry (E1–E3), the catalog establishes strict tamper-evident requirements for high-assurance environments [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30]:

### Use Case E4: Tamper-Evident Evidence for Audit and Dispute Resolution
- **Objective**: Provide regulated organizations with non-repudiable proof of what an agent executed, verifiable by third-party auditors or courts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
- **Integrity Requirements**:
  - Merkle-chained, cryptographically signed event records binding execution steps to specific inputs and outputs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
  - Write Once, Read Many (WORM) storage guarantees preventing retrofitted trace modification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
  - RFC 3161 trusted timestamps certifying the precise chronological ordering of agent decisions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
  - Immutable approval chains linking human authorizations directly to executed payloads [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
  - Linkage between declared intent and observed runtime execution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
- **Grading Model**: Incorporates external evidence ladders, such as WitnessOS (spanning E0 Declared to E4 Anchored) and EU AI Act compliance grading frameworks, to benchmark verification rigor [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

# References
- Working Documents: USE-CASES.md (PR #30) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30]

It categorizes real-world autonomous and semi-autonomous systems to establish shared execution patterns, boundary scopes, and operational benchmarks [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].

The inventory standardizes workflow breakdowns to match the foundational [Workflow Primitives](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md) taxonomy [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32]:
- **Activity over Step**: The working group transitioned from linear 'step' nomenclature to discrete 'activities' across use case schemas and inventories [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].
- **Structural Composition**: Workflows decompose into composite activities that encapsulate capability calls, human approval checkpoints, and state transitions, reflecting non-linear and event-driven orchestration rather than rigid procedural steps [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Project Lifecycle Policy governs how technical projects enter, advance, and graduate within the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a, ^evt-technical-committee-pr-9]. Enforced by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) alongside the [Project Proposal Process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md), the policy establishes objective milestones and governance criteria across project tiers [^evt-technical-committee-pr-9].

# Architecture / Specification

## Lifecycle Stages
The policy defines distinct maturity stages for foundation projects [^evt-technical-committee-pr-9]:
- **Sandbox Stage**: Low-barrier intake tier designed to foster open experimentation, prototype development, and nascent community building under Foundation governance [^evt-technical-committee-pr-9].
- **Growth Stage**: Intermediate tier requiring tightened technical governance, active multi-organization contributions, and validated adoption [^evt-technical-committee-pr-9].
- **Graduated Stage**: Highest maturity tier reserved for stable, self-sustaining projects that exemplify cross-ecosystem impact and adherence to AAIF architectural standards.

## Review and Advancement
Progression between stages involves regular Technical Committee evaluations and verified operational health metrics, removing redundant proposal layers while enforcing rigorous growth criteria [^evt-technical-committee-pr-9].

proposed_concept.title: Workflow Primitives
proposed_concept.description: Foundational vocabulary and structural execution primitives defined by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group, establishing Activity as the atomic unit of work.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Workflow primitives define the standardized vocabulary and operational constructs used across the Agentic AI Foundation's Workflows and Process Integration Working Group to model, execute, and govern agentic workflows[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]. These primitives establish a vendor-neutral foundation for composing agent capabilities, managing runtime execution state, and enforcing deterministic coordination boundaries across single-agent and multi-agent workflows.

The working group formally replaced the earlier concepts of "Workflow Step" and "Workflow Task" with "Activity"[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31]. Defining Activity independently resolves circular definition issues, establishing it as the fundamental unit of work before defining composite workflows.

# Architecture / Specification

## Foundational Concepts

- **Activity**: A single, bounded task with defined inputs and outputs that can be tracked to completion[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31]. It represents the atomic building block of workflow execution.
- **Workflow**: The primary unit of structured, multi-activity work with a defined goal and outcome[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]. A workflow is composed of one or more Activities, their relationships, and the execution logic required to achieve the outcome.
- **Workflow Execution**: A runtime instance of a Workflow definition[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]. A single definition may spawn multiple concurrent executions, each maintaining its own independent execution state and lifecycle.
- **Workflow State**: The cumulative information representing the condition of a Workflow Execution at a specific point in time, encompassing execution progress and data necessary to resume or continue execution[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Workflow Context**: Shared information accessible to participants during execution informing decisions across activities and workflow boundaries, including inputs, shared metadata, run history, configuration, and references to external systems[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].

## Execution and Control

- **Control Flow**: The logic determining execution order, branching conditions, iteration, parallelism, and synchronization of Activities within a Workflow[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Trigger**: An event, signal, schedule, condition, or request initiating a Workflow Execution or advancing an active execution[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Lifecycle**: The sequence of execution states and transitions traversed by an execution from initialization to termination or completion[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Durability**: The capability of a Workflow Execution to preserve state across failures or interruptions, enabling resumption without progress loss[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Determinism**: The property whereby a workflow produces consistent execution behavior given identical inputs, execution state, and execution history[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].

## Coordination Models

- **Orchestration**: Centralized coordination where an orchestrator explicitly directs activity sequencing and invocation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Choreography**: Decentralized coordination where autonomous agents react to events without centralized dispatch[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Composition**: Combining workflows and activities into modular, higher-order workflows[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].

# Lifecycle History
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group drafted the initial terminology baseline in `workstreams/taxonomy/terms.md`[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]. In PR #31, the WG transitioned from `Workflow Step / Workflow Task` to `Activity` to decouple task boundaries from composite workflow definitions[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31]. The term set was subsequently submitted for cross-foundation harmonization with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing shared agentic workflow execution models, reference architectures, and taxonomy primitives across AAIF systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group defines shared models, orchestration patterns, and integration specifications for AI agent execution in enterprise and distributed environments[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]. It standardizes core workflow vocabulary, establishes reference architectures for agent execution patterns, and harmonizes operational integration mechanisms across foundation initiatives.

# Architecture / Specification

## Workstreams and Deliverables

- **Taxonomy Workstream**: Develops standard terminology for agentic workflows, published in `workstreams/taxonomy/terms.md`[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]. In PR #31, the working group resolved a core architectural circularity by replacing "Workflow Step" and "Workflow Task" with [Activity](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md), defined independently of composite workflows[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31]. The initial term set was submitted for cross-foundation review via PR #55 in the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].
- **Reference Architectures**: Standardizes workflow patterns including single-agent approval loops, parallel fan-out, and bounded remediation workflows.
- **Process Integration**: Bridges agent interactions with external systems, focusing on durability, determinism, and state persistence across human and automated triggers[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].

# Lifecycle History
The working group established its taxonomy workstream to align terminology across AAIF bodies[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]. In August 2026, the group restructured its core terms around the Activity primitive[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31] and engaged in cross-working-group review sessions with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing agentic terminology, resolving cross-group definition conflicts, and curating the open agentic AI landscape map.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative chartered to establish unified terminology, resolve cross-domain definitional conflicts, and curate the open-source and commercial agentic AI ecosystem landscape[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]. Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream coordinates domain editors across all active technical working groups to produce consistent conceptual boundaries and maintain the foundation's public taxonomy and landscape portal.

# Architecture / Specification

## Review Workflow and Term Harmonization

The workstream operates structured review syncs to evaluate candidate terms submitted by working groups:
- **Term Admission Pipeline**: Evaluates proposed terms across universal agent primitives, domain-specific concepts, and potential overlaps. During August 2026, the group held three review syncs evaluating 53 terms: 37 were approved for definition drafting, 15 were culled, and one (`Multi-agent misdirection`) was held for further debate[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].
- **Explicit Relationship Mapping**: Definition proposals track explicit relational links between adjacent concepts, including `Skill` and `Tool`, `Kill switch` and `Reversibility`, `Harness` and `Meta-harness`, and `Delegation` and `Handoff`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].
- **Cross-Group Representation**: Includes domain editors across groups, with expanded representation from [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) via Leonardo Galesky alongside Identity and Trust[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

## Deliverables

- **Unified Taxonomy Portal**: A publicly hosted portal and SKOS-aligned vocabulary defining core agentic primitives. The `Harness` definition merged as the first accepted definition in PR #37[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]. Active pull requests under review include `Human in the loop` (PR #40), `Meta-harness` (PR #48), Identity & Trust terms (PR #42), and the [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) initial term set (PR #55)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].
- **Agentic AI Landscape Map**: An interactive ecosystem catalog categorizing open-source and commercial technologies, with proposals expanding coverage into Attestation and Verifiable Evidence (PR #44) and Agentic Vulnerability Enumeration (PR #38)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

# Lifecycle History
The workstream initiated its formal intake and culling process in mid-2026[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]. In August 2026, the workstream shifted from initial intake to drafting definitions, merging its first formal definition (`Harness`) and establishing formal Domain Editor review loops across contributing working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group defines failure mode taxonomies, benchmarks, evaluation frameworks, and architectural patterns to improve the operational dependability of agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]. Chaired by Jordan Auge (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid), the group focuses on establishing concrete criteria for identifying, measuring, and mitigating non-deterministic failure modes and hallucinations across production agent deployments.

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Deliverables

- **D1 (Terminology and Taxonomy)**: Compiles standardized definitions for reliability and failure modes, managed under active review in PR #8[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]. Term batches are coordinated with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) for cross-foundation harmonization.
- **D2 (Gap Analysis and Survey Support)**: Develops empirical research instruments and gap analyses addressing real-world agent failure modes[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]. The working group formulated a practitioner survey under PR #9 targeting agent operators to gather comparable pain-point and prioritization metrics across industry deployments[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].
- **I1 (Internal Coordination Support)**: Supporting materials and cross-working-group engagement artifacts designed to facilitate phase 2 deliverable execution across AAIF working groups[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group prioritized review rounds over new scope due to seasonal PTO constraints[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]. The group advanced the D2 survey specification (PR #9) through meeting and Discord reviews while queuing D1 terminology subsets for contribution to the shared AAIF taxonomy[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation framework capturing causal agent execution, tool invocations, approval checkpoints, and cross-turn session continuity.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry framework developed within the AAIF Observability and Traceability Working Group to standardize causal execution tracing, tool invocations, approval gates, and multi-turn session correlation across autonomous agent runtimes. Rather than treating an agent as a monolithic black box or relying on an unbroken, process-bound span for extended workflows, the model captures discrete turns, tool calls, and pause-and-resume lifecycles while preserving cross-trace continuity.

# Architecture / Specification
The specification defines how agent interactions map to distributed trace structures across heterogeneous agent SDKs and runtime environments:
- **Session and Turn Correlation:** Supports tracking long-running tasks across disconnected traces and distinct runtime turns without requiring continuous, session-long spans[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43]. Workflows that pause, restart, or resume days later preserve continuity by joining conversation and turn identities across independent execution traces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43].
- **Dual-Runtime Baseline Validation:** The model separates runtime instrumentation gaps from missing core semantics by benchmarking identical workflows across [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and secondary agent SDKs[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40]. Telemetry gaps are systematically categorized as unsupported runtime behaviors, instrumentation defects, missing semantic conventions, or documentation guidance[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40].
- **Provider and Tool Call Semantics:** Distinguishes between requested tool invocations emitted by provider APIs and actual tool executions performed by runtime environments, preventing provider-only tool request payloads from falsely reporting tool completion[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46]. Standalone provider test harnesses isolate streaming, usage metrics, and error propagation from agent harness orchestration[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46].

# Lifecycle History
Following working group consensus on trace execution requirements, the working group initiated a nine-task execution plan to produce reproducible baseline traces, implement turn and session continuity across [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and partner SDKs, and publish standardized test harnesses for community contribution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46].

mutations.rationale: Update specification with cross-boundary telemetry verification through Agent Gateway and Goose, validating the five lifecycle stages and OTLP export.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Resource Discovery
proposed_concept.description: Decentralized discovery, verification, and admission specification enabling agents to find, trust, and consume tools and skills with lifecycle telemetry.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) is a decentralized discovery, verification, and admission specification enabling AI agents to locate, evaluate, and invoke tools, context sources, and skills across trust boundaries. The framework standardizes metadata negotiation, cryptographic verification of capabilities, and policy admission pipelines, while providing end-to-end telemetry correlating discovery decisions with downstream skill execution.

# Architecture / Specification
The ARD lifecycle model standardizes evaluation stages enforced by mediation gateways and runtime harnesses:
- **Five-Stage Lifecycle Telemetry:** Enforces observable state transitions covering discovery, provenance verification, governance checking, trust evaluation, and admission decisions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49]. Each stage emits structured events exportable via standard OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) pipelines[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49].
- **Skill Activation Correlation:** Bridges discovery and runtime activation by propagating W3C Trace Context between policy intermediaries such as [Agent Gateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) and agent harnesses like [Goose](../resources/goose.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49]. Admitted skills correlate subsequent activation and execution spans back to their governing admission decision, while quarantined skills emit audit events without generating simulated execution spans[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49].
- **Policy and Namespace Boundaries:** Validates experimental `ard.*` and `gen_ai.skill.*` namespaces across multi-agent environments to verify capability boundaries without requiring vendor-specific observability platforms[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49].

# Lifecycle History
The ARD lifecycle validation was established as a joint proof-of-concept between the LLM Primitives and Protocol Observability Feature Group and the Security workstream, testing cross-boundary admission and execution tracing using [Agent Gateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) and [Goose](../resources/goose.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol gap analyses, and lifecycle architectures for agent-mediated commercial transactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group develops vendor-neutral capability frameworks, protocol gap analyses, and governance models for automated, agent-mediated transactions. Chaired by representatives from Shopify and OpenAI, the group analyzes the technical requirements of delegated purchasing, merchant-agent negotiation, payment delivery rails, and post-transaction dispute accountability[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its deliverables across several core commerce domains:
- **Payment Delivery Layer and x402:** Incorporates transaction abstractions such as the Linux Foundation's x402 protocol into the group's Capability Map[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307]. The model decomposes payments into scheme, network, asset, and mechanism, using lightweight verify-and-settle contracts across HTTP, MCP, and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) transports to support both conversational cart transactions and autonomous per-use micropayments[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].
- **Dispute Resolution and Post-Transaction Evidence:** Addresses the breakdown of traditional card-present and session fraud signals in delegated agent commerce[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307]. The group investigates verifiable-intent records, Know-Your-Agent (KYA) identity provenance, and transaction metadata (agent ID, model version, platform) to establish legal and payment network burden-of-proof standards[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].
- **Consent Surfaces:** Identifies missing structured protocols for merchant terms and policy negotiations, preventing scenarios where autonomous agents silently accept human-oriented click-through agreements without explicit principal consent or auditable records[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group evaluated x402 payment rails and payment service provider (PSP) dispute requirements, establishing upcoming deep dives into the Order Network eXchange (OnX) standard and Machine Payment Protocol (MPP)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].

mutations.rationale: Update the working group charter and activities to reflect the nine-task Agent Behavior Trace Model execution plan and the ARD lifecycle telemetry workstream.

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing agent telemetry, causal execution traces, protocol boundary metrics, and resource lifecycle observability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group establishes vendor-neutral telemetry models, distributed tracing schemas, and operational monitoring standards across AI agent lifecycles, protocol boundaries, and underlying execution infrastructure.

# Architecture / Specification
The group coordinates several technical workstreams and feature groups:
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model Execution:** Implements a nine-task baseline and correlation roadmap standardizing cross-turn and multi-trace continuity without requiring monolithic session spans[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43]. Workstream efforts benchmark [Goose](../resources/goose.md) alongside independent agent runtimes to isolate implementation bugs from OpenTelemetry semantic convention gaps[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40], while packaging reusable provider API and tool execution test fixtures[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46].
- **Resource Lifecycle and Protocol Observability:** Operates through the LLM Primitives and Protocol Observability Feature Group to validate discovery and policy telemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49]. The group coordinates cross-boundary instrumentation between [Agent Gateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) and agent runtimes to trace [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) lifecycle stages (discovery, provenance, governance, trust, and admission) and correlate admission records with skill activation via W3C Trace Context[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49].
- **Boundary and Transport Monitoring:** Standardizes telemetry across Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent-to-Agent (A2A), and CLI subprocess boundaries, ensuring causal context is preserved during external tool execution and multi-agent delegation.

# Lifecycle History
Following discussions in August 2026, the working group formalized execution workstreams for both the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) nine-task implementation plan and the cross-boundary [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) lifecycle validation harness[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49].

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent with Human Approval Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture establishing an enforceable human approval gate and structural separation between agent proposal generation and execution publication.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Single-Agent with Human Approval architecture defines an execution pattern where an autonomous agent operates across read-only or staged workspaces to formulate action proposals that remain quarantined until an authorized human operator grants explicit approval.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36] This structure guarantees that autonomous reasoning cannot directly mutate production environments, live catalogs, or public documentation without human sign-off.

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group has validated this architecture against specific public-facing content update workflows, linking scenarios to items in the [Agentic Use Case Inventory](../resources/agentic-use-case-inventory.md).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]

# Architecture / Specification

### Boundary Separation and Lifecycle

The architecture defines three strict boundaries:

1. **Proposal Phase**: The agent ingests inputs, consults contextual knowledge sources, and generates candidate updates within an isolated staging branch or drafting buffer.
2. **Human Approval Gate**: An operator reviews the rendered candidate artifacts against organizational guidelines, utilizing a deterministic [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) or [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md). Rejections return actionable feedback to the agent loop, while approvals advance the proposal.
3. **Publication Phase**: An isolated publishing runner or privileged executor applies the approved payload to the target destination without further generative model modification.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]

### Validated Use Cases

Empirical validation records establish applicability across three high-frequency content scenarios:

- **FAQ and Knowledge-Base Updates**: Staged documentation revisions synthesized from issue resolutions or changelogs, gated before publication to customer-facing repositories.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]
- **Release Notes Generation**: Automated aggregation of commits and pull requests formatted for customer review prior to public tag release.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]
- **Listing Descriptions**: Autonomous generation and metadata tagging of marketplace catalog descriptions held for commercial review prior to listing activation.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08**: Validated against content use cases and integrated into the Workflows and Process Integration WG catalog via PR #36.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open threat models, security design patterns, cross-working-group review checklists, and actionable security baselines for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group develops threat models, security design patterns, governance checklists, and implementation baselines for agentic architectures across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d] The working group collaborates with sibling groups such as the [Identity and Trust Working Group](identity-and-trust.md) and [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](workflows-and-process-integration.md) to define security perimeters across agent autonomy boundaries.

# Architecture / Specification

### Active Workstreams and Deliverables

- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: A practitioner-focused guide detailing secrets management, tool invocation boundaries, and model evaluation. The initial release freezes in early September 2026 as the working group's first formal public deliverable.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d] Identity and trust topics are explicitly excluded from this version pending ownership demarcations with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d]
- **Actionable Static-Analysis Rules**: A companion workstream converting narrative best practices into executable static-analysis rules to scan agent SDK implementations (including Google, Amazon, and Microsoft SDKs) for configuration and permission vulnerabilities.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d]
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Architectural security blueprints, including the [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) pattern and forthcoming memory isolation patterns.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d]
- **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: An operational checklist and cross-group review program targeting active engagement with chairs across Governance, Observability, Workflows, Accuracy, and Commerce.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d]
- **Taxonomy Contributions**: Defining security and privacy terms for the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md), including scoping debates regarding sensitive execution versus privacy-preserving execution.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-09-01**: Working group meeting resolved to freeze and publish version 1.0 of the Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide, initiated SDK static-analysis rule development, and organized cross-WG review outreach.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group defines open specifications, telemetry models, and boundary tracing standards to provide visibility into agent reasoning, tool interactions, protocol exchanges, and lower-level execution environments.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611] Its work spans high-level behavioral models down to kernel- and network-level execution tracing.

# Architecture / Specification

### Focus Areas and Subgroups

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Specifying standardized data models to capture agent decision loops, context changes, and tool calls.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611]
- **Primitives and Protocol Observability Focus Group**: Oversees protocol tracing across Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent-to-Agent (A2A), and lower-layer system observability below Layer 7 (L6 down through syscalls and network interfaces) to provide end-to-end execution provenance.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611]
- **Agent Action Capsules**: Exploring tamper-evident cryptographic execution records (such as MeshLLM capsule implementations) that capture dispatched intents, execution outcomes, and authorization compliance.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611]
- **Terminology and Taxonomy**: Developing standard terms in coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-09-02**: Expanded Primitives and Protocol Observability focus group mandate to address sub-L7 and syscall observability, and initiated technical reviews of Agent Action Capsules.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611]

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group bridging global AI policy developments and technical agentic systems, tracking regulatory compliance requirements, and producing comparative gap analyses.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group monitors international policy, legislative instruments, and regulatory standards affecting autonomous agent systems.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a] The group maps statutory and administrative obligations against technical architecture patterns to identify gaps and support compliant open-source agent deployments.

# Architecture / Specification

### Operational Deliverables and Methodology

The working group executes a three-phase charter deliverable roadmap:

1. **Phase 1: Landscape Analysis**: Compilation and structural categorization of global policy instruments, legal statutes, and standards frameworks relevant to autonomous agent governance.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]
2. **Phase 2: Mapping and Gap Analysis**: Mapping policy instruments against approximately twelve standardized governance themes (e.g., accountability, transparency, human oversight). The group utilizes structured AI extraction prompts to consistently map best practices and regulations across these themes.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]
3. **Phase 3: Final Alignment Deliverable**: Consolidated technical recommendations and compliance matrices aligning AAIF architectural standards with international regulatory mandates.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07**: Completed Phase 1 landscape consensus on initial policy instruments and established twelve thematic mapping categories; progressed into Phase 2 gap analysis.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]

proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure governing project proposal intake, technical evaluation, Contribution Agreements, and voting gates required for AAIF project hosting.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Project Proposal Process specifies the submission workflow, review stages, and legal requirements for open-source initiatives seeking official hosting under the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF).[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1] Hosting levels comprise Sandbox, Growth, and Impact projects, evaluated based on ecosystem alignment, adoption, and technical maturity.

# Architecture / Specification

### Application and Review Stages

1. **Proposal Submission**: Project maintainers file a standardized proposal in the `aaif/project-proposals` repository detailing project origin, architectural scope, community traction, and alignment with the AAIF mission.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]
2. **Technical Committee (TC) Evaluation**: The [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) assesses architectural fitness, overlap with existing projects, and designated project tier readiness.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]
3. **Contribution Agreement Execution**: Based on contact information supplied in the proposal, a formal Contribution Agreement is issued to contributors. This agreement must be signed prior to final voting by the Governing Board.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]
4. **Dual Approval Gate**: Formal foundation acceptance strictly mandates affirmative approval votes from both the Technical Committee (TC) and the Governing Board (GB), followed by Linux Foundation countersignature.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1] Projects may not represent themselves as donated or contributed until all gates are finalized.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08**: Standardized repository intake templates and Contribution Agreement sequencing formalized across TC and GB governance channels.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards, delegation models, and cross-organizational trust architectures for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group (I&T) is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with identifying and developing vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and architectural viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]. Its mandate addresses systemic challenges introduced by autonomous agents operating across organizational boundaries, including proving provenance, managing multi-hop delegation chains, establishing trust, and verifying human-in-the-loop authorization evidence [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

The working group operates under the technical governance of the AAIF Technical Committee and coordinates closely with sister groups including [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Leadership
The working group leadership was appointed by the Platinum and Gold members of the working group for the inaugural term spanning March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]:
- **Chair**: Grant Miller (IBM)
- **Co-Chair**: Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE)

Working group meetings occur weekly on Thursdays, alternating between 6:30 AM and 9:00 AM Pacific Time via Linux Foundation (LFX) infrastructure [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3].

## Breakout Structure and Workstreams
The working group organizes its technical agenda into three distinct breakout workstreams designed to iterate on concrete specifications and architectural requirements [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]:
- **Use Cases**: Coordinated by Wei Chen; focuses on grounding identity and trust requirements in concrete enterprise and consumer operational scenarios.
- **Reference Architecture**: Coordinated by Brian Malone; articulates actor models, functional components, trust domain boundaries, and interoperability gaps required for delegated agent authority.
- **Taxonomy Coordination**: Led by liaisons Julianna Mealin and Leonardo Galesky; aligns identity, consent, and attestation terminology directly with the [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) cross-working-group workstream.

## Reference Work and Foundational Architectures
The group actively evaluates existing protocol efforts and reference designs to distinguish established foundations from unresolved agentic gaps [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]:
- [Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD)](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md), addressing discovery, metadata verification, and admission across federated registries.
- Workload identity standards such as SPIFFE/SPIRE evaluating the boundaries between static workload attestation and dynamic, human-delegated agent authority.
- Enterprise actor-chain patterns, token-exchange mechanisms, and workload attestation architectures.
- Tiered runtime defense models such as the NVIDIA Secure Agent Workspace reference architecture.
- Emerging standards track proposals, including the IETF AI Agent Authentication and Authorization Internet-Draft.

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-03-01**: Working group chair terms officially commence for Grant Miller and Alper Dedeoğlu [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3].
- **2026-03**: Published onboarding guide formalizing breakout workstreams across Use Cases, Reference Architecture, and Taxonomy Coordination [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

proposed_concept.title: Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual identity rules, typography tokens, dual surface palettes, component styling, and agent motif constraints across AAIF properties.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Brand Guidelines establish the visual identity, typography system, surface color models, and graphical asset usage rules across all Agentic AI Foundation digital interfaces, audit reports, presentation decks, and generated media [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. All generated outputs—ranging from Slack audit PDFs to community HTML reports—strictly follow the centralized design system source of truth maintained at `design/aaif-design-system.html` and its extracted token pipeline [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

# Architecture / Specification

## Single Source of Truth and Asset Pipeline
The design system enforces a single-seam update process to prevent styling drift across repository assets and reporting engines [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]:
- `design/aaif-design-system.html`: Canonical self-extracting design system bundle housing tokens, component definitions, the agent motif, and layout blueprints.
- `design/aaif-tokens.css`: Automatically extracted CSS `:root` token block prepended to generated reports. Hand-editing this file is prohibited.
- `scripts/extract_design_tokens.py`: Token extractor script whose `--check` flag enforces build-time synchronization in continuous integration.
- `assets/fonts/`: Houses Instrument Sans (SIL Open Font License), the foundation's sole typeface.
- Canonical Mark SVGs: `assets/aaif-mark.svg` (full lockup in black), `assets/aaif-mark-square.svg` (isolated square mark for headers and favicons), and `assets/aaif-logo-white.svg` (full lockup for black plates).

## Core Design Principles and Rules

### Color Palette and Accent Mechanics
- **Primary Accent is Black**: Defined as `--accent: var(--ink)`. Primary interactive actions are black, not vibrant colors [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Spectrum Accents**: Ten spectrum hues (`--spec-1` through `--spec-10`) serve as accents within individual surfaces, with exactly one hue leading at a time. Coral corresponds to `--spec-8` and must not be treated as the global primary brand color [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Surface Roles**: Ground pages use `--paper`. Tinted panels use `--paper-3`. The warm off-white token (`--paper-2`) is restricted to occasional section banding and must never serve as a default background [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

### Typography
- **Single Typeface**: Instrument Sans across 400, 500, 600, and 700 weights is used exclusively for both UI and display contexts [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Monospace Usage**: Monospace is reserved strictly for system metadata, code identifiers, and structural eyebrows—never for body prose [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Heading Styles**: Major headings are weight 500, with letter-spacing tracking `-0.02em` and line-height 1.05–1.15. Only minor headings (h5/h6) utilize weight 600 [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

### Flat Surface and Corner Treatment
- **Flat Layout**: Drop shadows are explicitly disallowed. Dimensional depth is created solely through 1px hairlines, surface tinting, and inset strokes [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Corner Radii**: Cards, tables, stats, and chips enforce square corners (`border-radius: 0`). Rounded corners (`--radius-pill`) are strictly reserved for genuine pills, buttons, and numeric badges [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

### Dual Surfaces Without Dark Mode
- **No Inverted Dark Mode**: The design system defines two intentional first-class surfaces: white editorial and black plate. There is no automated `prefers-color-scheme` dark mode block [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- Reports remain white editorial pages by default, utilizing black plates only for designated closing bands carrying distinct light-on-dark tokens [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

### Agent Motif Usage Constraints
- The **Agent Motif** (the graphical bot constructed from the mark's geometric primitives) is permitted only for empty states, loading sequences, event graphics, and graphical dividers [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- The agent motif is strictly forbidden in governance documents, board communications, press releases, and formal audit reports [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- Redrawing the AAIF mark from memory or screenshots is prohibited; official SVGs must be embedded directly with fill color modifications only [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-03**: Canonical design system specification formalized in community events repository, defining CI token extraction seams, dual-surface constraints, and agent motif governance [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation framework capturing causal agent execution, tool invocations, approval states, and upstream OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry framework and causal execution specification developed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group to track agent decision cycles, tool dispatches, and human approval gates[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]. It correlates distributed runtime spans across multi-turn interactions, bridging asynchronous infrastructure with standardized language model and tool telemetry.

The framework pairs runtime instrumentation prototypes with formal feedback channels into upstream telemetry standards such as OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions and AAIF vocabulary registries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].

# Architecture / Specification
Task 9 of the trace model execution plan standardizes the translation of AAIF empirical trace findings into external and cross-WG specifications[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]:

- **Upstream OpenTelemetry GenAI Conventions**: Submitting semantic convention enhancements and telemetry guidance to the OpenTelemetry GenAI repository, addressing gaps such as consistent turn-entry span identification[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].
- **Runtime Instrumentation Remediation**: Contributing instrumentation fixes directly to agent execution runtimes where critical identifiers (such as conversation or session keys) are tracked internally but omitted from emitted spans[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].
- **Cross-WG Vocabulary Harmonization**: Mapping trace schema attributes and event identifiers to the shared definitions maintained by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].
- **Dependency Sequencing**: Coordinating upstream proposals across prior trace evaluation milestones, including baseline instrumentation reviews and edge-case testing tasks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].

# Lifecycle History
Developed following August 2026 Observability and Traceability Working Group planning sessions as part of a formal nine-task execution plan[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]. Issue #47 formalizes Task 9 to systematically submit trace model findings, migration guidance, and semantic conventions upstream[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering secrets management, cross-cloud workload identity federation, secure tool invocation, guardrails, and blast-radius evaluation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide outlines baseline defensive controls, architectural guardrails, and identity patterns for production AI agent systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]. Maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), it establishes prescriptive constraints for credential isolation, runtime least-privilege, and tool authorization.

While baseline guidance specifies short-lived single-cloud workload identity tokens (e.g., 1-hour cloud default bounds), deployment patterns increasingly require federated workload identity controls for hybrid environments and multi-cloud agent execution paths[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].

# Architecture / Specification
Key operational domains defined within the guideline include:

- **Workload Identity and Federation**: Expanding baseline single-cloud IAM role constraints into multi-cloud and on-premises environments, recommending OpenID Connect (OIDC)-based federation patterns and managed trust relationships to avoid static credential fallback[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].
- **Cross-Cloud Role Assumption**: Enforcing strict least-privilege scoping and auditable boundary transitions when an autonomous agent running in one infrastructure provider accesses resources hosted across external IAM boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].
- **Token Lifetimes and Rotation**: Evaluating whether standard 1-hour token lifetimes provide sufficient blast-radius containment for autonomous agents or require reduced expirations in cross-domain delegating paths[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].
- **Blast Radius Evaluation**: Analyzing cumulative risk when identity chains span multiple cloud providers and hybrid infrastructure, preventing cross-domain privilege escalation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].
- **Secrets Management and Redaction**: Strict isolation of private keys, execution credentials, and sensitive payload tokens from runtime memory logs and telemetry pipelines[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].

# Lifecycle History
During ongoing reviews of the guidance, Issue #23 identified multi-cloud and hybrid workload identity as an active collaboration area between the Security and Privacy Working Group and the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Inventory
proposed_concept.description: Production workflow catalog categorizing real-world agent deployments into structured coordination archetypes, execution patterns, and verified citations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Inventory is an empirical catalog maintained by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) that collects and analyzes real-world deployments of agentic workflows[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]. Each entry is mapped against the schema defined in `schema-agentic-use-cases.md`, documenting execution structures, coordination models, and autonomy levels across industry sectors[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-48].

The catalog relies on verifiable, public vendor documentation describing operational architectures rather than marketing claims, ensuring reproducible pattern categorization[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].

# Architecture / Specification
The inventory classifies entries using standardized workflow dimensions and strict citation scrutiny[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]:

- **Verified Execution Classifications**: Concrete patterns are verified against technical writeups, including sequential pipelines (e.g., Clay waterfall enrichment), parallel fan-out multi-agent structures with AI planning (e.g., PagerDuty SRE agent), and AI-coordinated review workflows (e.g., LexisNexis Protege)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].
- **Unspecified and Grounded Boundaries**: Where vendor sources fail to describe concrete execution order or deterministic convergence mechanisms (such as incident post-mortem drafting or tax tracking), cells remain designated as `Unspecified: insufficient source detail` to preserve evidentiary integrity[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].
- **Schema Conformance**: All inventory rows link directly to the formal use case classification schema (`schema-agentic-use-cases.md`), aligning taxonomy terms such as single-agent vs. multi-agent coordination with broader AAIF [workflow primitives](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-48].

# Lifecycle History
Developed by the Workflows and Process Integration WG. PR #39 resolved initial unspecified cells with technical citations, audited link validity across vendors, and reverted claims lacking architectural proof[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]. PR #48 corrected internal links pointing to `schema-agentic-use-cases.md` across the inventory[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-48].

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing agent telemetry, causal execution traces, protocol boundary metrics, context propagation, and identity correlation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group develops open standards, semantic conventions, and reference architectures for instrumenting agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50]. Its charter spans distributed tracing across autonomous decision loops, protocol metrics at model and tool boundaries, and context propagation over asynchronous runtimes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].

The working group collaborates with upstream bodies such as OpenTelemetry and the W3C, as well as peer AAIF groups including [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].

# Architecture / Specification
Core technical workstreams under development include:

- **Agent Identity Telemetry and Propagation**: Developing semantic conventions and implementation patterns to propagate, correlate, and record agent identity across distributed traces, metrics, and structured logs (evaluating specifications such as aauth.dev and OpenID COAZ-MCP bindings)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].
- **Baggage and Boundary Traversal**: Utilizing W3C Baggage and OpenTelemetry Context Propagation protocols to ensure agent identity attributes (`agent.id`, `agent.role`, `agent.invocation_id`, `agent.principal.type`, `agent.delegation_depth`) survive non-HTTP boundaries, job queues, tool execution sandboxes, and streaming completions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].
- **High-Cardinality and Sampling Safeguards**: Conducting cardinality assessments to prevent high-frequency agent tool calls and subagent spawning from generating unsustainable telemetry storage costs[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].
- **Telemetry Sanitization and Boundary Policies**: Defining redlines prohibiting raw authentication tokens, private keys, message signatures, or user-identifiable payloads from leaking into spans or Application Performance Monitoring (APM) backends[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].
- **Causal Lineage Modeling**: Delivering reference trace architectures documenting causal lineage and identity preservation across the request path: `User Request -> Orchestrator Agent -> Sub-Agent -> Downstream Tool/Resource`[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].

# Lifecycle History
Chartered under the AAIF technical community. In addition to executing the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) tasks, the group opened Issue #50 to address agent identity propagation and observability impact across distributed systems in coordination with security and identity stakeholders[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50].

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation overseeing technical vision, standards, project progression, and working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) is the primary technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), responsible for steering technical vision, supervising technical standards, stewarding working groups, and evaluating project lifecycle transitions[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]. Formally established by the AAIF Governing Board, the TC manages technical intake and ensures alignment across foundation initiatives and cross-cutting workstreams[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092].

# Architecture / Specification

## Committee Membership
The inaugural TC membership was appointed directly by the AAIF Governing Board for a term running from March 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]:
- **David Soria Parra** (Anthropic) – TC Chair
- **Caitie McCaffrey** (Microsoft) – TC Co-Chair
- **Alan Blount** (Google)
- **Bradley Axen** (Block)
- **James Ward** (Amazon Web Services)
- **Nick Cooper** (OpenAI)
- **Sambhav Kothari** (Bloomberg)
- **Steve Faulkner** (Cloudflare)

## Supervised Impact Projects
The Technical Committee oversees the lifecycle and governance of core foundation technical assets, including projects accepted directly into the Impact Stage[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]:
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**: An open protocol enabling seamless integration between language model applications and external data sources or tools.
- **Goose**: An extensible open-source AI agent runtime designed for general-purpose tool execution, editing, and automated testing across foundation models (see [Goose Reference Architecture](../resources/goose.md)).
- **AGENTS.MD**: Standardized repository instruction and context conventions for AI agent development environments.

## Governance and Operational Scope
Under its operational rules, the TC manages project advancement across the tiers specified in the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) and enforces operational reporting standards defined in the [Working Group Submission Guidelines](../guidelines/working-group-submission-guidelines.md). The TC also adjudicates cross-cutting terminology disputes submitted through the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).

# Lifecycle History
The Technical Committee was chartered at the inception of the AAIF with founding members appointed by the Governing Board for the initial 2026 term[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation framework capturing causal agent execution, tool invocations, approval states, and turn relationships across OpenTelemetry spans.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and causal correlation framework developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to standardize representation of agent execution, multi-turn sessions, proposed actions, and external interactions across distributed systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41]. It provides a semantic contract mapping high-level agent lifecycle events to OpenTelemetry (OTel) spans, logs, and metrics[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Relationship Contract
The specification defines a formal identity and relationship model establishing how agent operational entities correlate across trace spans[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41]:
- **Conversations and Sessions**: Long-lived parent scopes that encapsulate multiple turns; sequential turns within a conversation may carry distinct trace IDs while remaining causally bound to the session identifier[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].
- **Turns and Calls**: Discrete conversational and algorithmic interactions, supporting standalone turn traces that preserve contextual caller links[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].
- **Proposed Actions**: Explicit declarations of an agent's intent to execute a tool, command, or state mutation. Proposed actions maintain stable identifiers so downstream gates or approvals can reference them even if execution is denied or aborted before span emission[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].
- **Observations and Resumptions**: Structured capture of environmental feedback, tool responses, and approval gate resumptions, including explicit handling for incomplete observations and missing target endpoints[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

## OpenTelemetry Semantic Crosswalk
The trace model maintains an alignment crosswalk with OTel GenAI semantic conventions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41]:
- Maps AAIF agent primitives (such as [approval checkpoints](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) and [proposal-execution splits](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)) to standardized span attributes.
- Defines state propagation semantics across [durable wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md) states where agent execution suspends pending asynchronous authorization or external tool responses[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

# Lifecycle History
Initiated by the Observability and Traceability Working Group, the model progressed following working group reviews in August 2026 into a formal nine-task execution plan, with Task 3 establishing the versioned relationship contract and OpenTelemetry crosswalk[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].
