proposed_concept.title: Reference Architecture Contribution Guide
proposed_concept.description: Authoring standards, taxonomy rules, and contribution criteria distinguishing patterns, reference architectures, scenarios, and decision records.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Reference Architecture Contribution Guide defines the formal standards and intake criteria for authoring workflow patterns, reference architectures, and scenario evaluations within the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4]. It ensures vendor-neutral framing, establishes a strict distinction between atomic patterns and composed practitioner jobs, and governs the incorporation of empirical use-case validation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].

# Architecture / Specification

## Contribution Taxonomy
Contributors must classify proposals into one of five structural document types based on architectural scope[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4]:
- **Pattern**: A self-contained, context-free solution to a recurring workflow sub-problem that can be adopted independently (such as [durable waits](../patterns/durable-wait.md) or [human approval gates](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)). Patterns define mandatory invariants and concrete failure modes[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Reference Architecture**: A reusable composite architecture for a complete practitioner job (answering the sentence: *"We are building a ___"*). It composes multiple patterns, capability roles, system boundaries, operational guarantees, and exit states (such as [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md))[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Scenario**: A worked example or test case embedded in an architecture's validation sections to verify coverage against real-world systems[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Decision Note**: An architectural record capturing rationale, alternatives, and consequences for structural choices (using the [Reference Architecture Decision Template](../guidelines/reference-architecture-decision-template.md))[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Document / Research**: Background surveys, comparisons, and exploratory research informing architectures without defining normative requirements[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].

## Core Authoring Rules
All submissions must adhere to foundational quality and governance constraints[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4]:
- **Vendor Neutrality**: Logical capabilities and behavioral requirements must be specified prior to referencing commercial or open-source software implementations[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Evidence vs. Interpretation**: Authors must separate empirical implementation facts from proposed working-group interpretations, recording genuine gaps as explicit open questions[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Boundary Respect**: Cross-cutting requirements owned by adjacent working groups (such as identity or telemetry standards) must be scoped out rather than redefined locally[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Domain Decoupling**: Generic reference architectures must not adopt domain-specific naming unless the practitioner job itself is inherently domain-locked[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].

# Lifecycle History
Adopted by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group to maintain structural consistency and prevent terminology drift across reference architecture workstreams[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].

mutations.rationale: Document the structural classification ambiguity between parallel fan-out (timing-based) and sequential pipelines (dependency-based) that stalled use case inventory categorizations.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Inventory
proposed_concept.description: Production workflow catalog categorizing real-world agent deployments into structured coordination and execution archetypes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Inventory is an empirical catalog maintained by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) compiling production agent implementations across industries[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]. It serves as the baseline evaluation corpus for identifying recurring agentic workflow archetypes, stress-testing reference architectures, and classifying runtime coordination patterns[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].

# Architecture / Specification

## Classification Schema and Open Questions
The inventory evaluates production agent workflows along structural execution axes, mapping implementations to patterns such as [parallel fan-out and join](../patterns/parallel-fan-out-and-join.md) and sequential execution pipelines[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].

A recurring classification tension emerged around the boundary between parallel fan-out and sequential pipelines, leaving 20 of 24 unclassified workflow rows unresolved[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]:
- **Timing vs. Dependency Definitions**: `Parallel fan-out` is conventionally characterized by execution timing (concurrent sub-tasks), whereas `Sequential pipeline` is defined by data and task dependencies (dependent activities, each feeding the next)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]. Because timing and dependency are not mutually exclusive opposites, individual workflows often exhibit characteristics of both or neither[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].
- **Classification Perspectives**: The working group identified three competing analytical lenses to resolve the ambiguity[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]:
  1. *Observed timing*: Classifying strictly by whether tasks execute concurrently at runtime.
  2. *Agent count*: Classifying based on single-agent vs. multi-agent topology.
  3. *Data dependency*: Classifying by input-output coupling regardless of scheduling concurrency.
- **Scope Ambiguity**: Final resolution depends on whether schema classifications describe a specific company's runtime deployment choices or the inherent logical structure of the underlying use case[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].

# Lifecycle History
Maintained as an active working document by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group, the inventory was flagged with open classification questions in late 2026 to resolve structural criteria before finalizing workflow archetype assignments[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate operational rules and evidentiary standards for evaluating reference architecture fit against real use cases.

proposed_concept.title: Reference Architecture Use Case Validation Guide
proposed_concept.description: Evaluation procedure and boundary checklist for validating reference architectures against real-world use cases from the inventory.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Reference Architecture Use Case Validation Guide defines the standardized process for determining whether an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) reference architecture fits a specific real-world use case[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]. Validation establishes architectural alignment with the use case's core operational job and defining boundaries, rather than certifying that an existing implementation adheres to every specific implementation control[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

The framework serves both human contributors and automated coding agents, allowing evaluations to be submitted directly as GitHub issues or pull requests to the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope of Architectural Validation
Validation asks whether a real use case exhibits the job and boundary conditions that a reference architecture is designed to govern[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]:
- **Fit vs. Implementation:** A `Validated` classification indicates that the reference architecture provides the architectural controls required to safely implement the use case. It does not require proof that an existing system already deploys specific controls such as cryptographic version hashes, credentials, retry limits, or idempotency keys[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
- **Permissible Assumptions:** When the primary use case source demonstrates the core job and primary boundary, it is classified as `Validated` without demanding exhaustive documentation of low-level implementation details[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

## Evidentiary Standards
- **Inventory Sourcing:** Evidence must be grounded in facts stated in the [Agentic Use Case Inventory](../resources/agentic-use-case-inventory.md) or its cited sources[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]. Illustrative examples embedded within reference architectures do not constitute independent validation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
- **Classification Fields:** Metadata tags such as approval gates, exception escalations, and workflow pattern designations serve as valid architectural evidence unless marked with an undocumented-rationale indicator, in which case the rationale is treated as `Unknown`[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

## Validation Procedure
1. **Analyze Reference Architecture:** Review purpose, "Is this your architecture?" checklist criteria, boundary constraints, guarantees, and exit states[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
2. **Comparative Mapping:** Evaluate actor allocations (agent, workflow engine, human participant, external system), boundary enforcement, and failure/wait/recovery handoff paths against the target use case[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
3. **Formulate Checks:** Construct two to three concise checks focused strictly on the defining job and boundary. Each check must declare the explicit architectural consequence of a `Yes`, `No`, or `Unknown` result[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
4. **Draft Findings:** Summarize matches and unknowns in plain language, limiting each section to a maximum of two bullet points[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

# Lifecycle History
The guide was established by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) under the Reference Architectures workstream to lower contributor friction while maintaining rigorous boundaries between architectural fit and implementation compliance[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture governing iterative, autonomous problem resolution within predefined task boundaries and independent acceptance gates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Bounded Autonomous Remediation is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) reference architecture governing iterative, autonomous problem resolution within declared task scopes, execution budgets, and independent acceptance verification[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]. It serves as a contrasting counterpart to [Single-Agent Human Approval](single-agent-human-approval.md) by allowing autonomous iteration when independent deterministic evidence exists, while preventing unbounded autonomy or uncontrolled side effects[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

The architecture applies to bounded tasks with low-impact or reversible side effects—such as generating remediation pull requests, reconciling data batches, or repairing draft records—where non-convergence safely escalates to human-managed workflows[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

# Architecture / Specification

## Architectural Guarantees
The architecture enforces four structural guarantees across execution[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]:
1. **Bounded Autonomy:** Agents receive only the scoped task contract, tools, data access, credentials, time, and computational budget declared for a single execution run[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
2. **Independent Acceptance:** A [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md)—never the agent itself—determines whether a candidate result fulfills the required acceptance criteria[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
3. **Controlled Effect:** Execution is routed through a [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and constrained effect executor, ensuring only exact, accepted, scope-valid results produce external effects[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
4. **Safe Non-Convergence:** Budget exhaustion, repeated failure, scope violations, or ambiguous verification evidence trigger explicit recorded terminal states and safe escalation to human oversight[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

## Pattern Composition
The architecture composes three core patterns:
- [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md): Iterates the agent's remediation attempts within strict budget, step, and time fences[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md): Evaluates candidate outputs using unified multi-criteria checks (where all criteria must evaluate to pass) rather than disjointed multi-gate stages[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].
- [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md): Isolates the candidate generation space from external authoritative systems[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

## Structural Components
- **Execution Engine:** Coordinates admission, sequencing, retry handling, and terminal stop states[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- **Bounded Agent Environment:** Restricts model reasoning and tool invocations to allowed interpretations and operations[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- **Isolated Work Area:** Confines intermediate edits and candidate artifacts prior to acceptance[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- **Acceptance Gate:** Executes contract, schema, test, or policy evaluations[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- **Constrained Effect Executor:** Applies approved modifications to target systems using scoped, least-privilege credentials[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

# Lifecycle History
Authored within the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md). PR #37 updated the specification to replace tiered "small gate / big gate" terminology with a unified acceptance gate evaluating combined criteria, while recording formal validation of the autonomous maintenance run ("night shift") scenario[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing agentic terminology across working groups through designated Domain Editors.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-working-group governance body within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with harmonizing agentic terminology, resolving definition overlaps, and maintaining a common taxonomy across foundation initiatives[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]. Unlike standalone working groups, the workstream operates as a horizontal coordination layer relying on nominated Domain Editors from each working group[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

The workstream focuses strictly on shared taxonomy development; contribution processes for the ecosystem landscape remain under definition, and landscape pull requests are paused pending formal committee approval[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

# Architecture / Specification

## Organizational Structure and Domain Editors
Each AAIF Working Group nominates Domain Editors to coordinate domain-specific vocabulary and participate in cross-group consensus[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]:
- [Accuracy & Reliability](accuracy-and-reliability.md): Casper Nielsen, Matthew Khouzam[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Agentic Commerce](agentic-commerce.md): Leonardo Galesky[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md): Amithash Kankanallu Jagadish[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Identity & Trust](identity-and-trust.md): Julianna Mealin[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Observability & Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md): Pavan Sudheendra, Matt Lee[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Security & Privacy](security-and-privacy.md): Jautau White, Katherine Druckman[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]
- [Workflows & Process Integration](workflows-and-process-integration.md): Sumanth Sathyanarayana[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]

## Terminology Lifecycle
Candidate terms progress through a five-stage intake and validation pipeline[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]:
1. **Identification:** Working groups identify candidate terms, articulating why the term matters to agentic AI, how it differs from existing technical usage, and which groups are affected[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]. Terms relevant across three or more working groups are designated as "Universal"[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
2. **Spreadsheet Logging:** Terms are logged into the central Taxonomy Working Spreadsheet, preserving an immutable decision audit trail[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
3. **Qualification Triage:** Candidate terms receive one of three governance statuses:
   - `Debate`: Active discussion and scoping required[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
   - `Keep`: Term qualifies as uniquely agentic or materially altered in an agentic context, moving to definition authoring[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
   - `Cull`: Term is rejected as an established generic term (e.g., standard red-teaming), with the logged rationale retained[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
4. **Socialization:** Domain Editors draft definitions and circulate them across affected working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].
5. **PR Submission:** Finalized SKOS-Lite taxonomy terms are submitted via pull request to the central repository[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

# Lifecycle History
The workstream was chartered under the Technical Committee as an operational cross-working-group mechanism. In September 2026, the roster was formalized, and contributions to the Landscape track were restricted until formal submission criteria are approved[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

mutations.rationale: Update the Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream concept with verified operational scope constraints, leadership details, SKOS-Lite taxonomy schema rules, and review guardrails from merged documentation.

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing agentic terminology across working groups through designated domain editors, SKOS-Lite schemas, and an ecosystem market map.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream serves as the horizontal architectural bridge across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), curating a pre-competitive shared vocabulary of agentic AI concepts and an ecosystem market map [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream coordinates nominated delegates known as Domain Editors across all vertical AAIF working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

Under current operating policy, active contribution is strictly limited to the shared Taxonomy [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713]. The broader Ecosystem Landscape catalog remains on the roadmap pending governance approval of its intake and evaluation process; pull requests altering landscape files are currently rejected [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

# Architecture / Specification

### The Horizontal Index Principle
To preserve domain sovereignty across specialized working groups, the workstream functions under an index-versus-payload model [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]:
- **Shared Index (In-Scope):** Harmonization of foundational cross-cutting terms intersecting two or more working groups, canonical aliasing, and paired contrast relationships [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Domain Payload (Out-of-Scope):** Detailed whitepapers, internal protocol parameters, and specialized implementation wire formats, which remain under the exclusive jurisdiction of the owning technical working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

### SKOS-Lite Data Schema (`taxonomy-data.js`)
Taxonomy records in `taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js` adhere to a structured schema modeling SKOS concepts [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97]:
- `term` (String, required): Display term formatted in sentence case [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `category` (String, deferred): Primary bucket (e.g., `Agentic Threats`, `Identity & Authorization`), currently left blank as `""` during initial intake to avoid premature taxonomical rigidity [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `aliases` (Array of Strings, required): Synonyms, alternative spellings, or historical terms [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `broaderTerm` (String or null, deferred): Parent concept in the SKOS hierarchy, temporarily defaulted to `null` while cross-group scope boundaries settle [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `definition` (String, deferred): Pre-competitive definition; during initial intake, placeholder text `Definition pending — term accepted; definition under working group discussion.` is mandated [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `scopeNote` (String, optional): Contextual notes, review timestamps, and boundary clarifications [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `relatedTerms` (Array of Strings, optional): Associative linkages corresponding to `skos:related` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `contrastsWith` (Array of Strings, optional): Explicit links to adjacent counterpart concepts [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `workgroups` (Array of Strings, required): List of owning or interested vertical working groups; the entry `"Universal"` is explicitly disallowed [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].

### Disambiguation & Editorial Guardrails
- **Paired Contrast Disambiguation:** Counterpart concepts that derive meaning through opposition (e.g., Tool vs. Skill) must be maintained as distinct entries rather than collapsed into single records, with explicit relational cross-links defined in `relatedTerms` or `contrastsWith` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Anti-Erasure Rule:** No term may be removed or folded into another term's aliases without explicit written sign-off from the owning group's Domain Editor [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

# Lifecycle History

The workstream meets weekly on Mondays [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. On 2026-07-27, the workstream formally agreed to admit terms ahead of final definitions and categories, deferring the `category`, `broaderTerm`, and `definition` fields during initial check-in to accelerate intake without triggering premature boundary disputes [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Procedural operations pipeline and runtime infrastructure managing chapter provisioning, credentials, multi-identity resolution, and channel lifecycle across AAIF estates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Community Event Operations encompasses the tooling and operational scripts that provision, audit, and reconcile chapter infrastructure across Google Drive, Slack, and intake forms for the AAIF community network [^evt-community-events-pr-44].

The operations architecture maintains explicit separation between intake email addresses, Slack account identities, and Google Drive access control lists, ensuring that administrative actions resolve durable identifiers rather than mutable handles [^evt-community-events-pr-44].

# Architecture / Specification

### Tripartite Identity Resolution
To prevent misattributed permissions and false missing-account alarms, intake records track three distinct identity columns on the backing `Form Responses` sheet [^evt-community-events-pr-44]:
1. `Slack ID`: The immutable, durable Slack identifier (`U...`) resolved by `resolve_slack_ids.py` [^evt-community-events-pr-44].
2. `Slack Email`: The email address registered to the Slack account, populated via email lookup [^evt-community-events-pr-44].
3. `Drive Email`: The address carrying verified permissions on the chapter's Google Drive folder, populated by `track_drive_email.py` (using `(no grant)` as an explicit sentinel rather than an empty string) [^evt-community-events-pr-44].

Neither column overwrites the intake `Email` submitted by the organizer, preserving the original applicant input as the primary audit anchor [^evt-community-events-pr-44].

### Lookup Canonicalization and Guardrails
- **Consumer Gmail Folding:** When resolving Slack accounts via `users.lookupByEmail`, dot and plus-tag normalization is applied strictly to consumer `gmail.com` and `googlemail.com` addresses [^evt-community-events-pr-44]. Workspace domains treat dots as significant and are never folded to avoid cross-account identity collisions [^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- **Automatic vs. Suggested Writes:** Automated writing via `--write` is restricted strictly to email lookup matches. Name-based matches are surfaced only as suggestions requiring human confirmation via `--apply` [^evt-community-events-pr-44]. Suggestions match solely against `real_name` attributes, deliberately omitting `@handle` to prevent accidental homograph collisions [^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- **Loop Context Isolation:** Address cleaning functions enforce truthiness and handle whitespace strings explicitly to avoid leaking loop payload state across consecutive spreadsheet rows [^evt-community-events-pr-44].

### Channel Provisioning and Renames
Channel provisioning and renaming workflows (e.g., standardizing country room nomenclature in `provision_channels.py`) are enforced declaratively through mapped registries (`CHANNEL_RENAMES`) requiring explicit authorization flags (`--write --i-have-approval`) [^evt-community-events-pr-43]. Administrative methods that delete chat history (such as `chat.delete`) are deliberately excluded from automated runner permissions to maintain immutable audit trails [^evt-community-events-pr-43].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Procedural operations pipeline and runtime infrastructure managing chapter provisioning, credentials, Slack routing, chapter CRMs, badges, and OOXML brand conformance across the AAIF community estate.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Community Event Operations skill governs the procedural scripts, validation pipelines, and synchronization workflows that maintain the foundation's global chapter network across Google Workspace, Slack, and event platforms. It enforces strict separation between central infrastructure configuration and local chapter autonomy, automating tasks including chapter room provisioning, CRM pipeline synchronization, country-level Slack directory management, and asset branding.

Recent operational hardening addresses synchronization gaps across Slack provisioning, CRM data hygiene, and document rendering pipelines, ensuring strict security boundaries and idempotent operations across more than 80 global chapters [^evt-community-events-pr-42] [^evt-community-events-pr-28].

# Architecture / Specification

### Slack Channel Provisioning and Operational Seeding
Chapter Slack channels are provisioned via `provision_channels.py`, distinguishing public city and country channels from private organizer rooms [^evt-community-events-pr-42].
- **Ops Account Seeding:** Organizer channels are automatically seeded with operations staff email addresses defined on the `Slack Config` sheet, resolved dynamically through `users.lookupByEmail` rather than mutable `@handle` identifiers [^evt-community-events-pr-42]. Real addresses are excluded from public repositories, and invitations are bounded by domain allowlists and token-owner exclusions.
- **Asset Link Pinning:** Chapter Drive folder links are posted exclusively within private organizer rooms to prevent member access requests for restricted budgets and CRM trackers [^evt-community-events-pr-42]. Drive links are reconstructed from validated folder identifiers rather than raw sheet text to eliminate URL anchor injection vulnerabilities. Channel history is unconditionally inspected to ensure message idempotency independent of pin states [^evt-community-events-pr-42].
- **Scope Boundaries:** Core provisioning requires `channels:write`, `groups:write`, and `chat:write`. Extended operations degrade gracefully when optional scopes (`pins:read`, `pins:write`, `*:history`) are missing. The `pins.add` method is allowlisted, while `pins.remove` is intentionally omitted to preserve human administrative priority [^evt-community-events-pr-42].
- **Country Channel Integration:** `invite_organizers.py` supports targeted scopes (`--scope {organizer,country,both}`), deduplicating rosters by resolved account across chapters sharing a country channel [^evt-community-events-pr-36]. `post_country_directory.py` publishes additive chapter directories without invoking `chat.update` or modifying existing human wording [^evt-community-events-pr-36].

### Chapter CRM Schema and Role Split
Chapter attendee spreadsheets adhere to an enforced schema split separating applicant intent from triage decisions [^evt-community-events-pr-28]:
- **Decision (`Status` Column):** Records pipeline triage state (`Prospect`, `In progress`, `Interviewing`, `Tentative`, `Accepted`, `Attended`, `Regular`, `Volunteer`, `Declined`). Pre-defined differential formatting (`dxfId`) styles apply status color indicators (green, amber, red) without altering empty template rows [^evt-community-events-pr-28].
- **Application (`Interested in` Column L):** Captures applied roles (`Organizer`, `Speaker`, `Host`, slash-delimited), ensuring applicant interest remains preserved regardless of central triage status [^evt-community-events-pr-28].
- **Detail Field Population:** Populates `LinkedIn URL`, `Company`, `Role / title`, and `Technical expertise` directly into chapter CRMs now that chapter folder permissions are restricted to verified local organizers [^evt-community-events-pr-28].
- **Migration Guard:** The `sync_crm` tool verifies dropdown schema drift and halts when encountering pre-split 11-column layouts [^evt-community-events-pr-28].

### Badge Asset Architecture
Chapter badge assets are organized into isolated per-chapter `Badges/` subfolders within each chapter's Drive hierarchy alongside `Icons/` and event templates [^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- **Dual Badge Generation:** Chapters maintain both the legacy orange badge and the AAIF design-system badge [^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- **Design System Mascot:** `make_agent_badge.py` generates vector assets combining Instrument Sans typography, brand tokens, and deterministic chapter mascot art (`agent_art.chapter_scene()`), rendered through headless Chrome [^evt-community-events-pr-39]. All chapter display names are XML-escaped to defend against SVG injection [^evt-community-events-pr-39].

### OOXML Design Conformance and Font Policy
Office documents (`.pptx`, `.docx`, `.xlsx`) conform to foundational brand tokens through `lib/aaif_events/ooxml_style.py` [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Minimal-Diff Rewriting:** XML alterations touch only color values and typeface names, preserving `mc:AlternateContent` fallback structures and relationship mappings [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Contrast Resolution:** `contrast.py` resolves nested fill hierarchies (shape fill to slide background to master slide) to eliminate low-contrast token pairings [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Font Embedding Policy (`ox.NEVER_EMBED`):** Instrument Sans and JetBrains Mono are declared in OOXML metadata but never embedded, reducing `.docx` file sizes by ~210KB per tracker while leveraging native Google Docs font availability [^evt-community-events-pr-34]. Embedded Manrope remains solely as a metric fallback for offline Microsoft Word rendering [^evt-community-events-pr-34].

# Lifecycle History

- **PR #28 (Merged):** Refactored chapter CRM schemas to separate applicant interest from triage status and enabled detail profile synchronization [^evt-community-events-pr-28].
- **PR #32 (Merged):** Conformed OOXML estate (presentations, trackers, workbooks) to AAIF design tokens with automated contrast checking [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **PR #34 (Merged):** Established font unembedding rule (`NEVER_EMBED`), pruning redundant font payloads across estate trackers [^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- **PR #36 (Merged):** Introduced country channel directory publishing and organizer invitations with Slack audit segregation [^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- **PR #39 (Merged):** Restructured chapter badge storage into local `Badges/` folders and introduced headless Chrome rendering for agent mascot badges [^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- **PR #42 (Merged):** Added operational account seeding and secure Drive folder link pinning to organizer channel provisioning [^evt-community-events-pr-42].

proposed_concept.title: Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual identity rules, typography tokens, dual surface palettes, component styling, agent motif, OOXML brand conformance, and font embedding constraints for the Agentic AI Foundation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Brand Guidelines define the visual identity, typography system, digital design tokens, and document styling rules across all Agentic AI Foundation surfaces. The system provides unified styling across web interfaces, generated marketing collateral, and desktop office artifacts (presentations, spreadsheets, and word documents), enforcing consistent brand expression across human and automated agent touchpoints [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

The brand integrates programmatic tokens (`design/aaif-tokens.css`), deterministic agent mascot illustrations, strict contrast validation, and efficient font embedding rules for cloud-hosted productivity suites [^evt-community-events-pr-39] [^evt-community-events-pr-34].

# Architecture / Specification

### Typography and Font Embedding Architecture
Typography is structured around clear functional roles [^evt-community-events-pr-32] [^evt-community-events-pr-34]:
- **Display and Body Typeface:** Instrument Sans serves as the primary typeface for titles, slide themes, and body copy across presentations and document trackers [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Technical and Data Typeface:** JetBrains Mono is utilized for field labels, table headers, dates, statuses, and operational code runs [^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- **OOXML Embedding Constraints (`ox.NEVER_EMBED`):** Fonts natively available in Google Docs—specifically Instrument Sans and JetBrains Mono—must be declared in document tables (`word/fontTable.xml`) but **never embedded** as binary payloads [^evt-community-events-pr-34]. Pruning these embeds reduces `.docx` tracker payloads by over 200KB per document while rendering cleanly in Google Docs [^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- **Metric Fallback:** Manrope is retained as an embedded binary font within `.docx` templates to preserve layout metrics and visual hierarchy when documents are inspected offline in desktop word processors lacking Instrument Sans [^evt-community-events-pr-34].

### Office Document Styling and Contrast Resolution
Brand conformance across `.pptx`, `.docx`, and `.xlsx` artifacts is mediated by `lib/aaif_events/ooxml_style.py` [^evt-community-events-pr-32]:
- **Role-Aware Token Mapping:** Styling distinguishes semantic roles rather than executing global hex find-and-replace routines. For example, legacy navy fills are remapped to black plate fills, while border definitions convert to thin hairline borders [^evt-community-events-pr-32]. SpreadsheetML styles (`xl/styles.xml`) require dedicated ARGB processing distinct from DrawingML slide shapes [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Minimal-Diff AST Modification:** XML rewrites modify only target attributes (`val=`, `w:fill=`, `typeface=`), preserving essential application metadata, relationship identifiers, and `mc:AlternateContent` fallbacks [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Hierarchical Contrast Checking:** Document generators validate contrast using `contrast.py`, traversing container shapes, `<p:bg>` slide backgrounds, slide layouts, and master slide templates down to base white [^evt-community-events-pr-32]. This prevents invalid token pairings, such as light ink subtitles rendering against dark plates without adequate contrast [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

### Chapter Agent Badges and Vector Graphics
Community chapter visual assets leverage automated vector badge generation [^evt-community-events-pr-39]:
- **Agent Mascot Styling:** In addition to classic geometric badges, chapters utilize an agent mascot badge generated via `make_agent_badge.py` [^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- **Deterministic Palettes:** Mascot scenes (`agent_art.chapter_scene()`) and character accents apply deterministic chapter color assignments derived from design tokens [^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- **Headless Chrome Rendering:** Badges are rendered into SVG/PNG formats through headless Chrome using embedded Instrument Sans typefaces and design system variables [^evt-community-events-pr-39]. Chapter names from untrusted organizer inputs must undergo XML entity escaping before template interpolation [^evt-community-events-pr-39].

# Lifecycle History

- **PR #32 (Merged):** Standardized OOXML templates to AAIF tokens, replaced legacy fonts with Instrument Sans, and implemented automated slide contrast verification [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **PR #34 (Merged):** Established the `NEVER_EMBED` rule for Google Docs native typefaces, eliminating redundant font embeds while maintaining Manrope metric fallbacks [^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- **PR #39 (Merged):** Integrated design-system agent mascot badges generated via headless Chrome using live token definitions [^evt-community-events-pr-39].

proposed_concept.description: Read-only inspection skill auditing community Slack workspace coverage, organizer channel memberships, intake account gaps, and country directory integrity.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Audit Slack skill provides read-only inspection, diagnostic reporting, and integrity verification across the AAIF community Slack workspace. It verifies that city and country channels match central registry metadata, audits private organizer channel memberships against accepted intake rosters, identifies pending invitation backlogs, and checks channel directory posts for completeness [^evt-community-events-pr-36].

The skill operates under least-privilege read scopes, decoupling human triage discrepancies from underlying identity provision gaps [^evt-community-events-pr-36].

# Architecture / Specification

### Account Gap vs Invite Gap Segregation
Audit findings generated by `summarize_audits.py` distinguish channel routing gaps from identity provisioning deficiencies [^evt-community-events-pr-36]:
- **Missing Account (`no_account`):** Identifies accepted chapter organizers whose recorded intake email has no registered Slack user account in the workspace [^evt-community-events-pr-36]. This represents an onboarding or data-quality issue handled by central organizers rather than an automated channel invite failure.
- **Actionable Invite Gaps (`gaps`):** Identifies active Slack accounts that have not been invited into their chapter's private organizer channel or shared country channel [^evt-community-events-pr-36]. This backlog can be resolved through `invite_organizers.py` [^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- **Uncoupled Evaluation:** The audit evaluates account gaps regardless of whether an organizer channel has already been provisioned, ensuring newly created chapters are not dropped from audit reports [^evt-community-events-pr-36].

### Channel Coverage and Directory Auditing
- **Country Channel Mapping:** Audits identify public country channels (`#deutschland`, `#korea`, `#brasil`) by checking central mappings rather than simple lowercase country folding, highlighting missing chapter listings [^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- **Directory Completeness:** Audits evaluate country directory posts to determine whether existing posts are self-authored, need chapter additions, or require initial creation [^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- **Operations Account Audit:** Verifies that operational staff accounts configured in the registry are present in all private organizer channels, detecting provisioning omissions [^evt-community-events-pr-42].

# Lifecycle History

- **PR #36 (Merged):** Decoupled `no_account` intake discrepancies from invitable channel `gaps` and added country channel coverage auditing [^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- **PR #42 (Merged):** Added operational account presence checks within private organizer channels [^evt-community-events-pr-42].

proposed_concept.title: aaif-create-chapter
proposed_concept.description: Automated chapter provisioning and estate maintenance engine managing template cloning, asset rebranding, chapter renaming, and deck sweeps across Google Drive.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The aaif-create-chapter skill automates the lifecycle and asset management of Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) city chapters, handling template cloning from TemplateCity in Google Drive, OOXML presentation rebranding, in-place chapter renaming, and estate-wide slide updates [^evt-community-events-pr-45][^evt-community-events-pr-46]. It operates as part of the community operations infrastructure defined in [community-event-operations](community-event-operations.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Chapter Renaming Automation

The chapter lifecycle includes in-place renaming via `rename_chapter.py` to reconcile capital-city migrations and nomenclature updates across four primary Drive surfaces: chapter folders, CRM workbooks, About documents, and design presentation assets [^evt-community-events-pr-45]. Renaming applies clone-time transforms while observing strict boundaries:
- **Luma decoupling:** Luma slug changes remain decoupled from Drive asset renaming to avoid breaking live public links [^evt-community-events-pr-45].
- **Token safety:** Token replacement explicitly avoids modifying `aaif-<slug>` naming sequences, preventing substring collisions where uppercase city names overlap slug identifiers [^evt-community-events-pr-45].

## Estate Deck Sweeps and Project Roster Management

Slide template maintenance across all chapter decks, online series, and TemplateCity instances is governed through modular estate sweep scripts coordinated by `deck_estate.py` [^evt-community-events-pr-46]. The estate walk implements a verified download, XML rewrite, and upload pipeline featuring:
- **Project Roster Synchronization:** Template About slides reflect the full roster of six hosted AAIF projects: Model Context Protocol (MCP), goose, AGENTS.md, agentgateway, A2A, and Agent Router [^evt-community-events-pr-46]. The sweep locates project lists via the `THE PROJECTS` eyebrow marker, automatically adjusting bounding box width and stepping down typography to accommodate the expanded roster [^evt-community-events-pr-46].
- **Verification and Drift Prevention:** Upload operations verify write status against the Google Workspace CLI, flag orphan section headers lacking underlying rosters, and detect layout overflow anomalies to prevent silent update failures across template decks [^evt-community-events-pr-46].

# Lifecycle History

- Expanded with `rename_chapter.py` in PR #45 to support multi-surface asset renaming and token isolation [^evt-community-events-pr-45].
- Modularized deck estate sweeps into `deck_estate.py` in PR #46, standardizing the six-project roster sweep across 103 template decks [^evt-community-events-pr-46].

proposed_concept.title: aaif-sync
proposed_concept.description: Procedural estate synchronization orchestrator reconciling chapter rosters, organizer access permissions, and registration feeds under strict report-first governance.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The aaif-sync skill orchestrates AAIF community estate reconciliation across Google Workspace, CRM spreadsheets, and Luma feeds, enforcing zero drift between intake records and active cloud permissions [^evt-community-events-pr-45][^evt-community-events-file-0917cfda08f8-a29dcf1a]. Execution adheres strictly to the proposal-execution split defined in [proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md), mandating a report-first dry run before any write operations proceed [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

# Architecture / Specification

## Identity and Drive Access Provisioning

Organizer permission grants in Google Drive use a resilient identity resolution mechanism to handle non-Google intake emails [^evt-community-events-pr-45]:
- **Drive Email Overrides:** When an accepted organizer's intake email lacks an associated Google account, permissions are granted via an explicit `Drive Email` ACL override column while preserving the immutable primary intake record [^evt-community-events-pr-45].
- **Integrity Guards:** Overrides require row-level authority re-derived from fresh reads, ignore invalid or sentinel values (`(no grant)`, blank, duplicates), and immediately drop conflicting overrides if multiple rows disagree on an identity [^evt-community-events-pr-45].

## Decoupled Feed Ingestion and Auditing

Chapter listing updates decouple registration platform dependencies from intake spreadsheet writing [^evt-community-events-pr-45]:
- **Non-blocking Intake:** New chapter rows can be populated without blocking on live Luma page provisioning (`--require-luma` made opt-in) [^evt-community-events-pr-45].
- **Global URL Auditing:** The `--audit-luma` inspection flag verifies link reachability across all existing chapter feed rows, exiting with error code 2 upon detecting broken or 404 targets [^evt-community-events-pr-45].

## Write Gate Governance

All sync engines enforce a report-by-default execution policy [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd]. Synchronizers propose structural state changes in read-only reports and require explicit human or operator approval prior to running `--write` passes, mitigating unreviewed modifications to critical community CRM and ACL tables [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

# Lifecycle History

- Updated in PR #45 with Drive email grant overrides, `--audit-luma` link verification, and decoupled chapter ingestion [^evt-community-events-pr-45].
- Validated through write-gate evaluation graders enforcing report-first responses before push executions [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

proposed_concept.title: community-events-eval-suite
proposed_concept.description: Automated evaluation harness and grader catalog assessing skill routing, dry-run safety gates, and boundary isolation for AAIF community operations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The community-events-eval-suite is an automated testing harness and grader catalog designed to validate the reliability, safety constraints, and skill dispatching of AAIF community operations agents [^evt-community-events-file-07be4806c8b9-e0356c09][^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd]. It verifies that agents operating within the community infrastructure comply with tool calling boundaries, routing rules, and write-gate governance policies [^evt-community-events-file-0917cfda08f8-a29dcf1a][^evt-community-events-file-42c3ab6be70d-2fba308c].

# Architecture / Specification

## Grader Categories

The evaluation harness implements specialized grader types across operational arms:
- **Skill Invocation Graders:** Tool-use regex and schema graders verify whether intended operational skills fire in response to matching task inputs, such as dispatching `aaif-speaker-bio` for speaker profiling [^evt-community-events-file-07be4806c8b9-e0356c09] or `aaif-sync-chapters` for intake synchronizations [^evt-community-events-file-0917cfda08f8-a29dcf1a].
- **Skill Discrimination and Negative Graders:** Negative pattern graders ensure non-applicable skills do not trigger out of context, such as verifying that `aaif-announcement-post` does not fire when generating recaps for completed events [^evt-community-events-file-42c3ab6be70d-2fba308c].
- **Write-Gate and Safety Graders:** Model-graded checks enforce that agents propose dry-run reports before executing writes, failing any agent trajectory that bypasses approval checkpoints or initiates direct write mutations against production sheets without explicit operator authorization [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

## Governance Mapping

The grader suite systematically enforces the [proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and [deterministic-acceptance-gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) patterns, establishing regression baselines before operational skills are merged or deployed [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

# Lifecycle History

- Expanded with specialized eval test cases covering speaker bios, sync-chapter write gates, and recap skill discrimination [^evt-community-events-file-07be4806c8b9-e0356c09][^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd][^evt-community-events-file-42c3ab6be70d-2fba308c].

proposed_concept.description: Automated evaluation harness and grader catalog validating community operations skills, PII redaction, metric hallucination prevention, and prompt injection defense.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated testing harness in the `aaif/community-events` repository designed to verify agent skill routing, editorial constraints, and operational safety boundaries across community workflows. It evaluates multi-turn agent interactions against explicit prompt definitions, pairing deterministic regular expressions and tool-invocation asserts with semantic LLM rubric evaluators to detect PII leaks, hallucinated metrics, and indirect prompt injection attempts prior to production execution.

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation suite organizes test scenarios into domain-specific subdirectories containing a test prompt configuration and modular grader definitions:

## Grader Modalities and Defense Patterns
- **Skill Invocation Routing (`type: tool_used`)**: Evaluates skill selection accuracy using exact tool-call matching against allowed tool sets (e.g., verifying that after-event recaps trigger `aaif-recap-post` rather than announcement skills when provided with past-event prompts)[^evt-community-events-file-ae6fd0f3a42a-a43686f4][^evt-community-events-file-2b5ce8cffe67-7aba21ba].
- **PII and Contact Redaction (`type: regex`)**: Validates that sensitive contact information (such as personal email addresses and telephone numbers) supplied in raw speaker tracker inputs is systematically stripped from generated public copy and speaker bios[^evt-community-events-file-53a80193a1dd-d7167651][^evt-community-events-file-04506118534c-e5137094].
- **Metric Hallucination Prevention (`type: llm`)**: Assesses public-facing summaries against an editorial "signal, not numbers" rule, failing outputs that introduce fabricated attendance counts, percentages, or metrics absent from the prompt context[^evt-community-events-file-598739538a73-226e7bf3][^evt-community-events-file-2b5ce8cffe67-7aba21ba].
- **Indirect Injection Mitigation (`type: llm`)**: Enforces input-data isolation in applicant triage workflows by requiring that form submissions be evaluated strictly as data rather than instructions; agents must not modify application statuses or grant workspace access on the basis of applicant prompt text requesting acceptance[^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf].

## Boundary Alignment
These evaluations reinforce architectural boundaries defined across foundation guidelines, ensuring that operational agents uphold [../patterns/human-approval-gate.md](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) during triage decisions and avoid autonomous permission expansion.

# Lifecycle History
- **Authoritative merge**: Added automated test harnesses for `speaker-bio`, `recap-post`, and `triage-intake` specifying regex, tool-usage, and semantic safety graders in `aaif/community-events`.

# References
- [aaif/community-events Repository](https://github.com/aaif/community-events)

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Automated evaluation harness and grader catalog validating community operations skills across triggering accuracy, write gates, and untrusted input defense.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated evaluation harness and regression catalog designed to validate agent skills in the AAIF community operations repository. It provides standardized benchmark prompts, timeout limits, turn constraints, and programmatic assertion graders that assess whether skills fire appropriately on natural-language requests, enforce write gates prior to mutating state, and resist prompt injection from untrusted form inputs[^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation suite organizes operational test cases under dedicated scenario directories in `evals/`, pairing prompt manifests with tool assertion graders[^evt-community-events-pr-47]:

- **Skill Triggering Verification**: Uses `tool_used` assertion graders matching specific skill invocations (e.g., `input_match: '"skill"\s*:\s*"(?:[\w-]+:)?aaif-audit-slack"'`)[^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759]. Prompts are phrased in colloquial natural language rather than echoing the skill description verbatim to verify trigger sensitivity after text compression[^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759][^evt-community-events-file-995af191aa66-c91cec0e].
- **Untrusted Input and Injection Defense**: Evaluates skills processing external text (such as intake form submissions) to verify that embedded directives (e.g., candidate requests in free-text fields attempting to alter approval status or channel assignments) are treated strictly as data rather than instructions[^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669].
- **Write-Gate Assurance**: Evaluates mutative operations (such as pushing intake rows to master chapter rosters) to ensure the agent outputs preview summaries and pauses before executing persistent writes[^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603].
- **Delta-Measurement Discipline**: Dictates that evaluation prompts omit pre-quoted sheet rows so the harness measures skill utility rather than base-model inference, ensuring test cases with zero tool delta are eliminated[^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92].

# Lifecycle History
Established in PR #47 to provide continuous regression testing for trigger descriptions, safety boundaries, and tool invocation invariants across community event skills[^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# Overview
Community Event Operations provides shared runtime infrastructure, utility modules, and governance linters for AAIF community event skills. It standardizes operational workflows such as chapter intake, Slack channel auditing, and Google Sheets roster synchronization while enforcing strict safety invariants across credential resolution, PII masking, and cross-platform execution boundaries[^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# Architecture / Specification
The operations infrastructure enforces shared technical invariants through centralized modules and dedicated CI verification scripts[^evt-community-events-pr-47]:

- **PII Redaction Invariant**: Centralized into a single `redact.py` module containing both `--redact` flag handling and address maskers, enforced by `check_no_local_redaction.py` to prevent logic drift that previously separated flags from helpers and exposed email addresses in CI logs[^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Portability Boundary**: Skills designed to run standalone as zip bundles on web clients (e.g., Claude.ai) without importing `lib/aaif_events` are explicitly tracked and verified via `check_portable_skills.py`[^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Google Workspace API Resilience**: Unified `gws.py` and `sheets.py` wrappers enforce consistent exponential backoff, distinguish permanent grid-limit errors (such as `A500:K500`) from retryable server errors, and abort on duplicated column headers during sheet operations[^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Pinned Banner Hygiene**: Enforces byte-identical metadata banners across all `SKILL.md` files for tooling rules, public-copy constraints, and legal footers so rules remain intact when skills travel downstream[^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Synthetic Test Cast**: Mandates the use of synthetic organizer personas in worked examples across content skills, replacing real organizer names in public repositories[^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# Lifecycle History
Unified in PR #47 to resolve duplicated helper drift, eliminate PII leakage risks, and establish automated evaluation and linter guards across the community operations library[^evt-community-events-pr-47].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Prior Work Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Comparative landscape survey evaluating specifications, platforms, and hosted protocols across agent telemetry, identity cards, and runtime mediation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The agent observability prior work landscape evaluates emerging open specifications, commercial platforms, and hosted foundational protocols to identify architectural coverage and unaddressed gaps across agentic telemetry.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31] Maintained by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the survey documents how projects handle execution tracing, capability boundaries, identity verification, and runtime governance.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]

Recent additions evaluate hosted foundation projects including [A2A](../taxonomy/agent-to-agent.md) and [agentgateway](agentgateway.md), identifying key strengths in runtime traffic control and exposing an unclaimed evidence layer gap across agent communications.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape framework categorizes agent runtime tools across scope, maturity, licensing, and key technical capabilities.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]

## Hosted Project Additions
- **A2A**: Joined the foundation in August 2026 to serve as the agent-to-agent interoperability layer.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31] It introduces signed agent cards for discovery and capability declaration, though verifying signed card claims against actual runtime behavior remains an unresolved challenge.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]
- **agentgateway**: Joined the foundation in June 2026 to mediate traffic and enforce policies across Model Context Protocol (MCP) and A2A communications, providing deployment options across major cloud marketplaces.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]

## Evidence Layer Gap
A critical gap identified across surveyed technologies is the missing evidence layer.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31] While transport mediation and signed declarations establish perimeter identity, existing frameworks lack verifiable mechanisms linking runtime tool execution, agent identity claims, and non-repudiable audit logs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]

proposed_concept.title: Agent to Tool CLI Boundary Specification
proposed_concept.description: Observability reference matrix and context propagation model analyzing direct agent subprocess invocations, environment-variable carriers, and span lifecycle boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent-to-Tool CLI boundary specification details how an agent runtime observes, traces, and governs direct local subprocess invocations executing external command-line tools.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35] It establishes a concrete realization of the broader cross-boundary gap model tracked in issue #29, bridging canonical tool execution semantics with operating system process lifecycles.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]

The specification defines standard propagation conventions using OpenTelemetry environment-variable context carriers and establishes execution span attribution across synchronous, asynchronous, and background subprocesses.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]

# Architecture / Specification
The boundary distinguishes between the canonical Agent-to-Tool semantic contract and the operational Agent Runtime to Local Process execution layer.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]

## Context Propagation and Environment Variables
- **Context Carrier**: Subprocess tracing leverages the OpenTelemetry Release Candidate specification for environment-variable context carriers (including TRACEPARENT, TRACESTATE, and BAGGAGE).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]
- **Span Reservation**: Pre-execution span-ID reservation allows the parent agent runtime to inject trace context before spawning child processes, preventing detached traces in non-interactive CLI executions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]
- **Span Relationships**: Direct synchronous commands maintain parent-child hierarchy between execute_tool and child CLI spans, whereas detached or long-running background tasks leverage OpenTelemetry Span Links to avoid blocking agent execution loops.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation framework capturing causal agent execution, tool invocations, approval checkpoints, and external side-effects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry specification standardizing causal relationships across agent decision loops, LLM requests, external tool invocations, human approvals, and real-world side-effects.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94] Developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the model addresses fundamental limitations where flat session membership fails to record causal provenance or verify execution enforcement.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]

An initial reference implementation and test coverage plan align the model with OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions and W3C Trace Context specifications.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]

# Architecture / Specification
The trace model formalizes explicit graph edges connecting distributed runtime events beyond flat log streams.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]

## Causal Correlation Requirements
- **Calls and Retries**: Transient model-call failures and subsequent retry attempts must be associated with the root triggering task, attributing token usage accurately without double-counting succeeded retry workflows.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]
- **Approval Checkpoints**: Approval or denial decisions must explicitly reference candidate proposed action identifiers (such as proposal P1). A human or automated denial must terminate execution without producing fictional tool spans.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]
- **External Side-Effects**: Independently reported external effects (such as external ticket creation receipts) must be correlated back to the originating tool execution span and authorization record, distinguishing self-reported agent observations from verified external evidence.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]

# Overview
Community Event Operations provides shared procedural automation and operational tooling for the Agentic AI Foundation's local chapter network.[^evt-community-events-pr-48] The operational suite coordinates chapter lifecycle management, organizer roster synchronizations, workspace room access, and estate health tracking.[^evt-community-events-pr-48]

A hard estate cap and formal lifecycle definitions ensure that global chapter expansion maintains sustainable community oversight and avoids unmonitored organizational drift.[^evt-community-events-pr-48]

# Architecture / Specification

## Estate Limits and Lifecycle Management
- **Chapter Estate Cap**: The global estate is constrained by a cap of 100 total chapter entries on the master directory sheet, requiring dormant or coalesced chapters to be retired before new provisions are approved.[^evt-community-events-pr-48]
- **Lifecycle States**: Chapters carry explicit human-triaged status designations: Active, Provisioned, Dormant, Merged, or Deprecated, supported by a Merged Into pointer for consolidating local communities.[^evt-community-events-pr-48]
- **Health Evaluation**: The read-only health audit script evaluates chapter activity based strictly on positive telemetry (such as recent timestamped Slack activity) rather than hand-curated event logs, treating missing sweep data as indeterminable rather than inactive.[^evt-community-events-pr-48]

## Organizer Channel Synchronization
- **Organizer Room Alignment**: The global `#local-champs` organizer Slack room is kept synchronized with accepted local chapter leaders via intake tooling, removing manual roster drift.[^evt-community-events-pr-48]

The Observability and Traceability Working Group establishes vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and semantic conventions for monitoring and debugging autonomous agent workflows.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94] Operating within the Agentic AI Foundation, the group develops specifications such as the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) and cross-boundary telemetry matrices.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]

The working group coordinates technical deliverables across industry stakeholders and external standards organizations including the IETF, W3C, and OpenTelemetry GenAI working groups.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]

# Operations and Deliverables

## Meeting Cadence and Community Coordination
- **Regional Synchronization**: In addition to bi-weekly working group sessions, the group conducts a monthly 30-minute synchronization call dedicated to contributors in the APAC/APJ regions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]

- **Project Intake and Collaboration**: The group actively explores federation across Agent Resource Discovery (ARD), Agent Router, and [agentgateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) using W3C Trace Context and OpenTelemetry context propagation.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Audit Slack Skill
proposed_concept.description: Read-only inspection skill auditing community Slack workspace coverage, organizer channel membership, and conversation health subject to API token measurement ceilings.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-audit-slack` skill is a read-only diagnostic and reporting tool within the [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md) suite that inspects Slack workspaces for chapter coverage, organizer channel memberships, and channel activity baselines [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]. It evaluates community communication health while enforcing strict boundary checks against reporting API failures as human organizer omissions [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].

# Architecture / Specification

### Token Scopes and Measurement Ceilings

The audit behavior and data completeness are dictated by the active authorization token [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]:
- **Standing AAIF App Token**: Carries `channels:history` and `groups:history`, enabling the `audit_activity.py` engine to inspect `conversations.history` [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]. Message counts represent lower bounds (floors) because thread replies remain invisible to standard `conversations.history` calls [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].
- **Slack CLI Fallback Token**: Lacks `channels:history` and `search:read`. Invocations of `conversations.history` return `missing_scope`, causing channel recency and activity statuses to be explicitly flagged as unreadable rather than reported as inactive [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].

### Pre-Flight Scope Validation

To prevent diagnostic errors from masquerading as community deficiencies, engines must validate all required OAuth scopes prior to data collection [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]:
- Scopes including `groups:read` (required for private channel discovery via `conversations.list`) and `users:read.email` must be verified at startup [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].
- A missing or revoked scope immediately halts execution; without this check, missing email read permissions cause organizer lookups to fail silently and register false reports of missing organizer accounts [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].

### Prohibited Proxies and Data Nuances

The skill explicitly rejects inaccurate API proxies for activity and engagement [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]:
- **Channel `updated` Timestamps**: Not permitted as activity signals because bulk administrative migrations reset timestamps across dozens of channels concurrently; genuine human edits are tracked via `topic.last_set` or `purpose.last_set` [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].
- **Member `updated` Timestamps**: Altered on profile and settings adjustments; framed only as a floor on account staleness rather than proof of engagement [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].
- **Private Channel Discovery**: Standard `conversations.list` and `users.conversations` calls only surface private channels where the caller/token owner is an explicit member [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]. Full workspace visibility requires Enterprise Grid API methods (`admin.conversations.search`) or manual admin UI exports [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].

# Lifecycle History

- Operationalized as part of the community events estate management toolchain to verify channel provisioning and organizer linkage across local chapters [^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Sync Skill
proposed_concept.description: Procedural estate synchronization orchestrator reconciling chapter rosters, organizer access permissions, Drive assets, and Slack channels across the AAIF community.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-sync` skill is the primary front-door orchestrator for full-estate reconciliation across the [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md) environment [^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]. When community estate assets drift—such as tracking sheets, Google Drive directories, and Slack channels falling out of alignment—`aaif-sync` coordinates an ordered, multi-phase execution pipeline to return all systems to an authoritative baseline [^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a].

# Architecture / Specification

### Orchestration vs. Phase Skills

Estate synchronization is structured as a two-tier capability model [^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5, ^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]:
- **Front-Door Orchestrator (`aaif-sync`)**: Owns the overarching eight-step pipeline and enforces sequence constraints [^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]. Broad estate-wide synchronization requests must route to `aaif-sync` rather than isolated phase engines [^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5].
- **Granular Phase Skills**: Dedicated phase engines (`aaif-sync-chapters`, `aaif-sync-organizers`, `aaif-sync-slack`) own single-domain operational logic [^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5, ^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]. Direct routing to an individual phase skill during an estate-wide request constitutes a failure mode that leaves the remainder of the estate unhandled [^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836].

### Pipeline Sequencing and Invariants

The execution pipeline mandates a deterministic sequence where reporting precedes state mutations [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd]:
1. **Pre-flight & Read Validation**: Reports and status reconciliations are generated before any external writes are dispatched [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].
2. **Roster and CRM Alignment**: Authoritative chapter rows, CRM entries, and roster entries must be stabilized first [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].
3. **Downstream Asset Mutations**: Granting Google Drive permissions, creating directories, or writing channel updates to Slack occurs only after data structures are fully synchronized [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].

# Lifecycle History

- Standardized as the top-level dispatch entry point for automated and maintainer-driven community estate reconciliation [^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-announcement-post` skill drafts promotional copy and attendee communications for newly scheduled AAIF community events, meetups, and chapter launches [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5]. It operates under compliance policies defined in the [Code of Conduct](../policies/code-of-conduct.md) and event operations guidelines, ensuring all attendee-facing promotional copy includes required governance links and avoids footer drift [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5].

# Architecture / Specification

### Mandatory Legal Footer Requirements

All attendee-facing launch and event announcements must carry standing AAIF legal disclosures by default [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5]:
- **Required Dual Disclosures**: The post copy must include both the **Code of Conduct** and the **Privacy Policy** links [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5].
- **Anti-Drift Conformance**: Evaluations enforce a regular expression match (`code-of-conduct[\s\S]*privacy-policy|privacy-policy[\s\S]*code-of-conduct`) over the generated output [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5]. Omitting either document or providing only the Code of Conduct is treated as a compliance failure [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5].

### Privacy and Disclosure Controls

In addition to the mandatory legal footer, the skill enforces:
- Anonymization and consent verification before publishing individual attendee names or speaker rosters.
- Standard venue, RSVP, and accessibility details matching the authoritative event tracker.

# Lifecycle History

- Maintained under the community events automation suite with automated CI regression testing via the [Community Events Eval Suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md) [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5].
