proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Automated evaluation harness and grader catalog validating community operations skills across triggering, execution sequencing, and legal compliance.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated testing harness in the `aaif/community-events` repository that evaluates procedural skills and agent behaviors against real-world operations workflows [^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a]. The suite runs standardized test cases to verify correct tool selection, execution ordering, and compliance with standing policies across event automation agents [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5, ^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].

# Architecture / Specification

### Eval Harness Structure

Each evaluation test case specifies operational boundaries, timeouts, and grading criteria:
- **Configuration Manifests**: YAML frontmatter defines execution limits (e.g., `max_turns`, `timeout_seconds`, `allowed_tools`) and scenario tags [^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a].
- **Graders**: Multi-arm verification routines evaluate output artifacts and runtime traces using deterministic regex checks or LLM-judged criteria [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5, ^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].

### Documented Test Cases and Graders

- **`sync-front-door`**: Tests agent dispatch when an operator reports general community estate drift across Google Sheets, Google Drive, and Slack [^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a].
  - `skill_fires`: Confirms invocation of the general orchestrator [AAIF Sync Skill](../skills/aaif-sync.md) rather than a narrow engine [^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836].
  - `not_a_phase_skill`: Uses trace regex matching to ensure sub-skills (`aaif-sync-chapters`, `aaif-sync-organizers`, `aaif-sync-slack`) do not trigger independently for broad estate prompts [^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5].
  - `order_is_respected`: Evaluates whether the plan enforces reporting and CRM setup before granting Drive access or mutating Slack state [^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].
- **`announcement-post`**: Validates outbound promotional copy generated by the [AAIF Announcement Post Skill](../skills/aaif-announcement-post.md) [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5].
  - `legal_footer`: Regex grader verifying that both the [Code of Conduct](../policies/code-of-conduct.md) and Privacy Policy links appear concurrently to prevent footer drift [^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5].

# Lifecycle History

- Established to benchmark operational reliability, tool triggering precision, and legal compliance across AAIF community management skills [^evt-community-events-file-60baba93c961-5853f27a, ^evt-community-events-file-a7c09511caf9-8abab7d5].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation specification defining core agent execution entities, causal relationships, turn-boundary invariants, and boundary interpretation rules.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and correlation specification developed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group to standardize how causal agent execution, tool invocations, and governance decisions are captured across disparate runtime and control plane boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51] It establishes a unified data model linking user prompts, model reasoning, proposed actions, policy authorizations, and external tool effects.

# Architecture / Specification
The draft shared contract (v0.1) defines explicit identities, causal relationships, and interpretation rules across agent execution lifecycles.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]

## Core Identities
The contract models agent runtime activity through eight primary identity types:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]
- **Conversation**: The top-level interaction session encompassing multi-turn exchanges.
- **Runtime Session**: The execution lifetime of a specific agent runtime or worker instance.
- **Turn**: An atomic cycle of agent perception, evaluation, and action initiation.
- **Model Call**: Direct invocations and completions against foundation models.
- **Proposed Action**: An explicit intent generated by the agent prior to policy evaluation or execution.
- **Approval Decision**: A governance evaluation (authorized, rejected, or deferred) emitted by a human or policy engine.
- **Tool Execution**: An invocation of a local subprocess, network endpoint, or external capability.
- **External Effect**: A persistent side effect or state modification produced outside the agent boundary.

## Causal Relationships and Boundaries
The model identifies six foundational relationships linking these entities, capturing causal ancestry from model outputs to tool invocations and state changes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51] It enforces candidate turn-boundary rules and maps attributes across OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions and AAIF taxonomy terms.

## Interpretation Rules
To support deterministic audit and dispute analysis, the trace contract mandates three normative evaluation rules:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]
- **Missing Observations**: An unobserved or missing event must be classified as unknown rather than zero or non-existent.
- **Deduplication**: Duplicate telemetry events must resolve deterministically via immutable correlation keys.
- **Order Invariance**: Reordered event arrivals from distributed transports must yield identical evaluation results.

# Lifecycle History
Introduced as a specification draft within the Observability and Traceability Working Group to address cross-boundary agent telemetry.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]

proposed_concept.title: Three-State Reconciliation
proposed_concept.description: Evaluation model comparing an agent claim against independent observation across agreement, contradiction, and explicit absence of evidence.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Three-state reconciliation is an evaluation model that compares an agent claim against an independent observation, resolving into one of three explicit states: agreement, contradiction, or no independent evidence.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54] By treating the absence of independent evidence as an explicit, first-class outcome rather than a silent default or failure, the model enables auditors to distinguish between verified consistency and unobserved claims.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54]

# Architecture / Specification
Traditional two-state reconciliation models (such as matched or mismatched) collapse unverified claims into silent defaults, creating significant blind spots for dispute resolution and compliance audits.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54] Three-state reconciliation resolves observations across three discrete outcomes:
- **Agreement**: An independent boundary observation corroborates the self-reported agent claim.
- **Contradiction**: An independent observation directly conflicts with or disproves the agent claim.
- **No Independent Evidence**: No corroborating or conflicting telemetry exists at the boundary.

The model originated in the Observability and Traceability Working Group to reconcile agent self-reported telemetry against independent control-plane observations, interacting directly with concepts like `../taxonomy/witness-scope.md` and evidence strength categorization.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54]

# Lifecycle History
Proposed in the Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream issue #54 following initial framing in Observability and Traceability WG issue #36.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-54]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Estate Sync
proposed_concept.description: Procedural estate synchronization orchestrator reconciling chapter rosters, organizer access permissions, and Slack channels across a seven-phase pipeline.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-sync` skill is a procedural estate synchronization orchestrator and single operational front door that reconciles community chapter records, organizer rosters, and communication channels.[^evt-community-events-pr-49] It defines the authoritative execution order, human-in-the-loop gates, and telemetry reporting across the AAIF community operations estate.[^evt-community-events-pr-49]

# Architecture / Specification
The synchronization engine structures operational tasks across a two-axis matrix indexed by phase (subject area) and stage (gather, plan, execute):[^evt-community-events-pr-49]

## Seven-Phase Pipeline
The pipeline executes sequentially across seven functional phases:[^evt-community-events-pr-49]
1. **Intake & Triage**: Ingests incoming role applications and reports triage queue depth as an exit condition without automated decision-making.
2. **Chapters**: Reconciles active community chapter status and metadata.
3. **Organizers**: Reconciles individual organizer assignments and directory permissions.
4. **Drive Access**: Synchronizes Google Drive asset permissions and folder ownership.
5. **Slack Channels**: Audits public and organizer channel naming, members, and regional routing.
6. **CRM & Roles**: Reconciles per-role volunteer tracker sheets and data validation rules.
7. **Estate Reporting**: Compiles health metrics and ranked finding tables into an aggregate HTML report.

## Execution Controls and Invariants
- **Human Triage Gate**: The runner reports pending queue depth and exits without deciding applications, enforcing human review.[^evt-community-events-pr-49]
- **Write Protection**: All mutations require the explicit `--write` flag; dry runs generate plans and findings without altering remote state.[^evt-community-events-pr-49]
- **Stateless Execution**: The orchestrator retains no state across executions, relying on live data and a local cache bounded by a one-day maximum age (`MAX_AGE`).[^evt-community-events-pr-49]
- **Ops Notes Preservation**: Preserves human-maintained `Ops Notes` columns across sheets and health reports without programmatic modification.[^evt-community-events-pr-49]

# Lifecycle History
Refactored in community-events PR #49 into a unified, code-driven procedural pipeline with phase-by-stage indexing and centralized HTML estate reporting.[^evt-community-events-pr-49]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Slack Audit
proposed_concept.description: Configuration-driven Slack inspection skill auditing chapter channels, organizer rooms, and regional fallbacks against community spreadsheet mappings.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-audit-slack` skill is a read-only community inspection engine that audits Slack workspace coverage, organizer channel memberships, and channel categorization against the AAIF Community Chapters List.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6] Operating as a gather step within the broader `../skills/aaif-sync.md` pipeline, it matches channels through spreadsheet configuration rather than hardcoded code mappings.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6][^evt-community-events-pr-49]

# Architecture / Specification
The audit engine reads channel assignments directly from columns in the Chapters List spreadsheet:[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]
- **Slack Channel**: The chapter's dedicated public channel (e.g., `#bay-area` for San Francisco).
- **Organizer Channel**: The private coordination channel for local leads (e.g., `<city>-organizers`).
- **Country Channel**: A regional channel serving a city without granting chapter coverage (e.g., `#india` for Chennai), preventing false coverage claims.
- **Ops Notes**: Free-text human operational notes quoted verbatim by health checks without automated modification.

## Matching Rules and Configuration Order
Matching vocabularies reside on the `Slack Config` tab of the spreadsheet, evaluated in strict row order:[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]
- **Public channel prefixes**: Evaluated top-to-bottom starting with `(none)` (bare city slug), followed by prefixes such as `meetup-`, `aaif-`, and `mlops-`.
- **Organizer channel suffixes**: Evaluated sequentially (e.g., `-organizers`, `-organisers`, `-chapter-leads`).
- **Staff email domain**: Identifies foundation staff to distinguish authorized operators from unassigned members in organizer channels.
- **Human Alias Confirmation**: The audit prohibits auto-mapping aliases; near-miss candidates are reported for manual confirmation before spreadsheet entry.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]

# Lifecycle History
Transitioned from a local JSON channel map into a configuration-driven spreadsheet model and integrated as a gather engine in `aaif-sync`.[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6][^evt-community-events-pr-49]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation specification defining core agent execution entities, turn boundaries, model invocation links, and observable side-effect relationships.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and correlation specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to record and query agent activity across turns, interruptions, and system boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. The specification maps agent interaction semantics to [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) conventions, establishing standard relationships between conversational continuity, model calls, authorization checkpoints, and external state changes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

Rather than mandating custom runtimes or backend storage engines, the model relies on language-neutral fixtures and existing OpenTelemetry collector tooling to observe agent trajectories without inspecting internal or private agent state[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification establishes four baseline behavioral inquiry scopes that conformant implementations must answer[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]:
- **Continuity:** Determines which interaction turns belong together across session pauses, restarts, or multi-turn conversational exchanges.
- **Calls and Retries:** Correlates exact foundation model invocations and retry attempts to specific turns without double-counting work.
- **Approvals:** Links governance and approval decisions to proposed actions and tracks whether those actions subsequently executed[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].
- **Effects:** Binds tool executions to independently observed external environment or system state changes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

### Turn and Boundary Semantics
The trace model evaluates candidate conventions such as assigning one trace per turn as a default while preserving incoming caller trace contexts[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. In accordance with [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) terminology, the model differentiates conversation continuity, runtime/protocol sessions, and overall agent trajectories[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. Evidence rules mandate that unobserved data indicates an unknown state rather than zero or success, observed approval does not imply verified enforcement, and payload content capture remains strictly opt-in[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

# Lifecycle History
The working group formalized an implementation plan of record comprising nine structured tasks to establish baseline scenarios, build shared test suites, implement correlation in [Goose](../resources/goose.md) alongside a second independent agent/SDK, validate cross-reader query paths, and submit findings upstream to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic convention workstreams[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body convening practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies to establish shared telemetry conventions, boundary observability models, and causal execution tracing standards[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]. The working group focuses on aligning existing instrumentation frameworks, identifying semantic gaps in agent tracking, and delivering guidance and specifications for interoperability across heterogeneous agent runtimes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group maintains an active portfolio of technical documentation, landscape analyses, and empirical execution programs:
- **[Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md):** A nine-task implementation plan of record standardizing session/turn continuity, model call retries, approval checkpoint binding, and external side-effect correlation across OpenTelemetry primitives[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].
- **[Prior Work Survey](../resources/agent-observability-prior-work.md):** A landscape review tracking industry specifications, runtime monitors, and evaluation platforms[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- **[Use Case Catalog](../resources/agent-observability-use-cases.md):** An operational inventory analyzing enterprise requirements for debugging, cost accounting, security auditing, and compliance tracking[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].

# Governance and Leadership
The working group is co-chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog) for the March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027 term, appointed by Platinum and Gold working group members[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]. The working group convenes biweekly on Wednesdays at 10:00 AM Pacific Time via public Linux Foundation Zoom conferences, documenting minutes and action items through LFX tools and GitHub issues as the durable source of truth[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Procedural operations pipeline and shared infrastructure managing chapter provisioning, estate lifecycle, and hardened Google Workspace execution boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Community Event Operations encompasses the core operational scripts, shared library boundaries, and verification harnesses that govern the Agentic AI Foundation's distributed community estate[^evt-community-events-pr-51]. The infrastructure coordinates chapter provisioning, recurring online series setup, slide generation, and roster synchronization across Google Drive, Google Sheets, Slack, and Luma under strict structural hygiene rules[^evt-community-events-pr-51].

# Architecture / Specification
The shared execution layer enforces strict boundary protections to ensure that automation errors or network timeouts cannot silently corrupt shared Drive folders, duplicate spreadsheet structures, or leak authentication tokens[^evt-community-events-pr-51].

### Non-Idempotent Retry Guarding
Network operations executed through the Google Workspace CLI wrapper (`gws`) distinguish between safe read retries and potentially destructive non-idempotent mutations[^evt-community-events-pr-51]. Calls sending `drive.files.create`, `drive.files.copy`, `appendDimension`, `insertDimension`, or `addSheet` explicitly disable automated retry attempts via `aaif_events.gws.NO_RETRY`[^evt-community-events-pr-51]. Because a write that succeeds on the server but times out on the client would otherwise create duplicate folders, files, or renamed duplicate sheet tabs, a dedicated lint rule (`scripts/check_non_idempotent_retries.py`) programmatically validates all write call sites[^evt-community-events-pr-51].

### Centralized Wrapper and Credential Scrubbing
To avoid configuration drift and security regressions, isolated script-local `gws` implementations were eliminated across chapter and series provisioning workflows in favor of centralized library bindings[^evt-community-events-pr-51]. The shared wrapper strips execution payloads and standard output from exception messages, reporting only CLI verbs and stderr to prevent token or table row leakage in public tracebacks[^evt-community-events-pr-51]. Environment scrubbing rules ensure OAuth client secrets and refresh tokens are isolated, while environment filtering regexes maintain strict boundary matches across Slack and Workspace tokens[^evt-community-events-pr-51].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate 18-step pipeline architecture, ephemeral run memo caching, concurrency pools, and macOS stay-awake process controls from community-events PRs #52 and #53.

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Estate Synchronization
proposed_concept.description: Procedural estate synchronization orchestrator executing an 18-step pipeline across Slack and Google Workspace with ephemeral run-memo caching and sleep prevention.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-sync` skill is a multi-step operational engine designed to reconcile AAIF community chapter rosters, organizer access permissions, CRM sheets, and Slack workspace configurations into a consistent estate state[^evt-community-events-pr-52]. The skill orchestrates an end-to-end 18-step synchronization pipeline that runs sequentially across external identity and storage providers[^evt-community-events-pr-52][^evt-community-events-pr-53].

# Architecture / Specification
The synchronization engine operates across several dedicated scripts and shared libraries in `lib/aaif_events`, enforcing specific operational boundaries and caching invariants[^evt-community-events-pr-52]:

- **18-Step Pipeline:** Standard execution runs all 18 synchronization steps sequentially without ad-hoc phase omissions, ensuring comprehensive reconciliation of chapters, organizers, resources, and communication channels[^evt-community-events-pr-52][^evt-community-events-pr-53].
- **Ephemeral Run Memos:** Read latency against rate-limited APIs is mitigated using run-scoped memo files (`AAIF_SLACK_RUN_MEMO` and `AAIF_GWS_RUN_MEMO`) managed via `jsoncache.RunMemo`[^evt-community-events-pr-52]. Memos are created with `0600` file permissions, operate append-only, and are strictly deleted upon process termination, interrupt, or crash[^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **Cache Invalidation Under Mutation:** Slack memos cache resolved account queries (`users.lookupByEmail`, `users.info`) for the duration of a run[^evt-community-events-pr-52]. Google Workspace memos cache successful Sheet and Drive reads during read-only report runs; write runs (`--write`) disable Google Workspace read memos entirely to guarantee that subsequent steps read updated state written by preceding steps[^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **Parallel Chapter Processing:** High-overhead steps such as `sync_crm` utilize thread pools (e.g., six parallel workers) to process Drive folder reads concurrently while maintaining deterministic, sequential planning and sanitization folder paths[^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **Process Sleep Prevention:** On macOS hosts, the runner initializes a background `caffeinate -i -w <pid>` subprocess linked to the runner's process identifier, preventing system sleep and session timeouts from stalling or invalidating long-running runs[^evt-community-events-pr-53].

# Lifecycle History
Originally, multi-step report runs executed redundant API calls across separate subprocess steps, taking upwards of 50 minutes[^evt-community-events-pr-52]. In September 2026, PR #52 added `jsoncache.RunMemo` and worker pools to reduce execution to approximately 11 to 21 minutes[^evt-community-events-pr-52]. PR #53 subsequently added macOS `caffeinate` process guards to prevent OS sleep during the full 18-step pipeline[^evt-community-events-pr-53].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation specification defining core agent execution entities, turn boundaries, causal relationships, and upstream instrumentation contracts.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model (ABTM) is an open telemetry and correlation specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48]. It standardizes causal trace representations for agent systems, capturing reasoning turns, tool dispatch boundaries, protocol transitions, and multi-agent coordination[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification architecture is structured around five core delivery pillars governed by the working group's execution plan[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48]:

- **Shared Relationship Contract:** A normative relationship data model establishing causal parent-child, delegation, and dependency links across disparate agent framework components and protocol boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].
- **Reference Agent Implementations:** Concrete implementations demonstrating trace emission across two distinct agent frameworks or SDKs to validate multi-framework compatibility[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].
- **Provider API Examples:** Mapping reference architectures and payload bindings for common model provider APIs to ensure standardized span attribution across hosted LLM interactions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].
- **Reusable Conformance Tests:** A portable test suite enabling runtimes and telemetry SDKs to validate conformance against the ABTM structural event and relationship schemas[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].
- **Upstream Contributions:** An evidence-backed roadmap feeding findings and profile definitions into external telemetry bodies such as OpenTelemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the Observability and Traceability Working Group consolidated its tactical direction into an execution plan (PR #48 closing issue #39), decomposing implementation into tracked issues (#40 through #47) covering relationship semantics, reference agent pairings, provider bindings, and test harnesses[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing shared agentic workflow execution models, reference architectures, taxonomy definitions, and enterprise process patterns.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group is an AAIF technical working group co-chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]. The group standardizes runtime execution patterns, state management primitives, and integration architectures for deploying autonomous and human-in-the-loop agents into enterprise workflows[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical deliverables into three designated work streams[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]:

- **Reference Architectures Work Stream:** Scopes and authors formal reference architectures modeling production workflow patterns, including [bounded autonomous remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md) and [single-agent human approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].
- **Taxonomy Work Stream:** Defines standardized execution concepts and runtime vocabulary (such as [workflow primitives](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md)) in close coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].
- **Critical Use Cases Work Stream:** Inventories and evaluates enterprise operational workflows to identify common integration topologies, failure points, and pattern candidates[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

# Lifecycle History
In June 2026, the working group established work stream leadership and initiated candidate evaluation for initial reference architectures and use cases[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]. During this period, the group flagged cross-working-group terminology overlap to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), recommending formal authority for the global taxonomy work stream to enforce consistent definitions across all foundation groups[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group bridging global AI policy developments and technical agentic systems, tracking regulatory baselines and comparative compliance frameworks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group bridges emerging global regulatory frameworks and technical standards for agentic AI architectures.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319] Co-chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase), the group translates statutory and oversight regimes across jurisdictions into actionable architectural baselines, control placement rules, and gap analyses for foundational agent components.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]

# Architecture / Specification

In August 2026, the working group established a formal baseline of 16 core themes against which comparative policy and regulatory gap analyses are structured:[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]

1. **Governance & accountability**: Ownership structures, approval gates, RACI matrices, and formal risk acceptance.
2. **Use-case classification & risk tiering**: Permitted versus prohibited deployments and tiered operational controls.
3. **Architecture**: Reference patterns, trust boundaries, and control placement across agent tiers.
4. **Agent identity & delegation**: Authentication, authorization models, acting-on-behalf-of assertions, and federated registries, coordinated with `../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md`.
5. **Guardrails & policy constraints**: Business rule enforcement, policy-as-code, and system-level boundaries.
6. **Data protection & privacy**: Personally identifiable information (PII) governance, data minimization, retention horizons, and jurisdictional residency.
7. **Security & access controls**: Least-privilege role assignment, secrets segregation, environmental segmentation, and granular tool permissions.
8. **Model/agent risk management**: Model validation, robustness benchmarks, drift detection, and change-control procedures.
9. **Human oversight**: Human-in-the-loop (HITL) and human-on-the-loop (HOTL) escalation paths, automated oversight gates, and out-of-band intervention mechanisms like `../patterns/kill-switch.md`.
10. **Action management**: Pre-execution verification checks, dual control enforcement, and reversibility mechanisms.
11. **Monitoring & logging**: Verifiable audit trails, prompt/tool call logs, and structured decision traces.
12. **Testing & red teaming**: Adversarial prompt injection defense, tool invocation abuse testing, and autonomy failure evaluations.
13. **Third-party & supply chain**: Vendor due diligence protocols and end-to-end model and tool provenance tracking.
14. **Incident response**: Autonomous failure detection, containment runbooks, and mandatory statutory reporting workflows.
15. **Transparency & user disclosure**: Agent self-disclosure, behavioral notices, and system explanations.
16. **Recordkeeping & auditability**: Long-term retention schedules and deterministic execution reproducibility.

To ensure consistent extraction across diverse regional policy instruments, the group maintains a standardized "golden source" prompt methodology that extracts authoritative statutory requirements against each theme.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]

# Lifecycle History

- **August 2026**: Finalized the 16-theme regulatory baseline and golden-source extraction prompt; planned cross-regional comparative gap analysis delivery for October 2026.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]

proposed_concept.description: Production workflow catalog categorizing real-world agent deployments into structured coordination and execution archetypes across industry verticals.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Use Case Inventory is a curated catalog of production agent workflows maintained by `../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md`.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51] It classifies empirical implementations across triggers, human-in-the-loop gates, coordination topologies, and orchestration archetypes to ground architectural reference patterns in real-world deployment patterns.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]

# Architecture / Specification

Recent catalog additions incorporate specialized software development lifecycle (SDLC) production cases, including automated **Upstream SDK release impact analysis** sourced from MCP Inspector tooling:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]

- **Classification Dimensions**:
  - *Trigger*: `Scheduled` (nightly workflow execution via cron).
  - *HITL Pattern*: `None` (analysis generates informational issue comments, leaving adoption decisions external to the workflow).
  - *Agent Count*: `Single-agent sufficient`.
  - *Coordination*: `Single-agent, orchestrated` (agent searches codebase within fixed procedural pipeline).
  - *Workflow Pattern*: `Sequential pipeline` (repository sweep, dependency fetch, impact analysis, security scan, and artifact posting).
  - *Duration*: `Short` (bounded by CI runtime limits).

- **Boundary and Security Controls**:
  The workflow models `../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md` enforced strictly through runtime job permissions rather than interactive human approval gates:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]
  1. An initial deterministic task files the tracking issue.
  2. The analysis agent executes inside an isolated container with a read-only token and restricted file inspection tools (`Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`), treating external release notes as untrusted context.
  3. Candidate outputs are passed through an automated scanner for credential leakage before being promoted as artifacts to a separate write-scoped task that updates the repository.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]

# Lifecycle History

- **September 2026**: Added MCP Inspector upstream SDK release impact analysis demonstrating permission-enforced proposal-execution isolation without runtime convergence gates.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards, delegation models, and cross-organizational trust architectures for autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity and Trust Working Group establishes vendor-neutral standards, delegation primitives, and verification architectures governing autonomous agent identities across organizational boundaries.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10] The group coordinates technical identity mechanisms with statutory obligations articulated by `../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md` to prevent semantic drift between engineering protocols and regulatory mandates.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]

# Architecture / Specification

Technical terminology in identity specifications frequently overlaps with legally defined terms under regional privacy and digital identity regimes.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10] The working group analyzes key semantic boundaries across statutory jurisdictions:

- **Operator**: In engineering contexts, the term answers operational control ("who operates the agent"); in regulatory regimes such as EU AI Act Article 3(8), it serves as a strict statutory umbrella encompassing providers, deployers, product manufacturers, authorized representatives, importers, and distributors.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]
- **Relying Party**: Technical protocols treat any verifier as a relying party, whereas under eIDAS 2 (Regulation 2024/1183, Article 5b) a relying party is a legally registered entity mandated to declare intended use prior to requesting attributes from digital wallets.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]
- **Consent & Consent Receipts**: Engineering specifications often conflate transaction authorization with data processing consent. Under GDPR Articles 4(11) and 7 (standardized in ISO/IEC 27560), consent represents a lawful basis for personal data processing; conversely, under PSD2 Article 64, consent denotes payment authorization governed by strong customer authentication.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]
- **Attestation**: Cryptographic runtime evidence under RATS models differs from legal electronic attestations of attributes (qualified or non-qualified) defined in eIDAS 2.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]
- **Mandate**: Distinguished between application-level authorization tokens and civil-law agency contracts or European Digital Identity (EUDI) powers of representation.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]

Additionally, reference architectures must map every delegation hop—from user/sponsor through workspace devices, logical agents, and external tool calls—to specific legal custodian roles (e.g., GDPR Article 28 data processors vs Article 30 controllers; EU AI Act Article 19 provider logs vs Article 26(6) deployer logs) to ensure valid chain-of-custody for `../standards/evidence-record-spec.md`.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]

# Lifecycle History

- **September 2026**: Initiated formal alignment review reconciling engineering delegation terminology with statutory legal definitions and custodian role requirements across EU and global regimes.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing agent telemetry, causal execution traces, protocol boundary metrics, and verifiable audit logging.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes vendor-neutral telemetry, event envelopes, distributed execution traces, and audit-log architectures for agentic workflows.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54] In collaboration with `../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md`, the working group aligns trace models such as `../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md` with regional compliance, retention, and verification mandates.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group's audit-logging specifications incorporate explicit jurisdictional requirements to resolve auditability, retention, and identifier obligations:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54]

- **Retention vs. Recording Obligations**: Logging specifications distinguish between logging capability duties and log retention duties under the EU AI Act. Article 12 mandates high-risk system technical design capabilities for automatic event recording; statutory retention obligations are governed separately under Article 19 for providers and Article 26(6) for deployers (mandating a retention floor of at least six months from operative enforcement dates).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54]
- **Jurisdictional Parameterization of Event Envelopes**: Common audit schemas must parameterize metadata fields rather than standardizing on single-regime assumptions. While GDPR Article 6 mandates explicit "consent basis" tracking, US state privacy acts operate primarily on opt-out mechanisms, Korea's PIPA and Singapore's PDPA utilize consent frameworks, and Japan's APPI structures compliance around documented intended purposes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54]
- **Identifier Privacy and Natural Person Attribution**: Persistent pseudonymous identifiers constitute personal data under GDPR/UK GDPR Recital 30, differing from traditional US PII definitions. Furthermore, systems subject to EU AI Act Article 12(3)(d) must capture the verified identities of natural persons overseeing or validating automated outputs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54]

# Lifecycle History

- **September 2026**: Addressed legal-technical divergence in log retention specifications, clarifying EU AI Act Articles 12, 19, and 26(6) distinctions and multi-regime audit metadata parameterization.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-54]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Use Cases
proposed_concept.description: Catalog categorizing agent observability requirements into nine operational domains and establishing cross-cutting telemetry mandates across trust, governance, completeness, and causality.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Observability Use Cases catalog defines practitioner requirements and cross-cutting telemetry mandates for observing AI agent behavior across development, operational monitoring, security, and compliance lifecycles.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3] Maintained by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the catalog acts as the requirements baseline for specifications including the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) and runtime exporter implementations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]

The catalog highlights critical gaps where traditional application performance monitoring (APM) and isolated LLM call spans fail to capture multi-turn decision trajectories, dynamic context compaction, tool invocation retry loops, and asynchronous cross-agent delegations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]

# Architecture / Specification

## Cross-Cutting Telemetry Requirements
The catalog defines five universal requirements applicable across all agent observability use cases:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]
- **Source and Trust:** Telemetry records must identify their producer and observation point, distinguishing agent self-reporting from framework, gateway, sandbox, operating system, or external security-sensor vantage points. Records must indicate available signing or attestation mechanisms without asserting that signatures guarantee factual completeness.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]
- **Privacy and Governance:** Telemetry metadata must support data minimization, access control, residency, retention, and field-level masking. Raw secrets, API tokens, and credentials must never be exported.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]
- **Completeness and Sampling:** Telemetry must declare sampling policies, dropped-event counters, and collection gaps, clearly differentiating auditable compliance streams from discardable diagnostic traces.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]
- **Schema Evolution:** Payloads must identify schemas, semantic conventions, instrumentation packages, agent harnesses, model identifiers, and tool versions to ensure reliable historical replay and regression testing.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]
- **Correlation and Causality:** Emitted events must provide stable identifiers and causal linkages across sessions, tasks, delegations, and external artifacts, avoiding sole reliance on wall-clock time or strict parent-child span trees.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]

## Use Case Classification Categories
The inventory structures operational scenarios into nine categories:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]
- **A. Debugging and Root Cause Analysis:** Reconstructing observable decision context, prompts, tool calls, and effective context window states without exposing private chain-of-thought (A1); detecting token spikes, execution bottlenecks, and tool retry loops (A2); and reproducing behavior deterministically (A3).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]
- **B. Cost Management and Optimization:** Tracking per-session costs (B1), computing cost per successful outcome (B2), and identifying computational and token waste across retries (B3).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]
- **C. Code Attribution and Provenance:** Attributing AI-generated lines in codebases (C1) and conducting security audits of generated code (C2).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]
- **D. Evaluation and Quality Assurance:** Measuring task-specific performance benchmarks (D1), detecting behavioral regressions (D2), and performing comparative evaluation across models and configurations (D3).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]
- **E. Safety and Compliance:** Tracking real-world external actions (E1), identifying unauthorized scope expansion (E2), maintaining immutable audit logs for regulated environments (E3), and generating tamper-evident evidence for third-party audit and dispute resolution (E4).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53]
- **F. Multi-Agent Systems:** Tracing cross-agent execution boundaries (F1) and inspecting agent-to-agent negotiation protocols (F2).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]
- **G. Operational Monitoring:** Tracking live agent availability and anomalous loops (G1), and forecasting infrastructure resource demands (G2).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]
- **H. Research and Improvement:** Discovering emergent failure modes (H1), gathering trajectory datasets for fine-tuning (H2), and benchmarking implementations across platforms (H3).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]
- **I. Identity and Ownership:** Resolving cross-surface identity (I1), tracking principal delegation across multi-host agent execution fabrics.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53]

# Lifecycle History
The use cases document was established in March 2026 within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3] In August 2026, the specification was formally updated to integrate tamper-evident evidence capture (E4) and cross-surface identity resolution (I1), reconciling the core catalog with the working group's priority tracking matrix.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation specification defining core agent execution entities, turn boundaries, causal relationship testing, and independent multi-reader interpretation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and correlation specification designed to represent the causal structure, decision sequences, and operational boundaries of AI agents.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42] Developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the model extends standard distributed tracing primitives to capture agent turns, multi-step planning, tool interactions, and delegation trees across heterogeneous runtimes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]

The specification addresses core failure modes where conventional traces lose causal integrity during record loss, duplicate transmissions, or message reordering by decoupling causal relationships from strict wall-clock time and runtime-private memory state.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]

# Architecture / Specification

## Conformance Test Kit and Relationship Verification
To ensure vendor-neutral telemetry interoperability, the specification defines a standardized test kit and contribution template (Task 4 of the execution plan):[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]
- **Relationship Integrity Checks:** Test fixtures evaluate whether exported traces maintain consistent causal relationships when records arrive out of order, are duplicated, or experience drops.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]
- **Synthetic Fixtures and Tooling:** The test kit pairs language-neutral synthetic payloads with explicit expected answers, reusing OpenTelemetry conformance tooling while asserting agent relationship models.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]
- **Content Privacy Segregation:** Test suites require opt-in content capture, maintaining strict separation between deterministic static fixtures and live runtime integration scenarios.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]

## Independent Multi-Reader Interpretation
To verify that the trace model avoids producer-specific lock-in, the specification mandates dual-reader independent verification (Task 7 of the execution plan):[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]
- **Dual Query Paths:** At least two independently implemented telemetry readers or query engines must process identical exported telemetry and reach consistent semantic conclusions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]
- **State Isolation:** Readers must operate without access to private runtime memory, hidden fixture mappings, or shared trace reconstruction libraries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]
- **Three-State Effect Reconciliation:** Conformance requires readers to reconcile incomplete or conflicting evidence consistently. For example, when an approval and execution record exist but an external service receipt is removed, both readers must report the outcome as "unconfirmed" rather than asserting that the action never occurred.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]

# Lifecycle History
The trace model is developed under a nine-task execution plan established by the Observability and Traceability Working Group following August 2026 technical sessions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45] Active workstreams focus on publishing the reusable relationship test kit (Task 4) and demonstrating independent reader interpretation across multi-agent exports (Task 7).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open threat models, security design patterns, cross-working-group review processes, and operational governance policies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes threat models, architectural security controls, privacy-enhancing practices, and cross-discipline review frameworks for agentic systems across the Agentic AI Foundation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076] The working group manages the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) guide and the [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]

Beyond authoring foundational security guidance, the group monitors international AI standards bodies and assesses container and microVM runtime isolation technologies for autonomous agent sandboxes.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Contribution Policies
The working group enforces several operational policies to maintain code and documentation quality:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]
- **Standing PR Review Windows:** Formal review windows and comment deadlines are codified into `CONTRIBUTING.md` to establish predictable merge timelines rather than per-pull-request negotiations.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]
- **Taxonomy Merge-After-Quiet-Period:** For terminology definitions, pull requests without active objections are merged following an agreed quiet period, with subsequent refinements handled through iterative Git commits.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]
- **AI Provenance in Definitions:** A dedicated taxonomy browser tool logs model provider tokens and records the human edit distance directly into commit messages, providing transparent provenance for AI-assisted definitions.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]

## Workstreams and Cross-Working Group Dependencies
The working group advances several active deliverables:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]
- **Security Best Practices:** Merging the first edition of the best practices guide and converting non-blocking review items into tracked GitHub issues.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]
- **Threat Modeling Framework:** Developing a comparative gap analysis evaluating CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF against agentic risks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist:** Operational reviews depend on formal delegate representation from peer working groups, including [Accuracy and Reliability](accuracy-and-reliability.md), [Workflows and Process Integration](workflows-and-process-integration.md), [Governance, Risk and Regulatory](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md), and [Agentic Commerce](agentic-commerce.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]
- **External Standards and Runtimes:** Coordinating with ETSI TC SAI regarding European Norm cybersecurity requirements for AI agents, and investigating microVM isolation technologies (such as Eclipse Enclave) to enforce hard network and execution boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]

# Lifecycle History
The working group holds biweekly technical meetings with alternating schedules to accommodate global participants across the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076] In September 2026, the group finalized the first iteration of the security best practices guide, adopted standing review windows, and instituted automated provenance recording for generated taxonomy contributions.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing shared agentic workflow execution models, reference architectures, workflow primitives, and enterprise process integration patterns.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (WG Workflows & Process Integration) develops standard execution primitives, interaction models, and vendor-neutral reference architectures for integrating autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents into enterprise workflows and business processes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. Chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato), the working group focuses on practical composition patterns, human approval checkpoints, boundary governance, and terminology harmonization across AAIF workstreams.

# Workstreams and Deliverables

The working group organizes its technical program across three primary workstreams [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]:

- **Taxonomy**: Responsible for defining core workflow primitives and execution vocabularies. In August 2026, the workstream delivered the group's first shipped asset, the Phase One Core Terms draft, becoming the first working group in the AAIF to formally deliver an asset through plenary approval [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. The taxonomy adopted "activity" as the foundational unit composed into "workflows" to avoid circular definitions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].
- **Reference Architectures**: Develops vetted, job-oriented architectural patterns and validation methodologies. Initial deliverables locked for charter completion include the [Workflow Architecture Principles](../guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md), the [Reference Architecture Contribution Guide](../guidelines/reference-architecture-contribution-guide.md), the [Single-Agent Human Approval Architecture](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) ("human-approved operation"), and the [Bounded Autonomous Remediation Architecture](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Catalogs production agentic implementations to validate proposed topologies and surface gaps in execution primitives and operational guidance [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

# Architecture / Specification

## Four-Outcome Validation Method

To evaluate reference architectures against real-world use cases without coupling to vendor-specific implementation details, the working group instituted an architectural fit assessment model [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]:

1. **Validated**: Direct architectural fit against a documented production use case where boundary controls and operational jobs match completely.
2. **Partial**: Alignment on core operational jobs but divergence in parallel execution topologies or state handoffs.
3. **Candidate**: Sound theoretical model awaiting verification against additional use case inventory entries.
4. **No Fit**: Structural mismatch between the proposed reference architecture and the execution boundaries required by the use case.

## Operational Governance

To prevent review bottlenecks and maintain architectural clarity, the working group maintains a standing rule capping pull requests at approximately 10 files, while deferring speculative primitives and oversized experimental prototypes into focused follow-up PRs [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

# Lifecycle History

- **August 2026**: Shipped Phase One Core Terms as the first completed AAIF deliverable [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. Merged the architecture principles and contribution guide, merged the human-approved operation reference architecture, finalized review for bounded autonomous remediation, and formulated the four-outcome validation method [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing agent telemetry, causal execution traces, protocol boundary metadata, and cross-surface behavioral auditing.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group (WG Observability & Traceability) establishes vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, causal execution data models, and cross-boundary correlation standards across agent runtimes, protocol gateways, and monitoring backends [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group ensures agent decision-making, planning, and tool interactions emit verifiable, tamper-evident telemetry without leaking raw chain-of-thought data or proprietary model internals.

# Workstreams and Deliverables

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Standardizing portable telemetry context and causal link structures across agents, SDKs, gateways, and [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) collector pipelines [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. Matthew Lee leads the implementation effort, developing reference libraries, synthetic workloads, and conformance suites [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability**: Led by Zayne Turner, defining boundary metadata mappings across agent-to-skill, skill-to-tool, agent-to-agent, and agent-to-MCP interfaces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Agent Resource Discovery (ARD) Trust-Pipeline Observability**: Joint effort with [Agent Gateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) tracing the full [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) lifecycle, spanning client discovery, identity verification, decision logging, and skill invocation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **State, Context & Reasoning**: Exploring causal tracking for retrieval, context assembly, and memory mutation across persistent agent runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

# Architecture / Specification

## Cross-Boundary Observability Model

The working group models agent operations across structured boundaries, mapping execution metadata to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions while contributing specialized attributes for multi-agent delegation, long-running durable executions, and verification audits [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. Seven domain terms were accepted into the AAIF global taxonomy in August 2026: Reasoning, Agent Trajectory, Context Propagation, Memory Access, Context Assembly, Retrieval, and Traceability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

## Governance and Consolidation

In August 2026, the working group folded its Multi-Agentic Observability - Orchestration & Coordination focus group directly into the broader WG plenary to streamline participation and align prototype validation with [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) reference architectures [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

# Lifecycle History

- **August 2026**: Confirmed initial scope for the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md), implemented ARD trust-pipeline demonstration with Agent Gateway, published the full-stack tracing landscape survey, and gained acceptance for seven core observability terms in the AAIF cross-WG taxonomy [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation specification defining core agent execution entities, turn boundaries, and portable context propagation across gateways and backends.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and correlation specification stewarded by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. It defines standardized metadata structures, turn boundaries, and causal trace linkages that preserve execution context across heterogeneous agents, SDKs, protocol proxies, and observability backends without replacing underlying telemetry protocols such as OpenTelemetry GenAI [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

# Architecture / Specification

## Portable Telemetry Context

The trace model uses portable telemetry context as an envelope mechanism to propagate causal relationships, task identifiers, and execution intent across asynchronous hops [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]:

- **Canonical Identifiers**: Unambiguous correlation keys spanning multi-agent delegation, subagent task dispatch, and durable execution recovery [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Plan-to-Execution Linking**: Explicit telemetry attributes connecting agent plans and selection decisions to subsequent tool calls and outcome states, avoiding the security and privacy risks of capturing raw internal chain-of-thought tokens [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Audit and Evidence Integrity**: Structured spans and verification attributes capturing policy decisions, discovery proofs, and permission evaluations across protocol gateways [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

## Implementation and Conformance Architecture

The model's delivery framework comprises three interdependent components [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]:

1. **Reference Library**: Standard implementation demonstrating context injection, extraction, and span enrichment for common agent execution frameworks.
2. **Synthetic Workloads**: End-to-end multi-agent scenarios designed to stress trace propagation across protocol boundaries and long-running sessions.
3. **Conformance Test Suite**: Validation harness evaluating whether SDKs, gateways, and observability sinks correctly preserve causal chains and span semantics.

# Lifecycle History

- **August 2026**: Initial scope locked by the Observability and Traceability Working Group, establishing portable context as a companion to OpenTelemetry GenAI and assigning reference implementation leadership to Matthew Lee [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

proposed_concept.title: Platform-Neutral Accuracy and Reliability Survey
proposed_concept.description: Platform-neutral 16-question survey instrument evaluating real-world AI system deployments, failure modes, accuracy challenges, and operational priorities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Platform-Neutral Accuracy and Reliability Survey is an empirical research instrument authored by the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) to gather structured data on production agentic AI deployments, operational failure modes, and industry mitigation strategies [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]. Designed to remain independent of any proprietary framework or model vendor, the survey collects standardized responses across engineering teams, operators, and researchers to inform AAIF benchmark profiles and reliability taxonomies.

# Architecture / Specification

## Survey Structure and Sections

The survey contains 16 questions organized into five structured sections [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]:

- **Section 1: Eligibility (Q1)**: Filters respondent organizations based on deployment lifecycle stage. Includes an early-exit branch directing ineligible participants to an informative exit page [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].
- **Section 2: About the System (Q2–Q5)**: Captures architecture topologies, agent autonomy levels, runtime integration patterns, and domain contexts. Q2 supports extensible write-ins via a required free-text field on selection of "Something else", while Q5 is optional [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].
- **Section 3: Benefits and Challenges (Q6–Q8)**: Assesses observed business benefits versus operational hurdles using 5-point choice matrices that include explicit "Not sure" response anchors [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].
- **Section 4: Accuracy and Reliability (Q9–Q13)**: Probes specific failure modes, hallucination frequency, deterministic verification approaches, human approval gates, and regression testing practices [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].
- **Section 5: Future Priorities (Q14–Q16)**: Evaluates organizational roadmap requirements for benchmarking, standardized evaluations, and guardrail architectures. Q16 provides optional qualitative feedback [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].

## Response Mechanics and Validation

All questions are mandatory with the exception of Q5 and Q16 [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]. The instrument incorporates deterministic branching logic for early screen-outs at Q1, matrix constraint validation, and inline text collection for open-ended category expansions to ensure analytical consistency across deployments [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].

# Lifecycle History

- **August 2026**: Merged complete platform-neutral 16-question specification, response mechanics, and validation flows into the Accuracy and Reliability Working Group repository under PR #9 [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open threat models, security design patterns, cross-working-group review gates, and runtime protection guidance for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (WG Security & Privacy) serves as the primary body within the Agentic AI Foundation defining security baselines, threat modeling frameworks, and privacy boundaries for autonomous agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. Chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), the working group formulates cross-cutting security patterns, reviews protocol implementations, and establishes evaluation standards for operational agent environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Active Workstreams

The group operates five principal technical tracks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]:

- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, this effort analyzes traditional threat modeling frameworks—such as OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF—while incorporating STRIDE, PASTA, and user-interface/human-user-agent (UI/HUA) considerations alongside Model Context Protocol security [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f] (see [../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md)).
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing practical guidance for agent builders covering credential isolation, identity delegation, and HUA execution paths [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f] (see [../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)).
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, formulating structured architectural blueprints and templates for secure agent deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Cross-Working Group Security Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing intake gates and security assessments across AAIF workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f] (see [../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)).
- **Taxonomy / Landscape Coordination**: Delegated to Jay White and Katherine Druckman, harmonizing privacy and security terms with the [../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Governance and Operational Focus

The working group adopted a public-by-default policy for general meeting recordings [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22]. In August 2026, the WG submitted a request to the [../governance/technical-committee.md](../governance/technical-committee.md) seeking clarification on how external donations—such as the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol—impact inter-group jurisdictional boundaries and cross-WG protocol security work [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Comparative gap analysis evaluating traditional cybersecurity methodologies, CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF against multi-agent autonomous runtime threat profiles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis is a technical assessment driven by the [../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to identify structural inadequacies when applying legacy software security methodologies to autonomous multi-agent architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. Under active development by workstream leads Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, the analysis maps conventional threat modeling systems against agent-specific risk surfaces [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Architecture / Specification

The gap analysis evaluates industry frameworks against agent-native vulnerabilities [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]:

- **Baseline Frameworks Evaluated**: Analyzes OWASP Top 10 for LLMs/Agentic systems, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and the NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Methodology Alignments**: Assesses how classic methodologies like STRIDE (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, Elevation of Privilege) and PASTA (Process for Attack Simulation and Threat Analysis) correspond to multi-step dynamic agent execution graphs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
- **Protocol and Interface Vectors**: Incorporates threat dynamics emerging from the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and user-interface/human-user-agent (UI/HUA) interaction channels [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Lifecycle History

The workstream draft (PR #8) entered active review in August 2026, establishing bi-weekly coordination sessions and integrating feedback regarding protocol boundary expansions and human-in-the-loop threat dimensions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing agent telemetry, causal execution traces, protocol boundary metrics, and operational evaluation across multi-agent environments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group (WG O&T) defines standardized telemetry models, distributed execution tracing, and cross-boundary observability specifications for autonomous AI agents [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38]. The working group establishes correlation standards across language model invocations, tool boundaries, inter-agent protocols, and host operating environments.

# Specifications and Key Initiatives

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model (ABTM)**: Developing the foundational specification for agent telemetry and turn-level causal graphs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38] (see [../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)). The group instituted a neutral trace model recommendation plan defining candidate evaluation criteria and adopt/extend/new decision paths [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].
- **Cross-Boundary Observability**: Specifying telemetry propagation across Model Context Protocol (MCP), CLI tools, and agent-to-agent interfaces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38] (see [../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md)).
- **External and Internal Liaison Operations**: Maintains a formal liaison tracker coordinating with OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, W3C Trace Context, Agent Trace, Monocle, and AGNTCY, as well as internal AAIF working groups [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18].
- **Operational Requirements and Prior Work**: Maintaining structured catalogs of production use cases, evidence requirements, and ecosystem tooling comparisons [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38] (see [../resources/agent-observability-use-cases.md](../resources/agent-observability-use-cases.md) and [../resources/agent-observability-prior-work.md](../resources/agent-observability-prior-work.md)).

# Lifecycle History

In August 2026, the group delivered its monthly report covering the ABTM scope, scheduled September implementation milestones, and published cross-boundary telemetry contributions for [../governance/technical-committee.md](../governance/technical-committee.md) review [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38].

proposed_concept.description: Structured catalog categorizing agent observability requirements across operational domains, evidence assurance ladders, and jurisdictional legal compliance boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog compiles functional, diagnostic, and audit telemetry requirements for autonomous agents across nine operational domains [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]. Managed by the [../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the catalog maps developer tracing, evaluation instrumentation, and legal-evidentiary requirements to cross-boundary agent telemetry models.

# Architecture / Specification

The catalog organizes requirements across several core structures [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]:

- **Operational Domains**: Covers debugging, performance diagnostics, security forensics, multi-agent coordination, human-in-the-loop supervision, and regulatory compliance.
- **Evidence-Grade Ladder Qualification**: Employs distinct alphanumeric grades to designate verification rigor (e.g., integrity protection, hardware attestation, immutable append-only logs), explicitly distinguished from section use case identifiers to avoid numbering collisions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].
- **Jurisdiction and Legal Weight Requirements**: Mandates that where telemetry obligations derive from legal or statutory duties (such as EU AI Act record retention or timestamping under RFC 3161), the record must state the governing jurisdiction and legal role of the record holder [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]. Technical timestamping integrity is decoupled from legal evidentiary weight, which remains determined by the relying party's jurisdiction [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].

# References

Complementary prior-work analysis and ecosystem telemetry benchmarks are tracked in [../resources/agent-observability-prior-work.md](../resources/agent-observability-prior-work.md).
