proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog
proposed_concept.description: Architectural catalog defining reusable, implementation-independent security and privacy design patterns for agentic AI runtime governance and containment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog is an architectural reference produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) that establishes reusable, implementation-independent patterns for mitigating recurring security and privacy challenges in agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8]. The catalog provides structural design templates applicable across platforms, frameworks, deployment models, and execution environments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8].

Positioned as a foundational architectural tier, the catalog directly complements the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md), providing the theoretical and architectural mechanisms that the guide translates into practical operational and implementation guidance[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8].

# Architecture / Specification
The catalog categorizes recurring architectural mechanisms and trade-offs across eight core domains[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8]:
- **Runtime Security and Governance**: Boundary controls, policy mediation, and containment for executing agents.
- **Agent Control and Containment**: Enforcement mechanisms governing tool invocation, blast radiuses, and agent lifecycle states.
- **Secure Tool Invocation**: Verification, authorization gates, and protection around external API, tool, and service interactions.
- **Agent Memory Protection**: Lifecycle management and integrity safeguards for short-term and persistent agent memory stores.
- **Privacy-Preserving Execution**: Data sanitization, context scoping, and prevention of cross-boundary data leakage.
- **Secure Multi-Agent Collaboration**: Trust evaluation and message protection during peer delegation.
- **Security Monitoring and Intervention**: Continuous observation, auditability, anomaly detection, and out-of-band intervention.
- **Auditability and Recovery**: Verifiable state logging and post-incident restoration mechanisms.

The catalog explicitly scopes identity establishment, authentication, and credential management as upstream inputs managed by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8].

# Lifecycle History
The catalog was initiated as Working Draft 0.1 within the Security & Privacy Working Group's design patterns workstream[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3bbe1dee7e1d-99b84ed8].

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless triage agent and sandboxed GitHub Actions runner executing Flue 2.0 workflows with automated dual-leg model health canaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Submission Analyser is a headless triage agent and GitHub Actions runner deployed across AAIF repositories to evaluate incoming proposals, issues, and pull requests against working group submission guidelines and architectural taxonomy criteria[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10]. Built on Flue 2.0, the analyser executes structured assessment prompts using foundation model providers while enforcing strict read-only execution boundaries during automated diagnostic evaluations[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].

# Architecture / Specification
The agent workflow operates in automated CI environments and incorporates a dedicated daily model canary pipeline to detect endpoint entitlement shifts, token expirations, and provider outages prior to production triage runs[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10]:
- **Dual-Leg Canary Matrix**: Evaluates both primary (`claude-opus-4.7`) and fallback (`gpt-5.4`) Copilot models independently with `fail-fast: false` to ensure an outage on the primary path does not mask a broken fallback leg[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].
- **Dry-Run Isolation**: Canary executions set `DRY_RUN=1` against a fixed, closed issue, performing full analysis and rendering while omitting Google Workspace and Discord publishing credentials[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].
- **Least-Privilege Token Permissions**: Execution relies on GitHub token permissions (`copilot-requests: write`, `contents: read`, `issues: read`) rather than personal access tokens (PATs), binding Copilot inference entitlement directly to the repository organization[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].

# Lifecycle History
The daily model canary pipeline was introduced into `.github/workflows/canary.yml` to protect against silent endpoint breaking changes and entitlement revocations on the individual Copilot endpoint[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes telemetry formats, causal trace models, evaluation harnesses, and protocol boundary metrics across agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59]. The group defines observability specifications spanning kernel, network, application, and model layers to enable transparent inspection and post-mortem evaluation of autonomous agents.

In governance coordination with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group implements standardized cadence tracking and health metrics following [working group reporting templates](../guidelines/working-group-reporting-template.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group produces core standards and architectural references, including protocol boundary models for MCP and tool CLIs, the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md), and telemetry integration guides for OpenTelemetry and Linux tracing tools.

Operational governance incorporates automated health reporting[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9373ed8bd5e2-54fdeb4c][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59]:
- **Monthly Metrics Automation**: A scheduled GitHub Actions workflow executes on the 1st of each month using the `issue-metrics` action to calculate monthly open/closed counts, time-to-first-response, and resolution durations for issues and pull requests[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9373ed8bd5e2-54fdeb4c][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59].
- **Reporting Issue Generation**: Aggregated monthly data is automatically compiled and published as a repository issue labeled `monthly-report` for inclusion in monthly Technical Committee review submissions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9373ed8bd5e2-54fdeb4c][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59].

# Lifecycle History
In September 2024, the working group automated monthly reporting metrics via GitHub Actions in response to Technical Committee review feedback[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59].

proposed_concept.title: Approval Checkpoint
proposed_concept.description: Runtime governance pattern binding human or policy approval records to exact execution payloads and tracking decision, execution, and confirmed effect as separate audit records.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Approval Checkpoint pattern binds an authorized human or policy decision to the exact action payload that executes, enforcing strict validity windows and maintaining three structurally decoupled audit records: decision, execution attempt, and confirmed effect.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5] Maintained under the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) design patterns catalog, the pattern mitigates failure modes where approval flags are reused after expiration, applied to modified parameters, or conflated with confirmed downstream execution.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern formalizes enforcement semantics across three distinct lifecycle phases:

1. **Binding Approval to Action**: An approval record explicitly binds the action or tool identifier, target resource, arguments (either directly or as a cryptographic digest over a named canonical serialization), constraints, approver identity, validity interval, and usage limits.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5] For sensitive payloads, digests preserve data minimization. Where dynamic variance is legitimate (such as timestamps), allowed variance fields must be explicitly enumerated.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]
2. **Execution-Point Verification**: Verification occurs strictly at the enforcement point where the action is executed. The enforcement point independently recomputes bound fields and digests directly from the candidate payload, ignoring self-reported claims from the agent.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5] Validity intervals are verified against the enforcement point's clock with defined skew tolerance. If an approval record fails integrity verification, it is flagged as an integrity failure rather than a mismatch; if unavailable, execution is denied.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]
3. **Tripartite Record Decoupling**: Systems must record decision, execution, and effect as separate, correlated entities:
   - **Decision Record**: Captures the approval authority, validity window, and bound action digest.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]
   - **Execution Record**: Tracks the execution attempt using an execution identifier assigned by the enforcement point, against which usage quotas are charged.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]
   - **Effect Record**: Documents the confirmation returned by the downstream target service, correlated by a service-scoped receipt identifier. Absence of confirmation designates an unconfirmed effect, not non-occurrence.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]

# Lifecycle History
Candidate specification drafted by the Security and Privacy Working Group within the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md) as pattern category Runtime Governance (SP-XXX).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26] Intersects with the [Kill Switch](kill-switch.md) pattern when cooling-off queues hold high-risk actions pending release.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]

# References
- Catalog Draft: `workstreams/design-patterns/DRAFT-approval_checkpoint_pattern.md`[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]
- Implementation Guidance: [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]

mutations.rationale: Update pattern with authoritative details from PR #26 covering out-of-band containment loops, shutdown resistance, asynchronous task orphaning, and open discussions on credential revocation handling.

proposed_concept.title: Kill Switch
proposed_concept.description: Architectural control plane pattern establishing an independent, out-of-band containment loop to halt agent execution, sever network communication, invalidate credentials, and roll back state.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Kill Switch pattern establishes an independent, out-of-band runtime control plane capable of immediately halting an agent's execution, severing its external network communications, revoking active session credentials, and initiating state rollback outside the agent's internal reasoning loop.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01] Designed for systems architects and safety engineers, the pattern addresses fundamental agentic failure modes where naive OS-level process termination (`SIGKILL`) fails due to model evasion, shutdown resistance, machine-speed runaway feedback loops, credential leakage, or orphaned asynchronous background tasks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern separates declarative trigger criteria (policies defining when to stop) from technical enforcement architecture, organizing runtime containment into a coordinated three-phase loop: **detect → halt → rollback**.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]

- **Containment Execution**: Execution termination is managed entirely server-side, isolated from the agent's prompt context and memory to prevent model subversion.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]
- **Network and Tool Denial**: Immediately blocks tool dispatch interfaces, agent-to-agent gateways, and outbound network traffic to prevent lateral movement.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]
- **Credential Revocation**: Automatically invalidates ephemeral tokens, API keys, and session delegations across all distributed components to decommission background scripts and child tasks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]
- **Reversibility and Rollback**: Reads the in-flight execution log (such as the execution records structured under [Approval Checkpoint](approval-checkpoint.md)) to trigger compensating transactions against external services using both execution and service identifiers.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]

Working group discussions track an open implementation risk where in-process sidecars or SDK enforcement points receive HTTP 401/403 errors upon policy credential revocation; systems must ensure such rejections are treated as hard refusals and circuit-breaker events rather than failing open as transient network outages.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27]

# Lifecycle History
Merged into the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md) as a foundational containment pattern.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26] Complements [Attested Isolated Runtime](attested-isolated-runtime.md) for hardened enforcement boundaries and protected credential release.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]

# References
- Catalog Draft: `workstreams/design-patterns/DRAFT-kill_switch_pattern.md`[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]
- Working Group Discussion: Issue #27 on credential revocation interaction with circuit breakers[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27]

proposed_concept.title: Attested Isolated Runtime
proposed_concept.description: Architectural security pattern isolating policy evaluation and evidence signing inside hardware-attested enclaves to secure agent governance when operating on untrusted infrastructure.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Attested Isolated Runtime pattern (also known as TEE-isolated agent runtime or confidential agent execution) isolates policy enforcement and audit evidence generation within a hardware-attested Trusted Execution Environment (TEE), leaving the primary agent workload outside the enclave boundary.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb] Developed by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the pattern addresses scenarios where an agent processes regulated or confidential data on infrastructure operated by an untrusted third party (such as public cloud providers or partner tenants), rendering policy verdicts, execution measurements, and audit trails tamper-evident against privileged host operators.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern structures confidential governance across four architectural requirements:

1. **Enforcement Isolation**: The policy enforcement point runs inside a hardware enclave while the LLM or agent runtime remains outside, mitigating the threat of privileged host inspection or in-memory manipulation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]
2. **Enclave Key Generation**: Cryptographic signing keys are generated inside the enclave boundary and sealed to hardware measurement registers, ensuring that relying parties can verify that logs and decisions originated from untampered policy bundles.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]
3. **Policy Sealing and Appraisal**: Governance policies are sealed to specific measurement baselines, releasing secrets or authority credentials only when remote attestation appraisal succeeds.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]
4. **Verifiable Unit-of-Work Evidence**: Emits verifiable attestation evidence per transaction, enabling relying parties (such as peer agents, tool APIs, or external auditors) to appraise compliance without direct access to runtime infrastructure.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]

# Lifecycle History
Drafted as the initial pattern under the Privacy-Preserving Execution topic area in the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26] Works in tandem with [Kill Switch](kill-switch.md) for scoped credential release and [Approval Checkpoint](approval-checkpoint.md) for immutable decision logging.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]

# References
- Catalog Draft: `workstreams/design-patterns/DRAFT-attested-isolated-runtime.md`[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d74b6b55d493-0ef833eb]

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog
proposed_concept.description: Architectural catalog defining reusable, implementation-independent security and privacy design patterns for autonomous and agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog is an open repository workstream maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) that documents reusable, vendor-neutral architectural patterns for designing secure and privacy-respecting agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50] Led by Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase), the catalog establishes standardized pattern templates, domain classifications, and baseline criteria for runtime governance, containment, and confidential computation across AAIF initiatives.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]

# Architecture / Specification
The catalog organizes patterns into specialized domains and requires all submissions to adhere to a normative template structure defining intent, problem forces, solution mechanics, consequences, and validation criteria.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50] Core active pattern drafts include:

- **Runtime Governance**: [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) (binding authorizations to executed actions and decoupling decision, execution, and effect records).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]
- **Control and Containment**: [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) (out-of-band runtime execution halts, lateral network denial, and credential revocation).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]
- **Privacy-Preserving Execution**: [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) (hardware-enforced enclave policy isolation and verifiable execution evidence).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26]

# Lifecycle History
Established under PR #26 with initial drafts for Approval Checkpoint, Attested Isolated Runtime, and Kill Switch.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26] Maintained collaboratively with contributions across member organizations including Circle, JPMorgan Chase, IBM, TELUS, Global Payments, Huawei, Bluerock, and Ericsson.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50]

# References
- Catalog Index: `workstreams/design-patterns/README.md`[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50]
- Workstream Landing Page: `workstreams/design-patterns/DRAFT-design_patterns_catalog.md`[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering secrets management, MCP protocol security, skill supply-chain verification, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and incident forensics for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide provides practical, actionable controls and architectural decision frameworks for builders designing and deploying agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] Authored within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) as Deliverable 4, the guide synthesizes implementation-level recommendations spanning secrets management, secure tool invocation under the Model Context Protocol (MCP), skill verification, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066] It explicitly scopes out underlying workload identity and delegation-chain architectures, deferring identity federation, SPIFFE/SVID attestation, and capability token standards to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]

# Architecture / Specification

### 1. Secrets Management
Static, long-lived credentials stored in environment variables, filesystem layers, or memory represent an active attack surface subject to extraction via prompt injection or unsafe deserialization (e.g., CVE-2025-68664).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] The guide mandates shifting from static secrets to short-lived, ephemeral attestations prioritized across five tiers:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]
- **Workload Identity:** Native platform-attested identities (AWS IRSA, GCP Workload Identity, Azure Managed Identity) generating short-lived (1-hour) tokens, eliminating static credentials from environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]
- **Dynamic Secrets Engines:** Per-request credential generation with configurable TTLs (e.g., HashiCorp Vault) for databases and third-party APIs.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]
- **Network-Layer Injection:** Sidecar or proxy injection isolating credentials entirely from the agent runtime for legacy interfaces.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]
- **Confidential Computing:** Hardware-protected enclaves (Intel TDX, AMD SEV-SNP) providing memory isolation and enclave-attested key release for high-assurance or multi-tenant workloads.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]
- **OAuth Token Exchange (RFC 8693):** Per-hop credential scope reduction during delegation chains.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]

### 2. Secure Tool Invocation and MCP Protocol Security
MCP tool invocation surfaces risks including [tool poisoning](../taxonomy/tool-poisoning.md) (e.g., instructions hidden in tool descriptions via invisible Unicode tags), [rug pulls](../taxonomy/rug-pull.md) (unannounced metadata mutations), cross-server shadowing, and conversation hijacking.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf] Defense requires both connection-level and content-level verification:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]
- **Pre-Deployment Server Evaluation:** Mandatory source repository validation, activity verification (≥90-day threshold), cross-referencing public vulnerability registries, and static/runtime vulnerability scans (such as Cisco MCP Scanner or Invariant mcp-scan).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]
- **Transport Enforcement:** Treating stdio MCP servers as untrusted local binaries requiring isolated sandbox execution; requiring OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, TLS, and token audience binding (RFC 8707) across all HTTP connections.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]
- **Gateway Traffic Mediation:** Routing multi-server agent traffic through mediation proxies such as [agentgateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) for unified policy enforcement, payload inspection, and tool description hash auditing.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]
- **Supply Chain & Skill Verification:** Automated pre-scanning of skills using dataflow analysis to block undeclared domains and dynamic execution constructs (`eval()`), combined with manual verification of declared permissions against stated purpose.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]

# Lifecycle History

The guide was developed under the lead of Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson) with contributions from 17 participating organizations.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066] Draft v0.1 was reviewed and approved to merge via PR #9 during the September 29, 2026 working group meeting, transitioning the deliverable into an actively maintained living document.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821] Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam serve as mandatory reviewers for future guide revisions, and changes to the deliverable adhere to the foundation's contributor rule prohibiting authors from self-merging deliverable PRs.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]

# References

- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)
- [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)
- [agentgateway](../resources/agentgateway.md)
- [Attested Isolated Runtime Pattern](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)
- [Tool Poisoning](../taxonomy/tool-poisoning.md)
- [Rug Pull](../taxonomy/rug-pull.md)

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open threat models, security design patterns, cross-working-group review checklists, and operational best practices for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the mission of the Agentic AI Foundation by establishing security and privacy as a shared, proactive discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56] The working group develops vendor-neutral threat models, architectural design patterns, operational security best practice guides, and security review checklists that consumers, infrastructure providers, and peer working groups adopt to distribute responsibility for safe agent autonomy.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]

# Architecture / Specification

### Governance and Leadership
The working group operates under leadership appointed by Platinum and Gold members with terms extending from March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]
- **Chair:** Alex Frazer (Runlayer)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]
- **Co-Chair:** Junjie Bu (Google)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]

Working group decisions govern pull requests and repository hygiene under formal review standards: PR authors are prohibited from self-approving or self-merging pull requests that land changes in the `deliverables/` folder, while workstream leads retain direct editorial velocity in dedicated workstream directories.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]

### Meetings and Cross-Region Operations
The group holds biweekly general meetings on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT via LFX Zoom.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56] To accommodate contributors in Asia-Pacific and South American time zones (such as Japan and Brazil), the group established a six-week trial of an alternate-week APAC meeting tentatively scheduled for 10:00 PM ET, bridged directly by Alex Frazer to maintain continuous alignment across both cohorts.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]

### Deliverables Portfolio
The working group drives five primary deliverables:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b]
1. **Shared Taxonomy and Landscape:** Cross-working-group vocabulary aligning definitions for constraints, guardrails, and agent interfaces, supported by custom contribution helper tooling.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]
2. **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design:** Structured framework led by Fernando Lucktemberg evaluating existing frameworks (e.g., OWASP, CSA MAESTRO) and scheduling dedicated threat modeling sessions.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]
3. **Design Patterns Catalog:** Implementation patterns led by Sagar Dashora and Dan Kommatas addressing containment mechanisms such as kill switches and hardware-attested enclaves.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b]
4. **[Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md):** Practical builder guidance led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam addressing secrets elimination, MCP protocol hardening, and skill validation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]
5. **[Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md):** Review questionnaire led by Govindaraj Palanisamy to audit peer working group deliverables against fundamental baseline controls.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]

# Lifecycle History

The working group initiated orientation sessions in February 2026, adopted its core mission and deliverable slate in April 2026, and officially ratified its charter on May 26, 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b] GitHub repositories transitioned to public status in June 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b] In late September 2026, the group addressed the influx of AI-generated public pull requests, initiated an APAC meeting branch, and merged the v0.1 release of the Security Best Practices Guide as an active living standard.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821]

# References

- [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md)
- [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)
- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Create Chapter Skill
proposed_concept.description: Automated chapter provisioning and estate maintenance engine managing template cloning, paragraph-level text rebranding, and map projection calculations for new regional chapters.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-create-chapter` skill provisions and initializes digital assets for newly formed Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) regional chapters by cloning canonical Google Drive templates, rebranding document and slide contents, and computing accurate geographic map markers[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]. It functions as a specialized automation engine within [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md).

# Architecture / Specification
The chapter creation engine is implemented in `scripts/create_chapter.py` and enforces several deterministic processing guarantees[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]:

- **Paragraph-level Rebranding**: To prevent formatting errors and text-run splitting in Office Open XML (OOXML), the engine concatenates paragraph text runs, executes rebranding transforms on the complete string, and writes the output into the initial text run[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]. City abbreviation casing (such as `SF`) is dynamically evaluated based on adjacent context.
- **Gall Stereographic Map Projection**: Presentation decks place location markers on slide 5 via `reposition_map_marker`. The calculation converts latitude and longitude coordinates to canvas pixels using a Gall Stereographic projection where `lon2x` is linear in longitude and `lat2y` is linear in `(1 + √2/2)·tan(lat/2)`[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49].
- **Projection Calibration**: The projection mapping was fitted against Natural Earth 110m coastlines composited over template map imagery (`image18.png`), achieving a mean residual of 0.64 pixels; calibration optimizes against coastline vertices rather than historic hand-placed slide dots[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49].
- **Drive Layer Integration**: Cloud asset operations utilize Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) endpoints (`files.copy`, `create`, `get`, `update`)[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49].
- **Offline Validation**: The engine provides an offline `--rebrand-local` mode that accepts explicit `--lat` and `--lon` coordinates to verify local template copies against regression suites without initiating network calls or external mutations[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49].

# Lifecycle History
Maintained in the `aaif/community-events` repository, calibrated against San Francisco baseline assets and verified using unit test suites that enforce canvas boundary limits and shape guards[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Audit Slack Skill
proposed_concept.description: Configuration-driven Slack inspection skill auditing chapter channels, organizer rooms, and regional rosters against centralized chapter records.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-audit-slack` skill provides diagnostic verification of Slack channels and memberships across Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) chapter communities, reconciling local workspace states against centralized intake records and roster spreadsheets[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]. It detects configuration drift, missing member joins, and critical exposure risks.

# Architecture / Specification
The audit suite is split into specialized sub-engines emitting HTML summaries and machine-readable `audit.json` caches[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]:

- **Organizer Engine (`audit_organizers.py`)**: Reconciles accepted organizers against channel memberships by querying Slack API methods (`conversations.list`, `conversations.members`, `users.lookupByEmail`, `users.info`)[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]. Email serves as the sole identity join between intake sheets and Slack accounts.
- **Pre-provisioning Flag (`--planned-ok`)**: Accounts for the transition window before channels are instantiated or while temporary private squat channels await admin conversion, downgrading missing or private channels to planned notes rather than aborting execution[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].
- **Roster Ingestion Precedence**: Matches intake rules where human assignment in `Chapter` takes precedence over `City (New)` and `City (Existing)` fields. Status filtering strictly matches exact strings `Accepted` and `Existing (from MLOps)`[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].
- **Severity Classification**: A public organizer channel (`-organizers`) represents the highest-severity finding (`public!`), alerting administrators that sensitive logistical, financial, or speaker communications are exposed to the general workspace[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].
- **Source of Truth Invariant**: The authoritative channel map resides in the centralized Chapters List; inconsistencies must be fixed in the upstream spreadsheet rather than modified within generated audit reports[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].

# Lifecycle History
Developed in `aaif/community-events` as part of the shared operations infrastructure defined in [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md)[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation specification defining core agent execution entities, turn boundaries, and an evidence-first four-phase execution plan for standardizing agent behavioral traces.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and correlation specification defined by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to establish standardized semantics, entity relationships, and causal trace boundaries across heterogeneous agent runtimes and frameworks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

# Architecture / Specification
Responding to inconsistent GenAI convention support across commercial and open-source agent SDKs, the specification's roadmap centers on empirical trace observations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]:

- **Four-Phase Evidence-First Plan**: Restructures execution into four sequential phases—agree, evidence, interpret, and contribute—driven by an active register of observed telemetry gaps[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].
- **Baseline Reference Implementation**: Uses the open-source AAIF agent [Goose](../resources/goose.md) as the primary baseline implementation for capturing and evaluating OpenTelemetry signals[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].
- **Charter Dimension Coverage**: Establishes milestone 1 criteria delineating modeled, enabled, and deferred coverage across the working group's three foundational behavioral dimensions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].
- **Upstream OpenTelemetry Alignment**: Channels empirical findings into targeted contribution proposals for OpenTelemetry semantic convention working groups[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

# Lifecycle History
Originated in the AAIF Observability and Traceability Working Group, transitioning from parallel task tracks to an evidence-led milestone schedule scheduled for initial draft delivery in late 2026[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability and Authorization Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Packaging conventions, capability abstractions, directory resolution, and runtime authorization boundaries ensuring cross-client interoperability for agent plugins and skills.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Plugin Portability guidelines establish architectural conventions, capability abstractions, and mandatory authorization boundaries for packaging agent plugins and skills across heterogeneous client environments such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

# Architecture / Specification
Portable agent plugins adhere to standardized manifests, directory isolation, and permission boundaries[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]:

- **Manifest Hierarchy**: A root `plugin.json` serves as the canonical shared manifest under the [Agent Plugins](../standards/agent-plugins.md) specification for cross-client compatibility, while client-specific manifests (such as `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) provide catalog overlays without duplicating skill definitions[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- **Path Resolution via `<skill-root>`**: File paths within skill specifications must be relative to the directory containing `SKILL.md`. Instructions use `<skill-root>` as an abstract placeholder resolved by the agent runtime rather than an environment variable or hardcoded path[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- **Capability Abstractions**: Workflows and skills declare standard capability primitives rather than vendor-specific tool names, including reading bundled files, executing Python/subprocesses, reading web pages, presenting local files, and requesting human approval[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- **Authorization and Mutation Boundaries**: Invoking or loading a skill does not constitute grant of mutation authority. Operations remain strictly read-only by default; write flags (`--write`, `--apply`, `--create`) and explicit approval tokens (`--i-have-approval`) require distinct human confirmation before execution, adhering to [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- **Secret and Context Isolation**: Secrets must be resolved exclusively through environment variables or secure keychains and never echoed into prompts, CLI arguments, or generated reports[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

# References
- [Agent Plugins Standard](../standards/agent-plugins.md)
- [Agent Skills Standard](../standards/agent-skills.md)
- [Human Approval Gate Pattern](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Create Chapter Skill
proposed_concept.description: Automated chapter provisioning, estate maintenance, and asset lifecycle engine executing template rebranding, coordinate projections, in-place renames, and batch backfills.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-create-chapter` skill provisions, rebrands, renames, and maintains local AAIF chapter workspaces and presentation collateral across Google Workspace and OOXML documents.[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3] In addition to initial cloning and localized branding from template structures, the skill provides dedicated maintenance operations for in-place chapter renaming and batch estate backfills covering geographic projections, footer templates, and working group project rosters.[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62]

# Architecture / Specification

### Chapter Renaming (`rename_chapter.py`)

Renaming an active chapter applies an in-place transformation across four decoupled surfaces to maintain estate consistency without corrupting package relationships:[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]

1. **Drive Folder Structure**: Renames the chapter root folder (e.g., `Scotland` to `Edinburgh`).
2. **File and Subfolder Names**: Renames chapter spreadsheets and assets (e.g., `Scotland CRM.xlsx`).
3. **OOXML Text Ingestion**: Modifies text occurrences within `.docx`, `.pptx`, and `.xlsx` archives (e.g., `AAIF Scotland` to `AAIF Edinburgh`).
4. **Document Metadata (`docProps`)**: Updates Dublin Core and extended document properties holding chapter labels.

To prevent broken external references, relationship parts (`.rels`) exclusively receive slug substitutions and are protected from generic city name replacements.[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3] Luma event slugs are preserved unless explicitly passed via `--slug-from` and `--slug-to`, preventing 404 generation when chapter event URLs remain decoupled from municipal renames.[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3] Pre-flight backups are written to `backups/rename-<UTC>/` before uploads occur.

### Estate Backfill Framework

Estate maintenance scripts operate in plan-first mode by default, executing read-only audits that compute drift before any write operation is dispatched:[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62]

- **Map Dots (`backfill_map_dots.py`)**: Re-positions geographic markers on presentation slide 5 using the Gall Stereographic projection. Target coordinates are joined from the `Generated Geolocation` column in the central tracking sheet via Google Drive folder URLs rather than folder names.[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62] Decks matching within a 1-pixel tolerance are treated as no-ops.
- **Host Footer (`backfill_host_footer.py`)**: Replaces and harmonizes host and sponsor footers across template decks.
- **Projects Roster (`backfill_projects.py`)**: Synchronizes technical project listings and foundation working group summaries across chapter slide templates.

# Lifecycle History

Originally designed for initial chapter provisioning and Drive cloning, the skill was expanded to cover operational recovery routines following the capital-city migration and projection formula alignments.[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62] [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification Schema
proposed_concept.description: Classification taxonomy and schema defining core architectural dimensions and supporting fields to categorize real-world production agent workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Use Case Classification Schema is an analytical framework established by the Critical Use Cases workstream of the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to describe and compare agentic workflows across production deployments.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc] The schema defines twelve columns categorized into five structural classification dimensions and seven supporting descriptors evaluated against cited production systems rather than generic use case titles.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc]

# Architecture / Specification

### Core Classification Dimensions

A classification dimension captures a deliberate structural design fork rather than an observational artifact of an execution trace:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc]

- **Trigger**: The event initiating execution, categorized into external system events, automated or recurring schedules, or direct human invocation.
- **HITL Pattern**: The placement and requirement of human intervention, mapping where a human participant must review, modify, or approve workflow progression.
- **Agent Count**: The number of independent reasoning entities deployed, reflecting intentional separation of tool permissions, domain models, or task boundaries.
- **Coordination**: The runtime control plane deciding subsequent actions, contrasting deterministic code or scripted state machines with runtime LLM-driven planning.
- **Workflow Pattern**: The macroscopic structural execution topology, such as linear sequential pipelines, parallel fan-out/join branches, or bounded evaluation loops.

### Supporting Implementation Fields

Seven descriptive and evidentiary fields record deployment specifics without functioning as fixed categorical dimensions:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc]

- **Duration**: Measured runtime of agent execution, strictly isolating active agent reasoning and tool usage from time spent in human approval queues or downstream systems.
- **Descriptive Identity**: Free-text identification comprising `Use Case`, `Description`, and `Tools & Systems`.
- **Evidentiary Context**: Verifiable implementation rationale documented via `Key Failure Mode`, `Preconditions`, and `Notes`.

# Lifecycle History

Maintained as a foundational schema for the companion [Use Case Inventory](../resources/agentic-use-case-inventory.md), the framework remains subject to harmonization with reference architecture design principles.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Use Case Inventory is an empirical catalog maintained by the Critical Use Cases workstream of the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303] It compiles named, production-deployed agentic workflows to extract recurring workflow shapes and architectural configurations using the criteria set forth in the [Agentic Use Case Classification Schema](../resources/agentic-use-case-classification.md).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303]

# Architecture / Specification

### Evidentiary Standard

Each row in the inventory represents an explicit deployment and must satisfy strict verification requirements to qualify as architectural evidence:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303]

- **Citation Target**: Each entry requires at least one verified, publicly accessible citation (with a target of three) confirming active production deployment.
- **Preferred Evidence**: Vendor announcements or product releases referencing an explicit, named customer deployment.
- **Acceptable Evidence**: Vendor product documentation showing substantial feature evidence demonstrating operation at scale, even if a customer entity is unnamed.
- **Unacceptable Sources**: Secondary blog commentary, analyst projections, academic prototypes, individual implementer notes, or unverified personal knowledge.
- **Supporting References**: Technical guides, architecture whitepapers, or engineering writeups may be cited within classification notes to clarify operational mechanisms, but only when referencing an already-verified primary vendor deployment.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303]

# Lifecycle History

The inventory workstream transitioned category groupings, classification schemas, and evidentiary standards toward formal working group review while actively verifying source citations and field values for catalog entries.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Working Group Meeting Notes Skill
proposed_concept.description: Progressively disclosed agent skill converting LFX meeting recordings, transcripts, and AI summaries into standard AAIF working group meeting notes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-wg-meeting-notes` skill standardizes how working group chairs draft, clean up, and publish meeting summaries across the Agentic AI Foundation.[^evt-working-group-chairs-file-fc8df0f0524f-110370cf] It consumes raw AI-generated summaries, meeting transcripts, and recording links, transforming them into a structured markdown document aligned with foundation reporting conventions.[^evt-working-group-chairs-file-8f3607b2d562-057d3b11]

# Architecture / Specification
The skill enforces explicit input requirements and evidentiary heuristics before emitting finalized meeting notes [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-fc8df0f0524f-110370cf]:

- **Required Inputs**: Working group name, meeting date in `YYYY-MM-DD` ISO format, resource URLs (AI summary, transcript, recording), and raw text bodies for both the AI summary and full transcript.
- **Truth Resolution Rule**: Whenever the AI summary and transcript contradict one another, the transcript is treated as authoritative and takes precedence.
- **Decisions vs. Deliverables vs. Action Items**: Decisions are recorded only when the group reached consensus during the call. Deliverables denote formal artifacts produced by the working group (such as specifications or reports), whereas Action Items record granular operational tasks assigned to individuals. Action item owners and due dates must never be hallucinated; missing fields default to `TBD`.
- **Empty Sections**: Any section without applicable content is marked with `- None` rather than omitted.

### Output Template Structure
Generated records follow a mandatory structural template [^evt-working-group-chairs-file-8f3607b2d562-057d3b11]:
1. `# <Working Group Name>`
2. `## Meeting — YYYY-MM-DD`
3. `## Resources` (links for AI Summary, Transcript, and Recording)
4. `## Topics Discussed`
5. `## Decisions`
6. `## Deliverables`
7. `## Action Items` (table with `Owner`, `Action`, and `Due` headers)

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Community Estate Sync Skill
proposed_concept.description: Procedural estate synchronization orchestrator executing reconciliation across Slack and Google Drive chapters with non-destructive retirement candidate reporting.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-sync` skill automates estate synchronization and operational state auditing across AAIF community assets, including Google Workspace sheets and Slack channels.[^evt-community-events-pr-55] It reconciles roster changes, chapter organizer qualifications, and event trackers while safeguarding historical data against accidental automated deletion.

# Architecture / Specification
The synchronization engine follows strict non-destructive state management principles for chapter records [^evt-community-events-pr-55]:

- **Non-Destructive Row Preservation**: Chapter rows on the central Chapters List are never cleared or deleted automatically by the sync engine. This invariant prevents accidental destruction of renamed cities, shadow chapters operating without rosters by design, and hand-written operational metadata such as Chapter Summary, Image links, and Ops Notes.
- **Retirement Candidates**: Live chapter rows lacking a qualifying local organizer are reported as retirement candidates rather than wiped. Formal retirement requires explicit human action by designating `Status=Deprecated`, or `Status=Merged` along with a corresponding `Merged Into` target.
- **Ambiguity Holds**: The engine holds chapter status and suppresses candidate flagging when organizer city data is ambiguous, such as malformed row data, near-miss naming, or unresolved organizers already assigned to the chapter.
- **Drift Reporting**: Retirement candidates surface on the run report Drift tab as pending human decisions. Because automated runs cannot clear them, candidate listings leave sync exit codes unchanged to avoid perpetual drift alerts.

# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Inventory is an empirical catalog maintained by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) documenting reusable workflow patterns extracted from real-world agentic software.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46] It operates as a classification and evidence-sourcing initiative rather than an architectural prioritization exercise, grounding pattern definitions in confirmed commercial and open-source deployments.

# Architecture / Specification
The inventory functions alongside the [use case classification schema](agentic-use-case-classification.md) and enforces strict evidentiary rules [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46]:

- **Evidentiary Standard**: Every use case Notes field must cite a vendor product page or primary technical announcement demonstrating a confirmed, live production deployment. Speculative designs or unverified prototypes are excluded.
- **Citation Targets**: Each documented use case requires at least one verified deployment citation, with three citations serving as the target benchmark for cross-industry validation.
- **Source Hierarchy**: Sources are evaluated against preferred, acceptable, and unacceptable tiers to ensure objective auditability.
- **Verification Lifecycle**: Workstream schemas and category definitions are formally voted on by the working group, while individual inventory rows, citations, and classification values remain subject to ongoing maintainer verification.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering secrets management, protocol boundaries, and a tripartite people-process-technology security feature matrix.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guideline provides implementation-focused defense recommendations for autonomous agent developers, harness maintainers, and runtime operators.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20] Maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), it links high-level agentic threat models with concrete operational, administrative, and technological controls.

# Architecture / Specification
To ensure actionable adoption, each security best practice is mapped against a structured feature matrix categorizing supporting capabilities across three primary pillars [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]:

- **People**: Capabilities that require specialized skills, role-specific training, security knowledge, and operational awareness across personnel managing or deploying agentic systems.
- **Process**: Controls that mandate formalized operational strategies, documented organizational policies, repeatable review workflows, or standard operating procedures governing how security is carried out.
- **Technology**: Technical implementations consisting of physical or digital tooling, hardware primitives, sandboxed software execution layers, and automated policy enforcement systems.

This classification ensures that agentic defense strategies do not rely solely on automated guardrails or manual review in isolation, mandating balanced coverage across organizational, procedural, and technological boundaries.

# Overview
The `aaif-clean-data` operational skill provides automated data normalization and hygiene tooling for community intake pipelines, Google Sheets trackers, and chapter management records.[^evt-community-events-pr-56] It enforces proposal-execution splits, preview safety guarantees, and deterministic formatting rules across multi-tab event and chapter workbooks.

# Architecture / Specification
The skill operates as a CLI utility (`clean.py`) adhering to non-destructive inspection patterns:

- **Preview Safety**: Read-only previews run by default, evaluating workbook tabs and reporting whether an execution pass with `--write` would alter data.[^evt-community-events-pr-56]
- **Chapter Review Flags (`clean.py chapter-flags`)**: Applies red conditional formatting to unparsed city fields where user input begins with `Other` (case-insensitive) across intake forms (`Form Responses`) and role sheets (`Organizers`, `Hosts`, `Speakers`).[^evt-community-events-pr-56]
- **Formatting Scoping**: Formatting operations target single column ranges, replacing only tool-owned rules without modifying cell values, role tab formulas, or existing chapter assignments.[^evt-community-events-pr-56]
- **Verification and Guardrails**: Post-write readbacks confirm rule integrity, and test suites guard against PII leakage and formula overwrites.[^evt-community-events-pr-56]

# Lifecycle History
- **PR #56 (Merged)**: Added the `chapter-flags` subcommand to highlight `Other` city responses in red for chapter review without altering data values.[^evt-community-events-pr-56]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Blog Guidelines establish editorial standards, neutrality principles, stylistic requirements, and review processes for publications on the Agentic AI Foundation blog.[^evt-foundation-pr-7] The guidelines ensure technical rigor, ecosystem vendor-neutrality, and consistent terminology across contributor submissions.

# Architecture / Specification
Editorial contributions must adhere to core stylistic and structural requirements:

- **Language and Casing**: Submissions must follow US English spelling conventions and sentence-case capitalization across titles and section headers.[^evt-foundation-pr-7]
- **Factual Claims and Neutrality**: Categorical or sweeping assertions must be backed by verifiable data; unsupported claims are prohibited.[^evt-foundation-pr-7]
- **Source Attribution**: Claims regarding external architectures, benchmarks, or protocols must provide direct primary-source hyperlinks rather than secondary aggregations.[^evt-foundation-pr-7]
- **Official Naming**: Open-source projects, working group outputs, and foundation bodies must use their official recognized names and abbreviations consistently.[^evt-foundation-pr-7]

# Lifecycle History
- **PR #7 (Open)**: Proposed standardizing sentence case, US English spelling, official project naming, and primary-source link requirements while disallowing unsupported categorical claims.[^evt-foundation-pr-7]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering secrets management, context redaction, host sandboxing, and protocol boundaries for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide establishes actionable security controls for engineering, configuring, and deploying autonomous AI agents and harnesses.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33] It outlines vulnerability mitigation strategies spanning secret leakage, host privilege escalation, and memory-based persistence.

# Architecture / Specification
The guide defines threat vectors and protective controls across agent configuration and execution lifecycles:

- **Configuration Auditing**: Secret auditing must inspect client configuration files (`.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `claude_desktop_config.json`) and skill bundles that frequently embed plaintext API credentials in repository environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33]
- **Context and Memory Redaction**: Tool outputs containing environment variables or authorization tokens must be redacted before entering transcripts, causal traces, or persistent agent memory to prevent memory-based privilege retention (OWASP ASI03).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33]
- **Host Boundary Sandboxing**: Deny-rules at execution hooks must block access to ambient host credentials, such as SSH keys, browser cookies, and cloud CLI session caches, paired with short-lived tokens to mitigate sandbox escapes.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33]
- **Standards Alignment**: Maps threat surfaces to recognized industry classifications, specifically OWASP MCP01 and ASI03.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33]

# Lifecycle History
- **Issue #33 (Open)**: Identified auditing gaps in the quick start guide regarding agent config repositories, transcript credential leakage into agent memory, and host-level credential access during sandbox breakouts.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33]

# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an AAIF technical body tasked with establishing failure mode taxonomies, verification frameworks, and empirical evaluation benchmarks for agentic AI deployments.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-10] It coordinates cross-working-group efforts to identify reliability bottlenecks across production agent systems.

# Architecture / Specification
ARWG organizes work into sequenced milestone deliverables and empirical studies:

- **Deliverable 1 (D1)**: Focuses on baseline failure mode taxonomy and categorization of agentic unreliability.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-10]
- **Deliverable 2 (D2)**: Implements the [Accuracy and Reliability Survey](../resources/accuracy-and-reliability-survey.md), gathering empirical data on deployment failure patterns, verification pipelines, and runtime monitoring.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-10]
- **Phase 2 Execution**: Prepares cross-working-group coordination for advanced evaluation harnesses and mitigation strategies.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-10]

# Lifecycle History

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering secrets management, context redaction, host sandboxing, and protocol defenses for agentic workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide provides actionable implementation guidance for developers and operators deploying autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agent systems. Developed by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the deliverable focuses on credential isolation, runtime execution sandboxing, tool supply-chain defense, and protocol-level boundary mediation.

# Architecture / Specification

### Threat Taxonomy and Framework Mapping
The best practices guide maps behavioral agent threats and operational mitigations against standardized industry frameworks, specifically MITRE ATLAS and the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (ASI)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32]. Active integration efforts align specific risk areas to ATLAS v5.6.0 technique codes and ASI classifications[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32]:
- **Credential Access and Leakage:** Addressing prompt injection dumps and environment harvesting via AML.T0055 (Unsecured Credentials), AML.T0083 (Credentials from AI Agent Configuration), AML.T0106 (Exploitation for Credential Access), and ASI03[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32].
- **Tool and Supply Chain Poisoning:** Mitigating description poisoning, tool shadowing, and [rug pulls](../taxonomy/rug-pull.md) via AML.T0110 (AI Agent Tool Poisoning), AML.T0104 (Publish Poisoned AI Agent Tool), AML.T0010.005, and ASI02/ASI04[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32].
- **Context and Memory Integrity:** Countering state corruption and exfiltration using AML.T0080 (AI Agent Context Poisoning: Memory/Thread) and ASI06[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32].
- **Autonomous Execution Containment:** Enforcing delegation limits, circuit breakers, and [kill switches](../patterns/kill-switch.md) mapped to AML.T0101 and ASI08/ASI10[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32].

### Sandboxing and Host Isolation Boundaries
While execution sandboxing restricts filesystem interactions to working-directory scope, security reviews emphasize that sandbox mode alone does not contain all blast radiuses[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34]. Specifically, host sandboxes may narrow local filesystem permissions but remain vulnerable to egress leaks via alternate runtimes and trust handoffs where an agent writes a payload that an unconstrained host process subsequently executes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34]. Comprehensive isolation requires paired network egress controls and host execution barriers.

### Confidential Computing and Credential Lifecycles
Deploying agents inside confidential computing environments protects guest memory from unauthorized hypervisor or host inspection, but hardware isolation does not eliminate bearer token exposure risks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37]. If guest software leaks or mishandles a bearer token, the token's validity window and permission scopes dictate the blast radius[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37]. Confidential virtual machines must therefore be coupled with short-lived credentials, explicit authorization checks, and strict in-guest access boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37].

# Lifecycle History

Originally drafted under pull request #9 within the Security and Privacy Working Group, the deliverable entered review tracking for framework alignment and threat model precision[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32]. Subsequent issues #32, #34, and #37 track open refinements concerning ATLAS/ASI tagging, sandbox containment bounds, and guest credential exposure models[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37].

# References

- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)
- [Kill Switch Pattern](../patterns/kill-switch.md)
- [Rug Pull](../taxonomy/rug-pull.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation specification defining core agent execution entities, turn boundaries, and OpenTelemetry semantic conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry specification stewarded by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md). It standardizes the representation of agent execution cycles, causal reasoning steps, tool interactions, and protocol boundaries across heterogeneous multi-agent frameworks.

# Architecture / Specification

### OpenTelemetry Alignment and Semantic Conformance
Rather than introducing a distinct telemetry format, the model reframes its scope around identifying semantic gaps in existing [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) implementations and standardizing agent-specific semantic conventions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd]. While many modern agent software development kits (SDKs) integrate OpenTelemetry, they emit divergent and semantically inconsistent span attributes, event hierarchies, and turn boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

The specification focuses on:
- **Semantic Convergence:** Defining canonical attribute names and structure for agent model invocations, prompt iterations, context injections, and tool dispatches[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].
- **Upstream Contribution:** Submitting standardized agent telemetry conventions directly to OpenTelemetry and related industry bodies[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].
- **Conformance Framework:** Establishing testable conformance criteria to validate that agent SDKs and runtimes emit interoperable, semantically aligned traces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

### Industry and Liaison Engagement
To ensure multi-runtime interoperability, the working group coordinates conformance and semantic alignment with external standards organizations, including FINOS for compliance testing, and engages ecosystem liaisons across major cloud and AI infrastructure providers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

# Lifecycle History

Originally proposed as an independent agent execution trace specification, the working group adjusted strategy during its September 2026 proceedings to target OpenTelemetry semantic harmonization and conformance benchmarking directly[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

# References

- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing vendor-neutral standards for telemetry, distributed execution tracing, performance monitoring, and auditability across autonomous agent systems. The working group develops specifications, white papers, and semantic conventions bridging agent runtimes and observability backends.

# Architecture / Specification

### Key Deliverables and Initiatives
- **[Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md):** Harmonizing agent execution telemetry by identifying semantic gaps in [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md), contributing upstream conventions, and authoring a conformance framework for agent SDKs[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].
- **Agentic Observability White Paper:** Producing practical practitioner guidance addressing debugging, system reliability, cost governance, and telemetry collection across enterprise deployments, accompanied by interactive demonstrations and potential IETF RFC submissions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].
- **Cross-Workstream Attestation:** Coordinating with the [Attestation and Evidence Working Group](../working-groups/attestation-and-evidence.md) on joint initiatives for verifiable execution records and compliance logging[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

### Contribution and Operational Governance
The working group institutes human-in-the-loop contribution policies requiring human participation in substantive architectural decisions while leveraging automated agents for initial formatting, linting, and error detection reviews[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd]. Terminology and taxonomy maintenance transitioned from spreadsheets to structured GitHub issues to improve traceability and community discovery[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

# Lifecycle History

In September 2026, the working group consolidated its telemetry strategy around OpenTelemetry semantic convergence, initiated planning for practitioner white papers, and established liaison tracks with external bodies such as FINOS for conformance validation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

# References

proposed_concept.title: Workflow Primitives
proposed_concept.description: Structural vocabulary and modular execution primitives standardizing agent task boundaries, execution steps, budgets, and handoff contracts.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Workflow primitives provide a foundational, composable vocabulary and structural execution building blocks defined by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]. The catalog standardizes common operational units—such as triggers, agent steps, execution budgets, and handoffs—enabling consistent cross-architecture composition across single-agent and multi-agent reference systems [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29].

# Architecture / Specification
The primitive framework organizes workflow execution across modular categories and boundary contracts [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]:

- **Primitive Catalog (P1–P19)**: Identifies shared runtime building blocks including `Trigger`, `AgentStep`, `Budget`, and `Handoff` [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]. A subset (P1–P12) specifically defines the core control loop for single-agent systems incorporating human approval checkpoints [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-54].
- **Boundary Contracts**: Defines strict invariant contracts across primitive transitions, specifically mandating schema satisfaction for the `AgentStep` boundary and `Handoff` interfaces [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29].
- **Multi-Agent Topologies (T1–T6)**: Standardizes execution network topologies that route inter-agent communication, coordinating with patterns like [parallel-fan-out-and-join](../patterns/parallel-fan-out-and-join.md) and [branch-isolation](../patterns/branch-isolation.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29].

# Lifecycle History
Originally drafted as part of the foundational taxonomy for the Workflows and Process Integration WG, the primitive set was expanded under draft PR #29 to formalize the P1–P19 catalog, contracts, and multi-agent topologies [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]. PR #54 subsequently mapped primitives P1–P12 directly into the [single-agent-human-approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) reference architecture [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-54].

# References
- Workflows and Process Integration Working Group: [working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)
- Single-Agent Human Approval: [architectures/single-agent-human-approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md)

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Human Approval
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture establishing an enforceable human approval gate and structural separation between agent proposal generation and execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Single-Agent Human Approval reference architecture establishes an enforceable human authorization gate and architectural separation between an agent's proposal generation and its concrete execution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-54]. It formalizes how autonomous task loops pause execution at defined policy boundaries, transferring mutable execution intent to human reviewers through deterministic verification interfaces [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-54].

# Architecture / Specification
The architecture synthesizes core workflow primitives and structural governance patterns:

- **Primitive Alignment (P1–P12)**: Grounded in workflow primitives P1 through P12, mapping explicit stages for invocation triggers, context assembly, proposal synthesis, and checkpoint transitions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-54].
- **AgentStep and Handoff Contracts**: Enforces formal boundary contracts on each primitive transition, requiring verifiable state snapshots prior to entering approval states [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29].
- **Proposal-Execution Split**: Integrates the [proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) pattern, preventing direct tool dispatch by the planning agent without an out-of-band authorization record [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-54].
- **Durable Checkpoints**: Employs [durable-wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md) and [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) patterns to persist pending proposals without consuming active compute or risking race conditions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-54].

# Lifecycle History
Authored within the [workflows-and-process-integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) working group, this reference architecture was initially structured around human-in-the-loop governance patterns. PR #54 aligned the architecture with the standardized P1–P12 workflow primitives catalog to ensure consistency with broader multi-agent architectures [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-54][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29].

# References
- Workflow Primitives: [taxonomy/workflow-primitives](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md)
- Workflows and Process Integration Working Group: [working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)
