proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards, delegation models, and cross-organizational trust frameworks for autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group establishes vendor-neutral standards, verifiable delegation models, and cross-organizational trust frameworks for agentic systems [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12]. Operating across decentralized identifiers, verifiable credentials, and hardware-rooted attestation, the working group standardizes how autonomous agents authenticate, establish identity provenance, and prove delegation bounds to relying parties [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's charter focuses on identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12]. Key architectural areas include:

- **Attestation Component Decomposition**: Addressing architectural gaps where hardware attestation signs over execution environments but lacks uniform links to agent identities [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12]. Proposals decompose the monolithic attestation block into three distinct layers:
  1. *Platform Evidence*: Signed hardware/firmware measurement reports and endorsement chains (e.g., AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX, NVIDIA H100) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].
  2. *Identity Binding*: Cryptographic statements tying an agent identifier or public key to platform measurements via structures like `REPORT_DATA`, paravisor runtime claims `user-data`, or TPM quote `qualifyingData` [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].
  3. *Appraisal*: Relying party policy evaluation generating trusted verification verdicts [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].
- **Cross-Group Coordination**: Delegates runtime confidential execution mechanics to [security-and-privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) (such as the [attested-isolated-runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) pattern) while maintaining focus on identity claims and trust semantics [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].

# Lifecycle History
The Identity and Trust WG charter initially established single-box attestation components within its reference architecture. In Issue #12, maintainers proposed the three-part decomposition into platform evidence, identity binding, and appraisal to resolve cross-platform verification failures across Azure Confidential VMs, GCP N2D SEV-SNP, and GPU environments [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12].

# References
- Attested Isolated Runtime: [patterns/attested-isolated-runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)
- Security and Privacy Working Group: [working-groups/security-and-privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream harmonizes terminology, conceptual models, and ecosystem mapping across all Agentic AI Foundation working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79]. Operating through cross-working-group liaisons, the workstream curates universal vocabularies, vertical domain terms, and landscape classifications into unified, machine-readable specifications [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream manages definition lifecycles, contributor tooling, and terminology indexes [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79]:

- **Taxonomy Data Architecture**: Maintains foundational terms across universal, security, observability, workflows, and commerce domains. PR #79 transitioned data storage from dynamic JavaScript modules (`taxonomy-data.js`) to structured JSON (`taxonomy/taxonomy.json`) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79].
- **Schema Validation with Zod**: Validates contributor entries against standardized schemas using Zod, eliminating custom JavaScript syntax parsers in CI pipelines and preventing execution of contributor-controlled code [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79].
- **Explorer and Automation**: Provides interactive explorer tools and CI validation workflows to verify entry completeness, field boundaries, and cross-references [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79].

# Lifecycle History
Initially maintained as structured JavaScript data files, the taxonomy source was refactored in PR #79 into declarative JSON paired with Zod schema validation to streamline intake and reduce syntax parsing errors [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Working Group Meeting Notes Generator
proposed_concept.description: Progressively disclosed agent skill converting LFX meeting recordings, transcripts, and AI summaries into standardized working group meeting notes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-wg-meeting-notes` skill provides an automated, standardized procedure for transforming raw meeting records—including meeting recordings, automated transcripts, and AI-generated summaries—into structured Markdown meeting notes for Agentic AI Foundation working groups [^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]. Originally developed as internal prompts within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the skill has been genericized across the foundation to ensure consistent archival and reporting practices [^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].

To prevent unnecessary context consumption, the skill adheres to a strict on-demand loading model and requires explicit naming during agent invocation [^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].

# Architecture / Specification

### Package Layout and Progressive Disclosure

The skill is packaged as an independent folder containing two required artifacts [^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]:
- `SKILL.md`: Runtime instructions directing the agent how to parse transcript timelines, reconcile conflicting topic summaries, and extract firm consensus items.
- `template.md`: Canonical output schema constraining the generated document structure.

The skill does not load into the agent context window by default; users must explicitly invoke it by name (for example, `Using the aaif-wg-meeting-notes skill, write the notes for the meeting`) [^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].

### Ingestion and Section Mapping

The agent processes three primary inputs: LFX or platform meeting recordings, full transcripts, and automated AI summaries. It maps these sources into five standardized document sections [^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]:
1. **Topics Discussed**: Core technical discussions and debate threads.
2. **Decisions**: Explicit determinations reached by attendee consensus or chair ruling.
3. **Deliverables**: In-flight specifications, whitepapers, or repository contributions.
4. **Action Items**: Assigned tasks with designated owners and target completion dates.
5. **Source Links**: Direct references linking back to the raw recording, full transcript, and source AI summary.

# Lifecycle History

- Proposed in `aaif/working-group-chairs` PR #2 as part of the shared agent skills initiative for foundation leadership, adapting prompts proven in the Security & Privacy WG [^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Working Group Monthly Report Generator
proposed_concept.description: Reusable agent skill synthesizing monthly working group meeting notes, GitHub repository activity, and previous reports into standardized Technical Committee updates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-wg-monthly-report` skill automates the monthly synthesis of working group progress for submission to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]. It ingests historical meeting notes, repository commits and pull requests, and prior monthly reports to generate a draft report matching the [Working Group Reporting Template](../guidelines/working-group-reporting-template.md) [^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].

The skill outputs candidate reports to `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md`, establishing an explicit proposal stage before the working group chair reviews and submits a formal pull request [^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].

# Architecture / Specification

### Package Organization

Following AAIF skill conventions, the component is distributed as a directory containing [^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]:
- `SKILL.md`: Procedural instructions detailing input aggregation, delta identification across months, and tone normalization.
- `template.md`: Schema matching the foundation-wide monthly report standard.

### Input Sources and Synthesis Model

The agent reconciles three distinct evidence surfaces [^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]:
1. **Monthly Meeting Notes**: Notes produced by [`skills/aaif-wg-meeting-notes`](../skills/aaif-wg-meeting-notes.md) capturing decisions and action item completions during the calendar month.
2. **GitHub Activity**: Pull requests, merged specifications, and closed issues within the respective working group repository.
3. **Prior Month Report**: The preceding submission, used to verify progress against committed milestones and carry forward ongoing deliverables.

### Ecosystem Highlights

The template guides the agent to contextualize group accomplishments against external industry milestones (e.g., OWASP, AARM, Model Context Protocol developments), allowing working groups to adjust ecosystem domain references as appropriate [^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].

# Lifecycle History

- Proposed in `aaif/working-group-chairs` PR #2 as a shared governance skill adapted from operational workflows established in the Security & Privacy WG [^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Engine
proposed_concept.description: Procedural operations pipeline and shared infrastructure managing chapter provisioning, estate lifecycle sync, and intake normalization across AAIF chapters.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Event Operations Engine (`community-event-operations`) is the shared operational infrastructure managing AAIF local chapter provisioning, access control synchronization, Slack workspace auditing, and intake data hygiene [^evt-community-events-pr-57]. The pipeline enforces deterministic mapping between applicant intake forms, Google Drive asset estates, CRM trackers, and communication channels [^evt-community-events-pr-57].

To accommodate nationwide organizing models, the engine provides runtime city folding that aggregates municipal chapters into unified country chapters while preserving backward-compatible intake values [^evt-community-events-pr-57].

# Architecture / Specification

### Country Chapter Folding (`chapter_for`)

In `lib/aaif_events/cities.py`, the `chapter_for()` resolver establishes centralized chapter normalization [^evt-community-events-pr-57]:
- Metropolitan city names selected in intake forms are folded into designated country chapters (e.g., Tokyo maps to `AAIF Japan`; Wellington and Auckland map to `AAIF New Zealand`) [^evt-community-events-pr-57].
- All downstream engines reading city data—including `sync_chapters.resolve_city`, `sync_about`, `sync_crm`, `sync_access`, and the Slack channel audit—must resolve cities through `chapter_for()` to prevent dual-chapter registration bugs [^evt-community-events-pr-57].
- In [`skills/aaif-clean-data`](../skills/aaif-clean-data.md), `COUNTRY_CHAPTER_FOLDS` explicitly overrides the persistent Chapters List so that retired municipal rows cannot reclaim reassigned cities [^evt-community-events-pr-57].

### Migration Execution Precedence

Because folds execute dynamically at runtime, physical asset updates must strictly precede codebase synchronization merges [^evt-community-events-pr-57]:
1. Target rows in the Chapters List, Google Drive directories, CRM entries, Luma event pages, and About documentation must be renamed first.
2. Code-level fold definitions are merged subsequently; merging prior to asset renames causes synchronization daemons to interpret the fold as a novel chapter, generating duplicate rows and overwriting organizer rosters [^evt-community-events-pr-57].

# Lifecycle History

- Updated via PR #57 in `aaif/community-events` to consolidate Tokyo into AAIF Japan and Wellington/Auckland into AAIF New Zealand [^evt-community-events-pr-57].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing agent telemetry, causal execution traces, protocol boundary metrics, and layered systems observability across AI runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group develops open standards, telemetry models, and comparative evaluations for monitoring agentic AI workflows and runtime infrastructure [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721]. Its work spans from foundational binary trace formats up through kernel metrics, hardware accelerator tracing, network protocol capture, and high-level agent telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721].

The group produces the AAIF Reference Architecture Assessments, evaluating tracing and profiling platforms through the specific lens of agentic infrastructure demands [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721].

# Architecture / Specification

### Five-Layer Assessment Stack

The working group organizes its reference architecture assessments across a bottom-up five-tier stack [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721]:

1. **Layer 01 — Foundations**: Trace encoding mechanisms and baseline formats, including the [Common Trace Format](../resources/common-trace-format.md), Linux tracing framework trade-offs ([LTTng vs. perf vs. FTrace](../resources/linux-tracing-comparison.md)), and multi-trace correlation engines ([Trace Compass](../resources/trace-compass.md)).
2. **Layer 02 — Kernel Tracing**: OS-level instrumentation and resource attribution, covering FTrace, Linux perf, LTTng-UST, kernel driver tracepoints, hypervisor pre-emption/stolen-time dynamics, container cgroup CFS throttling, and runtime syscall security monitoring (Falco, Sysdig).
3. **Layer 03 — Hardware Accelerators**: GPU and NPU kernel dispatch profiling, tensor core utilization, and framework-to-hardware correlation across vendors.
4. **Layer 04 — Network**: Wire-level protocol inspection, packet capture, and transport validation for agentic interfaces.
5. **Layer 05 — AI Agent Observability**: High-level execution telemetry, including runtime lifecycle events, LLM tracing backends, and agent product analytics sinks.

This layered model underpins the group's cross-boundary observability frameworks, ensuring agent reasoning steps can be causally mapped to underlying kernel, accelerator, and network events [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721].

# Lifecycle History

- Active technical working group chartered by the Technical Committee.
- Established the structured five-tier tracing landscape assessment catalog in `aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group bridging global AI policy developments and technical agentic systems, tracking regulatory frameworks, AI BOMs, and evidence logging standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment (GRRA) Working Group serves as a bridge between global AI policy developments and technical advancements in agentic AI systems within the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]. Approved on June 1, 2026, and chaired by Deborah Eng with co-chair Sriram Natarajan, the working group addresses gaps in cohesive regulatory guidance, standards interoperability, and risk mitigation strategies for organizational agent deployments [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].

# Scope and Deliverables
The working group's technical activities span policy monitoring, governance architecture, and compliance gap analysis [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]:

- **Policy and Standards Tracking**: Identifying and monitoring emerging global AI regulations and standards impacting agentic systems, including the EU AI Act, TC260 guidelines, and national agentic frameworks [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf, ^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].
- **Organizational Protocol Governance**: Examining enterprise implementation of protocols such as MCP within existing corporate governance processes [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].
- **Future Specifications**: Developing proposals for an [AI Agent Bill of Materials](../taxonomy/ai-agent-bill-of-materials.md), action reversibility and undo infrastructure, human-in-the-loop patterns, incident reporting policies, and vertical domain frameworks like the FINOS AI Governance Framework [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].
- **Phase 2 Gap Analysis**: Evaluating conformity anchors for tamper-evident logging across converging standards including ISO/IEC 24970, prEN 18229-1, and IETF draft-sharif-agent-audit-trail, distinguishing self-reported telemetry from independently attestable records [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-9].

Explicitly excluded from the group's scope is providing formal legal advice or commercial compliance solutions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].

proposed_concept.title: Identity & Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards, delegation models, and cross-organizational trust architectures for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity & Trust (I&T) Working Group promotes vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization within the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]. Approved on May 12, 2026, and chaired by Grant Miller, the group establishes mechanisms that allow agents to be discovered across platforms, prove operational provenance, convey delegated human or organizational authority, and enable auditable cross-boundary interactions [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059].

# Scope and Boundaries
The working group's scope covers six technical dimensions [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059]:

- **Agent Identity, Authentication, and Provenance**: Mechanisms for uniquely identifying agents, authenticating sessions, and conveying operational provenance.
- **Delegation and Authority Chains**: Formats for representing agents acting on behalf of humans, teams, or services, including authorization boundaries.
- **Authorization and Consent Models**: Short-lived, fine-grained authorization patterns, human approvals, and policy constraints governing agent actions.
- **Trust Evaluation**: Frameworks for reasoning about cross-organizational agent verification and policy compliance.
- **Agent Discovery Metadata**: Metadata schemas supporting discovery, trust establishment, and alignment with [Observability & Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md).
- **Enterprise and Consumer Contexts**: Coverage across organizational deployments and consumer agent architectures.

Explicitly out of scope are ratifying formal standards on behalf of external SDOs, defining comprehensive execution security controls (governed by [Security & Privacy](security-and-privacy.md)), normative ethical frameworks, and running production identity infrastructure [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-e2016059].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol gap analyses, and lifecycle evidence standards for autonomous commercial transactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group establishes vendor-neutral capability maps, protocol gap analyses, and lifecycle standards governing AI-mediated and autonomous commercial transactions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]. The group focuses on defining purchasing, authorization, payment execution, and dispute workflows across agent, platform, merchant, payment provider, and risk system perimeters [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].

# Capability Map and Verification Contracts
The working group's Capability Map and Gap Analysis deliverable defines core capabilities across all purchasing phases [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]:

- **Evidence Binding**: Post-purchase audit records binding claimed commercial actions to delegation IDs, transaction IDs, shopper identities, and signed claims to resolve disputes without renegotiation [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
- **Signal Provenance**: Multi-party source attribution distinguishing self-reported from independently observed signals across merchants, agents, platforms, and payment providers [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
- **Authorization Strength for State Changes**: Required proof bundles and renewed human approvals governing order modifications, cancellations, refunds, and dispute initiations [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
- **Verdict Envelope Specification**: A standardized, machine-readable contract containing three-state classifications (`supported`, `contradicted`, `unresolvable`), verifier identity and signature, RFC 8785 evidence fingerprints, evaluated verification checks, witness scope, and freshness timestamps [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
- **Cross-WG Alignment**: Coordinating with [Identity & Trust](identity-and-trust.md) for delegation and identity primitives, and [Observability & Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md) for audit log and telemetry boundaries [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].

proposed_concept.title: Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual identity rules, typography tokens, official vector logo asset inventory, and trademark usage policies governing AAIF materials.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Brand Guidelines govern visual identity, typography tokens, surface palettes, and official logo assets across Agentic AI Foundation digital repositories, event collateral, and publications [^evt-community-events-pr-41]. The guidelines ensure consistent, high-fidelity visual presentation across both human contributor assets and automated agent tooling [^evt-community-events-pr-41].

# Logo Asset Inventory and Usage Rules
Official vector assets are maintained in repository asset trees and indexed in source-of-truth tables to facilitate immediate discovery [^evt-community-events-pr-41]:

- **Authoritative Vector Assets**: Primary logo files are located in `assets/`, including `aaif-mark.svg` (which constitutes the complete full lockup despite its filename), alongside auxiliary lockups and chapter icons [^evt-community-events-pr-41].
- **Redrawing Prohibition**: Contributors and automated asset-generation agents are strictly prohibited from redrawing, tracing, or approximating the AAIF mark from screenshots or raster artifacts; all production assets must reference official vector files directly [^evt-community-events-pr-41].
- **Agent Discovery Layout**: Design documentation must surface logo inventory and asset paths in top-level tables rather than concluding sections, ensuring single-hop resolution by automated agents [^evt-community-events-pr-41].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to establishing comprehensive threat modeling methodologies, reusable security design patterns, cross-working-group review workflows, and implementation best practices for autonomous agent deployments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e]. The working group operates across multiple workstreams to ensure consistent security postures and verification baselines across agent runtimes, protocol adapters, and memory substrates.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its technical agenda across five core workstreams established during its formation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e]:
- **Threat Modeling and Gap Analysis**: Analyzes traditional cybersecurity frameworks against unique agentic risks, publishing comparative gap assessments such as the [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].
- **Security Best Practices**: Produces practical builder guidance, operational controls, and runtime hardening recommendations detailed in the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) and associated feature matrix[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Curates reusable, implementation-neutral security architectures and containment structures documented within the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].
- **Cross-WG Security Review**: Maintains evaluation checklists and lightweight review workflows—such as the [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)—to assess security implications across foundational specifications and reference architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Coordinates security and privacy nomenclature with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to ensure consistent terminology across cross-working-group deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].

# Lifecycle History
The working group transitioned from formation into execution in mid-2026, progressing through structured governance milestones reported to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e]:
- **June 2026**: Five core workstreams launched with confirmed leads; initial drafting began for threat modeling and best practices, and taxonomy work transferred to the cross-WG effort[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].
- **July 2026**: Initial pull requests published for the threat modeling gap analysis and best practices guide; design patterns catalog structure finalized[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].
- **August 2026**: Meeting recordings opened to the public, internal pull request merge governance validated, and cross-WG review coordination expanded[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].
- **September 2026**: Initial deliverable suite officially merged and registered as Drafts in the repository deliverables directory; initial design pattern drafts landed, merge governance rules instituted, and alternate-week APAC meetings initiated to accommodate global participation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture governing iterative, autonomous problem resolution of business tasks through bounded activities, deterministic gates, and fail-safe escalations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Bounded Autonomous Remediation Reference Architecture governs automated, multi-step problem resolution workflows operating under strict constraints, deterministic convergence criteria, and out-of-band escalation paths[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49]. The architecture distinguishes between an admitted **business task**—the overarching problem unit or bounded operational incident assigned to an agent execution run—and discrete **activities**, which represent the localized workflow subunits executed during remediation loops[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49].

# Architecture / Specification
The reference architecture organizes remediation execution into coordinated structural components that isolate diagnostic investigation, remediation planning, and corrective actions:
- **Task Admission and Boundary Scoping**: Ingests an incoming business task, validating that required telemetry, policy bounds, budget limits, and blast-radius thresholds are explicitly defined prior to activation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49].
- **Remediation Loop Activities**: Decomposes problem handling into discrete activities executed within a [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md), iteratively collecting diagnostics, evaluating hypotheses, and proposing targeted configuration changes or runtime repairs[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49].
- **Verification Gates**: Validates candidate remediations against a [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) or routes sensitive state modifications through an [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) before execution[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49].
- **Containment and Escalation**: Enforces budget ceilings, iteration limits, and [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) capabilities, aborting remediation activities and escalating the business task to human incident responders whenever anomalies or timeout thresholds occur[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49].

## Terminology Invariants
To prevent ambiguity across workflow components and lifecycle states, the architecture enforces strict semantic separation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49]:
- **Business Task**: The admitted, high-level operational problem, ticket, or remediable incident handled by a single workflow run[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49].
- **Activity**: An individual, granular workflow step or execution subunit executed by an agent or harness during investigation, mitigation, or verification cycles[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49].

# Lifecycle History
- **Proposed**: Formulated within the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md).
- **Terminology Alignment**: Updated in draft review to standardize 'business task' as the admitted problem scope and 'activity' as the workflow execution subunit across lifecycle definitions, gate criteria, and recovery flows[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-49].

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (WG Security & Privacy) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body co-chaired by Alexander Frazer and Junjie Bu that establishes vendor-neutral threat models, security design patterns, and operational security guidelines for agentic systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

The working group coordinates foundational security baselines across AAIF domains, interfaces with external standards bodies such as ETSI TC SAI, and maintains shared review checklists for cross-working-group evaluation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical output into primary workstreams:
- **Best Practices**: Publishes the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) and supporting feature matrices mapping practices to people, process, and technology controls.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **Threat Modeling**: Maintains the [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md), evaluating existing cybersecurity frameworks (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF) against agentic risks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **Design Patterns**: Curates the [Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md), covering architectural solutions including [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md), and [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **Cross-WG Review**: Maintains the [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md) to inspect specifications and reference architectures across other technical working groups.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25]

# Lifecycle History
In September 2026, the working group registered its first formal deliverables on `main` under `deliverables/`, including the Best Practices Guide and the Threat Modeling Gap Analysis.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1] Governance rules were established requiring that PR authors do not self-merge into `deliverables/`.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25] The group also instituted an alternating APAC-friendly meeting time slot and initiated requests to the Technical Committee regarding bilateral exchanges with ETSI TC SAI.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-25]

# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide is a practical builder reference developed by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to provide actionable controls across agent deployment, secrets isolation, sandboxing, and execution environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

Maintained as a living document by mandatory reviewers Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, the guide serves as the foundation for static analysis rule sets and comparative evaluations against commercial agent SDKs.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Architecture / Specification
The guideline articulates defensive principles for autonomous agents:
- **Core Security Controls**: Practical configurations for runtime isolation, prompt injection mitigation, context redaction, and boundary protection.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **Feature Matrix**: A companion matrix mapping each recommended practice to people, process, and technology requirements, authored by Erin Farr.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **Domain Scope Boundaries**: Workload identity and cross-organizational trust topics are intentionally deferred to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Lifecycle History
The guide's initial draft merged on 2026-09-30 under `deliverables/DRAFT-agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md` following review across 88 comments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1] Subsequent evolution is tracked via GitHub issues and pull requests, including static analysis rule conversion and alignment with frameworks such as Google ADK.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

proposed_concept.description: Comparative gap analysis evaluating traditional cybersecurity methodologies, CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF against agentic AI threat vectors.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis is an evaluative study produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) assessing standard cybersecurity frameworks against unique agentic AI threat surfaces.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, the resource evaluates OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework across eight agentic threat domains to establish baseline taxonomy and focus areas for new threat models.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Architecture / Specification
The gap analysis structures threat modeling around eight agentic threat areas, recommending that AAIF adopt established industry frameworks as classification baselines while focusing novel working group efforts on agent-specific failure points:
- Autonomous goal divergence and intent drift
- Non-deterministic tool use and chaining vulnerabilities
- Multi-agent coordination and identity spoofing
- Environment feedback manipulation and unobserved side-effects

# Lifecycle History
The deliverable merged into `main` on 2026-09-30 as Draft v0.1 at `deliverables/DRAFT-agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md` via PR #8.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1] Dedicated threat modeling working sessions were established starting in October 2026 to expand upon identified framework gaps.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

proposed_concept.description: Architectural catalog defining reusable, implementation-independent security and privacy design patterns for autonomous agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog is an architectural resource curated by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) documenting reusable, implementation-neutral design patterns for securing agent systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

Led by Sagar Dashora and Dan Kommatas, the catalog provides standardized design templates and reference specifications that address critical agentic risks such as runaway execution, unverified actions, and compromised runtime environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Architecture / Specification
The catalog establishes a uniform pattern structure and incorporates initial foundational patterns:
- **Pattern Template**: Standardized schema ensuring consistency across problem statements, architectural diagrams, threat mappings, and implementation tradeoffs.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **[Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)**: Cryptographically or policy-bound authorization gates for high-impact actions.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **[Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md)**: Independent, out-of-band containment mechanisms to immediately halt rogue or misbehaving agent processes.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]
- **[Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)**: Hardware-attested, isolated execution boundaries safeguarding policy evaluation and secret handling.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

# Lifecycle History
The catalog landing page and its first three architectural pattern drafts merged into `main` on 2026-09-30 via PR #26.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1] Subsequent work includes follow-up refinements and the development of memory-related security patterns.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-60f28464dd94-24e4fdf1]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation specification defining core agent execution entities, turn boundaries, causal trace links, and evidence-grade test suites.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and correlation specification standardizing the representation of AI agent execution flows, interaction boundaries, and verifiable causal traces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57]. Developed within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the model defines standard schema conventions for capturing agent turns, tool invocations, state mutations, and evidentiary signatures across heterogeneous runtimes.

# Architecture / Specification
The specification structures agent telemetry into structured OpenTelemetry (OTLP) records, mapping runtime events across standard effect and evidence layers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].

## Validation and Test Kit
To verify conformant trace emission and ingestion, the specification includes a reference test kit comprising six normative OTLP/JSON test vectors evaluated through a basis-and-expectation harness [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57]:
- **Receipt Integrity**: Evaluation of handling for duplicate receipts, missing receipts, and cryptographic receipt signature validation versus corruption [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].
- **Correlation Consistency**: Verification of trace parsing when correlation identifiers (such as ticket IDs) are modified mid-stream [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].
- **Tenant Isolation**: Conformance checks preventing cross-tenant collision and unauthorized reuse of action identifiers across disjoint execution contexts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].

The test reader evaluates query context from an input `basis.json` definition prior to parsing `expected.json` ground truth [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57]. Synthetic cryptographic signatures in the test kit validate syntactic and structural parsing without asserting real-world target effects or authenticating external tenant metadata [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].

# Lifecycle History
- **PR #57**: Added the trace-model test kit introducing six OTLP/JSON validation cases, expectation reader, and CI qualification workflow covering receipt signatures, correlation modification, and multi-tenant action ID reuse [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-57].

# References
- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- [Evidence Record Spec](evidence-record-spec.md)
- [Trace Standard](trace.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering secrets management, context redaction, host sandboxing, and pre-execution authorization hooks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guideline provides implementation standards for securing autonomous AI agents against prompt injection, credential exfiltration, overprivileged tool execution, and supply-chain vulnerabilities [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31]. Maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the document outlines defense-in-depth requirements spanning execution sandboxes, data minimization, and runtime authorization controls.

# Architecture / Specification
The guideline outlines security controls across host isolation, network boundaries, credential protection, and tool execution controls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].

## Runtime Authorization and Pre-Execution Hooks
Runtime tool invocation security relies on deterministic enforcement boundaries rather than self-reported agent intent [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31]. Architectural proposals within the working group emphasize placing authorization controls behind deterministic pre-execution hooks rather than relying solely on human review tiers [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31]:
- **Deterministic Interception**: Every tool invocation is intercepted prior to execution, evaluating policy rules to return an allow, deny, modify, or ask verdict based on the specific tool name, payload arguments, and session context rather than a static operation category [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].
- **Approval Fatigue Mitigation**: Empirical measurements on human-in-the-loop oversight reveal significant approval fatigue (e.g., users approving ~97% of permission prompts and failing to catch dangerous commands after repeated prompting), motivating automated policy enforcement as the primary filter with human escalation reserved strictly for ambiguous decisions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].
- **External Decision Standards**: Alignment with emerging specifications such as the OWASP Agent Control Standard (ACS) for standardized pre-execution hook decision formats [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].

# Lifecycle History
- **Issue #31**: Proposed placing the four-tier authorization model behind pre-execution hooks (`allow`, `deny`, `modify`, `ask`) evaluated at runtime over tool arguments and context to counter empirical human approval fatigue [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].

# References
- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)
- [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)
- [Cross-WG Security Review Checklist](cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md)

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards, delegation models, and cross-organizational trust boundaries for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body developing standards, cryptographic delegation models, and verifiable identity frameworks for autonomous agents [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17]. The group establishes architectures for decentralized agent identification, verifiable authority delegation, mutual authentication, and runtime assertion boundaries between humans, agents, and external systems.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's charter encompasses verifiable credential formats, identity lifecycle operations, and execution-time trust verification [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-16] [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].

## Authority at Dispatch
The working group evaluates authority verification models at the point of action dispatch [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17]:
- **Contract Identification**: Requiring execution traces to bind to explicit, versioned contract identifiers, rejecting traces lacking verifiable contract metadata [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].
- **Freshness Constraints**: Tracking the chronological age of authority evidence against deployed freshness thresholds to mitigate replay and stale delegation risks [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].
- **Reference Catalogues**: Benchmarking authority delegation across reference runs (including MintID, Proofable, and Alakris) using automated verification tooling such as the agent-evidence-observer reader [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].

## Human-Backed Agent Credentials
The working group also investigates credential schemes backed directly by verified human principals to support authenticated delegation chains and identity continuity across multi-agent workflows [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-16].

# Lifecycle History
- **PR #16**: Added human-backed agent credential verification runs to the presentation queue [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-16].
- **PR #17**: Proposed authority-at-dispatch catalogue entry, evidence verification workflow enforcing versioned contract identifiers and freshness limits, and comparative reference runs [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].

- [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Automated regression evaluation suite and grader catalog benchmarking community operations skills across triggering, safety, and operational invariants.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite provides automated behavioral evaluation cases and grader definitions to benchmark agentic community operations skills against realistic operational prompts [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]. Operating independently of deterministic CI linters, the suite executes end-to-end model interactions using the Claude plugin eval framework to verify both trigger accuracy and strict adherence to operational constraints [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation framework structures test cases around specific historical failure modes, paired trigger tests, and security boundary violations [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]:

- **Dual-Arm Differential Scoring**: Each test case evaluates two arms by default—one run with the skill plugin enabled and one run without [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]. Graders marked `arm: with-only` measure the delta ($Δ$) directly attributable to the `SKILL.md` instructions rather than underlying base model capabilities [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
- **Coverage Domains**:
  - `announcement-post` and `recap-post`: Paired trigger discrimination preventing semantic confusion between pre-event RSVP promotion and post-event recaps [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
  - `speaker-bio`: Privacy leakage defense verifying that volunteered personal contact details (addresses, phone numbers) are stripped before publishing [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
  - `triage-intake`: Prompt injection resistance preventing untrusted form inputs from manipulating triage status [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
  - `sync-chapters-write-gate`: Read-default gate ensuring agent skills report changes and require explicit confirmation prior to mutation [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
  - `audit-slack`: Natural language triggering robust to colloquial inquiries rather than skill description token matching [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].
  - `check-setup`: Readiness activation for non-technical queries alongside credential defense steering tokens to system keychains instead of conversational transcripts [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07], [^evt-community-events-file-5a72ef6a708b-c7737da1], [^evt-community-events-file-a6116ffcd592-e614afed], [^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad].
- **Execution & Security Isolation**: The evaluation suite runs locally via `claude plugin eval . --no-publish --trust-plugin` with `--no-publish` enforcing that transcripts containing synthetic identity records remain local [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]. Because GitHub Actions (`validate.yml`) runs on fork pull requests without API credentials, model-graded evals are excluded from pull request CI [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07].

mutations.rationale: Document non-technical activation conditions and strict conversational token interception rules defined in setup check evaluation cases.

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Setup Verification Skill
proposed_concept.description: Diagnostic agent skill validating community operations environment configuration, tooling availability, and secure credential storage.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-check-setup` skill provides pre-flight system diagnostics and environment verification for community operations tooling [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-9d91ed07]. Designed to activate when operators ask natural language readiness questions (such as "is it all working?"), it guides users through prerequisite verification while strictly preventing the ingestion of authentication tokens into chat sessions [^evt-community-events-file-5a72ef6a708b-c7737da1], [^evt-community-events-file-a6116ffcd592-e614afed], [^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad].

# Architecture / Specification
- **Natural Language Triggering**: Matches colloquial readiness checks without requiring formal skill keywords or setup commands [^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad].
- **Credential Interception and Redirection**: Prohibits pasting secrets, API keys, or Slack tokens directly into conversational context [^evt-community-events-file-a6116ffcd592-e614afed]. When users offer tokens, the skill instructs them not to share secrets in chat and redirects them to native OS credential managers such as macOS Keychain Access [^evt-community-events-file-a6116ffcd592-e614afed].
- **Diagnostic Scopes**: Verifies local CLI bindings (including `gws`), environment credentials, and file permissions without mutating configuration files or remote services.

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Intake Data Cleaning Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational data normalization skill enforcing Google Workspace CLI native mutations, untrusted input containment, and gated approval workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-clean-data` skill normalizes, validates, and cleans community intake records in the AAIF Community Intake Ops spreadsheet [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]. Adhering to the proposal-execution split pattern (`../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md`), the skill operates in read-only analysis mode by default and requires explicit operator authorization before writing changes back to the sheet [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].

# Architecture / Specification
- **Tooling Constraints**: All Google Drive and Spreadsheet reads, modifications, and writes are restricted strictly to Python scripts executing via the `gws` CLI [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]. Third-party desktop office suites such as LibreOffice (`soffice`) and `unoconv` are explicitly banned due to font substitution issues and lossy OOXML round-tripping [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].
- **Untrusted Input Handling**: Free-text form submissions and cell contents are treated as untrusted data; instruction-like prompt injections within responses are barred from modifying statuses, chapter assignments, or granting permissions [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].
- **Write Gates and Modes**:
  - `scan`: Non-destructive read pass computing normalization proposals, city extractions, and duplicate flags [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].
  - `apply`: Writes validated changes using `RAW` values rather than `USER_ENTERED` to prevent accidental formula evaluation or formatting corruption [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].
  - Sensitive intermediate artifacts (such as `changes.json` containing PII) must be stored in temporary isolation (`mktemp -d`) and deleted post-execution [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].

# Overview
The `aaif-create-chapter` skill orchestrates community chapter provisioning and ongoing estate visual conformity across Google Workspace and Office documents [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]. Through its accompanying design system sweep engine (`restyle_design_system.py`), the skill audits and updates templates, themes, color palettes, and accessibility contrast standards across chapter assets [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].

# Architecture / Specification
- **Design System Sweep**: Governed by `restyle_design_system.py`, the engine audits and enforces design system tokens defined in `lib/aaif_events/ooxml_style.py` and background artwork from `lib/aaif_events/agent_art.py` [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].
- **Scope & Allowlisting**: Sweeps are strictly constrained to template definitions in `TEMPLATE_FILES` and chapter CRMs (`<City> CRM.xlsx`); personalized event decks and dated organizer work are explicitly skipped and named in audit reports to prevent unauthorized modifications [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].
- **OOXML & SpreadsheetML Handling**: Distinguishes between DrawingML presentations and SpreadsheetML workbooks, updating `xl/styles.xml` and themes while preserving cell values in `xl/worksheets/` and `xl/sharedStrings.xml` [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].
- **Non-Destructive Backups**: Operates read-only by default (`--check`), requiring `--write` to commit changes [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]. Prior to write operations, pre-change files are archived into `backups/restyle-<UTC>/`, with an immutable rule preventing pristine initial backups from being overwritten during subsequent runs [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].
- **Accessibility Verification**: Validates text legibility against WCAG AA contrast standards across slide background plates [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].

proposed_concept.description: Operational data normalization skill enforcing Google Workspace CLI native mutations, untrusted input containment, and proposed-diff approval gates for intake records.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-clean-data` skill normalizes community intake submissions within Google Sheets without silent data modification, functioning as Phase 1 of the automated estate synchronization pipeline.[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112] It inspects submitted responses, extracts and normalizes attendee or organizer locations, and produces explicit before-and-after diffs for operator review prior to applying any mutations.[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112]

City resolution serves as an essential gatekeeper for downstream community infrastructure: an intake entry with an unresolved city designation remains invisible to subsequent sync tasks, failing to populate chapter rosters, CRM lists, or Google Drive authorization grants.[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112] It operates as part of the broader [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md) suite.[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7]

# Architecture / Specification
The cleaning engine (`scripts/clean.py`) operates in two distinct operational phases:[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112]
- **Scan Mode (Read-Only)**: Detects data anomalies and proposes mechanical fixes such as trimming whitespace, re-casing all-upper or all-lower text, and canonicalizing LinkedIn profile URLs. It flags entries requiring human judgment, such as duplicate or invalid email addresses, missing names, and non-profile links.[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112] Entries reporting an unextracted `Other` city are highlighted with cell-scoped red formatting for chapter review without modifying underlying values.[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7]
- **Apply Mode (Write on Approval)**: Consumes an approved JSON changeset written to an isolated temporary directory. Mutations write directly to the primary `Form Responses` sheet using column header names rather than column letters, recording applied changes in an `Autofixes` column for audit provenance.[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112]

### Tooling and Environmental Invariants
- **Native Google Workspace CLI (`gws`)**: All Google Drive and Sheets interactions must execute via Python calling the `gws` command-line utility with authenticated API scopes.[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112]
- **Office Suite Prohibition**: Tools such as LibreOffice, `soffice`, or `unoconv` are strictly prohibited for file conversion, edits, or local previews due to font substitution and loss of native OpenXML and Google Docs formatting features.[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112]
- **Untrusted Input Treatment**: Sheet cell values are strictly handled as passive data and never as control directives.[^evt-community-events-file-f66a78711977-a26d3112]

# Lifecycle History
Introduced as part of the AAIF Community Events Toolkit, the workflow was expanded to accommodate granular role questionnaires (converting unified participation prompts into explicit per-role gates for organizers, hosts, speakers, and collaborators) and chapter review flags for submitted `Other` locations.[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7]

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Event Announcement Post Skill
proposed_concept.description: LinkedIn launch copy generation skill enforcing privacy protection, attendee disclosure controls, and mandatory Linux Foundation policy footers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-announcement-post` skill drafts LinkedIn announcement posts for AAIF chapter and virtual events when RSVPs open.[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9] Operating under strict privacy and house voice constraints, the skill generates concise (~120 words), scannable copy structured around a single hook, logistical details (what, when, where), speaker topics with clear takeaways, and a direct call to action linked to official registration platforms such as Luma or Gradual.AI.[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]

# Architecture / Specification
The skill enforces editorial constraints, automated tracker retrieval, and mandatory compliance footers:[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]

### Editorial and Privacy Invariants
- **House Voice**: Emphasizes practitioner practices over vendor promotional copy, prioritizing specific technical substance and builder-to-builder tone with a maximum of one emoji and three hashtags.[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]
- **Public-Copy Rule**: Prohibits the publication of non-public personal details, including email addresses, phone numbers, venue door codes, or attendee names from intake sheets.[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9] In assistant transcripts and generated drafts, omitted details must be referred to by field name rather than echoing private values.[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]
- **Mandatory Policy Footer**: Every published post must terminate with links to the Linux Foundation Code of Conduct (`https://events.linuxfoundation.org/about/code-of-conduct`) and Privacy Policy (`https://www.linuxfoundation.org/legal/privacy-policy`).[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]

### Tracker Ingestion
Event details can be parsed from manual user input or automatically fetched from the remote chapter event tracker using `fetch_tracker.py`:[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]
```bash
python3 <skill-root>/../aaif-event-status/scripts/fetch_tracker.py "<Chapter or Series>" --event "<Event Title>"
```
The tracker utility resolves Google Drive directories via authenticated `gws` tooling and withholds private venue and speaker contact coordinates at the extraction layer.[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-005d77f9]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-check-setup` skill performs non-destructive, read-only diagnostic checks to verify that an operator's local workstation is configured to execute the AAIF Community Events Toolkit.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77] Designed for non-technical community managers operating through agent runtimes like Goose or Claude Desktop, it validates Python 3 dependencies, Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) authentication, Community Intake sheet edit access, Slack tokens, Luma API keys, and Chrome PDF rendering capability.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77][^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7]

# Architecture / Specification
The verification suite runs via `scripts/check_setup.py` and adheres to strict operational boundaries:[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77]
- **Read-Only Verification**: Queries Google Sheets metadata, calls Slack `auth.test`, and queries Luma `calendars/get` without mutating remote state or logging raw credential values.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77]
- **Plain-Language Reporting**: Emits symbol-coded indicators (`✅` ready, `❌` blocking requirement, `⚪` optional) accompanied by jargon-free remediation instructions rather than stack traces.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77]
- **Decoupled Drafting**: Explicitly informs operators that copy-drafting skills (such as [AAIF Announcement Post](../skills/aaif-announcement-post.md)) operate on pasted inputs and do not require external API credentials.[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77]

### Credential Resolution Precedence
The toolkit resolves credentials across three tiers: active environment variables, repository root `.env` files, and the macOS keychain (`aaif-slack-read-token`, `aaif-slack-write-token`, and `luma-api-key`).[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7] Keychain lookups are cached per run to prevent repeated operating system authorization prompts, ensuring accessibility when invoked from sandboxed desktop assistant environments lacking inherited shell variables.[^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7]

proposed_concept.description: Configuration-driven Slack inspection skill auditing chapter channels, organizer rooms, and regional topic activity via three read-only analytical engines.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-audit-slack` skill audits the community Slack workspace to evaluate chapter channel provisioning, organizer placement, subject-matter room engagement, and overall member composition.[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73] Functioning as Phase 8 of the community estate synchronization pipeline in [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md), it acts as an independent, read-only verification harness decoupling verification from the provisioning engines.[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]

# Architecture / Specification
The audit framework coordinates three domain engines over a single workspace, backed by a unified activity measurement layer and an HTML report aggregator:[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]
- **Organizer Engine (`audit_organizers.py`)**: Checks whether accepted chapter organizers have designated public and private `-organizers` channels and verifies member assignments.[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]
- **Topics Engine (`audit_topics.py`)**: Assesses topical channels to identify stale, overlapping, or abandoned rooms.[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]
- **Members Engine (`audit_members.py`)**: Analyzes account statuses and baseline newcomer onboarding experiences.[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]
- **Activity Layer (`audit_activity.py`)**: Measures recent human message timestamps, message volumes, and unique poster counts to supply telemetry to the topics and members engines.[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]
- **Consolidated Summary (`summarize_audits.py`)**: Combines cached outputs into a standalone `slack-full-audit.html` deliverable, featuring section indices and a prioritized focus ranking.[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d]

### Cache Integrity and Security Boundaries
- **Filesystem Permissions**: Raw API response caches (`users.json`, channel lists) and generated audit reports contain personal identifiers and are restricted to `0600` file permissions within a `0700` data directory.[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d]
- **Repository Leakage Prevention**: Audit engines refuse execution if cache or report paths are detectable by `git add -A`, preventing accidental commits of member directories to public repositories.[^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-3e6d8b8d]
- **Untrusted Input Guardrails**: Channel descriptions, profile metadata, and sheet contents are parsed strictly as passive data and never interpreted as authorization directives.[^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-84165b73]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability and Execution Isolation Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Architectural guidelines and directory resolution rules ensuring agent skills run reliably across checkouts and headless plugin host environments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Agent skills and toolchains must operate reliably across diverse host execution topologies without assuming a full git checkout, a persistent shell environment, or an immutable current working directory [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]. In the Agentic AI Foundation reference implementation, runtime hosts such as Goose perform git checkouts while hosts such as Claude Desktop provision isolated, versioned directory trees devoid of git metadata [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].

# Architecture / Specification
The portability model resolves operational disparities through standardized path variables, tiered credential discovery, and isolated data containment:

- **Root-Relative Path Resolution**: Skill invocation commands in `SKILL.md` must prefix script paths with `<skill-root>` rather than assuming relative workspace roots like `skills/<name>/...` [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]. This invariant prevents path traversal failures when an agent executes commands from arbitrary session directories. Conformance is verified statically by `check_skill_portability.py` [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].
- **Tiered Secret Resolution**: Headless plugin hosts frequently launch subshells without inherited terminal environment variables. Credential lookups systematically fall back from the active process environment to the repo-root `.env` file, and finally to the host operating system keyring (such as macOS Keychain), ensuring installed plugins maintain connectivity without hardcoded tokens [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].
- **Isolated Scratch and Data Directories**: Plugin executions must never emit unmanaged scratch files or persistent state into the caller's working directory, which often coincides with synced user folders [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]. Runtime mutations must route through dedicated data storage routines (such as `aaif_events.datadir`) or ephemeral temporary directories via `mktemp -d` [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].
- **Drift Protection for Decoupled Copies**: Standalone utility scripts that duplicate core storage or secret-lookup logic without shared libraries must be tracked in unit testing (`tests/test_pinned_copies.py`) to prevent behavioral divergence [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].

# Lifecycle History
Portability testing established that eleven skills initially broke when executed outside the repository root [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6]. Static validation checks and pinned-copy verification suites were introduced to enforce runtime independence across Claude Desktop and Goose plugin environments [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].

# References
- [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md)
- [AAIF Check Setup](../skills/aaif-check-setup.md)
- [AAIF Backup](../skills/aaif-backup.md)

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Backup Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational backup skill generating immutable, timestamped snapshots of community estate sheets and local operational files.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-backup` skill creates automated, immutable, timestamped snapshots of critical operational artifacts across Google Drive and local file systems [^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7]. It protects primary estate registers—such as the Community Intake Ops sheet—against accidental corruption or unrecoverable agent edits while strictly keeping sensitive binary exports out of public version control [^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6].

# Architecture / Specification
The backup skill enforces strict storage segregation, naming conventions, and non-destructive recovery workflows:

- **Snapshot Directory Layout**: Snapshots follow a standardized path structure: `backups/<slug>/<UTC-timestamp>.<ext>` (for example, `backups/aaif-community-intake-ops/2026-07-03T142530Z.xlsx`) [^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7]. Each execution appends a new file without overwriting prior captures, establishing an audit-ready chronological version history [^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7].
- **Environment-Aware Storage Routing**: When run in a git checkout, snapshots are written to the repository's `backups/` directory, which is completely git-ignored except for documentation [^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7]. When executed from an installed plugin harness (such as Goose or Claude Desktop), snapshots automatically route to `~/Library/Application Support/AAIF/backups/` on macOS to persist across plugin version upgrades [^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7].
- **Execution Interfaces**: The underlying runner `backup.py` supports defaulting to the central Intake Ops spreadsheet or accepting arbitrary target file parameters:
  ```bash
  # Default: AAIF Community Intake Ops sheet
  python3 <toolkit>/skills/aaif-backup/scripts/backup.py

  # Arbitrary Drive file ID or local file path
  python3 <toolkit>/skills/aaif-backup/scripts/backup.py <driveFileId>
  python3 <toolkit>/skills/aaif-backup/scripts/backup.py ./path/to/file.xlsx
  ```
  [^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7]
- **Safe Restore Protocol**: Restoration is intentionally manual and non-destructive. Operators copy raw cell values back from exported snapshots rather than overwriting sheets entirely, preventing the destruction of operational formulas and conditional formatting [^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7].

# Lifecycle History
To safeguard privacy across public repositories, binary snapshot files (`.xlsx`, `.docx`, `.pptx`) are banned from source tracking via gitignore filters, and data directory isolation was introduced to prevent accidental mutations inside user workspaces [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-2d5d5bf6][^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7].

# References
- [Agent Plugin Portability Guidelines](../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md)
- [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-taxonomy-contributions` skill guides AI agents and contributors in routing, drafting, and validating terminology proposals and landscape additions for the Common Taxonomy and Landscape workstream (`aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape`) [^evt-public-agents-pr-3]. It automates pre-drafting validation and normalizes proposals into accepted community schemas [^evt-public-agents-pr-3].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill consolidates disparate contribution rules across schema definitions, contributing guides, and codebase comments into an executable agent decision model:

- **Contribution Routing**: Dispatches proposed additions to the appropriate contribution channel—such as submitting an issue for deferred terminology versus filing a pull request for complete landscape entries—preventing common triage misdirections [^evt-public-agents-pr-3].
- **Pre-Drafting Collision Checks**: Inspects the target repository for active pull requests or existing taxonomy entries prior to drafting, preventing duplicate term proposals [^evt-public-agents-pr-3].
- **Pre-Competitive Style Enforcement**: Scans and sanitizes submitted descriptions by stripping ungrounded marketing superlatives (e.g., 'the best open-source platform') to maintain the pre-competitive, objective tone required by landscape schemas [^evt-public-agents-pr-3].
- **Template and Schema Conformance**: Formats proposals into standardized `Define` issue templates and ensures required metadata fields—including name, homepage URL, pre-competitive description, and member status—conform to schema constraints [^evt-public-agents-pr-3].
- **Adaptive Context Retrieval**: Instructs agents to dynamically fetch upstream schema documentation before drafting, ensuring graceful adaptation to evolving workstream processes [^evt-public-agents-pr-3].

# Lifecycle History
Empirical evaluation demonstrated that an agent equipped with `aaif-taxonomy-contributions` executed schema-conformant landscape entries in 6 targeted tool calls compared to 15 exploratory calls required by an unassisted baseline [^evt-public-agents-pr-3].

# References
- [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)
- [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md)

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Reporting Template
proposed_concept.description: Standardized cadence, structure, review timeline, and pull request workflow for AAIF working groups delivering monthly activity reports to the Technical Committee.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Working Group Reporting Template standardizes how Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) working groups report operational milestones, technical deliverables, and decisions requiring [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) review. Monthly reports ensure cross-workstream visibility, track active deliverables across working groups, and provide a historical record of consensus and governance actions.

# Architecture / Specification

Working groups publish monthly reports into their local repository trees under standardized reporting directories. To allow automated discovery and aggregation across foundation repositories, report pull requests must strictly adhere to intake guidelines [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62]:

- **File Naming**: Report filenames are case-sensitive and follow standardized date formatting (e.g., `YYYY-MM.md`) within the designated reports path [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].
- **Pull Request Title**: Pull requests submitting monthly reports must follow the explicit format `[Report] <YYYY-MM>` rather than descriptive or working group names [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].
- **Labeling**: Every report submission pull request must be tagged with the `monthly-report` label [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].
- **Content Requirements**: Reports detail progress made during the reporting cycle, current roadmap milestones, meeting attendance summaries, cross-group collaborations, and explicit calls for Technical Committee decisions.

# Lifecycle History

Standardization efforts led by working groups, including the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), identified divergence between localized template instructions and the centralized Technical Committee reporting requirements [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62]. In response, reporting templates were updated to align pull request title conventions, label automation requirements, and case-sensitive filename constraints directly with centralized governance documentation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-62].

# References

- [Technical Committee Working Group Reporting Guidelines](https://github.com/aaif/technical-committee/blob/main/working-groups/reporting.md)
