proposed_concept.title: Goose
proposed_concept.description: Open-source general-purpose AI agent runtime and autonomous execution framework hosted by the AAIF with built-in telemetry and extensible tool integration.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Goose is an open-source, general-purpose autonomous AI agent runtime hosted by the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27]. Originally developed by Block, Goose provides a modular execution engine capable of interacting with host environments, invoking shell operations, calling external APIs, and managing local workflows through automated context and tool dispatch.

# Architecture / Specification

Goose functions as an autonomous execution harness that executes developer-driven and operational tasks through modular plugins and protocol integrations. Key architectural characteristics include:

- **Runtime Execution**: Operates as a local or containerized agent runtime handling model interaction, multi-turn reasoning loops, and deterministic action execution.
- **Protocol Interoperability**: Integrates native support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to access tools, persistent context, and external data services.
- **Telemetry and Observability**: Exposes structured execution traces and operational metrics compatible with open telemetry pipelines.
- **Landscape Categorization**: Positioned within the [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md) under the Autonomous Agent Frameworks subcategory as an official AAIF member-hosted project [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27].

# Lifecycle History

Goose was donated to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation at the foundation's public launch alongside the Model Context Protocol [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27]. Following its donation, the primary source repository transitioned from `block/goose` to the foundation-managed `aaif-goose/goose` organization, with official documentation maintained at `goose-docs.ai` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27].

# References

- [Goose Source Repository](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose)

proposed_concept.description: Interactive ecosystem catalog and market map tracking open-source and commercial technologies across agent frameworks, protocols, runtimes, and governance tooling.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive ecosystem catalog and market map managed by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md). It provides an authoritative, structured directory of open-source frameworks, commercial platforms, infrastructure services, and emerging standards across the agentic artificial intelligence ecosystem [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27].

# Architecture / Specification

The landscape data model and publishing pipeline rely on declarative YAML configuration coupled with automated validation and client-side rendering [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28]:

- **Data Schema (`landscape.yml`)**: Entries are grouped hierarchically into categories and subcategories. Each item defines mandatory fields (`name`, `homepage_url`, `description`, `project`) and optional repository locations (`repo_url`) conforming to foundation schema specifications [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27].
- **CI Validation Engine (`validate-landscape.mjs`)**: Automated pull request testing parses catalog files using the same `js-yaml` version and `FAILSAFE_SCHEMA` options as the browser client, enforcing strict type consistency and preventing unquoted string mismatches [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- **Denial-of-Service and Boundary Limits**: The validator enforces strict defense-in-depth resource bounds, including a 512 KB file size cap, a 500-item maximum, a 5,000-object/array graph limit, and a 20,000-reference traversal budget [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28]. It prohibits YAML merge keys, cyclic object aliases, and control characters [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- **Symlink Prevention**: An automated pre- and post-assembly check (`check-no-symlinks.sh`) prevents committed symbolic links from exposing runner-local files during artifact packing and deployment via GitHub Pages [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].
- **Browser Client Search**: The client application (`app.js`) executes search highlighting using bounded regular expression walks with Unicode case folding, preventing input injection and avoiding unconstrained string allocations [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].

# Lifecycle History

Originally deployed to map the emerging AI agent tooling ecosystem, the landscape expanded following the creation of the AAIF. Foundational projects donated at launch—including [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and Model Context Protocol—were integrated into member project categories such as Autonomous Agent Frameworks [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-27]. Continued growth prompted hardening of the intake pipeline, introducing strict static validation, parsing limits, and symlink protection to ensure repository integrity and rendering safety [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-28].

# References

- [Taxonomy and Landscape Repository](https://github.com/aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering secrets management, context redaction, host sandboxing, runtime hook enforcement, and network gateway checkpoints.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide provides implementation-focused guidance for securing autonomous agent systems, covering secrets hygiene, context sanitization, sandbox isolation, and runtime execution boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38] Within agent execution environments, the specification delineates operational security between internal runtime lifecycle hooks and external network perimeter controls.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]

# Architecture / Specification

The security architecture establishes a two-tiered enforcement model for governing agent tool interactions and external communication:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]

- **Runtime Hook Enforcement**: Runtime hooks serve as the primary execution enforcement point. At discrete stages across an agent run's lifecycle, the execution environment halts and passes the pending tool call or action—accompanied by the causal context that generated it—to local policy logic before execution proceeds.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]
- **Gateway Network Checkpoints**: Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateways, such as the AAIF [agentgateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) project, function as perimeter control checkpoints on the network path. A gateway provides a unified access endpoint for remote MCP servers, authenticating requests via OAuth, enforcing granular per-tool permission policies, and logging payload telemetry for audit and action event records.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]

Runtime hooks provide deep contextual policy evaluation at the point of generation, whereas network gateway checkpoints enforce authentication boundaries, authorization, and transport mediation across external network paths.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]

# Lifecycle History

In PR #38, the Security and Privacy Working Group revised Section 3.1 of the best practices guide to replace broad gateway enforcement with a dual-layer approach separating hook-based execution halts from gateway network checkpoints, incorporating agentgateway as an AAIF project.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group develops vendor-neutral capability models, protocol evaluations, and transaction lifecycle specifications for autonomous and agent-assisted commercial workflows.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-9] The group standardizes transactional boundaries, payment delegation mechanisms, and cross-platform agent purchasing protocols.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-9]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group evaluates emerging commercial architectures across four primary functional areas:

- **Commerce Taxonomy**: Defining normative concepts and interaction boundaries for [agent-initiated transactions](../taxonomy/agent-initiated-transaction.md), [agent-in-the-loop transactions](../taxonomy/agent-in-the-loop-transaction.md), and [agentic checkout](../taxonomy/agentic-checkout.md).
- **Protocol Comparative Analysis**: Conducting technical evaluations of transaction protocols—including onX, the Multi-Party Payment (MPP) protocol, and the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)—by analyzing problem scopes, runtime mechanisms, governance structures, and protocol handoff boundaries.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-9]
- **Payment Delegation and Trust**: Establishing verification models and authorization guarantees for [delegated payment](../taxonomy/delegated-payment.md) systems.
- **Lifecycle State Semantics**: Mapping state machines governing multi-agent commercial negotiations, checkout flows, and settlement reconciliations.

# Lifecycle History

In September 2026, the working group completed deep dives analyzing the August 2026 releases of onX, MPP, and UCP, mapping their architectural overlap, governance states, and handoff points across autonomous commerce workflows.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-9]

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation overseeing technical vision, standards, project lifecycles, and working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Technical Committee (TC) is the technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), operating as a directed fund of The Linux Foundation[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]. The TC assists the Governing Board by reviewing project proposals, recommending new technical projects, applying the project lifecycle policy, and establishing, managing, and archiving working groups[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].

# Architecture / Specification

## Composition and Leadership

The TC comprises representatives appointed by AAIF Platinum Members, with each Platinum Member appointing one representative[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]. Founding TC members were appointed by the AAIF Governing Board for a term spanning March 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-8f2953e0]:

- **David Soria Parra** (TC Chair) — Anthropic
- **Caitie McCaffrey** (TC Co-Chair) — Microsoft
- **Alan Blount** — Google
- **Bradley Axen** — Block
- **James Ward** — Amazon Web Services
- **Nick Cooper** — OpenAI
- **Sambhav Kothari** — Bloomberg
- **Steve Faulkner** — Cloudflare

## Operational Responsibilities

The TC facilitates communication and technical alignment between Foundation projects and the broader community by[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]:

- Establishing, administering, and archiving working groups across technical domains relevant to the AAIF, following the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md).
- Coordinating technical collaboration, overall priorities, and community technical roadmaps.
- Evaluating project submissions and recommending candidates to the Governing Board for acceptance as Technical Projects.
- Adjudicating project maturity transitions under the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md).
- Recommending technical infrastructure and resource priorities to the Governing Board.

## Voting and Consensus Mechanics

The TC operates as a consensus-driven body with explicit voting rules when formal decisions are required[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]:

- **Voting Rights**: Each appointed TC voting member holds one vote[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].
- **Quorum**: Formal voting requires a minimum quorum of 50% of TC voting members present. Discussions may proceed without quorum, but no binding votes may be held[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].
- **Lazy Consensus**: Proposals may be adopted via lazy consensus under a 7-day "silence-as-agreement" period. If any formal objection is recorded within 7 days, the decision defaults to an electronic vote requiring a majority vote of all TC voting members[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].
- **Deadlock and Amendments**: If a vote cannot be resolved internally, members may refer the decision to the Governing Board for resolution. Amending the TC Charter requires a two-thirds TC majority and final approval by the Governing Board[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].

# Lifecycle History

The Technical Committee Charter was formally adopted on March 3, 2026[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]. Foundational technical projects placed under TC oversight include Model Context Protocol (MCP) and [goose](../resources/goose.md), both categorized at the Impact Stage[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-8f2953e0].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Project Lifecycle Policy defines the official maturity stages, criteria, and operational reviews governing open-source technical projects hosted by the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]. Authoritative maintenance and enforcement of the policy is delegated by the AAIF Governing Board to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance Authority and Scope

Under Section 2 of the Technical Committee Charter, the TC implements, maintains, and enforces the Project Lifecycle Policy, subject to initial Governing Board approval[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]:

- **Project Evaluation**: The TC reviews candidate project proposals against AAIF mission scope, technical merit, and intellectual property requirements[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].
- **Lifecycle Decisions**: The TC adjudicates stage advancements and status changes across project maturity tiers—including Sandbox, Growth, and Impact stages[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04][^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-8f2953e0].
- **Governing Board Recommendations**: The TC advises the Governing Board on accepting new Technical Projects and prioritizing Foundation resources to support active projects[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].

# Lifecycle History

Previously hosted in the `aaif/project-proposals` repository, the authoritative Project Lifecycle Policy and the accompanying [Project Proposal Process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md) were migrated to the `aaif/technical-committee` repository following the adoption of the Technical Committee Charter in March 2026[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-ef6fdf4e][^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Audit Slack Skill
proposed_concept.description: Configuration-driven Slack inspection skill auditing chapter channels, organizer rooms, message integrity, and unsolicited commercial spam.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-audit-slack` skill provides automated, read-only inspection and hygiene auditing across the AAIF Slack workspace, validating regional chapter channels, organizer coordination spaces, and channel configurations[^evt-community-events-pr-61]. It operates alongside [community-event-operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md) to detect operational drift and commercial abuse while preventing untrusted message text from persisting to disk[^evt-community-events-pr-61].

# Architecture / Specification

## Spam and Commercial Outreach Detection

An on-demand inspection tool (`audit_spam.py`) scans public channels, reply threads, and token-owner direct message searches using heuristics designed to detect unsolicited commercial pitches[^evt-community-events-pr-61]:

- **Signal Ranking**: Ranks members based on detected services pitches, "DM me" conversion attempts, LinkedIn-account rental offers, financial solicitations, and identical messages cross-posted across three or more channels outside designated promotion areas[^evt-community-events-pr-61].
- **Scope Isolation**: Excludes shared external vendor rooms (`ext-*`) and organizer channels (`*-organizers`) from behavioral scoring[^evt-community-events-pr-61].
- **Untrusted Input Protection**: Message snippets print to terminal output within sanitized `<<msg>>` delimiters; no message text is written to persistent disk storage[^evt-community-events-pr-61].
- **Pagination Handling**: Because Slack's `conversations.history` API intermittently yields empty results when queried with timestamp boundaries (`oldest=`), the audit script pages without `oldest` and enforces evaluation boundaries locally with thread-reply lookback tracking[^evt-community-events-pr-61].
- **Human-in-the-Loop Governance**: Audit findings serve solely as administrative leads; deactivations and enforcement actions remain manual human decisions in the Slack admin console[^evt-community-events-pr-61].

# Lifecycle History

Expanded in PR #61 within `aaif/community-events` to add dedicated spam detection heuristics and register `conversations.replies` and `search.messages` in the Slack client allowlist[^evt-community-events-pr-61].

proposed_concept.title: Universal Recursive Autonomous Co-Founder Engine (URACE)
proposed_concept.description: Architectural blueprint specification and bootstrap runtime standard providing 72 modular building blocks for recursive multi-agent orchestration.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Universal Recursive Autonomous Co-Founder Engine (URACE) is a blueprint-first multi-agent orchestration and lifecycle specification designed to coordinate autonomous software development tasks without rigid framework dependencies[^evt-project-proposals-issue-60]. Rather than distributing heavy software libraries, URACE provides an install-as-bootstrap standard (`URACE.md`) containing 72 independent, reusable building blocks spanning architectural patterns, data schemas, authority boundaries, and regression gates[^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].

# Architecture / Specification

## Architectural Blueprint Model

URACE structures multi-agent coordination around reusable specifications that can be derived and embedded natively into target codebases[^evt-project-proposals-issue-60]:

- **Dynamic Context Loop**: Acts as an active runtime loop complementing static repository instruction files (such as `AGENTS.md`), dynamically enforcing protected boundaries, tracking evolutionary state, and validating execution goals[^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].
- **Executor Decoupling**: Decouples lifecycle logic from execution mechanics, intaking Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients or servers like [goose](../resources/goose.md) as pluggable "Executors" while URACE handles systemic rule verification and state governance[^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].
- **Token-Preserving Lifecycle Compaction**: Implements a compaction protocol (`urace /compact`) that periodically distills verbose execution logs into a semantic Cognitive Resume, preventing context window exhaustion during prolonged recursive runs[^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].
- **Deterministic Rule-Graph Tracking**: Maps codebase modifications back to an immutable, queryable snapshot graph of active human permissions (`urace /rules`), establishing clear provenance from agent actions to defined safety constraints[^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].
- **Zero-Dependency Portability**: Functions through a standalone bootstrap document dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0, executing structural primitives natively within any host environment[^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].

# Lifecycle History

Submitted in March 2026 as project proposal Issue #60 to the AAIF [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) seeking Sandbox stage admission under the Foundation's governance umbrella[^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].

proposed_concept.title: nono
proposed_concept.description: Open-source agent runtime security tool providing kernel-enforced sandboxing, credential isolation, and Sigstore-based instruction verification.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

`nono` is an open-source agent runtime security tool designed to isolate agent processes, tools, credentials, and configuration files via kernel-enforced sandboxing with minimal overhead and zero setup.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61] It applies composable security policies residing outside the agent's direct control to secure coding agents, general-purpose autonomous runtimes, custom agent frameworks, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]

Created in February 2026 by Luke Hinds, nono was submitted as a Sandbox project proposal to the Agentic AI Foundation with Technical Committee sponsorship from Bloomberg.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]

# Architecture / Specification

Nono operates as host-level security infrastructure complementary to network-layer proxies such as `agentgateway`:[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]
- **Kernel-Enforced Sandboxing:** Restricts agent file system access, network socket creation, and child process execution according to per-command profiles.
- **Instruction and Skill Attestation:** Integrates Sigstore cryptographic signatures to verify the provenance and integrity of agent instruction files (such as `AGENTS.md`), blocking tampered or unverified prompt directives at the operating system access layer.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]
- **Credential Protection:** Keeps sensitive API keys, authorization tokens, and secrets isolated from untrusted tool calls and rogue agent workflows.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]
- **Ecosystem Integration:** Enforces least-privilege constraints across runtimes such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md), Claude Code, OpenCode, and frameworks including ADK, Pydantic AI, and LangChain.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]

# Lifecycle History

- **February 2026:** Initial creation by Luke Hinds.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]
- **October 2026:** Submitted under Issue #61 to the AAIF Technical Committee for entry as an AAIF Sandbox project, sponsored by Sambhav Kothari.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing open threat models, security design patterns, cross-working-group review gates, and best practices for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6]. It produces open threat models, shared terminology, architectural security patterns, and actionable developer guides that enable providers, consumers, and peer working groups to uphold responsible and verifiable AI systems.

The group is chaired by Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google), appointed by Platinum and Gold members[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6]. Technical Committee governance ties chair terms to the anniversary of charter approval rather than calendar years[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group operates two alternating biweekly meetings to support global participation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-b90dcbe6]:
- **Primary Meeting**: Biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT / 1:00 PM ET.
- **APAC Meeting**: Biweekly on Mondays at 9:00 PM ET (alternating with the primary session)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

Key active deliverables and workstreams include:
- **Threat Modeling**: Completed the initial gap analysis evaluating classical methodologies (STRIDE, PASTA) against dynamic agent environments, moving into collaborative modeling integrating MITRE ATLAS and OWASP ASI[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns**: Architectural patterns cataloging hardened agent runtime controls, including merged drafts for `patterns/approval-checkpoint`, `patterns/attested-isolated-runtime`, and `patterns/kill-switch`[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices**: Practical builder guide opened to external community pull requests following its initial published draft[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
- **Cross-WG Security Review**: Standardized checklist and assessment workflow aligning with [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md), and [Accuracy and Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Integration**: Active harmonization of security and privacy definitions with [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

# Lifecycle History

In October 2026, the working group moved its APAC meeting slot to Mondays at 9:00 PM ET, celebrated the completion of the threat modeling gap analysis, published the first draft of the Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide for external contributions, and integrated cross-WG attestation and commerce standards initiatives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e3f78aaae09b-daf59b93].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing agentic terminology across working groups through designated Domain Editors and curated catalog taxonomies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream operates as a cross-cutting harmonization body within the Agentic AI Foundation, co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]. The workstream establishes shared definitions and reconciles terminology across AAIF working groups, resolving naming collisions and ambiguous concepts through structured delegate review.

# Architecture / Specification

Terminology intake and governance follow a formal Domain Editor workflow[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]:
- **Domain Editors**: Official representatives designated by each working group who author candidate definitions, review cross-cutting proposals, and ensure alignment with their respective charters[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].
- **Merge Rules**: A term definition may be merged asynchronously once two Domain Editors approve the pull request and open comments are resolved; live working group votes are reserved strictly for contested terms[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].
- **Review Filtering**: Terms that have passed workstream review are managed under a `Ready for Review` milestone to prioritize structured contributions over unsolicited proposals[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].

# Lifecycle History

In September 2026, the workstream merged seven definitions across four pull requests (`Human curated`, `Meta-harness`, `Human in the loop`, `Trust`, `Identifier`, `Attestation`, and `Delegation`), advancing the formal taxonomy to 8 defined terms[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a]. In the same period, the workstream formally paused work on the ecosystem Landscape deliverable to concentrate fully on the taxonomy and prevent unvetted vendor-inclusion disputes before Technical Committee review[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-60f28464dd94-f4687b4a].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing agent telemetry, causal execution traces, protocol boundary metrics, and cross-framework semantic conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group defines open standards and telemetry models for agentic execution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21]. Its mandate covers distributed tracing across LLM boundaries, causal trace propagation, hardware and container telemetry correlation, and interoperability with existing telemetry standards like OpenTelemetry and OCSF.

# Architecture / Specification

The working group focuses on several active integration streams:
- **Semantic Conventions & Seams**: Collaborative work with the OpenTelemetry (OTel) GenAI SIG and OCSF to define nine distinct integration seams across coding agents, agent SDKs, and AI gateways without requiring wholesale specification rewrites[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21].
- **Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) Observability**: Establishing explicit telemetry subsections and evidence propagation semantics in agent resource discovery workflows[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21].
- **Execution Replay and Runtime Verification**: Evaluating agent execution replay models, cryptographic audit logs, and context verification architectures such as CIGAR and Agent Action Capsules (AAC)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21].
- **Foundation Tooling**: Leveraging shared LFX MCP tools to automate meeting artifact ingestion and transcript processing for cross-working-group coordination[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21][^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-3].

# Lifecycle History

In October 2026, the working group reviewed context dissemination protocols and tamper-evident runtime verification demos, aligned on targeting specific OTel GenAI extension points rather than competitive specifications, and coordinated joint security and attestation seam mapping with the [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) working group[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7c02d5e673bb-b7cb2b21].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF WG Monthly Report Skill
proposed_concept.description: Modular operational skill generating evidence-based monthly working group status reports for Technical Committee review.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-wg-monthly-report` skill automates the compilation and authoring of standardized monthly reports submitted by working group chairs to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-working-group-chairs-file-b41d2241e043-0366462a]. The workflow consolidates progress, blockers, risks, and requested committee decisions into `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md`, ensuring every assertion maps to verifiable repository artifacts and commit history[^evt-working-group-chairs-file-b41d2241e043-0366462a][^evt-working-group-chairs-file-f863c50ea9a7-ebe3d9f2].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill explicitly disables autonomous model invocation (`disable-model-invocation: true`) to enforce human-in-the-loop validation by working group chairs prior to pull request submission[^evt-working-group-chairs-file-b41d2241e043-0366462a].

## Input Configuration
Execution requires or queries for:
- Working group name as used in official reports.
- Chair names and member organizational affiliations.
- Reporting month (defaulting to the most recently completed calendar month).
- Target GitHub repository path.
- Working group meeting notes for the active reporting period.
- GitHub team handle for TC reviewer assignment[^evt-working-group-chairs-file-b41d2241e043-0366462a].

## Operating Workflow
1. **Contract Validation**: Resolves repository reporting rules against [guidelines/working-group-reporting-template](../guidelines/working-group-reporting-template.md) and verifies local template paths[^evt-working-group-chairs-file-b41d2241e043-0366462a].
2. **Evidence Ledger Compilation**: Queries merged pull requests, closed issues, and published releases using the GitHub CLI within the month's calendar boundaries[^evt-working-group-chairs-file-b41d2241e043-0366462a].
3. **Report Generation**: Populates standard template sections: Summary, Progress Against Objectives, Ecosystem Highlights, Blockers and Risks, Decisions Needed from the TC, Next Month's Focus, and Metrics/Links[^evt-working-group-chairs-file-f863c50ea9a7-ebe3d9f2].
4. **Hand-Off and Pull Request Submission**: Validates that external statements cite durable artifacts, requires the pull request title `[Report] YYYY-MM`, attaches the `monthly-report` label, and assigns TC reviewers for asynchronous sign-off[^evt-working-group-chairs-file-b41d2241e043-0366462a][^evt-working-group-chairs-file-f863c50ea9a7-ebe3d9f2].

proposed_concept.title: Attestation and Evidence Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF working group establishing decentralized standards, evidence classes, and witness verification frameworks for agent actions and decisions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Attestation and Evidence Working Group (AE-WG) is a cross-cutting technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation established to define how statements about AI agent actions, decisions, authorizations, and outcomes are attested and verified across organizational boundaries without central authorities[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6]. The working group standardizes evidence classes, portable self-describing bundles, witness models, and offline verification mechanisms to ensure records remain independently checkable across systems[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6].

# Architecture / Specification
## Scope and Boundaries
- **In Scope**: Evidence vocabulary and grading scales; attestation formats for autonomous decisions, actions, and authorizations; commitment-before-observation mechanics; bilateral and multi-party attestation at runtime boundaries; verifiable offline disclosure and request bundles; and obligation mapping in coordination with Governance, Risk, and Regulatory[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6].
- **Out of Scope**: Telemetry transport wire formats (coordinated with [Observability & Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md)), identity credentials (coordinated with [Identity & Trust](identity-and-trust.md)), threat modeling (coordinated with [Security & Privacy](security-and-privacy.md)), payment settlement protocols (coordinated with [Agentic Commerce](agentic-commerce.md)), and foundation-managed central ledgers[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6].

## Governance and Deliverables
- **Cross-Group Coordination**: Governed by two co-chairs and seats dedicated liaison representatives from every active AAIF working group under [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) oversight[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6].
- **90-Day Roadmap**: Delivers Evidence Vocabulary v0, a witness and root-of-trust matrix (covering logs, cosigners, timestamp authorities, TEEs, and HSMs), evidence requirement analyses for sibling working group use cases, and an Evidence Classes and Gap Analysis 1.0 document for Technical Committee ratification[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-6].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering secrets management, context redaction, host sandboxing, and runtime isolation for autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guideline provides defensive engineering requirements and hardening strategies for developers deploying autonomous agent harnesses, tool runtimes, and execution environments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42]. The recommendations mitigate risks associated with credential exposure, context poisoning, tool privilege escalation, and lateral movement across multi-tenant infrastructures.

# Architecture / Specification
## Credential Isolation in Hardware Sandboxes
Hardware-isolated environments and confidential computing architectures (such as Intel TDX) isolate guest execution memory from untrusted host hypervisors, but do not automatically mitigate token exposure inside the guest software environment[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42].
- **Bearer Token Semantics**: In accordance with RFC 6750 §1.2, possession of a bearer token grants execution authority to any bearer holding it. Releasing a bearer token to guest software allows anyone controlling that guest context to exercise its permissions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42].
- **Exposure Controls**: Token risk must be constrained through short validity windows, tight audience restrictions, and granular authorization scopes rather than treating hardware isolation as an automatic defense against guest-level credential leakage[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-42].

## Runtime Tool Sandboxing
Autonomous agents executing dynamic or untrusted workflows must operate inside isolated runtimes governed by explicit policy proxies and compartmentalized credentials.

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing agent telemetry, causal execution traces, protocol boundary metrics, and auditable harness evaluation frameworks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes telemetry formats, causal execution traces, distributed profiling, and protocol boundary metrics across autonomous AI agents, harnesses, and tool interfaces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66]. Its mission covers vendor-neutral diagnostic frameworks enabling operators to trace agent decision trees, correlate tool invocations, and verify runtime execution integrity across distributed systems.

# Architecture / Specification
## Workstreams and Scope
- **Causal Tracing**: Defining execution trace schemas, span propagation, and event models within the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md).
- **Harness Evaluation Auditability**: Formulating minimal publication criteria for evidence harness evaluations, allowing independent parties to reproduce and falsify conformance claims[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66].

## Auditable Evaluation Properties
The working group is scoping eight observable properties required for auditable harness evaluation claims:
1. *Commitment before observation*: Publishing a fixed digest of the evaluation corpus prior to running trials[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66].
2. *Coverage identity*: Guaranteeing the published transcript covers exactly the committed test case set without omissions or duplicates[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66].
3. *Pinned trust root*: Publishing authentication keys out of band rather than within self-authenticating transcripts[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66].
4. *Separation of observation and judgement*: Maintaining strict separation between the runtime harness recording execution and the tool assessing conformity[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66].
5. *Typed outcomes and first-class refusals*: Recording explicit fields for attempted, observed, accepted, and verified effects, treating refusals as first-class outcomes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66].
6. *Benign cost accounting*: Documenting and measuring legitimate agent tasks blocked or denied by security checks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66].
7. *Adversarial maintenance*: Continually testing and repairing the evaluation suite while replaying historical test suites[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66].
8. *Temporal bounds and withdrawal*: Enforcing chronological ordering where authorization decisions strictly precede execution timestamps[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-66].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group establishes vendor-neutral standards, delegation architectures, and cryptographic trust frameworks for autonomous agents interacting across organizational boundaries[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-21]. The group addresses verifiable agent identity, delegation trees, and temporal existence proofs necessary for independent third-party verification.

# Architecture / Specification
## Temporal Evidence Verification Use Cases
The working group evaluates use cases where cryptographic signatures alone fail to prove when an agent artifact existed, relying on RFC 3161 Timestamp Authorities (TSA) and OpenTimestamps (OTS) proofs anchored into public ledgers[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-21]:
- **Pre-Dispute Evidence Bundles**: Proving that an evidence bundle digest (audit record, trace, or manifest) existed prior to a dispute without revealing bundle content before necessary[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-21].
- **Agent Card Reliance**: Proving that a delegator relied on a specific version of a counterpart agent's card by verifying that the card's timestamped digest precedes the delegation decision[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-21].
- **Mandate Precedence**: Proving temporal ordering in delegated transactions by demonstrating that human authorization and mandate creation occurred strictly prior to purchase and execution timestamps[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-21].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream harmonizing agentic terminology across working groups and curating an authoritative ecosystem market map.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) body chartered to curate a shared glossary of agentic AI concepts and maintain an authoritative, CNCF-style ecosystem architecture map.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-e6083ea5] Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream acts as a horizontal coordination bridge linking all vertical technical working groups to eliminate terminology silos, prevent duplicate market surveying, and deliver a unified technology blueprint for industry practitioners.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-e6083ea5]

The workstream operates under a federated governance structure where each vertical working group designates Domain Editors who hold review authority over terms relevant to their respective subject matter domains.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-e6083ea5] While its initial charter encompasses both terminology consolidation and ecosystem landscape mapping, active contribution is strictly limited to the taxonomy repository while the landscape contribution workflow remains in development on the roadmap.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-bb61ada3]

# Architecture / Specification

### The Horizontal Index Principle

To preserve domain sovereignty and avoid jurisdictional conflict across vertical working groups, the workstream enforces the "Horizontal Index" principle:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3]
- **Consolidation over Creation:** The workstream does not author specialized domain definitions from scratch; rather, it ingests, standardizes, and harmonizes glossaries developed by vertical working groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3]
- **In-Scope Index:** Foundational vocabulary and cross-cutting concepts spanning two or more working groups, along with universal ecosystem taxonomy structures, fall under workstream management.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3]
- **Out-of-Scope Payload:** Deep-dive domain whitepapers, specialized internal technical helpers, code-level wire protocol schemas, and low-level protocol designs remain the exclusive purview of their respective vertical groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-e6083ea5]

### SKOS-Lite Data Schema and Deferred Fields Policy

Taxonomy definitions are stored in `taxonomy/taxonomy.json` using a normalized Simple Knowledge Organization System (SKOS) Lite representation:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025]
- **Core Attributes:** Entries mandate `term` (unique sentence-case string), `aliases` (array of true synonyms), `workgroups` (array of sponsoring working groups), `scopeNote`, `relatedTerms` (`skos:related`), and `contrastsWith`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025]
- **Deferred Fields (as of 2026-07-27):** Under workstream consensus, terms are admitted ahead of final definitions to avoid premature rigidity. The `definition` attribute holds a standardized pending placeholder (`Definition pending — term accepted; definition under working group discussion.`), while `category` is initialized to empty string (`""`) and `broaderTerm` is initialized to `null` pending hierarchical mapping between groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025]
- **Workgroup Assignment Rules:** The value `"Universal"` is explicitly disallowed; entries with cross-cutting relevance across all groups use an empty array (`[]`) and document contextual boundaries within `scopeNote`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025]

### Epistemological Disambiguation Protocol

When reconciling cross-cutting terminology intersections, contributors and automated systems must apply the Paired Contrast Disambiguation Protocol:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3]
1. **Counterpart Disambiguation:** Terms that derive operational clarity by contrast (such as Tool versus Skill or Deterministic versus Agentic workflows) must not be merged into generic catch-all entries.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3]
2. **Mandatory Associative Linking:** Each term must link explicitly via `relatedTerms` or `contrastsWith`, and its eventual definition must document boundary differences.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3]
3. **Anti-Erasure Guardrails:** No concept may be deleted or collapsed into an alias without written sign-off from the owning Domain Editor.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-21:** Workstream charter approved with weekly synchronization cadence, establishing Junjie Bu and Gala Malbasic as co-chairs.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-e6083ea5]
- **2026-07-27:** Workstream established the deferred fields policy (`category`, `broaderTerm`, and `definition` staged as pending) to facilitate broad term intake across foundational groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025]
- **2026-09-28:** Successfully integrated seven core observability concepts (Reasoning, Agent Trajectory, Context Propagation, Context Assembly, Memory Access, Retrieval, and Traceability) from the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

# References

[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3]: Autonomous Agent & Contributor Guidance (`AGENTS.md`).
[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025]: Data Schema Specifications & Guidelines (`docs/data-schemas.md`).

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy Contribution and Schema Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Authoring standards, Zod schema validation rules, deferred fields policy, and review workflows for contributing terms to the AAIF taxonomy.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy Contribution and Schema Guidelines define the data structure, validation procedures, and submission workflow required to propose terminology additions to the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-bb61ada3] All vocabulary concepts are tracked in `taxonomy/taxonomy.json` and validated through automated Zod schemas to ensure deterministic build behavior, graph rendering, and search indexing across the public portal.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025]

Contributions are currently restricted to taxonomy terms; proposals modifying the ecosystem landscape catalog are out of scope until formal landscape contribution rules are ratified.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-bb61ada3]

# Architecture / Specification

### Taxonomy Glossary Schema Specification

Every term in `taxonomy/taxonomy.json` must be a valid JSON object matching the SKOS-Lite schema:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025]

| Field | Type | Constraint / Value Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `term` | String (Required) | Unique across the file; formatted in sentence case.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025] |
| `category` | String (Required) | **Deferred:** must be set to `""` for initial intake.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025] |
| `aliases` | Array of Strings (Required) | Synonyms or historical labels; use `[]` if none.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025] |
| `broaderTerm` | String or null (Required) | **Deferred:** must be set to `null` to maintain a flat initial taxonomy.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025] |
| `definition` | String (Required) | **Deferred:** must use exactly `Definition pending — term accepted; definition under working group discussion.`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025] |
| `scopeNote` | String (Optional) | Contextual rationale, meeting review dates, or inter-group boundary explanations.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025] |
| `relatedTerms` | Array of Strings (Optional) | Associative `skos:related` linkages; defaults to `[]`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025] |
| `contrastsWith` | Array of Strings (Optional) | Explicit contrast pairings (e.g., Tool vs. Skill); defaults to `[]`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025] |
| `workgroups` | Array of Strings (Required) | Array of aligned technical working groups; `"Universal"` is prohibited.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025] |

### Disambiguation and Anti-Erasure Rules

1. **Paired Contrast Mapping:** If a term is defined primarily in opposition to an adjacent concept, contributors must link both terms via `contrastsWith` and contrast their boundaries in `scopeNote` rather than merging them.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3]
2. **Domain Editor Sign-Off:** Pull requests that collapse look-alike concepts or delete existing terms require explicit approval from the nominated Domain Editors of the affected working groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-65b1abe3]

### Pre-Submission Validation Workflow

Contributors must validate changes locally before opening a pull request:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-bb61ada3]
1. Install dependencies via `npm ci --ignore-scripts`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-bb61ada3]
2. Run automated Zod validation and regression tests using `npm run check`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-bb61ada3]
3. Start the client preview server using `python3 -m http.server 8000` or `npx serve -l 8000` and visually inspect the taxonomy explorer at `http://localhost:8000/taxonomy/`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-bb61ada3]
4. Confirm zero console errors and verify all hyperlinks use secure `https://` URLs.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-bb61ada3]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-21:** Guidelines established following ratification of the Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream charter.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-e6083ea5]
- **2026-07-27:** Ratified deferred fields convention across `category`, `broaderTerm`, and `definition` to accelerate term intake.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-6a955025]

# References

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry and correlation specification standardizing agent execution entities, turn boundaries, and evidence-backed OpenTelemetry trace conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry and correlation specification stewarded by the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869] The specification defines structural representations for agent execution trajectories, turn boundaries, causal call chains, approval gates, and state-change outcomes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

Following an empirical survey of major coding agents and agent SDKs, the working group discovered substantial discrepancies in OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic convention compliance—including divergent span hierarchies, conflicting session identifiers, outdated token usage metrics, and absent human-in-the-loop approval representations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869] Consequently, the specification development strategy shifted from theoretical specification authoring to an evidence-driven methodology anchored on real-world runtime emissions from [Goose](../resources/goose.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

# Architecture / Specification

### Core Behavioral Dimensions

The trace model evaluates agent execution records against four foundational behavioral questions:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
1. **Continuity:** How execution identity, session parentage, and trajectory steps persist across multi-turn exchanges and agent interruptions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
2. **Calls and Retries:** How external tool invocations, retried failures, and fallback strategies are recorded across client and server protocol boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
3. **Approvals:** How interactive human-in-the-loop authorization gates and policy checks are represented within trace contexts.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
4. **Effects:** How tangible environmental side effects, tool outputs, and downstream state mutations are causally linked to initiating spans.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

### Evidence-Driven Reference Architecture (Goose Baseline)

Rather than implementing an isolated greenfield specification, the working group utilizes [Goose](../resources/goose.md)—the AAIF native general-purpose agent runtime—as its reference implementation platform:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
- **Baseline Telemetry Ingestion:** Capturing baseline OpenTelemetry spans and logs emitted by Goose during standardized multi-step tasks.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
- **Gap Register:** Logging identified telemetry omissions and span structural deficits against the four core behavioral dimensions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
- **Upstream Collaboration:** Proposing targeted semantic extensions directly to upstream OpenTelemetry working groups backed by empirical capture artifacts.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07-31:** Initial charter deliverable target scheduled for trace model recommendations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
- **2026-09-29:** Execution plan formally merged under lead Matthew Lee, restructuring follow-on workstreams into an evidence-first order and establishing the Goose reference capture harness.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

# References

[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]: Observability & Traceability Working Group September 2026 Report (`reporting/2026-09-report.md`).

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing agent telemetry, causal execution traces, protocol boundary metrics, and runtime observability models.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group establishes vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and telemetry conventions for monitoring, profiling, and causally reconstructing agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869] Co-chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the working group focuses on capturing agent trajectory across runtime primitives, tool interfaces, external Model Context Protocol boundaries, and distributed agent-to-agent interactions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

# Architecture / Specification

### Primary Workstreams and Focus Areas

The working group organizes its technical output across three primary sub-focus areas:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model:** Led by Matthew Lee, standardizing execution traces across session continuity, tool invocation retries, human approval gates, and downstream environmental effects using [Goose](../resources/goose.md) as an empirical reference harness.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
- **LLM Primitives & Protocols:** Led by Matthew Khouzam and Zayne Turner, examining boundary context propagation across Model Context Protocol servers and runtime engines. In September 2026, the focus group submitted an upstream lifecycle observability proposal to the [Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD)](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) specification, leveraging W3C Trace Context across discovery, policy evaluation, and resource binding.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
- **State, Context & Reasoning:** Led by Govindaraj, investigating agent state-space representations, lightweight harness-independent state inference layers, and observable task/subagent lifecycle topologies.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

### Cross-Boundary Observability

The group models propagation across protocol and process interfaces, having published an Agent-to-Tool boundary analysis using a local CLI realization that maps OpenTelemetry GenAI spans, W3C Trace Context, process context propagation, and timing boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07-31:** Published initial Working Methods, Prior Work Survey, and Use Case Inventory as living foundation documents.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
- **2026-09-28:** Successfully merged seven core domain terms (Reasoning, Agent Trajectory, Context Propagation, Context Assembly, Memory Access, Retrieval, and Traceability) into the foundation's shared repository via the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]
- **2026-09-29:** Merged execution plan pivoting the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) to an evidence-first strategy based on Goose baseline emissions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]

# References

[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-60f28464dd94-2a91d869]: Observability & Traceability Working Group September 2026 Report (`reporting/2026-09-report.md`).

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e]. Operating under the technical oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group produces open threat models, domain taxonomies, and design patterns that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to share responsibility for trustworthy agentic AI[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e].

# Leadership and Governance

The working group is led by chairs appointed by Platinum and Gold member representatives for terms spanning March 1, 2026, to January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e]:
- **Chair**: Alex Frazer (Runlayer)
- **Co-Chair**: Junjie Bu (Google)

To accommodate international participation across time zones, the working group conducts alternating biweekly sessions where leadership bridges notes and actions between meetings[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e]:
- **Primary Meeting**: Biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT (USA Pacific Time)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e].
- **APAC Meeting**: Biweekly on Mondays at 9:00 PM ET (USA Eastern Time), providing a working-hours schedule for contributors in Asia-Pacific time zones[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group coordinates several core workstreams and deliverables across the foundation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-2c5c574e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314]:
- **Security Design Patterns**: Standardizes structural governance patterns, including the [approval-checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), [attested-isolated-runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md), and [kill-switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) patterns cataloged in the [security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog](../resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314].
- **Security Best Practices**: Develops defensive operational rules and implementation baselines for host sandboxing and secrets management via the [agentic-ai-security-best-practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) guide[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314].
- **Threat Modeling and Risk Assessment**: Performs structured analyses comparing legacy security frameworks against unique agentic risk models in the [agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314].
- **Cross-WG Collaboration**: Evaluates multi-agent delegation with the [Attestation and Evidence Working Group](../working-groups/attestation-and-evidence.md), security review gates with the [cross-wg-security-review-checklist](../guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md), and common terms with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-a5dc3314].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy Explorer and Term Wizard
proposed_concept.description: Zero-backend browser application and wizard for browsing AAIF taxonomy terms and authoring schema-compliant pull requests.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy Explorer and Term Wizard is a zero-backend, single-page web application hosted within the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) repository that enables contributors to browse terms and submit standardized pull requests without local development tooling[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-62f724d00262-cc94b3ad]. Served entirely from static files (`index.html` and `taxonomy-data.js`), the tool bundles catalog search, relational mindmaps, AI-assisted authoring, and token-free GitHub PR submission workflows[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-62f724d00262-cc94b3ad].

# Architecture / Specification

The utility is structured around client-side execution, offline accessibility, and strict validation checks to maintain taxonomy integrity according to the [taxonomy-contribution-guide](../guidelines/taxonomy-contribution-guide.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-62f724d00262-cc94b3ad].

### Data Storage and Execution
Taxonomy definitions are assigned directly to `window.AAIF_TAXONOMY` within `taxonomy-data.js`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-62f724d00262-cc94b3ad]. Loading the script directly avoids server-side rendering, cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) limits, and raw repository API quotas[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-62f724d00262-cc94b3ad].

### Exploration and Term Visualization
The browsing component surfaces terms through search queries, categorical filters, responsive grid card layouts, detailed split-pane inspectors, and interactive visual mindmaps reflecting ontological connections[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-62f724d00262-cc94b3ad].

### AI-Assisted Proposal Drafting
The wizard includes an optional generation capability backed by the key-less Puter SDK[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-62f724d00262-cc94b3ad]:
- **Model Agnosticism**: Provides access to all models made available by the SDK without privileging or defaulting to a single commercial vendor[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-62f724d00262-cc94b3ad].
- **Constrained Outputs**: Cross-references and working group associations suggested by LLMs are constrained against existing vocabulary entries; ungrounded suggestions are rejected by validation passes[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-62f724d00262-cc94b3ad].
- **Provenance Tracking**: Measures character-level and list-overlap edit distance between the model draft and the contributor's final submission, recording the AI contribution ratio and model tag directly in commit metadata and pull request templates[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-62f724d00262-cc94b3ad].
- **Mandatory Review**: Imposes explicit confirmation prompts when an entry is submitted without human modification to prevent silent automated merges[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-62f724d00262-cc94b3ad].

### Validation Rules and Ingestion
Before generating a change payload, the wizard enforces strict integrity guardrails[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-62f724d00262-cc94b3ad]:
- **Alias Non-Collision**: Prevents an alias from colliding with any primary term slug[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-62f724d00262-cc94b3ad].
- **Referential Integrity**: Requires all related or contrasting terms to resolve against pre-existing taxonomy entities[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-62f724d00262-cc94b3ad].

Submissions are dispatched either via a token-less in-browser GitHub commit flow targeting the contributor's fork or via an automated shell script (`create-pr.sh`)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-62f724d00262-cc94b3ad].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing threat modeling frameworks, security design patterns, cross-working-group review checklists, and actionable security best practices for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (WG) defines threat models, defensive architecture patterns, runtime isolation baselines, and cross-cutting security evaluation checklists across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43]. Its scope covers vulnerabilities unique to agentic autonomous execution, context boundaries, dynamic tool discovery, and multi-agent delegation.

# Architecture / Specification

The working group manages several primary workstreams and shared deliverables:

- **Security Best Practices Guide**: Concrete builder guidance maintained in `guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md`, covering context sanitization, credential containment, and sandbox parameters [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43].
- **Threat Modeling Framework**: Following initial gap analysis work in `resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md`, the WG's threat modeling methodology extends STRIDE and PASTA methodologies with agent-specific matrices from MITRE ATLAS and OWASP ASI [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43].
- **Security Design Patterns Catalog**: Reusable implementation blueprints documented in `resources/security-and-privacy-design-patterns-catalog.md`, including containment and revocation mechanisms such as `../patterns/kill-switch.md` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43].
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Operational review criteria in `guidelines/cross-wg-security-review-checklist.md` applied across foundation working groups, with designated liaisons spanning Observability, Agentic Commerce, and Governance [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43].
- **Taxonomy Harmonization**: Security and privacy definitions maintained in cooperation with `../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md`, formally integrated into the cross-WG taxonomy [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43].

# Lifecycle History

Following initial foundation chartering, the WG shipped its initial baseline deliverables in late 2026 and opened external contribution streams for best practices and pattern submissions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43]. The group operates regular global working sessions alongside dedicated APAC timezone meetings [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-43].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification Schema
proposed_concept.description: Multi-dimensional taxonomy and classification schema characterizing agentic AI production deployments across operational shapes, human interaction models, and domain boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Use Case Classification Schema provides an objective multi-dimensional taxonomy for classifying, comparing, and indexing production AI agent deployments across industry sectors [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-58]. Developed under the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group, it establishes standardized criteria to separate business domain contexts from underlying technical execution topologies.

# Architecture / Specification

The schema establishes core architectural dimensions for characterizing agentic systems:

- **Autonomy Level**: Measures decision-making latitude, ranging from advisory assistance to fully autonomous execution.
- **Workflow Shape**: The macroscopic topology of agent coordination (such as single-agent loops, parallel fan-out, or multi-agent swarms). Proposed in ISSUE#58 to replace the label "Workflow Pattern" to prevent collision with formal reference architecture patterns and primitives defined in `../guidelines/reference-architecture-contribution-guide.md` [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-58].
- **Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) Shape**: The intervention model governing human oversight (such as approval gates, durable waits, or exception routing). Proposed in ISSUE#58 to replace "HITL Pattern" [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-58].
- **Boundary and Integration Context**: Integration interfaces spanning tool calls, Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoints, direct APIs, and data storage layers.
- **Evidentiary Standard**: Requirements mandating verified, publicly accessible production citations for all indexed rows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-58].

# Lifecycle History

Developed by the Critical Use Cases workstream of `../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md` to underpin the `../resources/agentic-use-case-inventory.md`. Revisions in late 2026 introduced terminology disambiguation between use case "shapes" and Reference Architecture "patterns" [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-58].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Inventory
proposed_concept.description: Curated catalog of production agent deployments cross-referenced by architectural shape, human-in-the-loop model, and verifiable primary source citations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Use Case Inventory is an evidence-backed repository cataloging verified, real-world AI agent deployments across enterprises and open-source ecosystems [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-59]. Governed by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group, every entry maps a deployment against standardized classification dimensions and links to primary source citations demonstrating genuine production usage [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-59].

# Architecture / Specification

The inventory enforces strict evidentiary standards to ensure catalog integrity:

- **Classification Dimensions**: Each entry records deployment parameters using `../resources/agentic-use-case-classification.md`, categorizing entries by autonomy level, Workflow Shape, and HITL Shape [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-58].
- **Primary Evidence Rule**: Rows must provide at least one publicly verifiable citation (vendor product documentation, technical whitepaper, or deployment announcement) accompanied by publication or retrieval dates [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-59].
- **Automated Link Rot Monitoring**: To address citation decay and vendor restructuring, automated recurring workflows inspect URLs in the Notes column [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-59]. The automation extracts targets, categorizes responses (resolves, redirects, 404, timeouts, or bot-blocked 403s), and generates triage issues when evidence is broken [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-59].
- **Content Integrity Checks**: Secondary validation evaluates whether surviving endpoints still substantiate original claims via content hash checks or targeted text inspection [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-59].

# Lifecycle History

Maintained by the Critical Use Cases workstream in `../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md`. Ongoing governance updates focused on automated citation hygiene to sustain evidentiary validity [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-59] and aligning column terminology with reference architecture guidelines [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-58].

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards, delegation models, cryptographic trust frameworks, and verifiable authority evaluation suites for autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity and Trust Working Group establishes standards, cryptographic protocols, and reference architectures governing autonomous agent identity, credential verification, and delegated authority [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]. It provides technical models to ensure agents operate within strictly bounded authority delegated by accountable principals without unnecessary disclosure of identity graphs [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group's Reference Architecture v1 defines normative invariants and verification checks for delegated authority:

- **Time-of-Use Verification**: Mandates that authority grants, action constraints, target objects, and status validity be evaluated at execution time rather than relying on self-reported assertions [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22].
- **Chain Separation**: Enforces structural separation between delegation chains (what an agent is permitted to execute) and accountability chains (which legal or human principal bears liability) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22].
- **Attenuation Across Hops**: Prohibits authority amplification across multi-hop agent delegations, requiring scopes to narrow or remain identical at each subsequent hop [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22].
- **Cascading Bounded Revocation**: Requires revocation of a principal or intermediate delegator to propagate predictably across all derived authority within documented time boundaries [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22].
- **Conformance Cases and Residual Reporting**: A proposed eight-case test appendix assesses implementations against common failure modes (revocation propagation, out-of-scope actions, stale status data, offline escalation approvers, delegation amplification, expired grants with valid identities, delegation graph surveillance leaks, and disputed revocations) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22]. Implementations must explicitly declare their "residual"—documenting the uncovered edge cases or accepted trade-offs rather than asserting unqualified conformance [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22].

# Lifecycle History

Chartered as an inaugural AAIF working group. In late 2026, the WG finalized Reference Architecture v1 principles and initiated community testing against reference delegation architectures [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-22].
