proposed_concept.title: AAIF Create Chapter Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational provisioning and rebranding skill that spins up new AAIF city chapters by cloning template assets and executing four-surface in-place renames via the Google Workspace CLI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-create-chapter` skill is an automated provisioning and design asset generation pipeline for spinning up new Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) city chapters within the community estate in Google Drive[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a]. It operates by cloning the standardized `TemplateCity` folder in Google Drive and executing structured rebranding passes across document text, presentation slides, attendee spreadsheets, and file naming conventions. It also governs in-place renaming operations across existing chapter estates through a coordinated four-surface transform[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].

Within the broader community operations architecture, this skill forms part of the estate lifecycle managed by [community-event-operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md), coordinating with diagnostic verification in [aaif-check-setup](../skills/aaif-check-setup.md), snapshot safeguards in [aaif-backup](../skills/aaif-backup.md), and directory reconciliation in [aaif-sync](../skills/aaif-sync.md).

# Operational Specification & Tooling Constraints

## Execution Tooling & File Integrity Rules

All interactions with Drive files are strictly restricted to the Google Workspace (`gws`) CLI driven by Python scripts[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a]:

- **Native Google Formats Preferred**: Files using `application/vnd.google-apps.*` are modified directly via the Docs, Sheets, or Slides APIs[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].
- **OOXML Binary Surgery**: Stored Office files (`.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`) are updated using byte-level Open Packaging Conventions (OOXML) surgery on zip package parts to preserve embedded fonts and unedited components[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].
- **Ban on Headless Office Suites**: The use of LibreOffice (`soffice`), `unoconv`, or desktop office suites is forbidden for edits, conversions, or local previews, as they substitute system fonts and corrupt proprietary markup[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a]. Previews must be generated via the Slides rendering API or via Google Doc PDF export pipelines[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].

## Template Asset Rebranding

When instantiating a chapter from `TemplateCity`, the skill targets a fixed set of template files including `Event Tracker.docx`, `Attendee CRM.xlsx`, and design subfolders (`Event Template/` and `Banners (...)`)[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a]. Rebranding strictly replaces:

- `San Francisco` / `SAN FRANCISCO` with the new city name, matching case[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].
- The abbreviation `SF` (e.g., `AAIF · SF`, `SF CHAPTER`) with the full city name[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].
- Luma slug identifiers `aaif-sanfrancisco` with `aaif-<slug>`[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].
- File and folder names containing old city references[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].
- Geographical network map positioning: Slide 5 ("THE NETWORK") of `Event Template/Slides.pptx` updates its green indicator dot and `<CITY> · TONIGHT` label to real geographic coordinates resolved via `--lat`/`--lon` flags or Nominatim geocoding[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].

Event-specific placeholder fields (dates, speakers, venues, and neighbourhood tokens) remain untouched for event-level configuration skills[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-7c3a1e3a].

# Chapter Renaming Architecture

Renaming an existing chapter is managed by `rename_chapter.py` as a four-surface update[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c]:

1. **Chapter Folder**: The root Drive folder name is renamed to match the new city entity[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].
2. **File and Subfolder Names**: Internal file handles and subdirectories (such as CRMs and icon directories) are updated[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].
3. **OOXML Document Content**: Internal body text within `.docx`, `.pptx`, and `.xlsx` archives is transformed[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].
4. **Document Metadata**: Packaging properties (`docProps`) such as internal chapter labels are updated to preserve consistency across synchronization workflows[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].

To prevent broken external references, Luma slug links are kept distinct from the chapter's physical name and are not updated unless explicitly passed via `--slug-from` and `--slug-to` flags[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c]. Furthermore, relationship files (`.rels`) only receive slug updates to prevent dangling internal relationship targets that cause document corruption[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c]. Pre-mutation backups are stored under `backups/rename-<UTC>/` prior to remote upload[^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-ba23000c].

proposed_concept.title: aaif-create-chapter
proposed_concept.description: Operational provisioning and rebranding skill that creates and renames AAIF city chapters, generates customized Drive assets, and renders localized Web Banners.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-create-chapter` skill automates the operational provisioning, asset replication, and rebranding required when establishing or renaming an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) city chapter [^evt-community-events-pr-65]. It clones templated Google Drive estates, rewrites Open Office XML (OOXML) text representations, and ensures graphical chapter collateral—such as square web banners—accurately reflect local chapter nomenclature [^evt-community-events-pr-65].

# Architecture / Specification
The provisioning pipeline operates as a sequence of templating, text substitution, raster rendering, and metadata verification steps [^evt-community-events-pr-65]:

## Asset Rebranding and Template Cloning
When a chapter is initialized, template folders containing presentation decks, sheets, and collateral are cloned. Text modifications to OOXML files replace template placeholders with the official chapter name [^evt-community-events-pr-65].

## Web Banner Generation Pipeline
Because graphical assets store text rasterized into image pixels rather than editable OOXML text runs, `Web Banner.png` cannot be rebranded solely via string replacement [^evt-community-events-pr-65]. Chapter banner generation uses `render_web_banner.py` [^evt-community-events-pr-65]:
- **Slide Source**: Derives the 2000x2000 banner image directly from slide four of the chapter's rebranded presentation deck (`Banners (…)/Square Logo.pptx`) [^evt-community-events-pr-65].
- **Server-Side Rasterization**: Exports the slide via Google Slides native export API (`slides_export.render_slide_png`) without relying on local headless office suites [^evt-community-events-pr-65].
- **Content Verification**: Validates that slide text explicitly matches "AAIF Community Events" concatenated with the exact chapter name before rendering, repeating this check on the drawn output [^evt-community-events-pr-65].
- **Drive Metadata Stamping**: Stamps the uploaded `Web Banner.png` file in Google Drive `appProperties` with the source presentation's `md5Checksum` and chapter name, allowing idempotent re-runs to skip unchanged assets and re-render only when decks change or renames occur [^evt-community-events-pr-65].
- **Failure Handling**: Clean provisioning writes exit with code 2 if banner generation fails; `rename_chapter` invocations exit with code 1 upon banner render failures [^evt-community-events-pr-65].

# Lifecycle History
Previously, binary template copies caused newly created and renamed chapters to retain template city names in their square banners [^evt-community-events-pr-65]. PR #65 introduced dynamic slide export, text validation guards, and Google Drive checksum caching to resolve estate-wide branding inconsistencies [^evt-community-events-pr-65].

# References
- Upstream skill pipeline: [community-event-operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md)
- Diagnostic verification: [aaif-check-setup](../skills/aaif-check-setup.md)

proposed_concept.title: aaif-check-setup
proposed_concept.description: Diagnostic agent skill validating local runtime dependencies, Google Workspace credentials, Slack and Luma secrets, and execution permissions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-check-setup` skill provides automated, read-only diagnostic verification for operators running the AAIF Community Events Toolkit across various client engines such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and Claude Desktop [^evt-community-events-pr-66][^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7]. It executes a structured series of pass/fail validation checks across Python runtimes, CLI dependencies, Google Workspace connections, and API credentials, offering actionable remediation instructions for failing items [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7].

# Architecture / Specification
The diagnostic utility is architected for standalone operation without third-party library dependencies, enabling direct execution from packaged zip archives or installed agent plugin locations [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7][^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9].

## Diagnostic Checks
The utility evaluates the following requirements [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7]:
- **Runtime and Tooling**: Python interpreter compatibility, plugin installation integrity, `gws` Google Workspace CLI availability, and Google Chrome presence [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7].
- **Google Workspace Connectivity**: Confirms presence of the local Google connection configuration file, reporting missing files directly rather than instructing non-functional terminal sign-ins [^evt-community-events-pr-66]. It verifies edit permissions on the central intake spreadsheet [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7].
- **API Credentials**: Tests read and write connectivity for Slack tokens and Luma API access [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7].

## Secret Resolution Order
Installed agent plugins execute without an interactive shell environment [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9]. The skill mirrors the standardized `aaif_events.credentials` secret resolution hierarchy [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7]:
1. Operating system environment variables [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7].
2. Repository root `.env` configuration file [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7].
3. macOS Keychain (`aaif-slack-read-token`, `aaif-slack-write-token`, and `luma-api-key`), with per-run caching to minimize security prompt interruptions [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7].

# Lifecycle History
Originally, diagnostic failures directed users toward interactive login flows or external administrative helpers [^evt-community-events-pr-66]. PR #66 restructured onboarding documentation and updated `aaif-check-setup` to diagnose missing Google connection files and support multi-operator self-service configurations without requiring administrative intermediaries [^evt-community-events-pr-66].

# References
- Community operations framework: [community-event-operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md)
- Chapter provisioning: [aaif-create-chapter](../skills/aaif-create-chapter.md)
- Goose agent runtime: [goose](../resources/goose.md)

proposed_concept.title: community-event-operations
proposed_concept.description: Procedural operations pipeline and shared infrastructure managing chapter provisioning, estate lifecycle, intake ingestion, CRM sync, and event communications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `community-event-operations` skill defines the core automation pipeline and operational guidelines governing AAIF local chapter management [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9]. It standardizes chapter intake, spreadsheet reconciliation, Google Drive estate provisioning, Slack workspace orchestration, and Luma calendar management across both technical and non-technical foundation operators [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7][^evt-community-events-pr-66].

# Architecture / Specification
The pipeline is structured to execute across disparate agent runtimes such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and Claude Desktop while maintaining data privacy and filesystem boundaries [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9]:

## Runtime Execution & Paths
- **Engine Differences**: Goose installs community skills as live git checkouts, whereas Claude Desktop packages static versioned folder trees lacking `.git` metadata [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9]. Commands reference root paths via `<skill-root>` rather than hardcoded repository structures [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9].
- **Working Directory Isolation**: Agent operations must never write intermediate or output files to the current working directory [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9]. Persistent state routes through `aaif_events.datadir`, while scratch files are managed inside isolated temporary directories (`mktemp -d`) [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9].
- **Credential Resolution**: Secrets cascade from process environment variables to local `.env` files, falling back to the macOS Keychain (`aaif-slack-read-token`, `aaif-slack-write-token`, `luma-api-key`) with run-level caching [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7].

## Privacy and PII Hygiene
Because repository files and GitHub Actions runner outputs are public, operational commands adhere to strict PII boundaries [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9]:
- Live organizer, speaker, and attendee identifiers (such as emails, phone numbers, and Slack user IDs) are prohibited in test fixtures, docstrings, commits, and logs [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9].
- Audit logs and backups must target paths ignored by version control (`.slack-audit-cache/`, `**/backups/*`, `slack-*-audit.*`) and must be removed after execution [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9].
- Automated CI verification (`scripts/check_no_real_pii.py`) enforces syntax and synthetic test data standards prior to merge [^evt-community-events-file-a54ff182c7e8-b01e6de9].

## Intake Pipeline and Role Gating
- **Multi-Role Intake Migration**: Community intake forms transitioned from single-select queries to independent Yes/No role questions covering Organizers, Hosts, Speakers, and Collaborators [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7]. Spreadsheet migration scripts (`migrate_intake_role_gates.py`) map compound candidate applications into corresponding Ops tabs [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7].
- **Geographic Sync**: City selection choices are periodically synchronized with the central Chapter List to harmonize national and metropolitan designations [^evt-community-events-pr-64].

# Lifecycle History
The toolkit originally relied on operator helpers and shared developer setups [^evt-community-events-pr-66]. Following PR #65, PR #66, and intake schema migrations, the pipeline gained standalone diagnostic tooling (`aaif-check-setup`), decoupled multi-operator onboarding, and automated presentation-to-banner rendering [^evt-community-events-pr-65][^evt-community-events-pr-66][^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-8cb799a7].

# References
- Diagnostic verification: [aaif-check-setup](../skills/aaif-check-setup.md)
- Chapter initialization: [aaif-create-chapter](../skills/aaif-create-chapter.md)
- Runtime host: [goose](../resources/goose.md)

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing agent telemetry, causal execution traces, protocol boundary metrics, and cross-framework observability interoperability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) to establish shared models for agent observability, trace structures, and causal execution telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d]. The working group focuses on the intersection of agent behavioral reasoning and execution with observable signals, prioritizing interoperability across disparate execution frameworks and monitoring ecosystems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group anchors its technical deliverables around shared telemetry foundations, including the Agent Behavior Trace Model, prior work landscape surveys, and real-world practitioner use-case inventories [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d]. Cross-ecosystem coordination is maintained via an explicit liaison model spanning external standards consortia and sibling AAIF workstreams [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f5077fe55915-f29d3cf9]:

- **External Liaisons**: Primary coordination with OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG (spanning turn spans and semantic conventions), Agent Trace (Cursor), AGNTCY, libp2p, HOL (Hedera), and Agent Action Capsule [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f5077fe55915-f29d3cf9].
- **Internal AAIF Workstreams**: Active alignment with [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) (proposing candidate terms like turn and agent step), [Accuracy and Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) (evaluating agent execution outcomes), [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), and [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f5077fe55915-f29d3cf9].
- **Cross-Boundary Implementations**: Engagement on discovery and runtime boundary tracing with Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD), A2A, and Agent Gateway [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f5077fe55915-f29d3cf9].

# Lifecycle History

The working group operates under the technical leadership of Chair Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Co-Chair Matthew Lee (Datadog), appointed by Platinum and Gold working group members for the term spanning March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d]. Formal working sessions occur biweekly on Wednesdays at 10:00 AM PT via LFX Zoom [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-1e66868d].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Procedural operations pipeline and shared infrastructure managing chapter provisioning, estate lifecycle syncs, and isolated operator credentials across Google Workspace, Slack, and Luma.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Community Event Operations infrastructure provides AI assistants—primarily [Goose](../resources/goose.md), Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Codex—with procedural skills to manage AAIF community events, local chapters, and communications across Google Drive, Slack, and Luma [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27] [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-23a10754]. The toolkit packages portable Agent Skills and plugin manifests allowing non-technical operators to execute event scheduling, chapter setup, and sync procedures safely [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27] [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-23a10754].

# Architecture / Specification

The toolkit enforces strict functional and credential boundary architectures across operational roles [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27] [^evt-community-events-pr-67]:

- **Content versus Ops Segmentation**: Pure content skills (drafting LinkedIn posts, carousels, speaker bios, slide copy, and invitations) execute with zero required backend credentials [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27] [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-23a10754]. Ops skills (chapter provisioning, monthly synchronization, and intake intake audits) require authenticated access [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27].
- **Per-Operator Credential Isolation**: The toolkit prohibits shared service accounts and shared tokens [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27] [^evt-community-events-pr-67]. Operators must generate their own Google OAuth client configuration file, their own user-scoped Slack token (`xoxp-`), and their own Luma API keys [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27] [^evt-community-events-pr-67]. Slack user tokens are mandated because channel creators join target channels automatically, while user tokens scope search and post permissions strictly to the individual operator [^evt-community-events-file-953dd2e86174-8ce1fa27] [^evt-community-events-pr-67].
- **Tooling Constraints**: Drive file manipulations strictly mandate native Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) and Docs/Sheets/Slides APIs driven via Python [^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451]. External suites such as LibreOffice or `soffice` are prohibited to prevent font substitution and OOXML degradation [^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451].

# Lifecycle History

Originally scoped with shared administrative credentials, the access architecture was updated in Pull Request #67 to enforce decentralized, per-operator credentials after identifying that shared user tokens granted multi-tenant visibility across private operator communications and direct messages [^evt-community-events-pr-67].

proposed_concept.title: aaif-check-setup
proposed_concept.description: Diagnostic agent skill validating local runtime dependencies, Google Workspace credentials, Slack and Luma authentication, and guiding credential remediation without leaking secrets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The `aaif-check-setup` skill is a read-only diagnostic capability within the AAIF community events toolkit that verifies whether a host computer is properly configured to execute operational automations [^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451]. It assesses Python 3 availability, plugin installations, Google Workspace (`gws`) CLI tokens and permission scopes, Community Intake sheet access, Slack authorization, Luma calendar keys, and headless Chrome [^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451].

# Architecture / Specification

The diagnostic engine runs via `python3 <skill-root>/scripts/check_setup.py` under clear boundary invariants [^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451]:

- **Non-Destructive Read-Only Operation**: Reads single sheet metadata, calls Slack `auth.test`, and Luma `calendars/get` without performing mutations or leaking raw keys/tokens into execution logs [^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451].
- **Remediation Guidance**: Translates diagnostic failures into non-technical step-by-step resolution paths [^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451]. For credential failures, it directs operators to authenticate their personal OAuth configuration and generate individual tokens, avoiding shared administrative token lookups [^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451] [^evt-community-events-pr-67].
- **Workspace Manipulation Isolation**: Verifies `gws` integration, reinforcing policy restrictions that ban third-party rendering suites like LibreOffice (`soffice`) in favor of direct API operations and temporary PDF previews [^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-6740e451].

# Lifecycle History

Updated in Pull Request #67 to adjust diagnostic resolution steps away from centralized credential distribution toward individual operator credential provisioning [^evt-community-events-pr-67].

mutations.rationale: Update the Single-Agent Process with Human Approval architecture specification and record its unanimous plenary vote and terminology updates.

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Process with Human Approval
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture enforcing human authorization before executing protected, irreversible, or policy-governed agent actions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Single-Agent Process with Human Approval reference architecture establishes an enforceable, human-mediated structural separation between probabilistic agent intent and protected system execution.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-2fb150b7] Governed by the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), this architecture standardizes the workflow pattern where an agent prepares a proposed action, a designated human approves or rejects it, and only then may a controlled executor apply the change.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-2fb150b7] It became the working group's second formally voted deliverable in September 2026.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e]

# Architecture / Specification
The architecture enforces separation of authority across discrete workflow roles:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-2fb150b7]
- **Proposer (Agent)**: An agent investigates, computes, and formats a candidate proposal (such as a financial refund or infrastructure change) but lacks capabilities or credentials to trigger external effects directly.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-2fb150b7]
- **Approval Gate & Durable Wait**: Persists the exact proposal payload and suspends execution via [durable wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md) across arbitrarily long human review cycles without losing state or duplicating pending operations.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-2fb150b7]
- **Workflow-Controlled Executor**: An automated component that acts only upon explicit human approval, strictly decoupled from the agent's invocation capabilities.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-2fb150b7]
- **System of Record**: Maintains an immutable audit trace capturing the full proposer intent, approver authorization, and execution outcome.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-2fb150b7]

Under working group taxonomy conventions, a "business task" denotes the overall request or problem handled by the workflow, while constituent steps are designated as activities.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-2fb150b7][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e]

Composed patterns include:
- [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
- [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)
- [Durable Wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md)

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-09-17**: Voted and approved unanimously at the WG Workflows & Process Integration plenary meeting.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e]
- **2026-10-02**: Follow-up PR #50 merged, aligning internal terminology to "business task" and "activity".[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e]

# References
- [Proposal/Execution Split Pattern](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
- [Human Approval Gate Pattern](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)
- [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](bounded-autonomous-remediation.md)

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture governing iterative, autonomous problem resolution through declared budgets, deterministic gates, and escalation paths.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Bounded Autonomous Remediation reference architecture governs workflows that resolve a specific, bounded problem autonomously without requiring human authorization for every intermediate step.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e] Developed by the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), it acts as a counterpart to the [Single-Agent Process with Human Approval](single-agent-human-approval.md) for scenarios where candidate actions have constrained impact, are reversible, and can be evaluated using independent deterministic evidence.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e]

# Architecture / Specification
The architecture guarantees bounded autonomy, independent acceptance, constrained side effects, and safe non-convergence handling:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e]
- **Execution Engine**: Governs the lifecycle of the business task, enforces admission criteria, tracks iteration budgets, and triggers safe termination or escalation.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e]
- **Isolated Work Area**: Limits agent tooling, credentials, and data access to a non-authoritative staging sandbox (such as a branch or draft record).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e]
- **Deterministic Acceptance Gate**: Evaluates the candidate result against explicit, repeatable validation rules, contracts, or test suites, preventing model self-assessment from certifying output validity.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677]
- **Constrained Effect Executor**: Applies only the accepted, scope-valid change to external systems.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e]
- **Escalation Surface**: Dispatches unresolvable tasks, exhausted budgets, or scope violations to human operators for review.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-d009744e]

Composed patterns:
- [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md)
- [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md)
- [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08-29**: Core reference architecture merged via PR #26.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e]
- **2026-09-15**: Validation record merged via PR #37 covering maintenance runs and scheduling tasks.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e]
- **2026-09**: PR #43 proposed minimum evidence standards based on action reversibility and blast radius, and PR #49 introduced terminology alignment.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e]

- [Proposal/Execution Split Pattern](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)

proposed_concept.title: Proposal/Execution Split
proposed_concept.description: Architectural governance pattern separating intent generation, authorization, and workflow execution into distinct roles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Proposal/Execution Split is a workflow governance pattern establishing that intent generation, authorization, and workflow execution belong to distinct, decoupled roles, each recorded independently in an audit trail.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2] Because probabilistic language model outputs cannot inherently guarantee regulatory or business compliance, this pattern prevents agents from executing actions directly, ensuring strict authorization and attribution at the boundary of protected side effects.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2]

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern partitions workflow responsibilities into three decoupled stages:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2]
1. **Proposer (Agent)**: Creates candidate data expressing intent. The proposal is an immutable data artifact rather than an executable capability.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2]
2. **Authorization Authority (Gate)**: Evaluates the exact candidate proposal against explicit policy rules or human approval. The authorization gate fails closed on missing, expired, or rejected checks.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2]
3. **Workflow-Controlled Executor**: A dedicated system capability invoked only after positive authorization to apply the approved change. Credentials and execution rights are held solely by the executor, never by the agent.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2]

Normative invariants:
- Intent, authorization, and execution remain structurally separated.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2]
- The authorization gate fails closed.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2]
- Authorization records bind cryptographically or immutably to the specific proposal version evaluated.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2]
- Execution cannot alter the authorized proposal payload.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-832c48c2]

# References

- [Durable Wait](durable-wait.md)
- [Single-Agent Process with Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md)

proposed_concept.title: Deterministic Acceptance Gate
proposed_concept.description: Architectural pattern evaluating candidate agent outputs against explicit, repeatable checks and scope rules rather than model self-assessment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Deterministic Acceptance Gate is an architectural pattern that evaluates candidate agent outputs against explicit, repeatable criteria and declared scope constraints before allowing workflow advancement.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677] Formulated by the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), this pattern eliminates reliance on probabilistic model self-assessment, which can produce unwarranted confidence in invalid results.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677]

# Architecture / Specification
The gate validates outputs using independent, automated mechanisms:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677]
- **Deterministic Evaluation**: Tests, schemas, contracts, and policy engines assess the candidate output reproducibly.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677]
- **Scope & Policy Constraints**: Validates that changes remain within authorized targets, permitted modification classes, tool boundaries, and blast-radius limits.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677]
- **Evidence Association**: Binds verification records to the exact version, artifact digest, or candidate identity evaluated.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677]

Key invariants:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-4c010677]
- Acceptance criteria are declared before candidate evaluation occurs.
- Evaluators operate independently of the generating model context.
- Acceptance evidence binds to the specific evaluated candidate digest.
- Passing technical checks is insufficient if scope or policy bounds are breached.
- Ambiguous, failed, or unavailable verification never defaults to permission.

# References
- [Bounded Convergence Loop](bounded-convergence-loop.md)
- [Proposal/Execution Split](proposal-execution-split.md)
- [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md)

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Estate Synchronization
proposed_concept.description: Procedural estate synchronization orchestrator executing reconciliation across Slack and Google Drive community assets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-sync` skill automates the reconciliation of AAIF community operational states across Google Workspace spreadsheets, Google Drive asset repositories, and Slack organization channels.[^evt-community-events-pr-68] It ensures community rosters, permissions, and directory entries remain synchronized without dropping pending changes or generating erroneous multi-account invites.[^evt-community-events-pr-68]

# Architecture / Specification
The synchronization framework executes coordinated reconciliation modules:[^evt-community-events-pr-68]
- **Drift and State Reporting (`sync.py`)**: Classifies sync execution states into `WROTE` for successful write passes, `DRIFT` when pending work requires `--write` execution, and `needs review` for open non-zero findings requiring operator inspection.[^evt-community-events-pr-68]
- **Organizer Invitations (`invite_organizers.py`)**: Counts unique individuals separately from channel-addition actions, holds invites for personas with conflicting records or multiple active accounts, and treats missing or deactivated accounts safely to prevent duplicate or incorrect invites.[^evt-community-events-pr-68]
- **Identity Suggestions**: Executes Slack identity lookups with `--suggest`, preventing unverified match writes without human confirmation.[^evt-community-events-pr-68]
- **CRM Synchronization (`sync_crm.py`)**: Reconciles community intake entries against central CRM records.[^evt-community-events-pr-68]

# References

- [AAIF Audit Slack](aaif-audit-slack.md)

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing shared agentic workflow execution models, reference architectures, and boundary control patterns.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (WG Workflows & Process Integration) develops vendor-neutral execution models, reference architectures, workflow primitives, and boundary control patterns for agentic systems within the Agentic AI Foundation.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e] Co-chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato), the group defines reliable integration patterns uniting non-deterministic LLM behaviors with deterministic enterprise process controls.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e]

# Architecture / Specification
The group's core activities span three workstreams:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e]
- **Reference Architectures**: Authors foundational workflow patterns and composite architectures, notably the [Single-Agent Process with Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) and [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e]
- **Critical Use Cases**: Curates real-world production agent implementations across industry verticals. In September 2026, the workstream adopted the designation "workflow shape" and "HITL shape" to distinguish empirical observations from prescriptive reference architecture patterns.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e]
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Coordinates with the cross-WG taxonomy workstream to harmonize execution nomenclature, defining "activity" for workflow execution subunits and adopting "business task" as the overarching problem handled by a workflow.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08-29**: Core specification for Bounded Autonomous Remediation merged via PR #26.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e]
- **2026-09-17**: Single-Agent Process with Human Approval passed plenary vote unanimously, becoming the WG's second voted artifact.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e]
- **2026-09-22**: Critical Use Cases and Reference Architectures aligned to differentiate observational "shapes" from normative patterns.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-60f28464dd94-4c7ddd9e]

# References

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Convergence Loop
proposed_concept.description: Architectural pattern safely iterating an agent-driven task within explicit budget limits until a deterministic acceptance condition passes or an escalation path triggers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Bounded Convergence Loop pattern governs iterative agent-assisted execution for bounded business tasks that cannot reliably be completed in a single pass.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8] Rather than granting an open-ended goal or allowing models to self-certify completion, the workflow admits an explicitly scoped task, exposes strictly bounded tools, and subjects every candidate result to evaluation by an independent deterministic gate.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8]

This pattern serves as a core primitive in [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md) and cooperates with [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](deterministic-acceptance-gate.md), [Proposal/Execution Split](proposal-execution-split.md), and [Durable Wait](durable-wait.md).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8]

# Architecture / Specification

## Operational Lifecycle
1. **Task Admission:** A bounded business task enters the workflow with declared constraints, required tools, and an explicit acceptance test before execution begins.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8]
2. **Bounded Execution:** The agent attempts the permitted remediation or authoring work within its sandboxed environment.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8]
3. **Deterministic Evaluation:** A deterministic gate assesses the candidate artifact. If the check passes and stays within scope, execution exits to controlled effect stages.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8]
4. **Budgeted Retry Evaluation:** If the gate rejects the candidate, the workflow evaluates configured retry criteria including iteration counts, elapsed time, and cost budgets. If criteria permit, a retry is dispatched; otherwise, the workflow halts or escalates to human review.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8]

## Mandatory Invariants
Any conforming implementation must enforce the following invariants:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8]
- The agent cannot declare its own convergence; an independent deterministic gate evaluates every attempt.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8]
- Every loop operates under an explicit budget containing an iteration limit and at least one of a time or cost boundary.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8]
- Attempt counters, gate outputs, and transition reasons must be durably recorded in audit state.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8]
- Following a process restart, the loop resumes from persisted state rather than resetting consumed attempt counters or budgets.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8]
- An output that passes technical verification but violates declared task scope is blocked from executing protected effects.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8]

# References
- Workflows and Process Integration WG: Reference Architectures repository.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-14b411d8]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Practical builder guidance covering secrets management, context redaction, host sandboxing, and runtime tool invocation controls for agentic deployments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide establishes implementable controls for builders deploying production agentic systems across secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99] The guideline focuses on blast-radius minimization and operational hardening, while delegating comprehensive identity delegation and SPIFFE/SVID workload attestation architectures to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99]

# Architecture / Specification

## Secrets Management: Ephemeral Attestation Hierarchy
Static, long-lived credentials and environment-variable secrets present durable attack surfaces vulnerable to prompt injection, deserialization leaks, and lateral movement.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99] The guide establishes five progressive secrets management patterns in adoption priority order:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99]
1. **Workload Identity:** Native platform attestation (AWS IRSA, GCP Workload Identity, Azure Managed Identity) exchanging cluster OIDC tokens for short-lived credentials without storing ambient secrets in container environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99]
2. **Dynamic Secrets:** Ephemeral credentials issued on demand by secrets management engines (e.g., HashiCorp Vault) with granular time-to-live expiration.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99]
3. **Network-Layer Injection:** Sidecars or proxy gateways attaching credentials to upstream calls out-of-band so agent processes never observe or serialize secret material.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99]
4. **Confidential Computing:** Hardware enclaves (Intel TDX, AMD SEV-SNP) providing VM-level isolation for high-sensitivity multi-tenant contexts, which must still be combined with short token lifetimes because guest software remains inside the trusted computing base.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99]
5. **OAuth Token Exchange (RFC 8693):** Cryptographic scope narrowing applied across each hop of multi-agent delegation chains.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99]

## Secure Tool Invocation and MCP Hardening
Model Context Protocol (MCP) deployments face structural security risks because OAuth 2.1 authentication is optional in the specification and stdio transport is exempt by default, creating exposure to tool poisoning, rug pulls, and cross-server shadowing.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99] Essential controls include:
- **Pre-Deployment Static Scanning:** Auditing source activity, checking public vulnerability registries, and executing static analysis before establishing server connections.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99]
- **Transport Isolation:** Treating third-party stdio servers as untrusted local binaries executing with full user privileges, while requiring OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and RFC 8707 audience-bound resource indicators across remote HTTP transports.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99]

# References
- Security & Privacy Working Group: Deliverable 4 (Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-eaf41d99]

proposed_concept.title: Zeko
proposed_concept.description: Open-source agentic rollup protocol providing zero-knowledge state verification and instant transaction ordering for multi-agent coordination.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Zeko is an open-source agentic rollup protocol designed to provide verifiable shared state, instant transaction confirmation, and recursive zero-knowledge proofs for autonomous AI agent coordination.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-68] Originating from the Mina ecosystem and extending to Ethereum settlement via SP1 and o1Labs, Zeko enables concurrent agents to coordinate resource reservations, execution budgets, conditional payments, and work commitments against verified state transitions without relying on centralized databases.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-68]

In March 2026, Zeko Labs submitted a project proposal seeking entry into the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) Sandbox stage.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-68]

# Architecture / Specification

## Rollup Mechanics
Zeko provides an off-chain rollup layer that confirms and orders competing agent transactions immediately, avoiding settlement latency on base-layer blockchains:[^evt-project-proposals-issue-68]
- **Recursive Proof Aggregation:** Uses zero-knowledge smart contracts to verify execution correctness and state transitions without requiring participants to re-execute every computational operation.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-68]
- **Settlement and Bridging:** Connects sovereign rollups to Ethereum testnets and mainnet via SP1 zero-knowledge verifiers, supporting optional confidential compute deployments on Phala TEE environments.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-68]
- **Selective Disclosure:** Leverages zero-knowledge proofs so applications can validate policy and budget compliance while protecting private inputs.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-68]

## AAIF Ecosystem Alignments
The proposal details reference integrations with foundational AAIF protocols and frameworks:[^evt-project-proposals-issue-68]
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP) and A2A:** Enabling concurrent agents to coordinate reservations and tool commitments against shared accepted state.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-68]
- **Goose:** Enforcing user-approved budget limits and recording authority transitions outside model context windows.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-68]
- **Agent Gateway:** Synchronizing decentralized resource accounting so requests routed through distinct proxies consume shared budgets.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-68]
- **OpenSandbox and OpenEnv:** Persisting verifiable resource allocations and job receipts across container restarts and reinforcement learning episode resets.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-68]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-03-02:** Project proposal submitted by Zeko Labs for admission to the AAIF Sandbox stage (`evt-project-proposals-issue-68`).[^evt-project-proposals-issue-68]

# References
- AAIF Project Proposal Issue #68: Zeko.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-68]

proposed_concept.title: Runkite
proposed_concept.description: Open-source self-hosted control plane for AI agents separating operational run lifecycle, approval gates, and spend accounting from model-loop execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Runkite is an open-source, self-hosted control plane for AI agents that decouples operational agent management from framework-specific model-loop implementations.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-69] Implemented as a Go core binary with SQLite/Postgres persistence and Redis queuing, Runkite coordinates run admission, dispatch, connector access, human approvals, spend accounting, and operational audit logging while orchestrating external Python and TypeScript runners over gRPC.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-69]

In March 2026, founder Sharan Harsoor submitted Runkite as a project proposal for admission into the AAIF Sandbox lifecycle stage.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-69]

# Architecture / Specification

## System Architecture
Runkite divides agent infrastructure into distinct operational layers:[^evt-project-proposals-issue-69]
- **Control Plane Binary:** Implemented in Go under Apache-2.0, providing HTTP endpoints for thread and run management, streaming events over Server-Sent Events (SSE) and WebSockets, and hosting an embedded operations UI.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-69]
- **Runner Protocol:** A gRPC contract connecting the control plane to language-specific runners (Python, TypeScript) that execute agent tasks using their native SDKs.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-69]
- **Connector and Decision Gateways:** Exposes configured agents as Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools and provides a pre-call policy decision API for independent application loops, dynamically resolving secret references at session time.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-69]

## Protocol and Framework Integrations
Runkite implements public streamable HTTP `/mcp` endpoints using the official MCP Go SDK, allowing external MCP clients to invoke managed agent runs as standard tools while mediating outbound connector access through explicit approval gates.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-69]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-03-02:** Project proposal submitted to AAIF Project Proposals repository requesting Sandbox stage admission (`evt-project-proposals-issue-69`).[^evt-project-proposals-issue-69]

# References
- AAIF Project Proposal Issue #69: Runkite.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-69]

proposed_concept.title: Recoverability
proposed_concept.description: Operational ability of an agentic system to detect failures, contain impact, and return to an acceptable state within bounded cost.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Recoverability defines the operational ability of an agentic system to detect execution failures, contain their blast radius, and restore system state to an acceptable condition within bounded computational and financial costs [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-106]. Introduced as part of the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) Deliverable 1 canonical glossary, the term formalizes recovery criteria for autonomous workflows [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-106].

# Architecture / Specification
The taxonomy definition establishes key boundaries distinguishing recoverability from adjacent operational concepts [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-106]:
- **Failure Detection and Containment**: Systems must actively identify anomalies or broken execution invariants and prevent unconstrained failure propagation.
- **Acceptable State vs. Reversibility**: Recoverability focuses on reaching a safe, well-defined acceptable state rather than requiring strict reversibility or total transaction rollback.
- **Cost Bounds**: State restoration must execute within declared resource and financial budget limits to prevent runaway recovery loops.

# References
- Taxonomy workstream PR #106 [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-106]

proposed_concept.title: Infrastructure
proposed_concept.description: The runtime, orchestration, networking, messaging, and data services supporting agent execution, distinct from tools and harnesses.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Infrastructure encompasses the runtime, orchestration, networking, messaging, and data services upon which an AI agent operates [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-105]. Voted as a universal taxonomy term within the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) Deliverable 1 glossary, it demarcates foundational execution environments from cognitive frameworks and external integrations [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-105].

# Architecture / Specification
The term establishes a taxonomic boundary separating infrastructure layers from higher-level agent components [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-105]:
- **Boundary from Harness and Tools**: Infrastructure provides foundational compute platforms and communication fabrics, distinctly separated from agent harness scaffolding and callable [tools](../taxonomy/tool.md).
- **Failure Attribution**: Establishes an explicit order of attribution when diagnosing agent anomalies, isolating whether failures originate in underlying network, storage, and orchestration platforms or within agent reasoning and tool interfaces.

# References
- Taxonomy workstream PR #105 [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-105]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Identity Primitives
proposed_concept.description: Draft foundational specification defining attestation models, accountability structures, revocability, and identity standards for autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Identity Primitives draft specification (v0.1) defines foundational identity, attestation, accountability, and revocation requirements tailored specifically to autonomous AI agents [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-26] [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-27]. Developed under the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), the standard addresses structural shortcomings in legacy workload and human identity standards that fail under long, dynamic, and autonomous agent delegation chains [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-28].

# Architecture / Specification
The draft specification establishes four core structural domains:
- **Agent Differentiation and Risk Amplification**: Section 1.1 highlights why agents exacerbate traditional identity gaps, citing longer delegation chains, dynamic runtime path selection, high operational autonomy without human-in-the-loop oversight, and unpredictable resource access [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-28].
- **Accountability and Delegation**: Section 3.2 structures accountability chains across principals, responsible parties, upstream authorities, and intermediate subagents [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-27].
- **Attestation Framework**: Section 3.4 outlines six core attestation types: identity, provenance, software, environment/hardware, approval, and intervention [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-26]. Identity attestation serves as the minimum requirement for authentication, while working group discussions evaluate how provenance, software, and hardware measurements should compose pre-issuance evidence [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-26].
- **Revocability and Cross-Domain Gaps**: Section 3.6 defines revocation triggers by principals, providers, and upstream accountable parties [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-27]. Section 4 documents nine standards interoperability gaps, including cross-domain revocation propagation and RFC 8693 nested token limitations [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-27] [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-28].

# References
- WG Identity and Trust Issue #26 [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-26]
- WG Identity and Trust Issue #27 [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-27]
- WG Identity and Trust Issue #28 [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-28]

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards, delegation models, cryptographic trust frameworks, and identity primitives for autonomous AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to establishing vendor-neutral identity primitives, cryptographic trust fabrics, verifiable delegation models, and lifecycle revocation mechanisms for autonomous agents [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-26] [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-27].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group is actively developing the [Agent Identity Primitives](../standards/agent-identity-primitives.md) specification (v0.1), focusing on several critical architectural areas [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-26] [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-27]:
- **Attestation Typing and Layering**: Investigating relationships across six core attestation categories—identity, provenance, software, environment/hardware, approval, and intervention—including how pre-issuance evidence conditions identity attestation issuance [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-26].
- **Revocation and Authority Standing**: Resolving cross-domain revocation propagation and clarifying whether legal or regulatory findings grant third parties standing to withdraw trust from root authorities [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-27].
- **Agent Identity Gap Analysis**: Evaluating nine critical interoperability gaps in existing specifications (such as RFC 8693 token exchange) that become pressing due to subagent spawning and dynamic runtime delegation [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-28].

# References
- WG Identity and Trust Issue #26 [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-26]
- WG Identity and Trust Issue #27 [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-27]
- WG Identity and Trust Issue #28 [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-28]

mutations.rationale: PR #102 in the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream introduces the canonical definition and four dimensions of Reliability.

proposed_concept.title: Reliability
proposed_concept.description: Stability of correct results across repeated agent runs and changing environmental conditions within a declared operational scope.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Reliability in agentic AI is the stability of correct results across repeated runs and changing conditions within a declared operational scope[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-102]. Authored as part of the Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) Deliverable 1 canonical glossary, the definition explicitly separates behavioral dependability from lower-level infrastructure and platform availability[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-102].

# Architecture / Specification
Reliability is evaluated across four core dimensions within the agent's declared scope note[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-102]:
- **Consistency**: Generating equivalent and reproducible outputs when presented with identical or functionally equivalent inputs across distinct sessions.
- **Robustness**: Retaining valid operational capabilities and bounded degradation in the presence of noisy, incomplete, or shifting external environment inputs.
- **Predictability**: Maintaining execution paths that conform strictly to stated behavioral parameters rather than exhibiting high-variance emergent actions.
- **Safety**: Preserving operational boundaries and avoiding harmful side effects even under boundary failures or partial service outages.

The concept stands in contrast to accuracy, which gauges the degree of correctness for an individual output against ground truth, and platform availability, which tracks raw uptime of compute, tool endpoints, and [infrastructure](../taxonomy/infrastructure.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-102].

# Lifecycle History
The term was voted KEEP in the Taxonomy Workstream consensus review and submitted for formal inclusion via pull request in the taxonomy registry[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-102].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification
proposed_concept.description: Multi-dimensional taxonomy and classification schema characterizing agentic AI production deployments across operational patterns and human interaction levels.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification schema is a standardized evaluation matrix created by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to characterize production agent implementations by operational pattern, automation tier, and risk level[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-62]. The schema indexes deployed enterprise and community workflows to guide adoption and reference architecture selection[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-62].

# Architecture / Specification
The schema classifies agentic deployments through several primary axes:
- **Interaction Topology**: Single-agent execution versus orchestrated multi-agent topologies such as parallel research or supervisor patterns.
- **Oversight and Approval**: Presence of deterministic gates, human authorization checkpoints, or unconstrained autonomous iterations.
- **Action Radius**: Read-only analysis, sandboxed state generation, or direct external side-effect execution across production tool interfaces.
- **State and Context Lifecycle**: Ephemeral single-turn tasks versus persistent, recoverable conversational and memory sessions.

# Lifecycle History
Following review, the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group formally approved the use case classification schema and its initial seed list of reference deployments, removing provisional draft markers from the specification while migrating remaining feature feedback into ongoing tracker issues[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-62].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing agent telemetry, causal execution traces, protocol boundary metrics, and trajectory data models.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes agentic instrumentation, causal execution tracing, and telemetry interchange across multi-agent environments[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a09ec8b0fa09-bfbbd7a5]. The group collaborates closely with upstream standards bodies including OpenTelemetry (OTel), the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF), and the Internet Research Task Force (IRTF) to establish vendor-neutral tracing models[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a09ec8b0fa09-bfbbd7a5].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group drives three primary technical workstreams[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a09ec8b0fa09-bfbbd7a5]:
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Defining normalized execution entities, step-turn semantics, and translation layers between OpenTelemetry Line Protocol (OTLP) and agent behaviors in cooperation with the OTel GenAI Special Interest Group[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a09ec8b0fa09-bfbbd7a5].
- **Trajectory Standardization**: Aligning agent run trajectories across formats such as Agent Trajectory Interchange Format (ATIF v2) and OTel distributed trace spans, reconciling log event representation with dedicated trajectory signals[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a09ec8b0fa09-bfbbd7a5].
- **Practitioner Guidance & White Papers**: Formulating vendor-agnostic guidance and reference architectures evaluated across IETF working groups (including DAWN and DMSC) and IRTF research groups[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a09ec8b0fa09-bfbbd7a5].

# Lifecycle History
In late 2026, the group appointed Dawn Wageshear as Technical Program Manager and initiated cross-organization alignment with the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG on trace payload signing and trajectory schemas[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a09ec8b0fa09-bfbbd7a5].

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards, delegation models, cryptographic trust frameworks, and runtime attestation protocols.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group establishes vendor-neutral standards, cryptographic identity profiles, delegation models, and trust architectures for autonomous AI agents[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-29]. Its remit spans runtime hardware attestation, mutual authentication, decentralized identifiers, and verifiable authority delegation across agent interactions[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-29].

# Architecture / Specification
The group investigates trust establishment at transport and application layers:
- **Attestation Protocols**: Evaluating runtime attestation mechanisms for confidential computing environments, specifically addressing security boundaries between early attestation and post-handshake attestation models[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-29].
- **Identity and Delegation Primitives**: Structuring tamper-evident receipts, authority-at-dispatch tokens, and credential delegation chains.
- **Standards Coordination**: Harmonizing attestation profiles across the Confidential Computing Consortium (CCC), IETF, and IRTF groups[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-29].

# Lifecycle History
Discussions in 2026 reviewed widespread industry deprecation and CVE advisories concerning early TLS attestation implementations (the EarlyAttestationTschüss research disclosure), prompting the working group to focus evaluation toward post-handshake attestation protocols such as SEAT-Expat[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-29].
