proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Procedural operations pipeline and shared infrastructure managing chapter provisioning, estate lifecycle automation, and cap constraints.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Community Event Operations provides automated procedures, validation guards, and sync scripts supporting the AAIF city chapter network and event lifecycle[^evt-community-events-pr-69]. It enforces operational governance limits on active chapters while orchestrating Drive folder creation, tracker synchronization, and roster management[^evt-community-events-pr-69].

# Architecture / Specification
The pipeline coordinates several automated utilities:
- **Chapter Provisioning Guard**: Enforces global chapter ceilings via `CHAPTER_CAP`, ensuring automated tools like `create_chapter.py` and `sync_chapters.py` do not exceed authorized organizational bandwidth[^evt-community-events-pr-69].
- **Sync Reconciliation**: Validates accepted organizers against official chapter lists, gating Drive folder generation and Luma feed updates until criteria are satisfied[^evt-community-events-pr-69].
- **Automated Verification**: Integrates unit and regression suites (`test_chapter_cap`, `test_chapter_health`, `test_sync`) to dynamically calculate expected boundaries and preserve estate integrity[^evt-community-events-pr-69].

# Lifecycle History
Following the onboarding of chapters in Columbus and Philadelphia that reached the initial 100-chapter ceiling, the operational chapter cap was expanded from 100 to 125 to permit continuous chapter intake without retiring active chapters[^evt-community-events-pr-69].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate automated CI taxonomy validation workflow specifications and maintainer-review gating rules to prevent data corruption and compute abuse.

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy Contribution Guide
proposed_concept.description: Authoring standards, automated schema validation workflows, and pull request review gates governing contributions to the AAIF taxonomy.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy Contribution Guide establishes the authoring standards, schema constraints, and pull request gating procedures required for modifications to the Agentic AI Foundation taxonomy repository [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-75f907b5]. It ensures data integrity and protects shared repository infrastructure against compute abuse during community review cycles [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-75f907b5].

# Architecture / Specification

Contributions modifying `taxonomy/taxonomy.json` must pass automated structural validation prior to merge into the push-protected `main` branch [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-75f907b5].

## Continuous Integration and Gating

To mitigate compute-abuse risks from anonymous pushes, automated validation workflows are gated behind maintainer actions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-75f907b5]:
- **Trigger Events**: The validation workflow fires on `pull_request_review` events (submitted or edited) and maintainer `workflow_dispatch` invocations [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-75f907b5].
- **Execution Environment**: Runs under Node.js 20 on Ubuntu with a strict five-minute timeout and automatic cancellation of superseded runs via GitHub concurrency groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-75f907b5].
- **Merge Reference Validation**: Pull request validation checks out the computed merge reference (`refs/pull/{number}/merge`) to evaluate the exact candidate state that would land on `main` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-75f907b5].
- **Execution Checks**: Dependencies are installed with `npm ci --ignore-scripts` before executing `npm run check` to verify JSON syntax and schema compliance [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-75f907b5].

# Lifecycle History

The automated validation workflow was instituted following data corruption regressions (such as unescaped quotes in taxonomy scope notes) to ensure machine-readable taxonomy integrity [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-75f907b5].

mutations.rationale: Document active draft proposals for agent identity in telemetry, accountability attributes, and asynchronous dispatch trace attribution.

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group standardizing agent telemetry, causal execution traces, protocol boundary metrics, and identity accountability attributes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes vendor-neutral telemetry models, distributed execution tracing, and protocol boundary metrics across agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-75]. Its remit includes defining causal context propagation across tool boundaries, capturing hierarchical agent task execution, and standardizing identity attribution in telemetry streams [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-75, ^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-76].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group standardizes telemetry interfaces, semantic conventions, and correlation models for agent runtimes and tools.

## Agent Identity and Accountability Telemetry

Recent working documents develop semantic conventions for agent identity and accountability attribution within distributed traces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-75, ^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-76]:
- **Accountability Attribute Group**: Introduces the `agent.accountability.*` attribute namespace, including result, reference, and assurance fields [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-75].
- **Span-to-Record References**: Employs `agent.accountability.ref` to correlate trace spans with audit records, bounded so that references neither resolve outside the deciding authority nor leak beyond its trust domain [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-75].
- **Redaction and Sanitization Rules**: Establishes redaction rules developed jointly with the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to sanitize identity attributes across trust boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-75, ^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-76].
- **Asynchronous Execution Tracing**: Models lifecycle events across asynchronous queues, separating approved span fields from local audit evidence while capturing dispatch refusals and post-dispatch revocations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-76].

# Lifecycle History

Draft proposals PR#75 and PR#76 extended the group's agent identity telemetry track (Issue #50), establishing attribution schemas and asynchronous trace semantics aligned with OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-75, ^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-76].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate work on the ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 operational viewpoint for reference architectures and multi-hop delegation evidence continuity.

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards, delegation models, cryptographic trust roots, and multi-hop operational viewpoints for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity and Trust Working Group establishes vendor-neutral identity primitives, cryptographic attestation mechanisms, and authority delegation frameworks for agentic AI deployments [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-25]. It defines how agents assert identity, inherit permissions from principals, verify counterparties across institutional trust boundaries, and maintain delegation continuity [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-25, ^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-30].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group models agent authority, verifiable identity assertions, and multi-party trust topologies.

## Reference Architecture Operational Viewpoint

The working group develops an operational viewpoint based on ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 to define authority and accountability flow across agent systems [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-25]:
- **Actor Model**: Formulates explicit operational roles for interacting entities, evaluating extensions for specialized roles such as Approver and Auditor [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-25].
- **Delegation Models**: Governs authority attenuation, shared execution limits, multi-parent delegation graphs, cross-organizational hops, and delegation finalisation [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-25].
- **Operational Rules and Scenarios**: Establishes candidate conformance scenarios (S1–S12) and normative rules (R1–R13) to validate authority handling during dispatch, timeout, and delegation replacement [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-25].

## Multi-Hop Delegation Evidence

In coordination with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the group explores delegation evidence across hops where telemetry cannot carry full proof artifacts [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-30]:
- **Verifiable Delegation Roots**: Specifying verification requirements for each intermediary hop back to an accountable root principal [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-30].
- **Trust Boundary Translation**: Recording identity mappings where identifiers are translated across distinct organizational or cryptographic boundaries [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-30].

# Lifecycle History

Discussions in Issue #25 and Issue #30 expanded the working group's scope to formal architectural viewpoints and cross-boundary delegation evidence continuity [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-25, ^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-30].

mutations.rationale: Document the initiation of Deliverable D2 on gap analysis and benchmark surveys addressing operational side-effect safety and durable execution.

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining failure mode taxonomies, evaluation frameworks, reliable architectures, and gap analysis benchmarks for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group develops evaluation benchmarks, failure mode classifications, and architectural patterns to ensure predictable and recoverable agent execution [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-16]. Its work centers on benchmarking agent performance, mitigating non-deterministic failure modes, and establishing standards for safe tool execution [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-16].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group structures its outputs around empirical surveys, failure classification schemas, and gap analysis deliverables.

## Deliverable Tracks

- **D1 Benchmark Framework**: Establishes foundational reliability definitions, failure taxonomies, and testing methodologies [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-16].
- **D2 Gap Analysis and Benchmark Survey**: Evaluates operational capabilities and tooling gaps across the production agent lifecycle using structured question cards [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-16].
- **Side-Effect Safety**: Analyzes guarantees required to enforce exactly-once execution when agent tool calls fail or time out [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-16].
- **Durable Execution**: Analyzes patterns such as [Durable Wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md) and state persistence to ensure recoverability following process interruptions [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-16].

# Lifecycle History

Deliverable D2 was drafted in PR#16, introducing a modular question-card format across lifecycle stages to track gaps in tooling, side-effect safety, and durable execution [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-16].

mutations.rationale: Defines Accuracy as an official AAIF taxonomy term specifying single-run correctness against declared criteria, originated by the Accuracy and Reliability Working Group.

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy
proposed_concept.description: Single-run correctness property of an agentic system evaluated against a declared correctness criterion.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
**Accuracy** is the property of an agentic execution whereby a single run produces correct outputs and behavior when evaluated against an explicitly declared correctness criterion.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-101] Originated by the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) as part of its canonical terminology and taxonomy deliverable, accuracy focuses on individual execution correctness rather than consistency across repeated invocations.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-101]

In the AAIF taxonomy, accuracy contrasts directly with [reliability](../taxonomy/reliability.md), which assesses the stability of correct results across repeated agent runs and changing environmental conditions.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-101]

# Architecture / Specification
The taxonomy scope note establishes two primary dimensions of accuracy within an agent execution:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-101]

- **Outcome Accuracy**: Evaluates whether the final artifact, response, or terminal state generated by the agent satisfies the declared correctness specification.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-101]
- **Action Accuracy**: Evaluates whether the intermediate tool calls, parameter selections, and protocol interactions executed by the agent follow expected procedures and valid execution constraints.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-101]

Both dimensions mandate an explicit, observable reference criterion against which correctness is measured, precluding undefined or subjective expectations during evaluation.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-101]

# Lifecycle History
- **Deliverable 1 Addition**: Defined by the Accuracy and Reliability Working Group via PR #101 in `ws-taxonomy-landscape`, voted KEEP in the canonical taxonomy workstream review.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-101]

mutations.rationale: Defines Robustness as an official AAIF taxonomy term characterizing reliability across input variations, shifting conditions, and faults.

proposed_concept.title: Robustness
proposed_concept.description: Reliability dimension measuring an agentic system's stability under meaning-preserving input rephrasings, shifting environmental conditions, and underlying faults.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
**Robustness** is the dimension of [reliability](../taxonomy/reliability.md) evaluating an agentic system's capacity to maintain correct operation in the presence of meaning-preserving input rephrasings, shifting conditions, and operational faults.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-103] Established by the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), robustness categorizes how an agent accommodates operational variance without catastrophic degradation or task failure.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-103]

# Architecture / Specification
The AAIF taxonomy structures robustness across three operational sub-types and delineates strict conceptual boundaries:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-103]

- **Prompt Robustness**: Resilience against syntactic rephrasing, semantic paraphrasing, irrelevant context, or formatting variance that preserves the underlying intent.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-103]
- **Fault Robustness**: Ability to withstand tool execution exceptions, transient network failures, and degraded model service availability during execution.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-103]
- **Environment Robustness**: Stability across external system changes, variable API latency, and shifting data schemas.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-103]

### Conceptual Boundaries
Robustness is distinguished from adjacent reliability concepts:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-103]
- Distinct from [recoverability](../taxonomy/recoverability.md), which focuses on detecting failures and returning the system to an acceptable state once a disruption has materialized.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-103]
- Separated from active threat mitigation under the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), reserving robustness specifically for non-adversarial perturbations and environmental volatility.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-103]

# Lifecycle History
- **Deliverable 1 Addition**: Defined by the Accuracy and Reliability Working Group via PR #103 in `ws-taxonomy-landscape`, voted KEEP in the canonical taxonomy workstream review.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-103]

mutations.rationale: Defines Safety as an official AAIF taxonomy term governing the prevention of prohibited, harmful, or unauthorized agent actions.

proposed_concept.title: Safety
proposed_concept.description: Reliability dimension ensuring an agentic system prevents prohibited, harmful, or unauthorized actions under prevailing governance policies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
**Safety** is the dimension of [reliability](../taxonomy/reliability.md) concerning the prevention of prohibited, harmful, or unauthorized actions by an agentic system under the policies in force.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-104] Standardized by the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), safety focuses on negative constraints and boundary enforcement during autonomous agent execution.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-104]

# Architecture / Specification
The taxonomy scope note establishes key reporting requirements and domain boundaries for safety:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-104]

- **Separate Metric Reporting**: Safety evaluation must be reported independently from general correctness or [accuracy](../taxonomy/accuracy.md) aggregates, preventing high task success rates from masking critical policy violations.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-104]
- **Policy Grounding**: Safety is evaluated strictly against active organizational, operational, and regulatory policies governing permitted actions and tools.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-104]
- **Scope Exclusion**: Explicitly excludes the distributed-systems definition of safety (such as invariant state preservation or avoiding deadlock/race conditions), applying exclusively to harm prevention, authorization bounds, and policy compliance.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-104]

# Lifecycle History
- **Deliverable 1 Addition**: Defined by the Accuracy and Reliability Working Group via PR #104 in `ws-taxonomy-landscape`, voted KEEP in the canonical taxonomy workstream review.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-104]
